manualTranslations.zh: 於是兵部侍郎張均及職方郎中韋述等建議曰：謹按《禮祭統》曰：「凡天之所生，地之所長，苟可薦者，莫不咸在。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun, Director of the Bureau of Operations Wei Shu, and others proposed: Respectfully, according to 《Li Jitong》, "Of all that Heaven produces and Earth grows, if it can be offered, nothing is not present.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, Wei Shu, and the others answered by citing 《Li Jitong》: "All things produced by Heaven and grown by Earth may be included when they are fit to offer.

manualTranslations.zh: 水草陸海，三牲八簋，昆蟲之異，草木之實，陰陽之物，皆備薦矣。」
manualTranslations.literal: Water plants and land and sea products, the three sacrificial animals and eight grain vessels, strange insects, fruits of plants and trees, and things of yin and yang are all fully offered."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Water plants, goods of land and sea, sacrificial animals, grain vessels, unusual creatures, fruits, and all things of yin and yang are provided for the offering."

manualTranslations.zh: 聖人知孝子之情深，而物類之無限，故為之節制，使祭有常禮，物有其品，器有其數。
manualTranslations.literal: The sages knew that the feelings of filial sons were deep and that the categories of things were without limit, so they made regulations for them, causing sacrifices to have constant rites, objects to have their grades, and vessels to have their numbers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sages knew filial feeling was deep but the range of possible offerings was endless, so they regulated sacrifice with fixed rites, ranked offerings, and counted vessels.

manualTranslations.zh: 上自天子，下至公卿，貴賤差降，無相逾越，百代常行無易之道也。
manualTranslations.literal: Above, from the Son of Heaven, down to dukes and ministers, noble and base differ by descending grades and do not overstep one another; this is the constant way practiced for a hundred generations and not changed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the emperor down through the high ministers, rank determined what could be used, with no overstepping. This was the enduring rule of successive ages.

manualTranslations.zh: 又按《周禮•膳夫》，「掌王之食飲膳羞：食用六穀，膳用六牲，飲用六清，羞用百有二十品，珍用八物，醬用百有二十甕」，則與祭祀之物，豐省本殊。
manualTranslations.literal: Again, according to 《Zhouli: Shanfu》, "He manages the king's foods, drinks, viands, and delicacies: food uses the six grains, viands use the six animals, drinks use the six clear liquors, delicacies use 120 kinds, rarities use eight things, and sauces use 120 jars"; thus these and the things of sacrifice differ fundamentally in abundance and simplicity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Zhouli: Shanfu》 says: "The officer manages the king's foods, drinks, viands, and delicacies," with many grains, animals, drinks, delicacies, rarities, and sauces; this shows that royal meals and sacrificial offerings differed by nature in abundance and restraint.

manualTranslations.zh: 《左傳》曰：「享以訓恭儉，宴以示慈惠，恭儉以行禮，慈惠以布政。」
manualTranslations.literal: 《Zuozhuan》 says: "The formal offering teaches reverence and frugality; the banquet displays kindness and favor. Reverence and frugality carry out ritual; kindness and favor spread government."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Zuozhuan》 says: "Formal offerings teach reverence and restraint; banquets display kindness and grace; reverence and restraint carry out ritual, and kindness and grace spread government."

manualTranslations.zh: 又曰：「享有體薦，宴有折俎。」
manualTranslations.literal: It also says: "At formal offerings there are whole-body presentations; at banquets there are cut-up stands."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It also says: "Formal offerings present whole victims; banquets serve cut meat."

manualTranslations.zh: 杜預曰：「享有體薦，爵盈而不飲，豆乾而不食，宴則相與食之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Du Yu said: "At formal offerings there are whole-body presentations; the cup is full but not drunk, and the dishes are dry but not eaten. At banquets, people eat them together."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Yu explains: "In formal offerings the cup is filled but not drunk, and the dishes are set out but not eaten; at banquets, the participants eat together."

manualTranslations.zh: 享之與宴，猶且異文，祭奠所陳，固不同矣。
manualTranslations.literal: If offerings and banquets even have different wording, then what is set out in sacrifices and libations is certainly not the same.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since even the terminology separates offerings from banquets, sacrificial displays plainly should not be treated as ordinary meals.

manualTranslations.zh: 又按《周禮》，籩人、豆人，各掌四籩、四豆之實，供祭祀與賓客，所用各殊。
manualTranslations.literal: Again, according to 《Zhouli》, the officers of baskets and dishes each manage the contents of the four baskets and four dishes, supplying sacrifices and guests, and the things used in each are different.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Zhouli》 also assigns separate basket and dish offerings for sacrifices and for guests, with different contents for each use.

manualTranslations.zh: 據此數文，祭奠不同常時，其來久矣。
manualTranslations.literal: On the basis of these several texts, sacrifices and libations have differed from ordinary occasions for a long time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: These passages show that sacrificial offerings have long been distinct from everyday food.

manualTranslations.zh: 且人之嗜好，本無憑准，宴私之饌，與時遷移。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, human tastes and preferences have no fixed standard, and the dishes of private feasts shift with the times.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Personal tastes have no stable rule, and private banquet fare changes from age to age.

manualTranslations.zh: 故聖人一切同歸于古，難平生所嗜，非禮亦不薦也；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore the sages in all cases returned them to antiquity; even what one liked in life, if it was not ritual, was not offered;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sages therefore brought sacrifice back to ancient norms: even favorite foods from life were not offered if they did not accord with ritual;

manualTranslations.zh: 平生所惡，是禮即不去也。
manualTranslations.literal: what one disliked in life, if it was ritual, was not removed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and even disliked foods were retained if ritual required them.

manualTranslations.zh: 《楚語》曰：「屈到嗜芰，有疾，召宗老而屬曰：『祭我必以芰。』
manualTranslations.literal: 《Discourses of Chu》 says: "Qu Dao liked water chestnuts. When ill, he summoned the clan elders and instructed them, saying, 'When sacrificing to me, be sure to use water chestnuts.'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Discourses of Chu》 records that Qu Dao loved water chestnuts and, when sick, told the clan elders, 'Use water chestnuts in my sacrifices.'

manualTranslations.zh: 及卒，宗老將薦芰，屈建命去之，曰：『祭典有之，國君有牛享，大夫有羊饋，士有豚犬之奠，庶人有魚炙之薦，籩豆脯醢，則上下安之。
manualTranslations.literal: When he died, the clan elders were about to offer water chestnuts, but Qu Jian ordered them removed, saying, 'The sacrificial canon has this: the ruler of a state has the ox offering, a great officer has the sheep presentation, a knight has the libation of pig and dog, common people have offerings of fish and roast meat, and with baskets and dishes of dried meat and mince, high and low are settled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Qu Dao died, the elders prepared water chestnuts, but Qu Jian had them removed, explaining that the ritual canon assigns oxen, sheep, pigs and dogs, fish and roasted meat, baskets, and dishes according to rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 不羞珍異，不陳庶侈，不以私欲幹國之典』遂不用。」
manualTranslations.literal: It does not present rare and strange things, does not set out common extravagances, and does not use private desire to interfere with the state canon'; accordingly they did not use them."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It does not present exotic delicacies or private extravagance, and it does not let personal desire disturb the state ritual. So the water chestnuts were not used."

manualTranslations.zh: 此則禮外之食，前賢不敢薦也。
manualTranslations.literal: This means that foods outside ritual were things earlier worthies did not dare to offer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus earlier worthies would not offer foods outside the ritual code.

manualTranslations.zh: 今欲取甘旨之物，肥濃之味，隨所有者皆充祭用，苟逾舊制，其何限焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Now if one wishes to take sweet and savory things, rich and heavy flavors, and, according to whatever exists, fill out sacrificial use with all of them, then exceeding the old system would leave no limit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If every sweet, rich, or savory food at hand is admitted into sacrifice, then once the old rules are exceeded there will be no limit.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖籩豆有加，豈能備也？
manualTranslations.literal: Even if baskets and dishes are increased, how could they be complete?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even adding more baskets and dishes, how could the offerings ever be exhaustive?

manualTranslations.zh: 《傳》曰：「大羹不致，粢食不鑿，昭其儉也。」
manualTranslations.literal: 《Tradition》 says: "The great soup is not richly seasoned, and the grain food is not finely polished, displaying frugality."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Tradition》 says: "The great soup is not richly seasoned, and the grain food is not finely polished, displaying frugality."

manualTranslations.zh: 《書》曰：「黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」
manualTranslations.literal: 《Documents》 says: "Millet and panicled millet are not the fragrance; bright virtue alone is fragrant."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Documents》 says: "Millet and panicled millet are not the fragrance; bright virtue alone is fragrant."

manualTranslations.zh: 事神在於虔誠，不求厭飫。
manualTranslations.literal: Serving spirits lies in reverent sincerity, not in seeking satiety.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Serving the spirits depends on sincerity, not on feeding them to fullness.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年一禘，不欲黷也。
manualTranslations.literal: The di sacrifice occurs once in three years because one does not wish to make it profane by frequency.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The di sacrifice is held only once every three years to avoid irreverent overuse.

manualTranslations.zh: 三獻而終，禮有成也。
manualTranslations.literal: It ends after the three offerings because ritual has completion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rite ends with three offerings because ritual must have a proper completion.

manualTranslations.zh: 《風》有《采蘋》、《采蘩》，《雅》有《行葦》《泂酌》，守以忠信，神其舍諸！
manualTranslations.literal: In the 《Airs》 there are 《Gathering Duckweed》 and 《Gathering Artemisia》; in the 《Ya》 there are 《Walking Among the Reeds》 and 《Clear Libation》. If they are kept with loyalty and trust, would the spirits reject them!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The 《Airs》 have 《Gathering Duckweed》 and 《Gathering Artemisia》; the 《Ya》 has 《Walking Among the Reeds》 and 《Clear Libation》. If offerings are kept with loyalty and trust, surely the spirits would not reject them!

manualTranslations.zh: 若以今之珍饌，平生所習，求神無方，何必師古。
manualTranslations.literal: If one uses today's precious foods, what one was accustomed to in ordinary life, seeking the spirits without method, there would be no need to take antiquity as teacher.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If current delicacies and everyday habits are enough to seek the spirits, then there is no reason to follow antiquity at all.

manualTranslations.zh: 簠簋可去，而盤盂杯案當在御矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The fu and gui vessels could be discarded, and plates, bowls, cups, and trays ought to be used instead.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On that logic, ritual vessels could be thrown out and replaced with plates, bowls, cups, and trays.

manualTranslations.zh: 《韶》《頀》可息，而箜篌笛笙當在奏矣。
manualTranslations.literal: 《Shao》 and 《Hu》 could be stopped, and harps, flutes, and mouth organs ought to be performed instead.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ancient music 《Shao》 and 《Hu》 could likewise give way to harps, flutes, and pipes.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡斯之流，皆非正物，或興於近代，或出於蕃夷，耳目之娛，本無則象，用之宗廟，後嗣何觀？
manualTranslations.literal: All things of this sort are not proper objects. Some arose in recent times, some came from foreign peoples. Pleasures of the ears and eyes originally have no model. If used in the ancestral temple, what will later descendants observe?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such things are not proper ritual objects. Some are recent innovations, others foreign imports, and pleasures for eye and ear have no ritual model; if used in the ancestral temple, what would descendants see?

manualTranslations.zh: 欲為永式，恐未可也。
manualTranslations.literal: If one wishes to make them a permanent rule, I fear it cannot be done.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They should not be made a permanent rule.

manualTranslations.zh: 且自漢已降，諸陵皆有寢宮，歲時朔望，薦以常饌，此既常行，亦足盡至孝之情矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, from the Han onward, all tombs have had resting palaces. At seasonal times and on new and full moons, ordinary foods are offered there. Since this is already regularly practiced, it is enough to exhaust the feeling of utmost filial piety.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since the Han, mausoleums have had halls where ordinary foods are offered seasonally and on new and full moons; this already satisfies the deepest filial feeling.

manualTranslations.zh: 宗廟正禮，宜仍典故，率情變革，人情所難。
manualTranslations.literal: For the correct rites of the ancestral temple, one should follow the precedents. To follow feeling and change them is difficult for human sentiment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The formal rites of the ancestral temple should follow precedent; changing them by emotion is hard to justify.

manualTranslations.zh: 又按舊制，一升曰爵，五升曰散。
manualTranslations.literal: Again, according to the old system, one sheng is called a jue, and five sheng are called a san.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The old system called a one-sheng vessel a jue and a five-sheng vessel a san.

manualTranslations.zh: 《禮器》稱：「宗廟之祭，貴者獻以爵，賤者獻以散。」
manualTranslations.literal: 《Ritual Vessels》 says: "In ancestral-temple sacrifices, the honored offer with the jue, and the lowly offer with the san."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Ritual Vessels》 says: "In ancestral-temple sacrifices, the honored offer with the jue, and the lowly offer with the san."

manualTranslations.zh: 此明貴小賤大，示之節儉。
manualTranslations.literal: This makes clear that the honored use the small and the lowly use the large, showing frugality.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This shows that high rank is marked by smaller vessels, a lesson in restraint.

manualTranslations.zh: 又按《國語》觀射父曰：「郊禘不過繭栗，蒸嘗不過把握。」
manualTranslations.literal: Again, according to 《Guoyu》, Guan Shefu said: "For the jiao and di sacrifices, they do not exceed cocoon and chestnut size; for zheng and chang sacrifices, they do not exceed what can be grasped."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Guoyu》 has Guan Shefu say: "The jiao and di sacrifices do not exceed cocoon and chestnut size; the zheng and chang sacrifices do not exceed what can be grasped."

manualTranslations.zh: 夫神，以精明臨人者也，所求備物，不求豐大。
manualTranslations.literal: Spirits come before people with pure brightness; what they seek is complete objects, not abundance and size.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Spirits attend in pure clarity; they require the prescribed set of offerings, not lavish quantity or size.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟失於禮，雖多何為？
manualTranslations.literal: If one loses ritual, even if there is much, what use is it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If ritual is lost, what use is abundance?

manualTranslations.zh: 豈可舍先王之遺法，徇一時之所尚，廢棄禮經，以從流欲。
manualTranslations.literal: One must not abandon the bequeathed laws of the former kings, follow what is fashionable for a moment, discard the ritual classics, and follow drifting desires.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One cannot abandon the former kings' rules, chase the fashion of the moment, and cast aside the ritual classics for passing desire.

manualTranslations.zh: 裂冠毀冕，將安用之！
manualTranslations.literal: If caps are torn and crowns destroyed, what use will they be!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What use is a cap torn apart and a crown destroyed!

manualTranslations.zh: 且君子愛人以禮，不求苟合，況在宗廟，敢忘舊章。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, the gentleman loves people by means of ritual and does not seek careless conformity; still less, in the ancestral temple, would he dare forget the old statutes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A gentleman cares for others through ritual and does not seek easy compliance; in the ancestral temple, he certainly cannot forget the old rules.

manualTranslations.zh: 請依古制，庶可經久。
manualTranslations.literal: We request that the ancient system be followed; perhaps it can endure for long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We request adherence to the ancient system, so the practice may endure.

sourceRange.text: 敕下百僚都省會議，禮部員外薛昭緯奏議曰：伏以禮貴從宜，過猶不及，祀有常典，理當據經。謹按德明追尊，實為遐遠，徵諸歷代，莫有其倫。自古典禮該詳，無逾周室。后稷實始封之祖，文王乃建極之君，且不聞后稷之前，別議立廟。以至二漢則可明徵劉累，梁、魏則近有蕭、曹，稽彼簡書，並無追號。迨於興聖，事非有據。蓋以始王於涼，遂列為祖。類長沙於後漢之代，等楚元于宋高之朝，悉無尊禮之名，足為憲章之驗。重以獻祖、懿祖，皆非宗有德而祖有功，親盡宜祧，理當毀瘞，行於二廟，亦出一時。且武德之初，議宗廟之事，神堯聽之，太宗參之，碩學通儒，森然在列，而不議立皋陶、涼武昭之廟，蓋知其非所宜立也。尊太祖、代祖為帝，而以獻祖為宣簡公，懿祖為懿王，卒不加帝號者，謂其親盡則毀明矣。《春秋左氏傳》：「孔子在陳，聞魯廟災。曰：『其桓僖乎？』已而果然。」蓋以親盡不毀，宜致天災，炯然之徵，不可忽也。據太常禮院狀所引至德二年克復後不作弘農府君廟神主，及晉韋泓「屋朽乃已」之議，頗為明據，深協禮經。其興聖等四室，請依禮院之議。

localRange.text: 敕下百僚都省會議，禮部員外薛昭緯奏議曰：

context.beforeSource: 可依晉韋泓『屋毀乃已』之例，因而廢之。
context.afterSource: 奉敕敬依典禮，付所司。

manualTranslations.zh: 敕下百僚都省會議，禮部員外薛昭緯奏議曰：伏以禮貴從宜，過猶不及，祀有常典，理當據經。
manualTranslations.literal: The edict was sent down for all officials to meet in the Department of State Affairs, and Xue Zhaowei, Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, memorialized: I submit that ritual values adapting to what is fitting; excess is like insufficiency. Sacrifice has constant canons, and principle should rest on the classics.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict was referred to the officials in the Department of State Affairs. Xue Zhaowei of the Ministry of Rites memorialized that ritual must fit the occasion, neither exceeding nor falling short, and that sacrifice should follow the classics.

manualTranslations.zh: 謹按德明追尊，實為遐遠，徵諸歷代，莫有其倫。
manualTranslations.literal: Respectfully considering Deming's posthumous honoring, it is truly remote; when examined through the successive ages, nothing is comparable to it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He argued that the posthumous honoring of Deming was extraordinarily remote, with no parallel in earlier dynasties.

manualTranslations.zh: 自古典禮該詳，無逾周室。
manualTranslations.literal: From antiquity, no ritual code has been more complete and detailed than that of the Zhou house.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among ancient ritual systems, none was more complete than that of Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 后稷實始封之祖，文王乃建極之君，且不聞后稷之前，別議立廟。
manualTranslations.literal: Hou Ji was truly the ancestor first enfeoffed, and King Wen was the lord who established the royal pivot; moreover, one does not hear that before Hou Ji they separately discussed establishing temples.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hou Ji was the first enfeoffed ancestor and King Wen the founder of royal order; no separate temples were proposed for ancestors before Hou Ji.

manualTranslations.zh: 以至二漢則可明徵劉累，梁、魏則近有蕭、曹，稽彼簡書，並無追號。
manualTranslations.literal: Coming down to the two Han, Liu Lei can be clearly cited; for Liang and Wei, there are nearer examples in Xiao and Cao. Examining those records, none had a posthumous title added.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han could trace themselves to Liu Lei, and Liang and Wei to the Xiao and Cao lines, yet their records show no such retroactive honorifics.

manualTranslations.zh: 迨於興聖，事非有據。
manualTranslations.literal: As for Xingsheng, the matter has no evidence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The case for Xingsheng had no evidentiary basis.

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋以始王於涼，遂列為祖。
manualTranslations.literal: It was only because he first became king in Liang that he was then listed as an ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was listed as an ancestor merely because he had first ruled in Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 類長沙於後漢之代，等楚元于宋高之朝，悉無尊禮之名，足為憲章之驗。
manualTranslations.literal: He is like Changsha in the Later Han line and equivalent to Yuan of Chu in the court of Gao of Song; all lacked names of honored ritual, which is sufficient as evidence for regulation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Comparable figures, such as Changsha for Later Han and Yuan of Chu for Emperor Gao of Song, received no such ritual honors; these cases supply the precedent.

manualTranslations.zh: 重以獻祖、懿祖，皆非宗有德而祖有功，親盡宜祧，理當毀瘞，行於二廟，亦出一時。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, Xianzu and Yizu were neither zong with virtue nor zu with merit. When kinship was exhausted they should be moved out; by principle they should be destroyed and buried. Their placement in the two temples also arose at one time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xianzu and Yizu were neither meritorious ancestors nor virtuous temple founders; once their kinship line was exhausted, ritual required removal and burial, and their two temples were only a temporary measure.

manualTranslations.zh: 且武德之初，議宗廟之事，神堯聽之，太宗參之，碩學通儒，森然在列，而不議立皋陶、涼武昭之廟，蓋知其非所宜立也。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of Wude, when ancestral-temple matters were discussed, Shenyao heard them and Taizong participated; eminent scholars and learned classicists stood densely in attendance, yet they did not discuss establishing temples for Gao Yao or Liang Wuzhao, because they knew these should not be established.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude, Gaozu and Taizong considered the temple system with many eminent classicists present, yet no one proposed temples for Gao Yao or Liang Wuzhao, because they knew such temples were improper.

manualTranslations.zh: 尊太祖、代祖為帝，而以獻祖為宣簡公，懿祖為懿王，卒不加帝號者，謂其親盡則毀明矣。
manualTranslations.literal: They honored Taizu and Daizu as emperors, but made Xianzu Duke Xuanjian and Yizu King Yi, and in the end did not add imperial titles; this shows clearly that when kinship was exhausted they were to be destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu and Daizu were honored as emperors, while Xianzu remained Duke Xuanjian and Yizu King Yi; the lack of imperial titles shows they were meant to be removed when kinship ended.

manualTranslations.zh: 《春秋左氏傳》：「孔子在陳，聞魯廟災。
manualTranslations.literal: 《Chunqiu Zuoshi zhuan》 says: "When Confucius was in Chen, he heard of a fire in the Lu temple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Chunqiu Zuoshi zhuan》 says: "When Confucius was in Chen, he heard that the Lu temple had burned.

manualTranslations.zh: 曰：『其桓僖乎？』
manualTranslations.literal: He said, 'Was it Huan and Xi?'
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He asked, 'Was it Huan and Xi?'

manualTranslations.zh: 已而果然。」
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward it was indeed so."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It later proved to be so."

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋以親盡不毀，宜致天災，炯然之徵，不可忽也。
manualTranslations.literal: This was because when kinship was exhausted and the temples were not destroyed, it was fitting that heavenly disaster arrived; this bright evidence cannot be ignored.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The point is that failing to remove temples after kinship ends can bring heavenly disaster; the evidence is clear and cannot be ignored.

manualTranslations.zh: 據太常禮院狀所引至德二年克復後不作弘農府君廟神主，及晉韋泓「屋朽乃已」之議，頗為明據，深協禮經。
manualTranslations.literal: According to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Institute statement, which cited that after the recovery in Zhide 2 no spirit tablet was made for Duke Hongnong, and also cited Wei Hong of Jin's proposal, "when the building decays, then stop," there is rather clear evidence, deeply agreeing with the ritual classics.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Ritual Institute cited clear evidence: after the restoration in Zhide 2 no tablet was made for Duke Hongnong, and Wei Hong of Jin had argued, "when the building decays, then stop." These points accord with the ritual classics.

manualTranslations.zh: 其興聖等四室，請依禮院之議。
manualTranslations.literal: As for the four chambers including Xingsheng, I request that the proposal of the Ritual Institute be followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He requested that the four chambers, including Xingsheng, follow the Ritual Institute's proposal.

sourceRange.text: 元和元年七月，順宗神主將祔，有司疑於遷毀，太常博士王涇建議曰：禮經「祖有功，宗有德」，皆不毀之名也。惟三代行之。漢、魏已降，雖曰祖宗，親盡則遷，無功亦毀，不得行古之道也。昔夏后氏十五代，祖顓頊而宗禹。殷人十七代，祖契而宗湯。周人三十六王，以后稷為太祖，祖文王而宗武王。聖唐德厚流廣，遠法殷、周，奉景皇帝為太祖，祖高祖而宗太宗，皆在百代不遷之典。故代宗升祔，遷代祖也；德宗升祔，遷高宗也。今順宗升祔，中宗在三昭三穆之外，謂之親盡，遷於太廟夾室，禮則然矣。或諫者以則天太后革命，中宗復而興之，不在遷藏之例，臣竊未諭也。昔者高宗晏駕，中宗奉遺詔，自儲副而陟元后。則天太后臨朝，廢為盧陵王。聖曆元年，太后詔復立為皇太子。屬太后聖壽延長，御下日久，奸臣擅命，紊其紀度。敬暉、桓彥範等五臣，俱唐舊臣，匡輔王室，翊中宗而承大統。此乃子繼父業，是中宗得之而且失之；母授子位，是中宗失之而復得之。二十年間，再為皇太子，復踐皇帝位，失之在己，得之在己，可謂革命中興之義殊也。又以周、漢之例推之，幽王為犬戎所滅，平王東遷，周不以平王為中興不遷之廟，其例一也。漢呂后專權，產、祿秉政，文帝自代邸而立之，漢不以文帝為中興不遷之廟，其例二也。霍光輔宣帝，再盛基業，而不以宣帝為不遷之廟，其例三也。伏以中宗孝和皇帝，于聖上為六代伯祖，尊非正統，廟亦親盡。爰及周、漢故事，是與中興功德之主不同，奉遷夾室，固無疑也。

manualTranslations.zh: 元和元年七月，順宗神主將祔，有司疑於遷毀，太常博士王涇建議曰：禮經「祖有功，宗有德」，皆不毀之名也。
manualTranslations.literal: In Yuanhe 1, seventh month, when Shunzong's spirit tablet was about to be enshrined, the offices were uncertain about removal and destruction, and Grand Ritual Erudite Wang Jing proposed: the ritual classics say, "Ancestors have merit, and zong have virtue"; these are both names for those not destroyed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 1, seventh month, as Shunzong's tablet was to be enshrined, officials were uncertain which tablet should be removed. Grand Ritual Erudite Wang Jing argued that the ritual classics say, "Ancestors have merit, and zong have virtue," both names for tablets never removed.

manualTranslations.zh: 惟三代行之。
manualTranslations.literal: Only the Three Dynasties practiced this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only the Three Dynasties truly followed this rule.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢、魏已降，雖曰祖宗，親盡則遷，無功亦毀，不得行古之道也。
manualTranslations.literal: From Han and Wei downward, although they were called zu and zong, when kinship was exhausted they were moved, and if they had no merit they were also destroyed; they could not practice the ancient way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward, even rulers called zu or zong were moved when kinship ended, and those without merit were removed; the ancient standard was no longer kept.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔夏后氏十五代，祖顓頊而宗禹。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly the Xiahou clan had fifteen generations, made Zhuanxu the ancestor, and made Yu the zong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Xia rulers counted fifteen generations, honoring Zhuanxu as ancestor and Yu as zong.

manualTranslations.zh: 殷人十七代，祖契而宗湯。
manualTranslations.literal: The Yin people had seventeen generations, made Xie the ancestor, and made Tang the zong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Yin counted seventeen generations, honoring Xie as ancestor and Tang as zong.

manualTranslations.zh: 周人三十六王，以后稷為太祖，祖文王而宗武王。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhou people had thirty-six kings, made Hou Ji the Grand Ancestor, made King Wen the ancestor, and made King Wu the zong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhou had thirty-six kings, with Hou Ji as Grand Ancestor, King Wen as ancestor, and King Wu as zong.

manualTranslations.zh: 聖唐德厚流廣，遠法殷、周，奉景皇帝為太祖，祖高祖而宗太宗，皆在百代不遷之典。
manualTranslations.literal: The sagely Tang has deep virtue and broad transmission, distantly models itself on Yin and Zhou, serves Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor, makes Gaozu the ancestor and Taizong the zong; all are within the canon of not being moved for a hundred generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Our Tang, rich in virtue and broad in succession, follows Yin and Zhou: Emperor Jing is Grand Ancestor, Gaozu is ancestor, and Taizong is zong, all within the canon of tablets never moved.

manualTranslations.zh: 故代宗升祔，遷代祖也；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus when Daizong was enshrined, Daizu was moved;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus Daizu was moved when Daizong was enshrined;

manualTranslations.zh: 德宗升祔，遷高宗也。
manualTranslations.literal: when Dezong was enshrined, Gaozong was moved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and Gaozong was moved when Dezong was enshrined.

manualTranslations.zh: 今順宗升祔，中宗在三昭三穆之外，謂之親盡，遷於太廟夾室，禮則然矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Now that Shunzong is being enshrined, Zhongzong is outside the three zhao and three mu; this is called kinship exhausted. Moving him to a side chamber of the Grand Temple is what ritual requires.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now that Shunzong is being enshrined, Zhongzong falls outside the three zhao and three mu. His kinship line is exhausted, so ritual requires moving him to a Grand Temple side chamber.

manualTranslations.zh: 或諫者以則天太后革命，中宗復而興之，不在遷藏之例，臣竊未諭也。
manualTranslations.literal: Some remonstrators think that Empress Zetian changed the dynasty and Zhongzong restored and revived it, so he is not within the precedent of removal and storage; I privately do not understand this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some object that because Empress Zetian changed the dynasty and Zhongzong restored it, he should not be treated as a tablet to be moved and stored. I do not understand this argument.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔者高宗晏駕，中宗奉遺詔，自儲副而陟元后。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly, when Gaozong died, Zhongzong received the testamentary edict and rose from crown prince to sovereign.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, Zhongzong followed the testamentary edict and ascended from heir apparent to sovereign.

manualTranslations.zh: 則天太后臨朝，廢為盧陵王。
manualTranslations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zetian governed at court, she deposed him as Prince of Luling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zetian took court power, she deposed him as Prince of Luling.

manualTranslations.zh: 聖曆元年，太后詔復立為皇太子。
manualTranslations.literal: In Shengli 1, the empress dowager issued an edict restoring and installing him as crown prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Shengli 1 she restored him as crown prince by edict.

manualTranslations.zh: 屬太后聖壽延長，御下日久，奸臣擅命，紊其紀度。
manualTranslations.literal: Because the empress dowager's sacred longevity was prolonged and she ruled those below for many days, wicked ministers monopolized commands and disturbed the order.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because the empress dowager lived and ruled for so long, wicked ministers seized authority and disrupted the order of government.

manualTranslations.zh: 敬暉、桓彥範等五臣，俱唐舊臣，匡輔王室，翊中宗而承大統。
manualTranslations.literal: Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and the other five ministers were all old Tang ministers; they rectified and assisted the royal house, supported Zhongzong, and had him inherit the great line.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and the other five ministers were old Tang servants who supported the royal house and helped Zhongzong resume the succession.

manualTranslations.zh: 此乃子繼父業，是中宗得之而且失之；
manualTranslations.literal: This was the son continuing the father's enterprise: Zhongzong obtained it and then lost it;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This was a son inheriting his father's work: Zhongzong gained the throne and then lost it;

manualTranslations.zh: 母授子位，是中宗失之而復得之。
manualTranslations.literal: and the mother giving the son the position: Zhongzong lost it and then obtained it again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: then his mother returned the position to her son, so Zhongzong regained what he had lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十年間，再為皇太子，復踐皇帝位，失之在己，得之在己，可謂革命中興之義殊也。
manualTranslations.literal: Within twenty years, he twice became crown prince and again trod the imperial position. Losing it lay in himself, obtaining it lay in himself; this can be called different from the meaning of dynastic change and restoration.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Over twenty years he twice became crown prince and returned to the imperial throne. The loss and recovery both belonged to his own line, so this differs from true dynastic restoration.

manualTranslations.zh: 又以周、漢之例推之，幽王為犬戎所滅，平王東遷，周不以平王為中興不遷之廟，其例一也。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, extending from the examples of Zhou and Han: King You was destroyed by the Quanrong and King Ping moved east, yet Zhou did not make King Ping an unmoved temple of restoration; this is the first example.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhou example is first: after King You was destroyed by the Quanrong and King Ping moved east, Zhou did not make King Ping an unmoved restoration temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢呂后專權，產、祿秉政，文帝自代邸而立之，漢不以文帝為中興不遷之廟，其例二也。
manualTranslations.literal: In Han, Empress Lü monopolized power, Chan and Lu held government, and Emperor Wen was installed from his residence in Dai, yet Han did not make Emperor Wen an unmoved temple of restoration; this is the second example.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Han example is second: when Empress Lü monopolized power and Lü Chan and Lü Lu governed, Emperor Wen came from Dai to take the throne, yet Han did not give him an unmoved restoration temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 霍光輔宣帝，再盛基業，而不以宣帝為不遷之廟，其例三也。
manualTranslations.literal: Huo Guang assisted Emperor Xuan and again made the foundation flourish, yet they did not make Emperor Xuan an unmoved temple; this is the third example.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The third example is Huo Guang's support of Emperor Xuan, which renewed the dynasty but still did not make Xuan an unmoved temple.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏以中宗孝和皇帝，于聖上為六代伯祖，尊非正統，廟亦親盡。
manualTranslations.literal: I submit that Emperor Xiaohe Zhongzong is, to the Sage Above, an elder uncle ancestor of the sixth generation; his rank is not in the direct line, and his temple has also exhausted kinship.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhongzong, Emperor Xiaohe, is a sixth-generation collateral ancestor to the present emperor, not in the direct line, and his temple kinship is exhausted.

manualTranslations.zh: 爰及周、漢故事，是與中興功德之主不同，奉遷夾室，固無疑也。
manualTranslations.literal: Extending to the precedents of Zhou and Han, this is different from a lord of restoration merit and virtue; respectfully moving him to the side chamber is certainly without doubt.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By the precedents of Zhou and Han, he is not a restoration ruler of enduring merit. There is no doubt that his tablet should be moved to the side chamber.

manualTranslations.zh: 天授二年，則天既革命稱帝，於東都改制太廟為七廟室，奉武氏七代神主，祔於太廟。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou, after Zetian had changed the mandate and claimed the imperial title, she restructured the Grand Temple in the eastern capital into seven temple chambers, received the spirit tablets of seven generations of the Wu clan, and enshrined them in the Grand Temple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tianshou 2: after Zetian's revolution and enthronement, the eastern-capital Grand Temple became seven chambers, where seven generations of Wu tablets were enshrined.

sourceRange.text: 太常博士張齊賢建議曰：昔孫卿子云：「有天下者事七代，有一國者事五代。」則天子七廟，古今達禮。故《尚書》稱「七代之廟，可以觀德」。《祭法》稱「王立七廟，一壇一墠」。《王制》云：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」莫不尊始封之君，謂之太祖。太祖之廟，百代不遷。袷祭之禮，毀廟之主陳於太祖，未毀廟之主，皆升合食于太祖之室。太祖東向，昭南向，穆北向。太祖者，商之玄王、周之后稷是也。太祖之外，更無始祖。但商自玄王以後，十有四代，至湯而有天下。周自后稷已後，十有七代，至武王而有天下。其間代數既遠，遷廟親廟，皆出太祖之後，故得合食有序，尊卑不差。其後漢高祖受命，無始封祖，即以高皇帝為太祖。太上皇高帝之父，立廟享祀，不在昭穆合食之列，為尊于太祖故也。魏武創業，文帝受命，亦即以武帝為太祖。其高皇、太皇、外處君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。晉宣創業，武帝受命，亦即以宣帝為太祖。其征西、豫章、潁川、京兆府君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。歷茲已降，至於有隋，宗廟之制，斯禮不改。故宇文氏以文皇帝為太祖，隋室以武元皇帝為太祖。國家誕受在命，累葉重光。景皇帝始封唐公，實為太祖。中間代數既近，列在三昭三穆之內，故皇家太廟，唯有六室。其弘農府君、宣、光二帝，尊于太祖，親盡則遷，不在昭穆合食之數。今皇極再造，孝思匪寧。奉二月二十九日敕：「七室已下，依舊號尊崇。」又奉三月一日敕：「既立七廟，須尊崇始祖，速令詳之」者。伏尋禮經，始祖即是太祖，太祖之外，更無始祖。周朝太祖之外，以周文王為始祖，不合禮經。或有引《白虎通義》云「后稷為始祖、文王為太祖、武王為太宗」，及鄭玄注《詩·雍》序云「太祖謂文王」以為說者。其義不然。何者？彼以禮「王者祖有功，宗有德，周人祖文王而宗武王」，故謂文王為太祖耳，非袷祭群主合食之太祖。今之議者，或有欲立涼武昭王為始祖者，殊為不可。何者？昔在商、周，契、稷始封，湯、武之興，祚由契、稷，故以契、稷為太祖，即皇家之景帝是也。涼武昭王勳業未廣，後主失國，土宇不傳。景皇始封，實基明命。今乃舍封唐之盛烈，崇西涼之遠構，考之前古，實乖典禮。魏氏不以曹參為太祖，晉氏不以殷王仰為太祖，宋氏不以楚元王為太祖，齊、梁不以蕭何為太祖，陳、隋不以胡公、楊震為太祖，則皇家安可以涼武昭王為太祖乎？漢之東京，大議郊祀，多以周郊后稷，漢當郊堯。制上公卿議，議者多同，帝亦然之。杜林正議，獨以為「周室之興，祚由后稷。漢業特起，功不緣堯。祖宗故事，所宜因循。」竟從林議。又傳稱，「欲知天上，事問長人」，以其近之。武德、貞觀之時，主聖臣賢，其去涼武昭王蓋亦近於今矣。當時不立者，必不可立故也。今既年代浸遠，方復立之，是非三祖二宗之意。實恐景皇失職而震怒，武昭虛位而不答，非社稷之福也。宗廟事重，禘祫禮崇，先王以之觀德。或者不知其說，既灌而往，孔子不欲觀之。今朝命惟新，宜應慎禮，祭如神在，理不可誣。請准敕加太廟為七室，享宣皇帝以備七代，其始祖不合別有尊崇。太常博士劉承慶、尹知章又議云：謹按《王制》：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」此載籍之明文，古今之通制。皇唐稽考前範，詳采列辟，崇建宗靈，式遵斯典。但以開基之主，受命之君，王跡有淺深，太祖有遠近。湯、文祚基契、稷，太祖代遠，出乎昭穆之上，故七廟可全。若夏繼唐、虞，功非由鯀；漢除秦、項，力不因堯。及魏、晉經圖，周、隋撥亂，皆勳隆近代，祖業非遠，受命始封之主，不離昭穆之親，故肇立宗祊，罕聞全制。夫太祖以功建，昭穆以親崇，有功百代而不遷，親盡七葉而當毀。或以太祖代淺，廟數非備，更于昭穆之上，遠立合遷之君，曲從七廟之文，深乖迭毀之制。皇家千齡啟旦，百葉重光。景皇帝浚德基唐，代數猶近，號雖崇于太祖，親尚列于昭穆，且臨六室之位，未申七代之尊。是知太廟當六，未合有七。故先朝惟有宣、光、景、元、神、堯、文武六代親廟。大帝登遐，神主升祔於廟室，以宣皇帝代數當滿，准禮復遷。今止有光皇帝已下六代親廟，非是天子之廟數不當有七，要由太祖有遠近之異，故初建有多少之殊。敬惟三后臨朝，代多儒雅，神祊事重，禮豈虛存，規模可沿，理難變革。宣皇既非始祖，又廟無祖宗之號，親盡既遷，其在不合重立。若禮終運往，建議復崇，實違《王制》之文，不合先朝之旨。請依貞觀之故事，無改三聖之宏規，光崇六室，不虧古議。

manualTranslations.zh: 太常博士張齊賢建議曰：昔孫卿子云：「有天下者事七代，有一國者事五代。」
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Ritual Erudite Zhang Qixian cited Xunzi: "The ruler of All Under Heaven serves seven generations; the ruler of one state serves five."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Ritual Erudite Zhang Qixian cited Xunzi: "The ruler of All Under Heaven serves seven generations; the ruler of one state serves five."

manualTranslations.zh: 則天子七廟，古今達禮。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the emperor has seven temples, a ritual standard accepted across antiquity and the present.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the emperor has seven temples, a ritual standard accepted across antiquity and the present.

manualTranslations.zh: 故《尚書》稱「七代之廟，可以觀德」。
manualTranslations.literal: 《Documents》 says, "Through seven generations of temples, one may observe virtue."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Documents》 says, "Through seven generations of temples, one may observe virtue."

manualTranslations.zh: 《祭法》稱「王立七廟，一壇一墠」。
manualTranslations.literal: 《Sacrificial Regulations》 says, "The king establishes seven temples, one altar, and one open ground."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: 《Sacrificial Regulations》 says, "The king establishes seven temples, one altar, and one open ground."

manualTranslations.zh: 《王制》云：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」
manualTranslations.literal: The 《Wang System》 says, "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The 《Wang System》 says, "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."

manualTranslations.zh: 莫不尊始封之君，謂之太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: All such systems honor the first enfeoffed lord as Grand Ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All such systems honor the first enfeoffed lord as Grand Ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖之廟，百代不遷。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Ancestor's temple remains unmoved for a hundred generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor's temple remains unmoved for a hundred generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 袷祭之禮，毀廟之主陳於太祖，未毀廟之主，皆升合食于太祖之室。
manualTranslations.literal: At the xia sacrifice, removed temple tablets are arrayed at the Grand Ancestor, while unremoved tablets are raised to share offerings in the Grand Ancestor's chamber.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the xia sacrifice, removed temple tablets are arrayed at the Grand Ancestor, while unremoved tablets are raised to share offerings in the Grand Ancestor's chamber.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖東向，昭南向，穆北向。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Ancestor faces east; zhao face south, and mu face north.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor faces east; zhao face south, and mu face north.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖者，商之玄王、周之后稷是也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Ancestors are exemplified by Xuan Wang of Shang and Hou Ji of Zhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestors are exemplified by Xuan Wang of Shang and Hou Ji of Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 太祖之外，更無始祖。
manualTranslations.literal: Beyond the Grand Ancestor there is no additional founding ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Beyond the Grand Ancestor there is no additional founding ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 但商自玄王以後，十有四代，至湯而有天下。
manualTranslations.literal: From Shang's Xuan Wang to Tang's possession of the realm lay fourteen generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Shang's Xuan Wang to Tang's possession of the realm lay fourteen generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 周自后稷已後，十有七代，至武王而有天下。
manualTranslations.literal: From Zhou's Hou Ji to King Wu's possession of the realm lay seventeen generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Zhou's Hou Ji to King Wu's possession of the realm lay seventeen generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 其間代數既遠，遷廟親廟，皆出太祖之後，故得合食有序，尊卑不差。
manualTranslations.literal: Since those lines were remote, both removed temples and kin temples stood after the Grand Ancestor, so joint offerings had proper order and rank was not confused.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since those lines were remote, both removed temples and kin temples stood after the Grand Ancestor, so joint offerings had proper order and rank was not confused.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後漢高祖受命，無始封祖，即以高皇帝為太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: When Han Gaozu received the mandate without a first-enfeoffed ancestor, he himself became Grand Ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu received the mandate without a first-enfeoffed ancestor, he himself became Grand Ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 太上皇高帝之父，立廟享祀，不在昭穆合食之列，為尊于太祖故也。
manualTranslations.literal: Gaozu's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor, received a temple and sacrifices but was not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings, because he was honored above the Grand Ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozu's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor, received a temple and sacrifices but was not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings, because he was honored above the Grand Ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏武創業，文帝受命，亦即以武帝為太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: Cao Cao founded Wei's enterprise, so when Emperor Wen received the mandate, Emperor Wu likewise became Grand Ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cao Cao founded Wei's enterprise, so when Emperor Wen received the mandate, Emperor Wu likewise became Grand Ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 其高皇、太皇、外處君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
manualTranslations.literal: Gao Huang, Tai Huang, Waichu Jun, and the others were honored as kin and not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gao Huang, Tai Huang, Waichu Jun, and the others were honored as kin and not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉宣創業，武帝受命，亦即以宣帝為太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: Sima Yi founded Jin's enterprise, so when Emperor Wu received the mandate, Emperor Xuan likewise became Grand Ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sima Yi founded Jin's enterprise, so when Emperor Wu received the mandate, Emperor Xuan likewise became Grand Ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 其征西、豫章、潁川、京兆府君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhengxi, Yuzhang, Yingchuan, Jingzhao, and other lords were honored as kin and excluded from the zhao-mu shared offerings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhengxi, Yuzhang, Yingchuan, Jingzhao, and other lords were honored as kin and excluded from the zhao-mu shared offerings.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷茲已降，至於有隋，宗廟之制，斯禮不改。
manualTranslations.literal: From those dynasties through Sui, the ancestral-temple rule remained unchanged.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From those dynasties through Sui, the ancestral-temple rule remained unchanged.

manualTranslations.zh: 故宇文氏以文皇帝為太祖，隋室以武元皇帝為太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus Northern Zhou treated Emperor Wen as Grand Ancestor, and Sui treated Emperor Wuyuan as Grand Ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus Northern Zhou treated Emperor Wen as Grand Ancestor, and Sui treated Emperor Wuyuan as Grand Ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 國家誕受在命，累葉重光。
manualTranslations.literal: Our dynasty received the mandate, and successive generations have renewed its brilliance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Our dynasty received the mandate, and successive generations have renewed its brilliance.

manualTranslations.zh: 景皇帝始封唐公，實為太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Jing, first enfeoffed as Duke of Tang, is truly the Grand Ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, first enfeoffed as Duke of Tang, is truly the Grand Ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 中間代數既近，列在三昭三穆之內，故皇家太廟，唯有六室。
manualTranslations.literal: Because the line is still close and Emperor Jing falls within the three zhao and three mu, the Tang Grand Temple has only six chambers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because the line is still close and Emperor Jing falls within the three zhao and three mu, the Tang Grand Temple has only six chambers.

manualTranslations.zh: 其弘農府君、宣、光二帝，尊于太祖，親盡則遷，不在昭穆合食之數。
manualTranslations.literal: The Hongnong Lord, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Guang stand in honor above the Grand Ancestor; once kinship is exhausted they are moved and are not part of the zhao-mu shared offerings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Hongnong Lord, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Guang stand in honor above the Grand Ancestor; once kinship is exhausted they are moved and are not part of the zhao-mu shared offerings.

manualTranslations.zh: 今皇極再造，孝思匪寧。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the imperial order has been restored, and filial concern remains unsettled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the imperial order has been restored, and filial concern remains unsettled.

manualTranslations.zh: 奉二月二十九日敕：「七室已下，依舊號尊崇。」
manualTranslations.literal: The edict of the twenty-ninth day of the second month said, "For the seven chambers and below, keep the old titles and honors."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict of the twenty-ninth day of the second month said, "For the seven chambers and below, keep the old titles and honors."

manualTranslations.zh: 又奉三月一日敕：「既立七廟，須尊崇始祖，速令詳之」者。
manualTranslations.literal: The edict of the first day of the third month added, "Since seven temples are being established, the founding ancestor must be honored. Examine this quickly."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The edict of the first day of the third month added, "Since seven temples are being established, the founding ancestor must be honored. Examine this quickly."

manualTranslations.zh: 伏尋禮經，始祖即是太祖，太祖之外，更無始祖。
manualTranslations.literal: Looking through the ritual classics, I find that the founding ancestor is the Grand Ancestor, and outside the Grand Ancestor there is no separate founder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Looking through the ritual classics, I find that the founding ancestor is the Grand Ancestor, and outside the Grand Ancestor there is no separate founder.

manualTranslations.zh: 周朝太祖之外，以周文王為始祖，不合禮經。
manualTranslations.literal: For Zhou to set King Wen as a founding ancestor beyond the Grand Ancestor does not fit the ritual classics.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For Zhou to set King Wen as a founding ancestor beyond the Grand Ancestor does not fit the ritual classics.

manualTranslations.zh: 或有引《白虎通義》云「后稷為始祖、文王為太祖、武王為太宗」，及鄭玄注《詩·雍》序云「太祖謂文王」以為說者。
manualTranslations.literal: Some explain this by citing 《Baihu tongyi》, "Hou Ji was founding ancestor, King Wen Grand Ancestor, and King Wu Grand Zong," and Zheng Xuan's note to the 《Shi: Yong》 preface, "Grand Ancestor means King Wen."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some explain this by citing 《Baihu tongyi》, "Hou Ji was founding ancestor, King Wen Grand Ancestor, and King Wu Grand Zong," and Zheng Xuan's note to the 《Shi: Yong》 preface, "Grand Ancestor means King Wen."

manualTranslations.zh: 其義不然。
manualTranslations.literal: That interpretation is wrong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That interpretation is wrong.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: Why?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why?

manualTranslations.zh: 彼以禮「王者祖有功，宗有德，周人祖文王而宗武王」，故謂文王為太祖耳，非袷祭群主合食之太祖。
manualTranslations.literal: They call King Wen Grand Ancestor because ritual says, "Rulers make ancestors of those with merit and zong of those with virtue; Zhou made King Wen ancestor and King Wu zong." But this is not the Grand Ancestor who receives all rulers in shared xia offerings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They call King Wen Grand Ancestor because ritual says, "Rulers make ancestors of those with merit and zong of those with virtue; Zhou made King Wen ancestor and King Wu zong." But this is not the Grand Ancestor who receives all rulers in shared xia offerings.

manualTranslations.zh: 今之議者，或有欲立涼武昭王為始祖者，殊為不可。
manualTranslations.literal: Some now wish to make Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor, but this is especially wrong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some now wish to make Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor, but this is especially wrong.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: Why?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why?

manualTranslations.zh: 昔在商、周，契、稷始封，湯、武之興，祚由契、稷，故以契、稷為太祖，即皇家之景帝是也。
manualTranslations.literal: In Shang and Zhou, Xie and Hou Ji were the first enfeoffed ancestors. Tang and Wu rose from their fortune, so Xie and Hou Ji became Grand Ancestors. For our imperial house, that role belongs to Emperor Jing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Shang and Zhou, Xie and Hou Ji were the first enfeoffed ancestors. Tang and Wu rose from their fortune, so Xie and Hou Ji became Grand Ancestors. For our imperial house, that role belongs to Emperor Jing.

manualTranslations.zh: 涼武昭王勳業未廣，後主失國，土宇不傳。
manualTranslations.literal: Liang Wuzhao Wang's merit was limited, his successor lost the state, and the territory did not continue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liang Wuzhao Wang's merit was limited, his successor lost the state, and the territory did not continue.

manualTranslations.zh: 景皇始封，實基明命。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Jing's first enfeoffment truly founded the Tang mandate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing's first enfeoffment truly founded the Tang mandate.

manualTranslations.zh: 今乃舍封唐之盛烈，崇西涼之遠構，考之前古，實乖典禮。
manualTranslations.literal: To abandon the great enfeoffment in Tang and exalt distant Western Liang violates ancient ritual precedent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To abandon the great enfeoffment in Tang and exalt distant Western Liang violates ancient ritual precedent.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏氏不以曹參為太祖，晉氏不以殷王仰為太祖，宋氏不以楚元王為太祖，齊、梁不以蕭何為太祖，陳、隋不以胡公、楊震為太祖，則皇家安可以涼武昭王為太祖乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Wei did not ancestralize Cao Can, Jin did not ancestralize the King of Yin, Song did not ancestralize King Yuan of Chu, Qi and Liang did not ancestralize Xiao He, and Chen and Sui did not ancestralize Duke Hu or Yang Zhen. How could Tang make Liang Wuzhao Wang Grand Ancestor?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei did not ancestralize Cao Can, Jin did not ancestralize the King of Yin, Song did not ancestralize King Yuan of Chu, Qi and Liang did not ancestralize Xiao He, and Chen and Sui did not ancestralize Duke Hu or Yang Zhen. How could Tang make Liang Wuzhao Wang Grand Ancestor?

manualTranslations.zh: 漢之東京，大議郊祀，多以周郊后稷，漢當郊堯。
manualTranslations.literal: In Eastern Han, a major debate over suburban sacrifice held that because Zhou offered to Hou Ji, Han should offer to Yao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Eastern Han, a major debate over suburban sacrifice held that because Zhou offered to Hou Ji, Han should offer to Yao.

manualTranslations.zh: 制上公卿議，議者多同，帝亦然之。
manualTranslations.literal: The court sent the issue to the ministers; most agreed, and the emperor was inclined to agree as well.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court sent the issue to the ministers; most agreed, and the emperor was inclined to agree as well.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜林正議，獨以為「周室之興，祚由后稷。
manualTranslations.literal: Only Du Lin argued correctly: "The rise of Zhou came through Hou Ji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only Du Lin argued correctly: "The rise of Zhou came through Hou Ji.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢業特起，功不緣堯。
manualTranslations.literal: Han arose on its own; its merit did not derive from Yao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han arose on its own; its merit did not derive from Yao.

manualTranslations.zh: 祖宗故事，所宜因循。」
manualTranslations.literal: The old precedents for ancestors and zong should be followed."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The old precedents for ancestors and zong should be followed."

manualTranslations.zh: 竟從林議。
manualTranslations.literal: The court ultimately followed Du Lin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court ultimately followed Du Lin.

manualTranslations.zh: 又傳稱，「欲知天上，事問長人」，以其近之。
manualTranslations.literal: Another tradition says, "To know Heaven, ask the elders," because they stand closer to it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Another tradition says, "To know Heaven, ask the elders," because they stand closer to it.

manualTranslations.zh: 武德、貞觀之時，主聖臣賢，其去涼武昭王蓋亦近於今矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wude and Zhenguan rulers were sagely and their ministers worthy, and they were closer to Liang Wuzhao Wang's time than we are.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wude and Zhenguan rulers were sagely and their ministers worthy, and they were closer to Liang Wuzhao Wang's time than we are.

manualTranslations.zh: 當時不立者，必不可立故也。
manualTranslations.literal: If they did not establish him then, he surely should not be established now.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they did not establish him then, he surely should not be established now.

manualTranslations.zh: 今既年代浸遠，方復立之，是非三祖二宗之意。
manualTranslations.literal: To establish him only after so many years would violate the intent behind the three ancestors and two zong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To establish him only after so many years would violate the intent behind the three ancestors and two zong.

manualTranslations.zh: 實恐景皇失職而震怒，武昭虛位而不答，非社稷之福也。
manualTranslations.literal: I fear Emperor Jing would be displaced and angered, while Wuzhao would hold an empty position and give no response; this would not benefit the state.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I fear Emperor Jing would be displaced and angered, while Wuzhao would hold an empty position and give no response; this would not benefit the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 宗廟事重，禘祫禮崇，先王以之觀德。
manualTranslations.literal: Temple affairs are weighty, and the di and xia rites are exalted; through them the former kings observed virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Temple affairs are weighty, and the di and xia rites are exalted; through them the former kings observed virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 或者不知其說，既灌而往，孔子不欲觀之。
manualTranslations.literal: Some fail to understand this. Confucius himself did not wish to watch after the libation had passed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some fail to understand this. Confucius himself did not wish to watch after the libation had passed.

manualTranslations.zh: 今朝命惟新，宜應慎禮，祭如神在，理不可誣。
manualTranslations.literal: Now that the dynasty's mandate has been renewed, ritual must be handled carefully. Sacrifice is performed as if the spirits were present; it cannot be falsified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now that the dynasty's mandate has been renewed, ritual must be handled carefully. Sacrifice is performed as if the spirits were present; it cannot be falsified.

manualTranslations.zh: 請准敕加太廟為七室，享宣皇帝以備七代，其始祖不合別有尊崇。
manualTranslations.literal: I request that the Grand Temple be expanded to seven chambers and Emperor Xuan be sacrificed to as the seventh generation; no separate honor should be given to another founding ancestor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I request that the Grand Temple be expanded to seven chambers and Emperor Xuan be sacrificed to as the seventh generation; no separate honor should be given to another founding ancestor.

manualTranslations.zh: 太常博士劉承慶、尹知章又議云：謹按《王制》：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」
manualTranslations.literal: Grand Ritual Erudites Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang also cited the 《Wang System》: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Grand Ritual Erudites Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang also cited the 《Wang System》: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."

manualTranslations.zh: 此載籍之明文，古今之通制。
manualTranslations.literal: This is the clear written rule and the common system of antiquity and later ages.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is the clear written rule and the common system of antiquity and later ages.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇唐稽考前範，詳采列辟，崇建宗靈，式遵斯典。
manualTranslations.literal: Tang examined earlier models, drew carefully on past rulers, built up the ancestral spirits, and followed this canon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tang examined earlier models, drew carefully on past rulers, built up the ancestral spirits, and followed this canon.

manualTranslations.zh: 但以開基之主，受命之君，王跡有淺深，太祖有遠近。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet founders and mandate-receiving rulers differ: royal traces may be deep or shallow, and Grand Ancestors may be remote or near.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet founders and mandate-receiving rulers differ: royal traces may be deep or shallow, and Grand Ancestors may be remote or near.

manualTranslations.zh: 湯、文祚基契、稷，太祖代遠，出乎昭穆之上，故七廟可全。
manualTranslations.literal: Tang and King Wen were rooted in Xie and Hou Ji; because those Grand Ancestors were remote and stood above the zhao-mu line, the full seven temples were possible.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tang and King Wen were rooted in Xie and Hou Ji; because those Grand Ancestors were remote and stood above the zhao-mu line, the full seven temples were possible.

manualTranslations.zh: 若夏繼唐、虞，功非由鯀；
manualTranslations.literal: Xia succeeded Tang and Yu, but its merit did not derive from Gun;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xia succeeded Tang and Yu, but its merit did not derive from Gun;

manualTranslations.zh: 漢除秦、項，力不因堯。
manualTranslations.literal: Han destroyed Qin and Xiang, but its power did not come from Yao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han destroyed Qin and Xiang, but its power did not come from Yao.

manualTranslations.zh: 及魏、晉經圖，周、隋撥亂，皆勳隆近代，祖業非遠，受命始封之主，不離昭穆之親，故肇立宗祊，罕聞全制。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei, Jin, Zhou, and Sui won their achievements in recent generations, not through remote ancestral enterprises; their mandate-receiving founders still lay within the zhao-mu kinship line, so their first temple systems were rarely complete.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei, Jin, Zhou, and Sui won their achievements in recent generations, not through remote ancestral enterprises; their mandate-receiving founders still lay within the zhao-mu kinship line, so their first temple systems were rarely complete.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫太祖以功建，昭穆以親崇，有功百代而不遷，親盡七葉而當毀。
manualTranslations.literal: The Grand Ancestor rests on merit; zhao and mu rest on kinship. Merit keeps a tablet unmoved for a hundred generations, while exhausted kinship after seven leaves requires removal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor rests on merit; zhao and mu rest on kinship. Merit keeps a tablet unmoved for a hundred generations, while exhausted kinship after seven leaves requires removal.

manualTranslations.zh: 或以太祖代淺，廟數非備，更于昭穆之上，遠立合遷之君，曲從七廟之文，深乖迭毀之制。
manualTranslations.literal: To force the seven-temple wording by adding a remote but movable ruler above the zhao-mu line, merely because the Grand Ancestor is near, would badly violate the rule of successive removal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To force the seven-temple wording by adding a remote but movable ruler above the zhao-mu line, merely because the Grand Ancestor is near, would badly violate the rule of successive removal.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇家千齡啟旦，百葉重光。
manualTranslations.literal: The imperial house opened a thousand-year dawn and renewed the brightness of a hundred generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The imperial house opened a thousand-year dawn and renewed the brightness of a hundred generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 景皇帝浚德基唐，代數猶近，號雖崇于太祖，親尚列于昭穆，且臨六室之位，未申七代之尊。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Jing founded Tang in deep virtue, but his generation is still near. Though honored as Grand Ancestor, by kinship he remains within the zhao-mu line and one of the six chambers, not yet creating the honor of seven generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing founded Tang in deep virtue, but his generation is still near. Though honored as Grand Ancestor, by kinship he remains within the zhao-mu line and one of the six chambers, not yet creating the honor of seven generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 是知太廟當六，未合有七。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the Grand Temple should have six chambers and not yet seven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the Grand Temple should have six chambers and not yet seven.

manualTranslations.zh: 故先朝惟有宣、光、景、元、神、堯、文武六代親廟。
manualTranslations.literal: The former court therefore had only six generations of kin temples: Xuan, Guang, Jing, Yuan, Shenyao, and Wenwu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The former court therefore had only six generations of kin temples: Xuan, Guang, Jing, Yuan, Shenyao, and Wenwu.

manualTranslations.zh: 大帝登遐，神主升祔於廟室，以宣皇帝代數當滿，准禮復遷。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Great Emperor died and his tablet was enshrined, Emperor Xuan's generations were complete, so ritual moved him out again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Great Emperor died and his tablet was enshrined, Emperor Xuan's generations were complete, so ritual moved him out again.

manualTranslations.zh: 今止有光皇帝已下六代親廟，非是天子之廟數不當有七，要由太祖有遠近之異，故初建有多少之殊。
manualTranslations.literal: Now there are only six generations of kin temples from Emperor Guang down. This does not mean the emperor should not have seven temples; it means the number at establishment varies because Grand Ancestors may be remote or near.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now there are only six generations of kin temples from Emperor Guang down. This does not mean the emperor should not have seven temples; it means the number at establishment varies because Grand Ancestors may be remote or near.

manualTranslations.zh: 敬惟三后臨朝，代多儒雅，神祊事重，禮豈虛存，規模可沿，理難變革。
manualTranslations.literal: The three former reigns had many learned classicists, and temple affairs were weighty. Their ritual model was not empty; it can be followed, and principle does not favor changing it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The three former reigns had many learned classicists, and temple affairs were weighty. Their ritual model was not empty; it can be followed, and principle does not favor changing it.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣皇既非始祖，又廟無祖宗之號，親盡既遷，其在不合重立。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Xuan is not the founder, and his temple has no zu or zong title. Since his kinship line was exhausted and he was moved, he should not be restored.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan is not the founder, and his temple has no zu or zong title. Since his kinship line was exhausted and he was moved, he should not be restored.

manualTranslations.zh: 若禮終運往，建議復崇，實違《王制》之文，不合先朝之旨。
manualTranslations.literal: To exalt him again after the ritual order has moved on would violate the 《Wang System》 and the former court's intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To exalt him again after the ritual order has moved on would violate the 《Wang System》 and the former court's intent.

manualTranslations.zh: 請依貞觀之故事，無改三聖之宏規，光崇六室，不虧古議。
manualTranslations.literal: We request following Zhenguan precedent, preserving the grand rule of the Three Sages, and honoring the six chambers without impairing the ancient judgment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We request following Zhenguan precedent, preserving the grand rule of the Three Sages, and honoring the six chambers without impairing the ancient judgment.

sourceRange.text: 會昌元年六月，制曰：「朕近因載誕之日，展承顏之敬，太皇太后謂朕曰：『天子之孝，莫大於丕承；人倫之義，莫大于嗣續。穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝厭代已久，星霜屢遷，禰宮曠合食之禮，惟帝深濡露之感。宣懿皇太后，長慶之際，德冠後宮，夙表沙麓之祥，實茂河洲之範。先朝恩禮之厚，中壺莫偕。況誕我聖君，纘承昌運，已協華於先帝，方延祚於後昆。思廣貽謀，庶弘博愛，爰從舊典，以慰孝思。當以宣懿皇太后祔太廟穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝之室。率是彝訓，其敬承之。』朕祇奉慈旨，載深感咽。宜令宣示中外，咸使聞知。」會昌六年五月，禮儀使奏：武宗昭肅皇帝祔廟，併合祧遷者。伏以自敬宗、文宗、武宗兄弟相及，已歷三朝。昭穆之位，與承前不同。所可疑者，其事有四：一者，兄弟昭穆同位，不相為後；二者，已祧之主，復入舊廟；三者，廟數有限，無後之主，則宜出置別廟；四者，兄弟既不相為後，昭為父道，穆為子道，則昭穆同班，不合異位。據《春秋》「文公二年，躋僖公」。何休云：躋，升也，謂西上也。惠公與莊公當同南面西上，隱、桓與閔、僖當同北面西上。」孔穎達亦引此義釋經。又賀循云：「殷之盤庚，不序陽甲；漢之光武，上繼元帝。」晉元帝、簡文，皆用此義毀之，蓋以昭穆位同，不可兼毀二廟故也。《尚書》曰：「七代之廟，可以觀德。」且殷家兄弟相及，有至四帝不及祖禰，何容更言七代，於理無矣。二者，今已兄弟相及，同為一代，矯前之失，則合復祔代宗神主於太廟。或疑已祧之主，不合更入太廟者。按晉代元、明之時，已遷豫章、潁川矣，及簡文即位，乃元帝之子，故復豫章、潁川二神主於廟。又國朝中宗已祔太廟，至開元四年，乃出置別廟，至十年，置九廟，而中宗神主復祔太廟。則已遷復入，亦可無疑。三者，廟有定數，無後之主，出置別廟者。按魏、晉之初多同廟，蓋取上古清廟一宮，尊遠神祗之義。自後晉武所立之廟，雖云七主，而實六代，蓋景、文同廟故也。又按魯立姜嫄、文王之廟，不計昭穆，以尊尚功德也。晉元帝上繼武帝，而惠、懷、湣三帝，時賀循等諸儒議，以為別立廟，親遠義疏，都邑遷異，於理無嫌也。今以文宗棄代才六七年，武宗甫邇復土，遽移別廟，不齒祖宗，在於有司，非所宜議。四者，添置廟之室。按《禮論》，晉太常賀循云：「廟以容主為限，無拘常數。」故晉武帝時，廟有七主六代。至元帝、明帝，廟皆十室。及成、康、穆三帝，皆至十一室。自後雖遷故祔新，大抵以七代為准，而不限室數。伏以江左大儒，通賾睹奧，事有明據，固可施行。今若不行是議，更以迭毀為制，則當上不及高曾未盡之親，下有忍臣子恩義之道。今備討古今，參校經史，上請復代宗神主於太廟，以存高曾之親。下以敬宗、文宗、武宗同為一代，於太廟東間添置兩室，定為九代十一室之制，以全臣子恩敬之義，庶協大順之宜，得變禮之正，折古今之紛互，立群疑之杓指。俾因心廣孝，永燭於皇明；昭德事神，無虧於聖代。敕曰：「宗廟事重，實資參詳。宜令尚書省、兩省、御史臺四品以上官、大理卿、京兆尹等集議以聞。」尚書左丞鄭涯等奏議曰：「夫禮經垂則，莫重于嚴配，必參損益之道，則合典禮之文。

sourceRange.text: 武德元年五月，備法駕迎宣簡公，懿王、景皇帝、元皇帝神主，祔於太廟，始享四室。貞觀九年，高祖崩，將行遷祔之禮，太宗命有司詳議廟制。諫議大夫朱子奢建議曰：按漢丞相韋玄成奏立五廟，諸侯亦同五。劉子駿議開七祖，邦君降二。鄭司農踵玄成之轍，王子雍揚國師之波，分塗並驅，各相師祖，鹹玩共所習，好同惡異。遂令歷代祧祀，多少參差，優劣去取，曾無畫一。《傳》稱「名位不同，禮亦異數。」《易》云「卑高以陳，貴賤位矣」。豈非別嫌疑，慎微遠，防陵僭，尊君卑佐，陞降無舛，所貴禮者，義在茲乎！若使天子諸侯，俱立五廟，便是賤可以同貴，臣可以濫主，名器無准，冠屨同歸，禮亦異數，義將安設？《戴記》又稱：「禮有以多為貴者，天子七廟，諸侯五廟。」若天子五廟，才與子男相埒，以多為貴，何所表乎？愚以為諸侯立高祖以下，並太祖五廟，一國之貴也。天子立高祖以上，並太祖七廟，四海之尊也。降殺以兩，禮之正焉。前史所謂「德厚者流光，德薄者流卑」，此其義也。伏惟聖祖在天，山陵有日，祔祖嚴配，大事在斯。宜依七廟，用崇大禮。若親盡之外，有王業之所基者，如殷之玄王，周之后稷，尊為始祖。倘無其例，請三昭三穆，各置神主，太祖一室，考而虛位。將待七百之祚，遞遷方處，庶上依晉、宋，傍愜人情。於是八座奏曰：臣聞揖讓受終之後，革命創制之君，何嘗不崇親親之義，篤尊尊之道，虔奉祖宗，致敬郊廟。自義乖闕里，學滅秦庭，儒雅既喪，經籍湮殄。雖兩漢纂修絕業，魏、晉敦尚斯文，而宗廟制度，典章散逸，習所傳而競偏說，執淺見而起異端。自昔迄茲，多歷年代，語其大略，兩家而已。祖鄭玄者則陳四廟之制，述王肅者則引七廟之文，貴賤混而莫辯，是非紛而不定。陛下至德自然，孝思罔極，孺慕逾匹夫之志，製作窮聖人之道，誠宜定一代之宏規，為萬世之彝則。臣奉述睿旨，討論往載，紀七廟者實多，稱四祖者蓋寡。校其得失，昭然可見。《春秋谷梁傳》及《禮記》、《王制》、《祭法》、《禮器》《孔子家語》，並云：「天子七廟，諸侯五廟，大夫三廟，士二廟。」《尚書》曰：「七世之廟，可以觀德。」至於孫卿、孔安國、劉歆、班彪父子、孔晁、虞喜、幹寶之徒，或學推碩儒，或才稱博物，商較今古，鹹以為然。故其文曰：「天子三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」晉、宋、齊、梁，皆依斯義，立親廟六，豈非有國之茂典，不刊之休烈乎？若使違群經之明文，從累代之疑議，背子雍之篤論，尊康成之舊學，則天子之禮，下逼於人臣，諸侯之制，上僭于王者，非所謂尊卑有序，名位不同者也。況復禮由人情，自非天墜，大孝莫重於尊親，厚本莫先于嚴配。數盡四廟，非貴多之道；祀逮七世，得加隆之心。是知德厚者流光，乃可久之高義；德薄者流卑，實不易之令範。臣等參議，請依晉、宋故事，立親廟六，其祖宗之制，式遵舊典。庶承宗之道，興於理定之辰；尊祖之義，成於孝治之日。
