manualTranslations.zh: 正第四品上階門下侍郎、中書侍郎舊正四品下階，《開元令》加入上階也、尚書左丞永昌元年進為正三品，如意元年復舊、吏部侍郎武德七年省諸司侍郎，吏部郎中為正四品上。
manualTranslations.literal: Senior fourth rank, upper grade — Chancellery Vice Minister and Secretariat Vice Minister: formerly senior fourth rank, lower grade; the Kaiyuan Code moved them to the upper grade. Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs: in the first year of Yongchang promoted to senior third rank; restored in the first year of Ruyi. Minister of Personnel: in the seventh year of Wude the various bureau vice ministers were abolished and the Personnel Bureau Director was senior fourth rank, upper grade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Senior fourth rank, upper grade — Chancellery Vice Minister and Secretariat Vice Minister were formerly senior fourth rank, lower grade; the Kaiyuan Code placed them in the upper grade. Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs was promoted to senior third rank in the first year of Yongchang (689) and restored in the first year of Ruyi (692). Minister of Personnel: in the seventh year of Wude (624) the various bureau vice ministers were abolished and the Personnel Bureau Director ranked senior fourth rank, upper grade.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞觀三年復置侍郎，其吏部郎中復舊為五品下、太常少卿、太子左庶子、太子少詹事、太子左右衛、左右司禦、左右清道、左右內率、左右監門率府率、中州刺史、軍器監武德初為正三品，七年省，八年復置，九年又省，十年復置北都軍器監、上都護府副都護、上府折沖都尉《武德令》統軍正四品下，後改為折沖都尉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan the vice ministers were restored and the Personnel Bureau Director returned to fifth rank, lower grade — Vice Director of Ceremonies; Heir Apparent Left and Right Subprefects; Junior Household of the Heir Apparent; Heir Apparent Left and Right Guards; Left and Right Imperial Escort, Clear Way, Inner Rate, and Gate Rate commanders; prefect of a middle-grade prefecture; Armory Directorate: in early Wude senior third rank, abolished in the seventh year, restored in the eighth, abolished again in the ninth, restored in the tenth as Northern Capital Armory Directorate; Deputy Protector-General of the Superior Protectorate; Army-Suppressing Commandant of an upper-grade prefecture — under the Wude Code army commander was senior fourth rank, lower grade, later changed to army-suppressing commandant.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan (629) the vice ministers were restored and the Personnel Bureau Director reverted to fifth rank, lower grade — Vice Director of Ceremonies; Heir Apparent Left and Right Subprefects; Junior Household of the Heir Apparent; Heir Apparent Left and Right Guards; Left and Right Imperial Escort, Clear Way, Inner Rate, and Gate Rate commanders; prefect of a middle-grade prefecture; and Armory Directorate: in early Wude senior third rank, abolished in the seventh year, restored in the eighth, abolished again in the ninth, and restored in the tenth as Northern Capital Armory Directorate; Deputy Protector-General of the Superior Protectorate; and Army-Suppressing Commandant of an upper-grade prefecture — under the Wude Code the army commander ranked senior fourth rank, lower grade, later redesignated army-suppressing commandant.

manualTranslations.zh: 《垂拱令》始分為上中下府，改定官品。
manualTranslations.literal: The Chuigong Code first divided prefectures into upper, middle, and lower grades and revised official ranks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Chuigong Code first divided prefectures into upper, middle, and lower grades and revised the official rank tables.

manualTranslations.zh: 自此已上職事官。
manualTranslations.literal: From this point upward are executive offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All of the above are executive offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 率及折沖為武，余並為文也、正議大夫文散官也、開國伯爵、忠武將軍武散官、上輕車都尉勳官正第四品下階尚書右丞永昌元年進為從三品，如意元年復舊、諸司侍郎、太子右庶子、左右諭德、左右千牛衛、左右監門衛中郎將、親勳翊衛羽林中郎將、下州刺史《武德令》，中州刺史，正四品，下州刺史，從四品上。
manualTranslations.literal: Rate commanders and army-suppressing commandants are military; the rest are civil — Grand Master of Direct Counsel, civil honorary rank; Founding Earl, noble rank; Loyal Martial General, military honorary rank; Supreme Commandant of Light Chariots, merit rank. Senior fourth rank, lower grade — Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs: in the first year of Yongchang promoted to junior third rank; restored in the first year of Ruyi; vice ministers of the various bureaus; Heir Apparent Right Subprefect; Left and Right Moral Guides; Left and Right Thousand-Ox and Gate Guard Middle Commandants; Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Middle Commandants of the Forest of Feathers; prefect of a lower-grade prefecture — under the Wude Code the middle-grade prefect ranked senior fourth rank and the lower-grade prefect junior fourth rank, upper grade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rate commanders and army-suppressing commandants are military offices; the rest are civil — Grand Master of Direct Counsel, a civil honorary rank; Founding Earl, a noble rank; Loyal Martial General, a military honorary rank; and Supreme Commandant of Light Chariots, a merit rank. Senior fourth rank, lower grade — Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs was promoted to junior third rank in the first year of Yongchang and restored in the first year of Ruyi; vice ministers of the various bureaus; Heir Apparent Right Subprefect; Left and Right Moral Guides; Left and Right Thousand-Ox and Gate Guard Middle Commandants; Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Middle Commandants of the Forest of Feathers; and prefect of a lower-grade prefecture — under the Wude Code a middle-grade prefect ranked senior fourth rank and a lower-grade prefect junior fourth rank, upper grade.

manualTranslations.zh: 《貞觀令》，一切為下州，加入正四品下。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhenguan Code made all lower-grade prefectures and added them to senior fourth rank, lower grade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Code treated all as lower-grade prefectures and placed them at senior fourth rank, lower grade.

manualTranslations.zh: 自此已上職事官。
manualTranslations.literal: From this point upward are executive offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All of the above are executive offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 中郎將為武，余並為文也、通議大夫文散官、壯武將軍武散官從第四品上階秘書少監、八寺少卿、殿中少監、太子左右衛、司禦、清道、內率、監門副率、太子親勳翊衛中郎將、太子家令、太子率更令、太子僕、內侍、大都護親王府長史已上職事官。
manualTranslations.literal: Middle commandants are military; the rest are civil — Master of Free Counsel, civil honorary rank; Robust Martial General, military honorary rank. Junior fourth rank, upper grade — Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; vice directors of the Eight Directorates; Vice Director of the Palace Directorate; Heir Apparent Left and Right Guards; Imperial Escort, Clear Way, Inner Rate, and Gate Vice Rate commanders; Heir Apparent Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Middle Commandants; Heir Apparent Household, Timing, and Stable Directors; Palace Attendant; Chief Administrator of Princely Establishments under Great Protectorates — the above are executive offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Middle commandants are military offices; the rest are civil — Master of Free Counsel, a civil honorary rank; Robust Martial General, a military honorary rank. Junior fourth rank, upper grade — Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; vice directors of the Eight Directorates; Vice Director of the Palace Directorate; the Heir Apparent's Left and Right Guards; Imperial Escort, Clear Way, Inner Rate, and Gate Vice Rate commanders; Heir Apparent Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Middle Commandants; the Heir Apparent's Household, Timing, and Stable Directors; Palace Attendant; and Chief Administrator of Princely Establishments under Great Protectorates — all executive offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 府率、中郎將為武，余並為文、太中大夫文散官、宣威將軍武散官、輕車都尉勳官從第四品下階國子司業、少府少監、將作少匠、京兆、河南、太原府少尹、大都督府、大都護府、親王府司馬、上州別駕已上職事文官。
manualTranslations.literal: Rate commanders and middle commandants are military; the rest are civil — Grand Master of Palace Counsel, civil honorary rank; Proclaimer of Might General, military honorary rank; Commandant of Light Chariots, merit rank. Junior fourth rank, lower grade — Vice Chancellor of the National University; Vice Director of the Palace Workshops; Junior Artisan of Construction; Vice Intendants of the Capital, Henan, and Taiyuan prefectures; Marshals of Princely Establishments under Great Area Commands and Great Protectorates; Vice Prefect of a superior-grade prefecture — the above are civil executive offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rate commanders and middle commandants are military offices; the rest are civil — Grand Master of Palace Counsel, a civil honorary rank; Proclaimer of Might General, a military honorary rank; and Commandant of Light Chariots, a merit rank. Junior fourth rank, lower grade — Vice Chancellor of the National University; Vice Director of the Palace Workshops; Junior Artisan of Construction; Vice Intendants of the Capital, Henan, and Taiyuan prefectures; Marshals of Princely Establishments under Great Area Commands and Great Protectorates; and Vice Prefect of a superior-grade prefecture — all civil executive offices.

sourceRange.text: 總章二年置司列、司戎少常伯各兩員。咸亨元年十二月詔：「龍朔二年新改尚書省百司及僕射已下官名，並依舊。其東宮十率府，有異上臺諸衛，各宜依舊為率府。其左司議郎除「左」字。其左、右金吾、左、右威衛，依新改」。永淳元年七月，置州別駕。光宅元年九月，改尚書省為文昌台，左、右僕射為文昌左、右相。吏部為天官，戶部為地官，禮部為春官，兵部為夏官，刑部為秋官，工部為冬官。門下省為鸞台，中書省為鳳閣，侍中為納言，中書令為內史。太常為司禮，鴻臚為司賓，宗正為司屬，光祿為司膳，太府為司府，太僕為司僕，衛尉為司衛，大理為司刑。司農依舊。左、右驍衛為左右威衛，左、右武衛為左、右鷹揚衛，左、右威衛為左右豹衛，左、右領軍衛為左右玉鈴衛。左、右金吾衛依舊。御史台改為左肅政台，專知京百官及監諸軍旅，並承詔出使。更置右肅政台，專知諸州案察。垂拱元年二月，改黃門侍郎為鸞台侍郎，文昌都省為都台，主爵為司封，秘書省為麟台，內侍省為司宮台，少府監為尚方監。其左、右尚方兩署除「方」字。將作監為營繕監，國子監為成均監，都水監為水衡監。其詹事府為宮尹府，詹事為太尹，少詹事為少尹。左、右內率府為左右奉裕率府，千牛為左右奉裕，左、右監門率府為左右控鶴禁率府，諸衛鎧曹改為胄曹，司膳寺肴藏署改為珍羞署。十月，增置天官侍郎二員。又置左、右補闕、拾遣各二員。三年，加秋官侍郎一員。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace's ten commandant offices, which had differed from the capital guard offices, shall each again be commandant offices as before.

manualTranslations.literal: For Left and Right Golden Crow, Left and Right Majestic Guard — follow the new changes."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Golden Crow and Left and Right Majestic Guards shall keep their new names."

manualTranslations.zh: 永淳元年七月，置州別駕。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongchun, prefectural Vice Directors were established.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongchun (682), prefectural vice directors were established.

manualTranslations.zh: 光宅元年九月，改尚書省為文昌台，左、右僕射為文昌左、右相。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Guangzai, Department of State Affairs was changed to Wenchang Terrace; Left and Right Vice Directors to Wenchang Left and Right Chancellors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Guangzai (688), the Department of State Affairs became the Wenchang Terrace, and the left and right vice directors became the Wenchang Left and Right Chancellors.

manualTranslations.zh: 吏部為天官，戶部為地官，禮部為春官，兵部為夏官，刑部為秋官，工部為冬官。
manualTranslations.literal: Ministry of Personnel became Heavenly Office; Household, Earthly Office; Rites, Spring Office; War, Summer Office; Punishments, Autumn Office; Works, Winter Office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Personnel became the Heavenly Office, Household the Earthly Office, Rites the Spring Office, War the Summer Office, Punishments the Autumn Office, and Works the Winter Office.

manualTranslations.zh: 門下省為鸞台，中書省為鳳閣，侍中為納言，中書令為內史。
manualTranslations.literal: Chancellery became Phoenix Terrace; Secretariat, Phoenix Pavilion; Palace Attendant, Supplicator; Secretariat Director, Inner Scribe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Chancellery became the Phoenix Terrace, the Secretariat the Phoenix Pavilion, the Palace Attendant the Supplicator, and the Secretariat Director the Inner Scribe.

manualTranslations.zh: 太常為司禮，鴻臚為司賓，宗正為司屬，光祿為司膳，太府為司府，太僕為司僕，衛尉為司衛，大理為司刑。
manualTranslations.literal: Director of Ceremonies became Bureau of Rites; Director of Guests, Bureau of Guests; Director of the Imperial Clan, Bureau of Dependents; Director of Banquets, Bureau of Provisions; Director of the Treasury, Bureau of Treasury; Director of the Stud, Bureau of Servants; Director of the Guard, Bureau of Guard; Director of Justice, Bureau of Punishments.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ceremonies became Bureau of Rites, Guests Bureau of Guests, the Imperial Clan Bureau of Dependents, Banquets Bureau of Provisions, the Treasury Bureau of Treasury, the Stud Bureau of Servants, the Guard Bureau of Guard, and Justice Bureau of Punishments.

manualTranslations.zh: 司農依舊。
manualTranslations.literal: Director of Agriculture followed the old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Agriculture kept its old name.

manualTranslations.zh: 左、右驍衛為左右威衛，左、右武衛為左、右鷹揚衛，左、右威衛為左右豹衛，左、右領軍衛為左右玉鈴衛。
manualTranslations.literal: Left and Right Valiant Cavalry became Left and Right Majestic Guards; Left and Right Martial Guards, Left and Right Soaring Hawk Guards; Left and Right Majestic Guards, Left and Right Leopard Guards; Left and Right Army Inspector Guards, Left and Right Jade Bell Guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Valiant Cavalry became Left and Right Majestic Guards; the Martial Guards became Soaring Hawk Guards; the former Majestic Guards became Leopard Guards; and the Army Inspector Guards became Jade Bell Guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 左、右金吾衛依舊。
manualTranslations.literal: Left and Right Golden Crow Guards followed the old.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Golden Crow Guards kept their old names.

manualTranslations.zh: 御史台改為左肅政台，專知京百官及監諸軍旅，並承詔出使。
manualTranslations.literal: Censorate was changed to Left Rectification Terrace, exclusively overseeing capital officials and supervising all armies, and also undertaking missions by imperial edict.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Censorate became the Left Rectification Terrace, charged exclusively with oversight of capital officials and military forces and with carrying out missions by imperial edict.

manualTranslations.zh: 更置右肅政台，專知諸州案察。
manualTranslations.literal: The Right Rectification Terrace was additionally established, exclusively overseeing investigation of all prefectures.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A Right Rectification Terrace was also established, charged exclusively with investigating the prefectures.

manualTranslations.zh: 垂拱元年二月，改黃門侍郎為鸞台侍郎，文昌都省為都台，主爵為司封，秘書省為麟台，內侍省為司宮台，少府監為尚方監。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Chuigong, Yellow Gate Vice Minister was changed to Phoenix Terrace Vice Minister; Wenchang Chief Department to Chief Terrace; Fiefs to Bureau of Enfeoffments; Archive Secretariat to Unicorn Terrace; Palace Domestic Service to Palace Affairs Terrace; Palace Workshops Directorate to Imperial Works Directorate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Chuigong (685), the Yellow Gate Vice Minister became Phoenix Terrace Vice Minister; the Wenchang Chief Department became the Chief Terrace; Fiefs became the Bureau of Enfeoffments; the Archive Secretariat became the Unicorn Terrace; the Palace Domestic Service became the Palace Affairs Terrace; and the Palace Workshops Directorate became the Imperial Works Directorate.

manualTranslations.zh: 其左、右尚方兩署除「方」字。
manualTranslations.literal: For the Left and Right Imperial Works offices, the character "works" was removed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Imperial Works offices dropped the character for "works" from their titles.

manualTranslations.zh: 將作監為營繕監，國子監為成均監，都水監為水衡監。
manualTranslations.literal: Works Directorate became Construction and Repair Directorate; Directorate of the Sons of the State, Academy of Equilibrium Directorate; Directorate of Waterways, Water Balance Directorate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Works Directorate became Construction and Repair; the Directorate of the Sons of the State became the Academy of Equilibrium; and the Directorate of Waterways became the Water Balance Directorate.

manualTranslations.zh: 其詹事府為宮尹府，詹事為太尹，少詹事為少尹。
manualTranslations.literal: The Household Administration became Palace Rectifier Office; Household Administrator, Grand Rectifier; Junior Household Administrator, Junior Rectifier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Household Administration of the Heir Apparent became the Palace Rectifier Office; its administrator became Grand Rectifier and the junior administrator Junior Rectifier.

manualTranslations.zh: 左、右內率府為左右奉裕率府，千牛為左右奉裕，左、右監門率府為左右控鶴禁率府，諸衛鎧曹改為胄曹，司膳寺肴藏署改為珍羞署。
manualTranslations.literal: Left and Right Inner Commandant Offices became Left and Right Offering Abundance Commandant Offices; Thousand-Ox, Left and Right Offering Abundance; Left and Right Gate Commandant Offices, Left and Right Crane-Control Forbidden Commandant Offices; armor bureaus of the guards changed to helmet bureaus; Provisions Directorate's dish storehouse changed to Delicacies Office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Inner Commandant Offices became Left and Right Offering Abundance Commandant Offices; the Thousand-Ox Guards became Left and Right Offering Abundance; the Gate Commandant Offices became Left and Right Crane-Control Forbidden Commandant Offices; guard armor bureaus were renamed helmet bureaus; and the Provisions Directorate's dish storehouse became the Delicacies Office.

manualTranslations.zh: 十月，增置天官侍郎二員。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month, two Heavenly Office Vice Ministers were added.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, two vice ministers of the Heavenly Office were added.

manualTranslations.zh: 又置左、右補闕、拾遣各二員。
manualTranslations.literal: Also established Left and Right Supplementation Omission and Left and Right Memorial Retrieval, two posts each.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Left and Right Supplementation Omission and Left and Right Memorial Retrieval were also created, two posts on each side.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，加秋官侍郎一員。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year, one Autumn Office Vice Minister was added.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the third year, one vice minister of the Autumn Office was added.

sourceRange.text: 正第五品上階諫議大夫、御史中丞《武德令》，從五品上。《貞觀令》，加入正五品上，五年又加入四品。如意元年復舊也、國子博士、給事中、中書舍人、太子中允、太子左右贊善大夫、都水使者、萬年、長安、河南、洛陽、太原、晉陽、奉先、會昌縣令武德元年敕：萬年、長安令為正五上。七年定令，改為從五品。貞觀初復舊也、親勳翊衛羽林郎將、中都督府、上都護府長史、親王府諮議參軍事《武德令》，正五品下也、軍器少監、太史少監、親王府典軍已上職事官。郎將、典軍為武，余並為文。《永徽令》，親王典軍從四品下。《垂拱令》改入五品也。、中散大夫文散官、開國子爵、定遠將軍武散官、上騎都尉勳官正第五品下階太子中舍人、尚食、尚藥、奉禦、太子親勳翊衛郎將、內常侍、中都督、上都護府司馬、中州別駕、下府折沖都尉已上職事官。郎將、折沖為武，余並為文也、朝議大夫文散官、寧遠將軍武散官。

localRange.text: 正第五品上階正第五品下階太子中舍人、尚食尚藥奉禦、太子親勳翊衛郎將、內常侍、中都督上都護府司馬、中州別駕、下府折沖都尉、已上職事官。郎將、折沖為武，余並為文也。朝議大夫、文散官。甯遠將軍。武散官。

manualTranslations.zh: 正第五品上階諫議大夫、御史中丞《武德令》，從五品上。
manualTranslations.literal: Senior fifth rank, upper grade — Remonstrance Official and Censor-in-Chief: under the Wude Code, junior fifth rank, upper grade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Senior fifth rank, upper grade — Remonstrance Official and Censor-in-Chief ranked junior fifth rank, upper grade under the Wude Code.

manualTranslations.zh: 《貞觀令》，加入正五品上，五年又加入四品。
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhenguan Code added them to senior fifth rank, upper grade; in the fifth year again added to fourth rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Code placed them at senior fifth rank, upper grade; in the fifth year they were again raised to fourth rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 如意元年復舊也、國子博士、給事中、中書舍人、太子中允、太子左右贊善大夫、都水使者、萬年、長安、河南、洛陽、太原、晉陽、奉先、會昌縣令武德元年敕：萬年、長安令為正五上。
manualTranslations.literal: Restored in the first year of Ruyi — Erudite of the National University; Drafting Officer; Secretariat Drafting Officer; Heir Apparent Middle Attendant; Heir Apparent Left and Right Moral Guides; Waterways Commissioner; magistrates of Wannian, Chang'an, Henan, Luoyang, Taiyuan, Jinyang, Fengxian, and Huichang — Wude first-year edict: Wannian and Chang'an magistrates were senior fifth rank, upper grade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Restored in the first year of Ruyi (692) — Erudite of the National University; Drafting Officer; Secretariat Drafting Officer; Heir Apparent Middle Attendant; Heir Apparent Left and Right Moral Guides; Waterways Commissioner; and magistrates of Wannian, Chang'an, Henan, Luoyang, Taiyuan, Jinyang, Fengxian, and Huichang — a Wude first-year edict made the Wannian and Chang'an magistrates senior fifth rank, upper grade.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年定令，改為從五品。
manualTranslations.literal: The code fixed in the seventh year changed them to junior fifth rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The code promulgated in the seventh year reassigned them to junior fifth rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞觀初復舊也、親勳翊衛羽林郎將、中都督府、上都護府長史、親王府諮議參軍事《武德令》，正五品下也、軍器少監、太史少監、親王府典軍已上職事官。
manualTranslations.literal: Restored at the beginning of Zhenguan — Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Commanders of the Forest of Feathers; chief administrator of a middle protectorate; chief administrator of a superior protectorate; advisory military aide of a princely establishment — under the Wude Code, senior fifth rank, lower grade; Vice Director of the Armory; Vice Director of the Astrological Service; military aide of a princely establishment — the above are executive offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Restored at the beginning of the Zhenguan era — Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Commanders of the Forest of Feathers; chief administrator of a middle protectorate; chief administrator of a superior protectorate; and advisory military aide of a princely establishment ranked senior fifth rank, lower grade under the Wude Code; Vice Director of the Armory; Vice Director of the Astrological Service; and military aide of a princely establishment — all executive offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 郎將、典軍為武，余並為文。
manualTranslations.literal: Commanders and military aides are military; the rest are civil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commanders and military aides are military offices; the rest are civil.

manualTranslations.zh: 《永徽令》，親王典軍從四品下。
manualTranslations.literal: The Yonghui Code made the military aide of an imperial prince junior fourth rank, lower grade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the Yonghui Code the military aide of an imperial prince ranked junior fourth rank, lower grade.

manualTranslations.zh: 《垂拱令》改入五品也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Chuigong Code changed it to fifth rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Chuigong Code reassigned it to fifth rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 、中散大夫文散官、開國子爵、定遠將軍武散官、上騎都尉勳官正第五品下階太子中舍人、尚食、尚藥、奉禦、太子親勳翊衛郎將、內常侍、中都督、上都護府司馬、中州別駕、下府折沖都尉已上職事官。
manualTranslations.literal: Master of Palace Attendance, civil honorary rank; Founding Viscount, noble rank; General for Settling the Distant, military honorary rank; Supreme Commandant of Cavalry, merit rank. Senior fifth rank, lower grade — Heir Apparent Drafting Officer; Providers of Food and Medicine; Heir Apparent Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Commanders; Regular Palace Attendant; middle protector; marshal of a superior protectorate; Vice Prefect of a middle-grade prefecture; Army-Suppressing Commandant of a lower-grade prefecture — the above are executive offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Master of Palace Attendance, a civil honorary rank; Founding Viscount, a noble rank; General for Settling the Distant, a military honorary rank; and Supreme Commandant of Cavalry, a merit rank. Senior fifth rank, lower grade — Heir Apparent Drafting Officer; Providers of Food and Medicine; Heir Apparent Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Commanders; Regular Palace Attendant; middle protector; marshal of a superior protectorate; Vice Prefect of a middle-grade prefecture; and Army-Suppressing Commandant of a lower-grade prefecture — all executive offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 郎將、折沖為武，余並為文也、朝議大夫文散官、寧遠將軍武散官。
manualTranslations.literal: Commanders and army-suppressing commandants are military; the rest are civil — Court Consultant, civil honorary rank; General for Pacifying the Distant, military honorary rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commanders and army-suppressing commandants are military offices; the rest are civil — Court Consultant, a civil honorary rank; and General for Pacifying the Distant, a military honorary rank.

sourceRange.text: 正第六品上階太學博士《武德令》，從六品上，貞觀年改、太子詹事府丞、太子司議郎、太子舍人、中郡長史《武德令》，中州別駕從五品上，貞觀年改也、太子典膳藥藏郎、京兆、河南、太原府諸縣令武德元年敕，雍州諸縣令階從五品上，七年定令改、親王府掾屬《武德令》，從五品下也、武庫中尚署令《武德令》依上署令，從七品下，太極年改武庫令階，開元年改中尚令階、諸衛左右司階、中府果毅都尉、鎮軍兵滿二萬人已上司馬已上職事官。司階、果毅為武，余並為文也、親勳翊衛校衛衛官、朝議郎文散官、昭武校尉武散官、驍騎尉勳官正第六品下階千牛備身左右衛官已上、王公已下高品子孫起家為之、太子文學、下州長史武德中，下州別駕，正六品，貞觀二十三年，改為長史丞。永淳元年，諸州置別駕官。天寶八載停別駕，下郡置長史。後上元二年，諸州置別駕，不廢下府長史也、中州司馬《武德令》，中州治中，從五品下，《貞觀令》改、內謁者監、中牧監、上牧副監已上文職事官、上鎮將武職事官。《武德令》，從四品下也、承議郎文散官、昭武副尉武散官。《武德令》有天策上將府諸曹參軍事，九年省也。從第六品上階起居郎、起居舍人、尚書諸司員外郎《武德令》，吏部員外郎正六品上，諸司員外郎正六品下。貞觀二年改、八寺丞、大理司直、國子助教《武德令》，從七品上、城門符寶郎、通事舍人、秘書郎《武德令》，正七品上、著作佐郎《武德令》，正七品上、侍御醫《武德》、《乾封令》，正七品上。

localRange.text: 正第六品上階正第六品下階從第六品上階起居郎、起居舍人、尚書諸司員外郎、《武德令》，吏部員外郎正六品上，諸司員外郎正六品下。貞觀二年改。八寺丞、大理司直、國子助教、《武德令》，從七品上。城門符寶郎、通事舍人、秘書郎、《武德令》，正七品上。著作佐郎、《武德令》，正七品下。侍御醫、《武德》、《乾封令》，正七品上。

manualTranslations.zh: 正第六品上階太學博士《武德令》，從六品上，貞觀年改、太子詹事府丞、太子司議郎、太子舍人、中郡長史《武德令》，中州別駕從五品上，貞觀年改也、太子典膳藥藏郎、京兆、河南、太原府諸縣令武德元年敕，雍州諸縣令階從五品上，七年定令改、親王府掾屬《武德令》，從五品下也、武庫中尚署令《武德令》依上署令，從七品下，太極年改武庫令階，開元年改中尚令階、諸衛左右司階、中府果毅都尉、鎮軍兵滿二萬人已上司馬已上職事官。
manualTranslations.literal: Senior sixth rank, upper grade — Erudite of the Imperial Academy: under the Wude Code, junior sixth rank, upper grade; changed in the Zhenguan era — Assistant of the Household of the Heir Apparent; Heir Apparent Discussion Gentleman; Heir Apparent Attendant; chief administrator of a middle-grade commandery — under the Wude Code the Vice Prefect of a middle-grade prefecture was junior fifth rank, upper grade; changed in the Zhenguan era — Heir Apparent Provision and Pharmacy Storehouse Attendant; magistrates of the various counties of the Capital, Henan, and Taiyuan prefectures — Wude first-year edict: Yong prefecture county magistrates junior fifth rank, upper grade; changed by the seventh-year code — staff member of a princely establishment: under the Wude Code, junior fifth rank, lower grade — Armory Central Storehouse Director: under the Wude Code followed upper storehouse director, junior seventh rank, lower grade; Taizi era changed armory director rank; Kaiyuan era changed central storehouse director rank; left and right rank officers of the various guards; Army Boldness Commandant of a middle-grade prefecture; marshal of a garrison with twenty thousand troops or more — the above are executive offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Senior sixth rank, upper grade — Erudite of the Imperial Academy ranked junior sixth rank, upper grade under the Wude Code and was changed in the Zhenguan era — Assistant of the Household of the Heir Apparent; Heir Apparent Discussion Gentleman; Heir Apparent Attendant; and chief administrator of a middle-grade commandery — under the Wude Code the Vice Prefect of a middle-grade prefecture ranked junior fifth rank, upper grade and was changed in the Zhenguan era — Heir Apparent Provision and Pharmacy Storehouse Attendant; magistrates of the various counties of the Capital, Henan, and Taiyuan prefectures — a Wude first-year edict made Yong prefecture county magistrates junior fifth rank, upper grade, later changed by the seventh-year code — staff member of a princely establishment ranked junior fifth rank, lower grade under the Wude Code — Armory Central Storehouse Director followed the upper storehouse director at junior seventh rank, lower grade under the Wude Code; the armory director rank was changed in the Taizi era and the central storehouse director rank in the Kaiyuan era — left and right rank officers of the various guards; Army Boldness Commandant of a middle-grade prefecture; and marshal of a garrison with twenty thousand troops or more — all executive offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 司階、果毅為武，余並為文也、親勳翊衛校衛衛官、朝議郎文散官、昭武校尉武散官、驍騎尉勳官正第六品下階千牛備身左右衛官已上、王公已下高品子孫起家為之、太子文學、下州長史武德中，下州別駕，正六品，貞觀二十三年，改為長史丞。
manualTranslations.literal: Rank officers and army-boldness commandants are military; the rest are civil — Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Company Commanders, guard officers; Gentleman for Court Discussion, civil honorary rank; Martial Proclaimer Company Commander, military honorary rank; Valiant Cavalry Commandant, merit rank. Senior sixth rank, lower grade — Thousand-Ox Bodyguards and above of the Left and Right Guards, entered by high-ranking descendants of princes and dukes downward — Heir Apparent Literary Instructor; chief administrator of a lower-grade prefecture: in Wude the Vice Prefect of a lower-grade prefecture was senior sixth rank; in the twenty-third year of Zhenguan changed to chief administrator.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rank officers and army-boldness commandants are military offices; the rest are civil — Personal, Merit, and Assisting Guard Company Commanders and guard officers; Gentleman for Court Discussion, a civil honorary rank; Martial Proclaimer Company Commander, a military honorary rank; and Valiant Cavalry Commandant, a merit rank. Senior sixth rank, lower grade — Thousand-Ox Bodyguards and above of the Left and Right Guards, posts entered by high-ranking descendants of princes and dukes downward — Heir Apparent Literary Instructor; and chief administrator of a lower-grade prefecture: in Wude the Vice Prefect of a lower-grade prefecture ranked senior sixth rank; in the twenty-third year of Zhenguan (649) the post became chief administrator.

manualTranslations.zh: 永淳元年，諸州置別駕官。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, vice-prefect posts were established in all prefectures.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchun (682), vice-prefect posts were established in all prefectures.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寶八載停別駕，下郡置長史。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao vice-prefects were suspended and chief administrators were placed in lower commanderies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianbao (749) vice-prefects were suspended and chief administrators were placed in lower commanderies.

manualTranslations.zh: 後上元二年，諸州置別駕，不廢下府長史也、中州司馬《武德令》，中州治中，從五品下，《貞觀令》改、內謁者監、中牧監、上牧副監已上文職事官、上鎮將武職事官。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, in the second year of Shangyuan, vice-prefects were established in all prefectures without abolishing the chief administrators of lower prefectures — Vice Marshal of a middle-grade prefecture: under the Wude Code, middle-grade administrative aide, junior fifth rank, lower grade; changed by the Zhenguan Code — Inner Usher Director; middle pasture superintendent; deputy superintendent of a superior pasture — the above are civil executive offices; garrison general of a superior garrison — military executive office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, in the second year of Shangyuan (675), vice-prefects were established in all prefectures without abolishing the chief administrators of lower prefectures — Vice Marshal of a middle-grade prefecture ranked as middle-grade administrative aide, junior fifth rank, lower grade under the Wude Code and was changed under the Zhenguan Code — Inner Usher Director; middle pasture superintendent; and deputy superintendent of a superior pasture — all civil executive offices; and garrison general of a superior garrison — a military executive office.

manualTranslations.zh: 《武德令》，從四品下也、承議郎文散官、昭武副尉武散官。
manualTranslations.literal: Under the Wude Code, junior fourth rank, lower grade — Gentleman for Supporting Discussion, civil honorary rank; Martial Proclaimer Deputy Commander, military honorary rank.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the Wude Code it ranked junior fourth rank, lower grade — Gentleman for Supporting Discussion, a civil honorary rank; and Martial Proclaimer Deputy Commander, a military honorary rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 《武德令》有天策上將府諸曹參軍事，九年省也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Wude Code had adjutants of the various bureaus of the Celestial-Strategy General-in-Chief's Office; abolished in the ninth year.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Wude Code provided for adjutants of the various bureaus of the Celestial-Strategy General-in-Chief's Office; the posts were abolished in the ninth year.

manualTranslations.zh: 從第六品上階起居郎、起居舍人、尚書諸司員外郎《武德令》，吏部員外郎正六品上，諸司員外郎正六品下。
manualTranslations.literal: Junior sixth rank, upper grade — Court Diarist; Court Diarist Attendant; vice directors of the Department bureaus — under the Wude Code, the Personnel Bureau Vice Director was senior sixth rank, upper grade; other bureau vice directors, senior sixth rank, lower grade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Junior sixth rank, upper grade — Court Diarist; Court Diarist Attendant; and vice directors of the Department bureaus — under the Wude Code the Personnel Bureau Vice Director ranked senior sixth rank, upper grade and the other bureau vice directors ranked senior sixth rank, lower grade.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞觀二年改、八寺丞、大理司直、國子助教《武德令》，從七品上、城門符寶郎、通事舍人、秘書郎《武德令》，正七品上、著作佐郎《武德令》，正七品上、侍御醫《武德》、《乾封令》，正七品上。
manualTranslations.literal: Changed in the second year of Zhenguan — Vice Directors of the Eight Directorates; Directing Investigator of Judicial Review; Assistant Instructor of the National University — under the Wude Code, junior seventh rank, upper grade — Gate Seal and Credential Attendant; Master of External Communications; Secretariat Clerk — under the Wude Code, senior seventh rank, upper grade — Compiler Assistant — under the Wude Code, senior seventh rank, upper grade — Attending Imperial Physician — under the Wude and Qianfeng codes, senior seventh rank, upper grade.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Changed in the second year of Zhenguan (628) — Vice Directors of the Eight Directorates; Directing Investigator of Judicial Review; and Assistant Instructor of the National University ranked junior seventh rank, upper grade under the Wude Code — Gate Seal and Credential Attendant; Master of External Communications; and Secretariat Clerk ranked senior seventh rank, upper grade under the Wude Code — Compiler Assistant ranked senior seventh rank, upper grade under the Wude Code — and Attending Imperial Physician ranked senior seventh rank, upper grade under the Wude and Qianfeng codes.

sourceRange.text: 」高祖即位，仍用隋之五銖錢。武德四年七月，廢五銖錢，行開元通寶錢，徑八分，重二銖四絫，積十文重一兩。一千文重六斤四兩。仍置錢監於洛、並、幽、益等州。秦王、齊王各賜三爐鑄錢，右僕射裴寂賜一爐。敢有盜鑄者身死，家口配沒。五年五月，又于桂州置監。議者以新錢輕重大小最為折衷，遠近甚便之。後盜鑄漸起，而所在用錢濫惡。顯慶五年九月，敕以惡錢轉多，令所在官私為市取，以五惡錢酬一好錢。百姓以惡錢價賤，私自藏之，以候官禁之弛。高宗又令以好錢一文買惡錢兩文，弊仍不息。至乾封元年封嶽之後，又改造新錢，文曰「乾封泉寶」，徑一寸，重二銖六分，仍與舊錢並行。新錢一文當舊錢之十。周年之後，舊錢並廢。

manualTranslations.zh: 」高祖即位，仍用隋之五銖錢。
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he continued to use the Sui dynasty's five-zhu coins.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he continued to use the Sui five-zhu coin.

manualTranslations.zh: 武德四年七月，廢五銖錢，行開元通寶錢，徑八分，重二銖四絫，積十文重一兩。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Wude, the five-zhu coin was abolished and the Kaiyuan tongbao coin was put into circulation; diameter eight fen, weight two zhu four lei; ten coins together weighed one liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wude 4 (621), the five-zhu coin was abolished and the Kaiyuan tongbao introduced—eight fen in diameter, two zhu four lei in weight, ten coins to the liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 一千文重六斤四兩。
manualTranslations.literal: One thousand coins weighed six jin four liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A thousand coins weighed six jin and four liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 仍置錢監於洛、並、幽、益等州。
manualTranslations.literal: Mint supervisors were also established in Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, and other prefectures.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mint supervisors were also established at Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, and other prefectures.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦王、齊王各賜三爐鑄錢，右僕射裴寂賜一爐。
manualTranslations.literal: The Prince of Qin and the Prince of Qi were each granted three furnaces for casting coin; the Right Vice Director Pei Ji was granted one furnace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin and the Prince of Qi were each granted three minting furnaces; Pei Ji, Vice Director of the Right, received one.

manualTranslations.zh: 敢有盜鑄者身死，家口配沒。
manualTranslations.literal: Whoever dared illicitly to cast coin would be executed, and his household registered for penal servitude and confiscation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Anyone who dared cast coin illicitly would be put to death, his household registered for penal servitude and his property confiscated.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年五月，又于桂州置監。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, a supervisor was also established at Guizhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year, a mint supervisor was also established at Guizhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 議者以新錢輕重大小最為折衷，遠近甚便之。
manualTranslations.literal: Commentators held that the new coin's weight and size were the most balanced compromise, greatly convenient near and far.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Observers judged the new coin's weight and size the happiest medium, and found it greatly convenient throughout the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 後盜鑄漸起，而所在用錢濫惡。
manualTranslations.literal: Later illicit casting gradually arose, and the coins in use everywhere became debased and poor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later illicit casting spread, and coin in circulation everywhere grew debased and wretched.

manualTranslations.zh: 顯慶五年九月，敕以惡錢轉多，令所在官私為市取，以五惡錢酬一好錢。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Xianqing, an edict was issued because debased coin was growing numerous, ordering that wherever official and private parties traded in the market, five debased coins would be exchanged for one good coin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Xianqing 5 (660), an edict declared that debased coin had grown too common and ordered that in all market transactions, public and private alike, five debased coins be taken for one good coin.

manualTranslations.zh: 百姓以惡錢價賤，私自藏之，以候官禁之弛。
manualTranslations.literal: The people, because debased coin was cheap in value, secretly hoarded it, waiting for the official prohibition to relax.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because debased coin fetched so little, the people hoarded it in secret, waiting for the ban to lapse.

manualTranslations.zh: 高宗又令以好錢一文買惡錢兩文，弊仍不息。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Gaozong also ordered that one good coin could buy two debased coins, yet the abuse still did not cease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gaozong then ordered that one good coin could purchase two debased ones—but the abuse only continued.

manualTranslations.zh: 至乾封元年封嶽之後，又改造新錢，文曰「乾封泉寶」，徑一寸，重二銖六分，仍與舊錢並行。
manualTranslations.literal: When the first year of Qianfeng came, after the fengshan ceremony, new coin was again cast, inscribed "Qianfeng quanbao," one cun in diameter, weighing two zhu six fen, still circulating alongside the old coin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the fengshan rite at Mount Tai in Qianfeng 1 (666), new coin was cast bearing the inscription "Qianfeng quanbao"—one cun across, two zhu six fen in weight—circulating alongside the old coin.

manualTranslations.zh: 新錢一文當舊錢之十。
manualTranslations.literal: One new coin was equivalent to ten old coins.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One new coin counted for ten of the old.

manualTranslations.zh: 周年之後，舊錢並廢。
manualTranslations.literal: After a full year, the old coin was altogether abolished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A year later, the old coin was abolished entirely.

sourceRange.text: 量入而為出，節用而愛人，度財省費，蓋用之必有度也，是故既庶且富，而教化行焉。周有井田之制，秦有阡陌之法，二世發閭左而海內崩離，漢武稅舟車而國用以竭。自古有國有家，興亡盛衰，未嘗不由此也。隋文帝因周氏平齊之後，府庫充實，庶事節儉，未嘗虛費。開皇之初，議者以比漢代文、景，有粟陳貫朽之積。煬帝即位，大縱奢靡，加以東西行幸，輿駕不息，征討四夷，兵車屢動。西失律于沙徼，東喪師於遼、碣，數年之間，公私罄竭，財力既殫，國遂亡矣。

manualTranslations.zh: 量入而為出，節用而愛人，度財省費，蓋用之必有度也，是故既庶且富，而教化行焉。
manualTranslations.literal: They measured income to set expenditure, economized in use while cherishing the people, and gauged wealth while sparing expense — for spending must indeed have limits; therefore, when the people were numerous and wealthy, transforming instruction was carried out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Revenue set the bounds of expenditure, frugality was practiced and the people cared for, and costs were weighed and expenses curbed — public spending had to stay within limits; only then could a populous, prosperous realm sustain civilizing order.

manualTranslations.zh: 周有井田之制，秦有阡陌之法，二世發閭左而海內崩離，漢武稅舟車而國用以竭。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou had the well-field system; Qin had the field-path law. The Second Emperor drafted those from the wards' left and the realm within the seas split apart; Emperor Wu taxed boats and carts and state funds were exhausted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhou instituted the well-field system and Qin the open-field law; when the Second Emperor conscripted commoners wholesale, the empire fell apart, and when Emperor Wu taxed boats and carriages, the treasury was drained dry.

manualTranslations.zh: 自古有國有家，興亡盛衰，未嘗不由此也。
manualTranslations.literal: From antiquity, those who possessed states and families — in rise, fall, flourishing, and decay — have never failed to proceed from this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From antiquity onward, the rise and fall of dynasties has always hinged on such fiscal choices.

manualTranslations.zh: 隋文帝因周氏平齊之後，府庫充實，庶事節儉，未嘗虛費。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui, relying on the Zhou house's pacification of Qi, found the treasuries full and all affairs economical; he never spent wastefully.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the Northern Zhou pacified Qi, Emperor Wen of Sui inherited full treasuries; he kept ordinary affairs frugal and never squandered public funds.

manualTranslations.zh: 開皇之初，議者以比漢代文、景，有粟陳貫朽之積。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, discussants compared him to Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing of Han; there was grain piled so long that the cords rotted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang era, commentators likened his reign to those of Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing of Han, when grain stores grew so vast that the ropes binding the sacks rotted away.

manualTranslations.zh: 煬帝即位，大縱奢靡，加以東西行幸，輿駕不息，征討四夷，兵車屢動。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he greatly indulged extravagance; moreover he traveled east and west, his carriage never resting, campaigning against the four barbarians, with troops and chariots repeatedly mobilized.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he gave free rein to extravagance, touring east and west without pause, campaigning against the frontier peoples, and mobilizing armies again and again.

manualTranslations.zh: 西失律于沙徼，東喪師於遼、碣，數年之間，公私罄竭，財力既殫，國遂亡矣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the west he lost discipline at the desert frontier; in the east he lost armies at Liao and Jie. Within a few years, public and private were exhausted; financial strength was spent, and the state then perished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the west his armies broke down on the desert frontier; in the east he lost forces in Liaodong and the Jie region. Within a few years both public and private coffers were empty, the state's resources were spent, and the dynasty collapsed.

sourceRange.text: 」建中元年二月，遣黜陟使分行天下，其詔略曰：「戶無主客，以見居為簿。人無丁中，以貧富為差。行商者，在郡縣稅三十之一。居人之稅，秋夏兩征之。各有不便者，三之。餘征賦悉罷，而丁額不廢。其田畝之稅，率以大曆十四年墾數為准。征夏稅無過六月。秋稅無過十一月。違者進退長吏。令黜陟使各量風土所宜、人戶多少均之，定其賦，尚書度支總統焉。」三年五月，淮南節度使陳少游請於本道兩稅錢每千增二百，因詔他州悉如之。八年四月，劍南西川觀察使韋皋奏請加稅什二，以增給官吏，從之。

sourceRange.text: 中宗和思皇后趙氏，京兆長安人。祖綽，武德中以戰功至右領軍衛將軍。父瑰，尚高祖女常樂公主，歷遷左千牛將軍。中宗為英王時，納后為妃。既而妃母公主得罪，妃亦坐廢，幽死於內侍省。則天臨朝，瑰為壽州刺史，坐與越王貞連謀被誅，公主亦坐死。神龍元年，贈后謚為恭皇后，贈瑰左衛大將軍。及中宗崩，將葬於定陵，議者以韋后得罪，不宜祔葬，於是追謚后為和思，莫知瘞所，行招魂祔葬之禮。太常博士彭景直上言：「古無招魂葬之禮，不可備棺槨，置轀鬻輬。宜據《漢書郊祀志》葬黃帝衣冠於橋山故事，以皇后禕衣於陵所寢宮招魂，置衣於魂輿，以太牢告祭，遷衣於寢宮，舒於御榻之右，覆以夷衾而祔葬焉。」從之。中宗韋庶人，京兆萬年人也。祖弘表，貞觀中為曹王府典軍。中宗為太子時，納后為妃，仍擢后父普州參軍玄貞為豫州刺史。嗣聖元年，立為皇后。其年，中宗見廢，后隨從房州。時中宗懼不自安，每聞制使至，惶恐欲自殺。后勸王曰：「禍福倚伏，何常之有？豈失一死，何遽如是也！」累年同艱危，情義甚篤。所生懿德太子、永泰、永壽、長寧、安樂四公主，安樂最幼，生於房州，帝自脫衣裹之，遂名曰裹兒，特寵異焉。及中宗復立為太子，又立后為妃。時昭容上官氏常勸后行則天故事，乃上表請天下士庶為出母服喪三年；又請百姓以年二十三為丁，五十九免役，改易制度，以收時望。制皆許之。

sourceRange.text: 高開道，滄州陽信人也。少以煮鹽自給，有勇力，走及奔馬。隋大業末，河間人格謙擁兵於豆子，開道往從之，署為將軍。後謙為隋師所滅，開道與其黨百餘人亡匿海曲。復出掠滄州，招集得數百人，北掠城鎮，臨渝至於懷遠，皆破之，悉有其眾。武德元年，隋將李景守北平郡，開道引兵圍之，連年不能克。景自度不能支，拔城而去。開道又取其地，進陷漁陽郡，有馬數千匹，眾且萬人，自立為燕王，都於漁陽。先是，有懷戎沙門高曇晟者，因縣令設齋，士女大集，曇晟與其僧徒五十人擁齋眾而反，殺縣令及鎮將，自稱大乘皇帝，立尼靜宣為耶輸皇后，建元為法輪。至夜，遣人招誘開道，結為兄弟，改封齊王。開道以眾五千人歸之，居數月，襲殺曇晟，悉並其眾。

sourceRange.text: 武德元年冬，軌僭稱尊號，以其子伯玉為皇太子，長史曹珍為左僕射。謹等議欲盡殺隋官，分其家產，軌曰：「諸人見逼為主，便須稟吾處分。義兵之起，意在救焚，今殺人取物，是為狂賊。立計如此，何以求濟乎！」乃署統師太僕卿，士政太府卿，薛舉遣兵侵軌，軌遣其將李贇擊敗於昌松，斬首二千級，盡虜其眾，復議放還之。贇言於軌曰：「今竭力戰勝，俘虜賊兵，又縱放之，還使資敵，不如盡坑之。」軌曰：「不然。若有天命，自擒其主，此輩士卒，終為我有。若事不成，留此何益？」遂遣之。未幾，攻陷張掖、燉煌、西平、枹罕，盡有河西五郡之地。

sourceRange.text: 大亮以為於事無益，上疏曰：臣聞欲綏遠者，必先安近。中國百姓，天下本根；四夷之人，猶於枝葉。擾於根本，以厚枝附，而求久安，未之有也。自古明王，化中國以信，馭夷狄以權。故《春秋》云：「戎狄豺狼，不可厭也；諸夏親暱，不可棄也。」自陛下君臨區宇，深根固本，人逸兵強，九州殷盛，四夷自服。今者招致突厥，雖入提封，臣愚稍覺勞費，未悟其有益也。然河西氓庶，積御蕃夷，州縣蕭條，戶口鮮少，加因隋亂，減耗尤多。突厥未平之前，尚不安業；匈奴微弱已來，始就農畝。若即勞役，恐致妨損。以臣愚惑，請停招慰。且謂之荒服者，故臣而不內。是以周室愛人攘狄，竟延七百之齡；秦王輕戰事胡，四十載而遂絕。漢文養兵靜守，天下安豐；孝武揚威遠略，海內虛耗。雖悔輪台，追已不及。至於隋室，早得伊吾，兼統鄯善，既得之後，勞費日甚，虛內致外，竟損無益。遠尋秦、漢，近觀隋室，動靜安危，昭然備矣。伊吾雖已臣附，遠在蕃磧，人非中夏，地多沙鹵。其自豎立稱籓附庸者，請羈縻受之，使居塞外，必畏威懷德，永為蕃臣，蓋行虛惠，而收實福矣。近日突厥傾國入朝，既不能俘之江淮，以變其俗；置於內地，去京不遠，雖則寬仁之義，亦非久安之計也。每見一人初降，賜物五匹、袍一領，酋帥悉授大官，祿厚位尊，理多縻費。以中國之幣帛，供積惡之凶虜，其眾益多，非中國之利也。

manualTranslations.zh: 大亮以為於事無益，上疏曰：臣聞欲綏遠者，必先安近。
manualTranslations.literal: Daliang thought this of no benefit to affairs and submitted a memorial, saying: Your subject has heard that those who wish to pacify the distant must first secure the near.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Daliang believed this was impractical and submitted a memorial: I have heard that to win over distant peoples one must first secure those nearby.

manualTranslations.zh: 中國百姓，天下本根；
manualTranslations.literal: The common people of China are the root of All Under Heaven;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people of the heartland are the foundation of the empire;

manualTranslations.zh: 四夷之人，猶於枝葉。
manualTranslations.literal: The peoples of the four barbarians are like branches and leaves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the foreign tribes are but branches and leaves.

manualTranslations.zh: 擾於根本，以厚枝附，而求久安，未之有也。
manualTranslations.literal: To disturb the root and trunk in order to fatten branch and attachment, and yet seek long security—never has there been such a thing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To strain the root while nourishing the branches in hope of lasting peace has never succeeded.

manualTranslations.zh: 自古明王，化中國以信，馭夷狄以權。
manualTranslations.literal: From antiquity enlightened kings civilized China through trust and controlled the barbarians of Yi and Di through power.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, wise rulers have governed the heartland through integrity and handled the frontier tribes through firmness.

manualTranslations.zh: 故《春秋》云：「戎狄豺狼，不可厭也；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "The Rong and Di are wolves—one cannot grow weary of guarding against them;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "The Rong and Di are wolves that can never be satisfied;

manualTranslations.zh: 諸夏親暱，不可棄也。」
manualTranslations.literal: the various Xia are kin and close—one cannot abandon them."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the civilized states are kin and must not be abandoned."

manualTranslations.zh: 自陛下君臨區宇，深根固本，人逸兵強，九州殷盛，四夷自服。
manualTranslations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended to rule the realm, deeply rooting and securing the foundation, the people are at ease and the troops strong; the Nine Provinces are abundant and flourishing, and the four barbarians submit of themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, you have strengthened the foundation at home. The people prosper and the army is strong; the realm flourishes and the frontier tribes submit willingly.

manualTranslations.zh: 今者招致突厥，雖入提封，臣愚稍覺勞費，未悟其有益也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now in summoning the Turks, though they enter the imperial domain, this subject in his foolishness slightly perceives labor and expense and does not yet discern where the benefit lies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet in summoning the Turks into the empire, I see only cost and trouble, and cannot perceive the benefit.

manualTranslations.zh: 然河西氓庶，積御蕃夷，州縣蕭條，戶口鮮少，加因隋亂，減耗尤多。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet the common folk of Hexi, long garrisoning against the barbarians, have prefectures and counties desolate and sparse, households few; moreover because of the Sui turmoil, losses are especially great.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people of Hexi have long borne the burden of frontier defense. Their prefectures are depopulated, their households few, and the Sui chaos reduced them still further.

manualTranslations.zh: 突厥未平之前，尚不安業；
manualTranslations.literal: Before the Turks were pacified, they still could not settle to their occupations;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before the Turks were subdued, they could not even farm in peace;

manualTranslations.zh: 匈奴微弱已來，始就農畝。
manualTranslations.literal: since the Xiongnu grew weak, they have only now begun to take up the plow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: only since the Xiongnu threat faded have they begun to return to the fields.

manualTranslations.zh: 若即勞役，恐致妨損。
manualTranslations.literal: If they are immediately put to corvée labor, I fear harm and loss will follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If forced into corvée duty now, I fear further damage.

manualTranslations.zh: 以臣愚惑，請停招慰。
manualTranslations.literal: In this subject's foolish perplexity, I ask that the summoning and soothing be stopped.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In my humble judgment, I ask that these recruitment and relief efforts be halted.

manualTranslations.zh: 且謂之荒服者，故臣而不內。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover those called the distant-wild service are treated as subjects but not brought within.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The regions called the wild domain are acknowledged as subjects but not absorbed within.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以周室愛人攘狄，竟延七百之齡；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore the Zhou house loved its people and repelled the Di, and in the end extended its span seven hundred years;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhou cherished its people and kept the barbarians at bay, and endured seven hundred years;

manualTranslations.zh: 秦王輕戰事胡，四十載而遂絕。
manualTranslations.literal: the King of Qin lightly engaged in warfare against the Hu, and in forty years it was extinguished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the First Emperor treated war with the Hu lightly, and his dynasty perished within forty years.

manualTranslations.zh: 漢文養兵靜守，天下安豐；
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han nourished the troops and kept quiet guard; All Under Heaven was secure and abundant;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han preserved his armies and held the frontier in peace, and the realm prospered;

manualTranslations.zh: 孝武揚威遠略，海內虛耗。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han displayed his power in distant strategy; within the seas resources were depleted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu projected power far abroad, and the empire was drained.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖悔輪台，追已不及。
manualTranslations.literal: Though he repented at Luntai, pursuit was already too late.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though he repented at Luntai, it was too late to recover.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於隋室，早得伊吾，兼統鄯善，既得之後，勞費日甚，虛內致外，竟損無益。
manualTranslations.literal: As for the Sui house, it early gained Yiwu and also controlled Shanshan; after gaining them, labor and expense daily grew; emptying the interior to fill the exterior, in the end there was loss without benefit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, early possession of Yiwu and Shanshan brought ever-rising costs—hollowing the interior to sustain the frontier, with loss and no gain.

manualTranslations.zh: 遠尋秦、漢，近觀隋室，動靜安危，昭然備矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Searching far back to Qin and Han and looking near at the Sui house, success and failure, security and peril, are plainly complete.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Looking back to Qin and Han and forward to the Sui, the lessons of strength and ruin are clear enough.

manualTranslations.zh: 伊吾雖已臣附，遠在蕃磧，人非中夏，地多沙鹵。
manualTranslations.literal: Though Yiwu has already submitted as a subject, it is far in the barbarian desert; its people are not of China; its land has much sand and salt.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though Yiwu has submitted, it lies deep in the barbarian wastes. Its people are not Chinese, and its soil is mostly sand and salt.

manualTranslations.zh: 其自豎立稱籓附庸者，請羈縻受之，使居塞外，必畏威懷德，永為蕃臣，蓋行虛惠，而收實福矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who on their own erect titles and call themselves vassal subordinates—please accept them in loose attachment, let them dwell beyond the passes; they will surely fear authority and cherish virtue, forever remain barbarian subjects—this covers showing empty grace while reaping real blessing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who declare themselves vassals should be received under loose suzerainty and kept beyond the frontier. Once they fear our strength and honor our virtue, they will remain tributaries forever—a nominal kindness that yields real gain.

manualTranslations.zh: 近日突厥傾國入朝，既不能俘之江淮，以變其俗；
manualTranslations.literal: Recently the Turks came to court with the whole nation; since they could not be settled in the Jiang-Huai to change their customs;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Turks recently submitted en masse. Since we cannot resettle them in the Jiang-Huai to change their ways,

manualTranslations.zh: 置於內地，去京不遠，雖則寬仁之義，亦非久安之計也。
manualTranslations.literal: placing them in the interior, not far from the capital—though this is the meaning of leniency and benevolence—it is also not a plan for long security.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: keeping them in the interior near the capital, though generous in intent, is no plan for lasting peace.

manualTranslations.zh: 每見一人初降，賜物五匹、袍一領，酋帥悉授大官，祿厚位尊，理多縻費。
manualTranslations.literal: Every time one person newly submits, he is given five bolts of goods and one robe; chieftains are all granted great offices—salaries thick, positions honored—reasonably much tying-up expense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each new defector receives five bolts of cloth and a robe; chieftains are given high rank and generous stipends—all of it a heavy drain on resources.

manualTranslations.zh: 以中國之幣帛，供積惡之凶虜，其眾益多，非中國之利也。
manualTranslations.literal: Using China's silks and cloth to supply accumulated-evil fierce barbarians—their numbers daily increase; this is not to China's benefit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To spend the empire's wealth feeding long-hostile barbarians only swells their numbers—to China's detriment.

sourceRange.text: 欽寂弟欽明，少以軍功歷左玉鈐衛將軍、安西大都護，封鹽山郡公。萬歲通天元年，授金紫光祿大夫、涼州都督。欽明嘗出按部，突厥默啜率眾數萬奄至城下，欽明拒戰。久之，力屈被執。賊將欽明至靈州城下，令說城中早降，欽明大呼曰：「賊中都無飲食，城內有美醬，乞二升，粱米乞二斗，墨乞一梃。」是時，賊營處四面阻泥河，惟有一路得入，欽明乞此物以喻城中，冀其簡兵陳將，候夜掩襲，城中無悟其旨者，尋遇害。兄弟同年皆死王事，論者稱之。

context.beforeSource: 輔乾，開元中官至光祿卿。
context.afterSource: 紹次子智仁，初，以父勳授溫州刺史，封孝昌縣公。
context.beforeLocal: 輔乾，開元中官至光祿卿。
context.afterLocal: 紹次子智仁，初，以父勳授溫州刺史，封孝昌縣公。

manualTranslations.zh: 欽寂弟欽明，少以軍功歷左玉鈐衛將軍、安西大都護，封鹽山郡公。
manualTranslations.literal: Qinji's younger brother Qinming—from youth through military merit he rose through General of the Left Jade Bell Guard, Grand Protector of Anxi, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yanshan Commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qinji's younger brother Qinming, through military merit from youth, rose to general of the Left Jade Bell Guard, grand protector of Anxi, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yanshan commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 萬歲通天元年，授金紫光祿大夫、涼州都督。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of the Wansui Tongtian era, he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness bearing the Purple Bag and Area Commander of Liang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wansui Tongtian era, he was appointed grand master for splendid happiness bearing the purple bag and area commander of Liang.

manualTranslations.zh: 欽明嘗出按部，突厥默啜率眾數萬奄至城下，欽明拒戰。
manualTranslations.literal: Qinming once went out to inspect his district; the Turk Mochuo led tens of thousands of men in a sudden descent to the walls, and Qinming resisted in battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qinming once went out to inspect his district when the Turk Mochuo led tens of thousands of men in a sudden descent to the walls. Qinming resisted in battle.

manualTranslations.zh: 久之，力屈被執。
manualTranslations.literal: After a long while, his strength gave way and he was captured.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After a long while his strength gave way and he was captured.

manualTranslations.zh: 賊將欽明至靈州城下，令說城中早降，欽明大呼曰：「賊中都無飲食，城內有美醬，乞二升，粱米乞二斗，墨乞一梃。」
manualTranslations.literal: The rebels brought Qinming to Ling Prefecture below the walls and ordered him to urge the city to surrender early. Qinming cried out: "The bandits have no food or drink at all! Inside the city there is fine sauce—give me two sheng; millet—give me two dou; and one stick of ink!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rebels brought Qinming to Ling Prefecture below the walls and ordered him to urge the city to surrender early. Qinming cried out: "The bandits have no food or drink at all! Inside the city there is fine sauce—give me two sheng; millet—give me two dou; and one stick of ink!"

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，賊營處四面阻泥河，惟有一路得入，欽明乞此物以喻城中，冀其簡兵陳將，候夜掩襲，城中無悟其旨者，尋遇害。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the bandit camp was hemmed in on four sides by muddy streams; only one road allowed entry. Qinming begged for these items to signal the city, hoping they would choose troops and deploy generals for a night raid, but those in the city did not grasp his meaning, and he was soon killed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time the bandit camp was hemmed in on four sides by muddy streams, with only one road in. Qinming begged for these items to signal the city, hoping they would choose troops and deploy generals for a night raid, but those in the city did not grasp his meaning and he was soon killed.

manualTranslations.zh: 兄弟同年皆死王事，論者稱之。
manualTranslations.literal: The brothers died the same year in the ruler's service; commentators praised them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The brothers died the same year in the ruler's service, and commentators praised them.

sourceRange.text: 柔遠子皎，長安中，累遷尚衣奉御。時玄宗在籓，見而悅之。皎察玄宗有非常之度，尤委心焉。尋出為潤州長史。玄宗即位，召拜殿中少監。數召入臥內，命之舍敬，曲侍宴私，與后妃連榻，間以擊球鬥雞，常呼之為姜七而不名也。兼賜以宮女、名馬及諸珍物不可勝數。玄宗又嘗與皎在殿庭玩一嘉樹，皎稱其美，玄宗遽令徙植於其家，其寵遇如此。及竇懷貞等潛謀逆亂，玄宗將討之，皎協贊謀議，以功拜殿中監，封楚國公，實封四百戶。玄宗以皎在籓之舊，皎又有先見之明，欲宣佈其事，乃下敕曰：朕聞士之生代，始於事親，中於事君，終於立身，此其本也。

localRange.text: 朕聞士之生代，始於事親，中於事君，終於立身，此其本也。

context.beforeSource: 則天時，至左鷹揚衛將軍、通事舍人、內供奉。
context.afterSource: 若乃移孝成忠，策名委質。

manualTranslations.zh: 柔遠子皎，長安中，累遷尚衣奉御。
manualTranslations.literal: Ruyuan's son Jiao—in the Chang'an era, through successive promotions he reached Palace Attendant for Imperial Robes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ruyuan's son Jiao, during the Chang'an era, rose through successive promotions to palace attendant for imperial robes.

manualTranslations.zh: 時玄宗在籓，見而悅之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time, while Xuanzong was in his princely domain, he saw Jiao and was pleased with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time, while Xuanzong was in his princely domain, he saw Jiao and was pleased with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 皎察玄宗有非常之度，尤委心焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Jiao perceived that Xuanzong possessed an extraordinary capacity, and gave him his heart above all others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jiao perceived that Xuanzong possessed extraordinary capacity and gave him his heart above all others.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋出為潤州長史。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was sent out as chief administrator of Run Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as chief administrator of Run Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄宗即位，召拜殿中少監。
manualTranslations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Jiao was summoned and appointed deputy director of the Palace Directorate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Jiao was summoned and appointed deputy director of the palace directorate.

manualTranslations.zh: 數召入臥內，命之舍敬，曲侍宴私，與后妃連榻，間以擊球鬥雞，常呼之為姜七而不名也。
manualTranslations.literal: He was repeatedly summoned into the sleeping chamber; the emperor dispensed with formality, treating him privately at banquets, sharing couches with the empress and consorts, occasionally playing polo and cockfighting with him, and often called him "Jiang Seven" rather than by name.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly summoned into the sleeping chamber. The emperor dispensed with formality, treated him privately at banquets, shared couches with the empress and consorts, occasionally played polo and cockfighting with him, and often called him "Jiang Seven" rather than by name.

manualTranslations.zh: 兼賜以宮女、名馬及諸珍物不可勝數。
manualTranslations.literal: He was also granted palace women, famous horses, and countless precious objects.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was also granted palace women, famous horses, and countless precious objects.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄宗又嘗與皎在殿庭玩一嘉樹，皎稱其美，玄宗遽令徙植於其家，其寵遇如此。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuanzong once admired a fine tree with Jiao in the palace courtyard; when Jiao praised its beauty, Xuanzong immediately ordered it transplanted to Jiao's home—such was the favor shown him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xuanzong once admired a fine tree with Jiao in the palace courtyard. When Jiao praised its beauty, Xuanzong immediately ordered it transplanted to Jiao's home—such was the favor shown him.

manualTranslations.zh: 及竇懷貞等潛謀逆亂，玄宗將討之，皎協贊謀議，以功拜殿中監，封楚國公，實封四百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: When Dou Huaizhen and others secretly plotted rebellion and Xuanzong prepared to suppress them, Jiao joined in planning and deliberation; for his merit he was appointed director of the Palace Directorate, enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Chu, with a substantive fief of four hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Dou Huaizhen and others secretly plotted rebellion and Xuanzong prepared to suppress them, Jiao joined in the planning. For his merit he was appointed director of the palace directorate, enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Chu, with a substantive fief of four hundred households.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄宗以皎在籓之舊，皎又有先見之明，欲宣佈其事，乃下敕曰：
manualTranslations.literal: Because Jiao had been an old companion from the princely days and had also shown foresight, Xuanzong wished to proclaim these matters, and thereupon issued an edict saying:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because Jiao had been an old companion from the princely days and had also shown foresight, Xuanzong wished to proclaim these matters and thereupon issued an edict saying:

sourceRange.text: 天寶六載，授皎男慶初等官。七載，贈皎吏部尚書，仍贈實封二百戶以充享祀。慶初襲封楚國公。慶初生未晬，玄宗許尚公主，後淪落二十餘年。李林甫為相，當軸用事，林甫即皎之甥，從容奏之，故驟加恩命。天寶十載，詔慶初尚新平公主，授駙馬都尉。永泰元年，拜太常卿。

manualTranslations.zh: 天寶六載，授皎男慶初等官。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, Jiao's son Qingchu and others were granted offices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao, Jiao's son Qingchu and others were granted offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 七載，贈皎吏部尚書，仍贈實封二百戶以充享祀。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year, Jiao was posthumously given Minister of the Civil Service and a substantive fief of two hundred households for sacrificial provision.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Jiao was posthumously made minister of the civil service and given a substantive fief of two hundred households for sacrificial provision.

manualTranslations.zh: 慶初襲封楚國公。
manualTranslations.literal: Qingchu inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of the State of Chu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qingchu inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of the State of Chu.

manualTranslations.zh: 慶初生未晬，玄宗許尚公主，後淪落二十餘年。
manualTranslations.literal: Qingchu was not yet a year old when born; Xuanzong promised he would marry a princess, but afterward he lapsed into neglect for more than twenty years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qingchu was not yet a year old when born. Xuanzong promised he would marry a princess, but afterward he lapsed into neglect for more than twenty years.

manualTranslations.zh: 李林甫為相，當軸用事，林甫即皎之甥，從容奏之，故驟加恩命。
manualTranslations.literal: When Li Linfu became chief minister and held real power at court, Li Linfu—Jiao's nephew—spoke of the matter at leisure in memorial, and therefore sudden honors were conferred.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu became chief minister and held real power at court, Li Linfu—Jiao's nephew—spoke of the matter at leisure in memorial, and sudden honors were therefore conferred.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寶十載，詔慶初尚新平公主，授駙馬都尉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao, an edict ordered Qingchu to marry Princess Xinping and appointed him commandant of the imperial son-in-law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao, an edict ordered Qingchu to marry Princess Xinping and appointed him commandant of the imperial son-in-law.

manualTranslations.zh: 永泰元年，拜太常卿。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, he was appointed minister of ceremonies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, he was appointed minister of ceremonies.

sourceRange.text: 子神勣，嗣聖元年，為左金吾將軍，則天使於巴州，害章懷太子，既而歸罪於神勣，左遷疊州刺史。尋復入為左金吾衛大將軍，深見親委。嘗受詔鞫獄，與周興、來俊臣等俱號為酷吏。尋以罪伏誅。神龍初，禁錮其子孫。

manualTranslations.zh: 子神勣，嗣聖元年，為左金吾將軍，則天使於巴州，害章懷太子，既而歸罪於神勣，左遷疊州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Shenji—in the first year of the Sisheng era, served as general of the Left Gold Crow Guard. When Zetian sent someone to Bazhou to kill Crown Prince Zhanghuai, blame was afterward placed on Shenji, and he was demoted to prefect of Die Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Shenji, in the first year of the Sisheng era, served as general of the Left Gold Crow Guard. When Zetian sent someone to Bazhou to kill Crown Prince Zhanghuai, blame was afterward placed on Shenji, and he was demoted to prefect of Die Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋復入為左金吾衛大將軍，深見親委。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he returned to court as grand general of the Left Gold Crow Guard and was deeply trusted and entrusted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to court as grand general of the Left Gold Crow Guard and was deeply trusted and entrusted.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘗受詔鞫獄，與周興、來俊臣等俱號為酷吏。
manualTranslations.literal: He once received edict to interrogate prisoners, and together with Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others was called a cruel official.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He once received edict to interrogate prisoners, and together with Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others was called a cruel official.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋以罪伏誅。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was executed for his crimes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon he was executed for his crimes.

manualTranslations.zh: 神龍初，禁錮其子孫。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, his descendants were placed under restriction.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, his descendants were placed under restriction.

sourceRange.text: 襄武王琛，高祖從父兄子也。祖蔚，周朔州總管。父安，隋領軍大將軍。武德初，追封蔚為蔡王，安為西平王。琛，義寧中封襄武郡公，與太常卿鄭元璹齎女妓遺突厥始畢可汗，以結和親。始畢甚重之，贈名馬數百匹，遣骨咄祿特勒隨琛貢方物。高祖大悅，拜刑部侍郎，進爵為王。歷蒲、絳二州總管。及宋金剛陷澮州，時稽胡多叛，轉琛為隰州總管以鎮之。馭眾寬簡，夷夏安之。三年，薨。子儉嗣，後隨例降爵為公。

context.beforeSource: 士及慮其為變，遂縊殺之。
context.afterSource: 河間王孝恭，琛之弟也。
context.beforeLocal: 士及慮其為變，遂縊殺之。

manualTranslations.zh: 襄武王琛，高祖從父兄子也。
manualTranslations.literal: Prince of Xiangwu Chen was a son of Emperor Gaozu's paternal cousin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangwu Chen was a son of Emperor Gaozu's paternal cousin.

manualTranslations.zh: 祖蔚，周朔州總管。
manualTranslations.literal: His grandfather Wei was area commander of Shuo prefecture under Zhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wei had been area commander of Shuo prefecture under the Northern Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 父安，隋領軍大將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: His father An was General-in-Chief of the Palace Guard under Sui.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father An had been General-in-Chief of the Palace Guard under the Sui.

manualTranslations.zh: 武德初，追封蔚為蔡王，安為西平王。
manualTranslations.literal: Early in Wude, Wei was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai and An as Prince of Xiping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in Wude, Wei was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai and An as Prince of Xiping.

manualTranslations.zh: 琛，義寧中封襄武郡公，與太常卿鄭元璹齎女妓遺突厥始畢可汗，以結和親。
manualTranslations.literal: Chen, during Yining, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangwu commandery; together with Director of Ceremonial Zheng Yuanshang he brought female entertainers as gifts to the Türk khagan Shibi to forge a marriage alliance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Yining era Chen was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangwu commandery. Together with Director of Ceremonial Zheng Yuanshang he brought female entertainers as gifts to the Türk khagan Shibi to cement a marriage alliance.

manualTranslations.zh: 始畢甚重之，贈名馬數百匹，遣骨咄祿特勒隨琛貢方物。
manualTranslations.literal: Shibi held them in great esteem, bestowed several hundred famous horses, and sent the Türk noble Kutlug Tegin to follow Chen in presenting tribute goods.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shibi received them with great honor, bestowed several hundred fine horses, and sent the Türk noble Kutlug Tegin to accompany Chen in presenting tribute.

manualTranslations.zh: 高祖大悅，拜刑部侍郎，進爵為王。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased, appointed him Vice Minister of Justice, and advanced his rank to prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased. He appointed Chen Vice Minister of Justice and promoted him to princely rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 歷蒲、絳二州總管。
manualTranslations.literal: He served in turn as area commander of Pu and Jiang prefectures.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served in turn as area commander of Pu and Jiang prefectures.

manualTranslations.zh: 及宋金剛陷澮州，時稽胡多叛，轉琛為隰州總管以鎮之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Song Jingang took Fen prefecture, and many Jié-Xiongnu peoples were rebelling at the time, Chen was transferred to area commander of Xi prefecture to pacify the region.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Song Jingang seized Fen prefecture and many Jié-Xiongnu groups were in revolt, Chen was transferred to area commander of Xi prefecture to pacify the region.

manualTranslations.zh: 馭眾寬簡，夷夏安之。
manualTranslations.literal: He governed his troops with leniency and simplicity; both barbarians and Chinese lived in peace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and restraint, and both barbarians and Chinese lived in peace under his rule.

manualTranslations.zh: 三年，薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in 620.

manualTranslations.zh: 子儉嗣，後隨例降爵為公。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Jian succeeded; later by precedent his title was reduced to marquis.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Jian succeeded him. Later, by precedent, his title was reduced to marquis.

sourceRange.text: ○永安王孝基淮安王神通子道彥孝察孝同孝慈孝友孝節孝義孝逸襄邑王神符子德懋文暕長平王叔良子孝協孝斌孝斌子思訓思誨叔良弟德良幼良襄武王琛河間王孝恭子晦孝恭弟瑊瑰廬江王瑗王君廓附淮陽王道玄江夏王道宗隴西王博乂永安王孝基，高祖從父弟也。父璋，周梁州刺史，與趙王祐謀殺隋文帝，事洩被誅，高祖即位，追封畢王。孝基，武德元年封永安王，歷陝州總管、鴻臚卿，以罪免。二年，劉武周將宋金剛來寇汾、澮。夏縣人呂崇茂殺縣令，舉兵反，自稱魏王，請援於武周。復以孝基為行軍總管討之，工部尚書獨孤懷恩、內史侍郎唐儉、陝州總管於筠悉隸焉。武周遣其將尉遲敬德潛援崇茂，大戰於夏縣，王師敗績，孝基與唐儉等皆沒於賊。後謀歸國，為武周所害，高祖為之發哀，廢朝三日，賜其家帛千匹。賊平，購其屍不得，招魂而葬之，贈左衛大將軍，謚曰壯。無子，以從兄韶子道立為嗣，封高平郡王。九年，降為縣公。永徽初，卒於陳州刺史。

sourceRange.text: 長平王叔良，高祖從父弟也。父禕，隋上儀同三司，武德初，追封郇王。叔良，義寧中授左光祿大夫，封長平郡公。武德元年，拜刑部侍郎，進爵為王。師鎮涇州，以御薛舉。舉乃陽言食盡，引兵南去，遣高墌人偽以降。叔良遣驃騎劉感率眾赴之，至百里細川，伏兵發，官軍敗績，劉感沒於陣。叔良大懼，出金以賜士卒。嚴為守備，涇州僅全。四年，突厥入寇，命叔良率五軍擊之。叔良中流矢而薨，贈左翊衛大將軍、靈州總管，謚曰肅。

context.beforeSource: 文暕子佺，開元中為宗正卿。
context.afterSource: 子孝協嗣，武德五年，封范陽郡王。
context.beforeLocal: 文暕子佺，開元中為宗正卿。

manualTranslations.zh: 長平王叔良，高祖從父弟也。
manualTranslations.literal: Prince of Changping Shuliang was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prince of Changping Shuliang was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.

manualTranslations.zh: 父禕，隋上儀同三司，武德初，追封郇王。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Yi held the Sui rank of Senior Master of Ceremony of the Third Rank; early in Wude he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Yi had held the Sui rank of Senior Master of Ceremony of the Third Rank. Early in Wude he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.

manualTranslations.zh: 叔良，義寧中授左光祿大夫，封長平郡公。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuliang, during Yining, was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Yining era Shuliang was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping commandery.

manualTranslations.zh: 武德元年，拜刑部侍郎，進爵為王。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Wude, he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and advanced in rank to prince.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 618 he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and promoted to princely rank.

manualTranslations.zh: 師鎮涇州，以御薛舉。
manualTranslations.literal: He led troops garrisoning Jing prefecture to guard against Xue Ju.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He took command at Jing prefecture to guard against Xue Ju.

manualTranslations.zh: 舉乃陽言食盡，引兵南去，遣高墌人偽以降。
manualTranslations.literal: Ju then falsely claimed his provisions were exhausted, led his troops southward, and sent a man from Gaodi to feign surrender.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ju then falsely claimed his provisions were exhausted, withdrew south, and sent a man from Gaodi to offer a fake surrender.

manualTranslations.zh: 叔良遣驃騎劉感率眾赴之，至百里細川，伏兵發，官軍敗績，劉感沒於陣。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuliang sent swift-cavalry commander Liu Gan to lead troops to meet them; when they reached Baili Xichuan, ambush troops sprang up, the imperial army suffered defeat, and Liu Gan perished in battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuliang sent swift-cavalry commander Liu Gan to meet them. At Baili Xichuan an ambush sprang up, the imperial army was routed, and Liu Gan fell in battle.

manualTranslations.zh: 叔良大懼，出金以賜士卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuliang was greatly frightened and distributed gold to reward the soldiers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuliang was terrified and distributed gold to reward his soldiers.

manualTranslations.zh: 嚴為守備，涇州僅全。
manualTranslations.literal: He tightened defenses; Jing prefecture barely survived intact.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He tightened the defenses, and Jing prefecture barely held.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年，突厥入寇，命叔良率五軍擊之。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year, when the Türks raided, Shuliang was ordered to lead five armies to attack them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 621, when the Türks raided, Shuliang was ordered to lead five armies against them.

manualTranslations.zh: 叔良中流矢而薨，贈左翊衛大將軍、靈州總管，謚曰肅。
manualTranslations.literal: Shuliang was struck by a stray arrow and died; posthumously appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard and area commander of Ling prefecture, posthumous title Su.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shuliang was struck by a stray arrow and died. He was posthumously appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard and area commander of Ling prefecture, with the posthumous title Su, Solemn.

sourceRange.text: 孝恭次子晦，乾封中，累除營州都督，以善政聞；璽書勞問，賜物三百段。轉右金吾將軍，兼檢校雍州長史，糾發奸豪，無所容貸，為人吏畏服。晦私第有樓，下臨酒肆，其人嘗候晦言曰：「微賤之人，雖則禮所不及，然家有長幼，不欲外人窺之。家迫明公之樓，出入非便，請從此辭。」晦即日毀其樓。高宗將幸洛陽，令在京居守，顧謂之曰：「關中之事，一以付卿。但令式跼人，不可以成官政，令式之外，有利於人者，隨事即行，不須聞奏。」晦累有異績。則天臨朝，遷戶部尚書。垂拱初，拜右金吾衛大將軍，轉秋官尚書。永昌元年卒，贈幽州都督。子榮，為酷吏所殺。

context.afterSource: 孝恭弟瑊，武德中，為尚書右丞，封濟北郡王，卒於始州刺史。

manualTranslations.zh: 孝恭次子晦，乾封中，累除營州都督，以善政聞；
manualTranslations.literal: Xiaogong's second son Hui, during Qianfeng, rose through successive removals to commissioner of Ying prefecture, known for good governance;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiaogong's second son Hui, during the Qianfeng era, rose through successive appointments to commissioner of Ying prefecture, where his good governance became known;

manualTranslations.zh: 璽書勞問，賜物三百段。
manualTranslations.literal: an imperial writ commended and inquired after him, granting three hundred bolts of goods.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a commendatory decree and three hundred bolts of goods.

manualTranslations.zh: 轉右金吾將軍，兼檢校雍州長史，糾發奸豪，無所容貸，為人吏畏服。
manualTranslations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Golden Guard, concurrently acting chief administrator of Yong prefecture; he exposed and prosecuted powerful wrongdoers without leniency, and officials and commoners alike feared and submitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Right Golden Guard and concurrently made acting chief administrator of Yong prefecture. He prosecuted powerful wrongdoers without mercy, and officials and commoners alike feared and respected him.

manualTranslations.zh: 晦私第有樓，下臨酒肆，其人嘗候晦言曰：「微賤之人，雖則禮所不及，然家有長幼，不欲外人窺之。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui's private residence had a tower overlooking a wineshop; the man once waited on Hui and said: "A man humble and low, though etiquette may not reach him, yet has elders and juniors in the family and does not wish outsiders to peep in.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui's residence had a tower that looked down on a wineshop. The proprietor once came to him and said, "I am a humble man, scarcely worth your notice, but my household has elders and children, and we do not want strangers peering in on us.

manualTranslations.zh: 家迫明公之樓，出入非便，請從此辭。」
manualTranslations.literal: My home presses against your lordship's tower — coming and going is inconvenient; I ask to take my leave from here."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your tower looms over my shop and makes coming and going difficult. I must ask to move elsewhere.

manualTranslations.zh: 晦即日毀其樓。
manualTranslations.literal: That same day Hui had the tower demolished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui had the tower torn down that very day.

manualTranslations.zh: 高宗將幸洛陽，令在京居守，顧謂之曰：「關中之事，一以付卿。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was about to visit Luoyang, he left Hui to guard the capital and turned to tell him: "Matters of Guanzhong — I entrust them entirely to you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong prepared to travel to Luoyang, he left Hui in charge of the capital. "I entrust all affairs of Guanzhong to you," he told him.

manualTranslations.zh: 但令式跼人，不可以成官政，令式之外，有利於人者，隨事即行，不須聞奏。」
manualTranslations.literal: Regulations alone constrain men and cannot by themselves make good government; beyond the regulations, wherever something benefits the people, carry it out as the occasion requires — no need to report for approval."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Statutes alone cannot make good government. Wherever something outside the statutes would benefit the people, do it at once—no need to seek approval.

manualTranslations.zh: 晦累有異績。
manualTranslations.literal: Hui repeatedly achieved outstanding results.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hui distinguished himself again and again.

manualTranslations.zh: 則天臨朝，遷戶部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: When Empress Wu held court, he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed power, he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

manualTranslations.zh: 垂拱初，拜右金吾衛大將軍，轉秋官尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Early in Chuigong he was appointed General of the Right Golden Guard Regiment, then transferred to Minister of Justice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in the Chuigong era he became General of the Right Golden Guard Regiment, then Minister of Justice.

manualTranslations.zh: 永昌元年卒，贈幽州都督。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang he died; posthumously appointed commissioner of You prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in 689 and was posthumously appointed commissioner of You prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 子榮，為酷吏所殺。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Rong was killed by harsh investigators.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Rong was executed by the era's notorious harsh investigators.
