manualTranslations.zh: 時有司表稅關市，融深以為不可，上疏諫曰：伏見有司稅關市事條，不限工商，但是行人盡稅者，臣謹按《周禮》九賦，其七日“關市之賦”。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the relevant offices memorialized to tax market passes, and Cui Rong deeply considered this inadvisable; he submitted a remonstrance, saying: I humbly see the regulations of the relevant offices on taxing market passes—they do not restrict [the tax] to artisans and merchants, but tax all who pass through; I respectfully note that among the Nine Levies in the Rites of Zhou, the seventh is "the levy on markets and passes."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time the relevant offices memorialized to levy taxes on market passes. Cui Rong strongly opposed this and submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: I humbly observe that under the regulations proposed by the relevant offices for taxing market passes, there is no restriction to artisans and merchants—all travelers would be taxed. I respectfully note that among the Nine Levies in the Rites of Zhou, the seventh is "the levy on markets and passes."

manualTranslations.zh: 竊惟市縱繁巧，關通末遊，欲令此徒止抑，所以鹹增賦稅。
manualTranslations.literal: I secretly consider that markets abound with cunning crafts and passes connect secondary pursuits—wishing to make these people cease and be restrained, therefore broadly increase levies and taxes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I gather the intent is that markets teem with cunning crafts and passes channel secondary pursuits—the hope is to restrain such people, and therefore levies are to be increased broadly.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹商度今古，料量家國，竊將為不可稅。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully weighs past and present, estimates state and household, and privately considers [this] cannot be taxed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have carefully weighed past and present and reckoned the interests of state and household, and I believe it cannot be taxed.

manualTranslations.zh: 謹件事跡如左，伏惟聖旨擇焉。
manualTranslations.literal: I respectfully set forth the facts as follows; I humbly hope Your Sagely Intent will choose among them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully set forth the facts below and humbly ask that Your Majesty's judgment decide among them.

manualTranslations.zh: 往古之時，淳樸未散，公田籍而不稅，關防譏而不征。
manualTranslations.literal: In ancient times, simplicity and purity had not yet dispersed—public fields were registered but not taxed; passes and barriers checked but did not levy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when society was still unsophisticated, public fields were registered but not taxed, and passes and barriers inspected travelers but imposed no levies.

manualTranslations.zh: 中代已來，澆風驟進，桑麻疲弊，稼穡辛勤，於是各徇通財，爭趨作巧，求徑捷之欲速，忘歲計之無餘。
manualTranslations.literal: From the middle ages onward, dissolute customs advanced swiftly; mulberry and hemp wore out, fieldwork grew laborious—thereupon each pursued circulating wealth, vied to pursue craftsmanship, seeking short cuts for speed, forgetting yearly reckoning left no surplus.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the middle ages onward, decadent customs spread rapidly. Mulberry and hemp production declined, farming grew ever more arduous, and people pursued circulating wealth, competed in craftsmanship, chased quick gains by shortcuts, and forgot that annual reckoning left nothing in reserve.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂使田萊日荒，倉廩不積，蠶織休廢。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon fields daily grew waste, granaries did not accumulate, sericulture and weaving ceased and were abandoned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The result was that fields fell daily into neglect, granaries went unfilled, and sericulture and weaving were abandoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 弊縕闕如，饑寒猥臻，亂離斯起。
manualTranslations.literal: Worn-out cotton garments were wanting; hunger and cold together arrived; disorder and dispersion arose thereby.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Clothing fell into shortage, hunger and cold came in their wake, and disorder and upheaval arose.

manualTranslations.zh: 先王懲其若此，所以變古隨時，依本者恒科，占末者增稅。
manualTranslations.literal: Former kings took warning from this—that is why they changed ancient ways according to the times: those based on fundamentals received fixed dues; those occupying secondary pursuits received increased taxes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Former kings took warning from this, which is why they adapted ancient ways to changing times: those engaged in basic occupations paid regular dues, while those in secondary pursuits faced added taxes.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫關市之稅者，謂市及國門，關門者也，唯斂出入之商賈，不稅來往之行人。
manualTranslations.literal: As for the tax on passes and markets, it refers to markets and the national gate—the gate of the pass—[it] only collects from merchants entering and leaving, not taxing travelers coming and going.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The tax on passes and markets applied to markets and to the national gate—the gate of a pass—and only collected from merchants entering and leaving, not from ordinary travelers passing through.

manualTranslations.zh: 今若不論商人，通取諸色，事不師古，法乃任情。
manualTranslations.literal: Now if merchants are not distinguished and all categories are universally taken, the matter does not take antiquity as teacher; the law is merely arbitrary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If today merchants are not distinguished and every category is taxed alike, the policy does not follow the ancients and the law becomes arbitrary.

manualTranslations.zh: 悠悠末代，於何瞻仰；
manualTranslations.literal: In this far-off degenerate age, toward what shall one look up?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In this distant degenerate age, to what can one look for guidance?

manualTranslations.zh: 濟濟盛朝，自取嗤笑。
manualTranslations.literal: In this flourishing court, full and splendid, [we] bring ridicule upon ourselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In this flourishing court, we invite ridicule upon ourselves.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖欲憲章姬典，乃是違背《周官》。
manualTranslations.literal: Although one wishes to take as model the Ji [Zhou] canon, this is in fact to violate the Rites of Zhou officials.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if one wishes to take the Zhou canon as model, this in fact violates the Rites of Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣知其不可者一也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject knows one reason why it is inadvisable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I know one reason why this will not work.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹案《易》《係辭》稱：“庖羲氏沒，神農氏作，日中為市，致天下之人，聚天下之貨，交易而退，各得其所。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes that the "Attached Words" of the Changes states: "When Fuxi passed away, Shennong arose; he made markets at midday, bringing together the people under Heaven, gathering the goods under Heaven; they traded and departed, each obtaining what suited him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that the Attached Words of the Book of Changes states: "When Fuxi passed away, Shennong arose. He established markets at midday, gathering people from across the realm and assembling goods from across the realm. They traded and withdrew, each obtaining what he needed.

manualTranslations.zh: ”《班志》亦云：“財者，帝王聚人守位，養成群生，奉順天德，理國安人之本也。
manualTranslations.literal: " Ban's Treatise also says: "Wealth is the foundation by which emperors and kings gather people, secure their positions, nourish the multitudes, accord with Heaven's virtue, and order the state and settle the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Ban Gu's Treatise also says: "Wealth is the foundation by which emperors and kings gather people, secure their positions, nourish the multitudes, accord with Heaven's virtue, and govern the realm and settle the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 仕農工商，四人有業。
manualTranslations.literal: Officials, farmers, artisans, and merchants—the four kinds of people each have their occupation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Officials, farmers, artisans, and merchants—the four classes each have their calling.

manualTranslations.zh: 學以居位曰仕，辟士殖穀曰農，作巧成器曰工，通財鬻貨曰商。
manualTranslations.literal: Learning in order to hold office is called "officialdom"; opening soil and planting grain is called "agriculture"; making cunning and completing vessels is called "craftsmanship"; circulating wealth and selling goods is called "commerce."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Learning in order to hold office is called "officialdom"; opening land and growing grain is "agriculture"; applying skill to fashion tools is "craftsmanship"; circulating wealth and selling goods is "commerce."

manualTranslations.zh: 聖王量能授事，四人陳力受職。
manualTranslations.literal: Sagely kings measured ability and assigned tasks; the four kinds of people displayed their strength and received office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sage kings assigned duties according to capacity, and the four classes each applied their strength and received their roles.

manualTranslations.zh: ”然則四人各業久矣。
manualTranslations.literal: " Thus the four kinds of people have each had their occupations for long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Thus the four classes have long had their distinct occupations.

manualTranslations.zh: 今復安得動而搖之！
manualTranslations.literal: How can one now again move and shake them!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How can we now move to shake them up!

manualTranslations.zh: 蕭何云：“人情一定，不可復動。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao He said: "Once human sentiment is settled, it cannot be moved again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiao He said: "Once custom is settled, it must not be disturbed again.

manualTranslations.zh: ”班固又云：曹參相齊，齊國安集，大稱賢相。
manualTranslations.literal: " Ban Gu also said: Cao Can served as chancellor of Qi; Qi was settled and tranquil, and he was greatly praised as a worthy chancellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Ban Gu also wrote: When Cao Can served as chancellor of Qi, Qi was settled and tranquil, and he was widely praised as a worthy chancellor.

manualTranslations.zh: 參去，屬其後相曰：“以齊獄市為寄，慎勿擾也。
manualTranslations.literal: When Can departed, he entrusted to his successor, saying: "Take the prisons and markets of Qi as your charge—be careful not to disturb them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Cao Can left office, he told his successor: "Regard the prisons and markets of Qi as your trust—be careful not to disturb them.

manualTranslations.zh: ”後相曰：“理無大於此者乎？
manualTranslations.literal: " The successor said: "Is there no principle greater than this?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " The successor asked: "Is there any principle more important than this?

manualTranslations.zh: ”參曰：“不然。
manualTranslations.literal: " Can said: "That is not so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Cao Can replied: "Not at all.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫獄市者，所以並容也，今若擾之，奸人安所容乎？
manualTranslations.literal: As for prisons and markets, they serve to accommodate all alike; if one now disturbs them, where will wicked men find accommodation?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prisons and markets serve to accommodate all alike; if you disturb them, where will wrongdoers find refuge?

manualTranslations.zh: 吾是以先之。
manualTranslations.literal: I therefore placed priority on this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is why I prioritized this.

manualTranslations.zh: ”夫獄市，兼受善惡。
manualTranslations.literal: " As for prisons and markets, they jointly receive good and evil alike.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Prisons and markets accommodate both the good and the wicked.

manualTranslations.zh: 若窮極，奸人無所容竄；
manualTranslations.literal: If driven to extremity, wicked men have nowhere to hide and flee;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If driven to extremity, the wicked have nowhere to hide;

manualTranslations.zh: 奸人無所容竄，久且為亂。
manualTranslations.literal: when wicked men have nowhere to hide and flee, before long there will be disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when the wicked have nowhere to hide, disorder is not long in coming.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦人極刑而天下叛，孝武峻法而刑獄繁，此其效也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Qin people used extreme punishments and the realm rebelled; Emperor Wu of Han used severe laws and prisons multiplied—such was their effect.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Qin used extreme punishments and the realm rebelled; Emperor Wu of Han used severe laws and prisons multiplied—such were the results.

manualTranslations.zh: 老子曰：“我無為而人自化，我好靜而人自正。
manualTranslations.literal: Laozi said: "If I do nothing, people transform themselves; if I love stillness, people right themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Laozi said: "When I do nothing, people transform themselves of their own accord; when I cherish stillness, people right themselves of their own accord.

manualTranslations.zh: ”參欲以道化其本，不欲擾其末。
manualTranslations.literal: " Can wished to transform the root by the Way, not to disturb the branch-tips.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Cao Can wished to transform the root through the Way, not to disturb the branches.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣知其不可者二也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject knows the second reason why it is inadvisable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I know a second reason why this will not work.

manualTranslations.zh: 四海之廣，九州之雜。
manualTranslations.literal: The Four Seas are vast; the Nine Provinces are diverse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The realm is vast and the provinces many and diverse.

manualTranslations.zh: 關必據險路，市必憑要津。
manualTranslations.literal: Passes necessarily occupy perilous routes; markets necessarily rely on strategic fords.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Passes necessarily stand on perilous routes; markets necessarily cluster at strategic crossings.

manualTranslations.zh: 若乃富商大賈，豪宗惡少，輕死重義，結黨連群，喑鳴則彎弓，睚眥則挺劍。
manualTranslations.literal: Such being the case, great merchants and wealthy traders, powerful clans and wicked youths, who lightly esteem death and heavily esteem righteousness, form factions and join groups—at a low cry they bend the bow, at the least grievance they draw the sword.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Consider the great merchants and wealthy traders, powerful clans and reckless youths, who hold loyalty dearer than life, form factions and bands, bend their bows at the slightest signal, and draw their swords at the slightest offense.

manualTranslations.zh: 小有失意，且猶如此，一旦變法，定是相驚。
manualTranslations.literal: Slightly displeased, they are already like this; once the law is changed, they are bound to alarm one another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even when only slightly wronged they behave this way; once the law is changed, alarm is certain.

manualTranslations.zh: 乘茲困窮，或致騷動，便恐南走越，北走胡，非唯流逆齊人，亦自攪亂殊俗。
manualTranslations.literal: Seizing this moment of hardship, they may give rise to unrest—for fear that some flee south to Yue, north to the Hu; not only would the people of Qi become rebellious refugees, they would also themselves stir up alien customs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seizing the opportunity of their hardship, unrest may erupt. People may flee south to Yue or north to the northern tribes—not only would common folk turn rebellious, but alien border peoples would also be thrown into disorder.

manualTranslations.zh: 又如邊徼之地，寇賊為鄰，興胡之旅，歲月相繼，倘同科賦，致有猜疑，一從散亡，何以製禁？
manualTranslations.literal: Again, on the border marches, bandits and foes are neighbors; travelers raising the Hu come year after year in succession—if subject to the same categories of levies, suspicion will arise; once they scatter and flee, how can one restrain and forbid?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: And on the frontier marches, where bandits are neighbors and Hu travelers pass year after year, if they face the same taxes, suspicion will arise; once they scatter, how can they be controlled?

manualTranslations.zh: 求利雖切，為害方深。
manualTranslations.literal: Though the quest for profit is keen, the harm is just then deep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though the pursuit of profit is urgent, the harm will be far deeper.

manualTranslations.zh: 而有司上言，不識大體，徒欲益帑藏，助軍國，殊不知軍國益擾，帑藏逾空。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet the relevant offices submit their words, not recognizing the larger pattern—merely wishing to enrich the vaults and support army and state, yet not knowing that army and state will grow ever more troubled and the vaults ever emptier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet the relevant offices submit this proposal without grasping the larger picture. They merely wish to fill the treasury and support the army and state, not realizing that the army and state will grow more troubled and the treasury ever emptier.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣知其不可者三也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject knows the third reason why it is inadvisable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I know a third reason why this will not work.

manualTranslations.zh: 孟軻又云：“古之為關也，將以禦暴；
manualTranslations.literal: Mencius also said: "In antiquity, passes were made to ward off violence;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mencius also said: "In antiquity, passes were established to keep out violence;

manualTranslations.zh: 今之為關也，將以為暴。
manualTranslations.literal: today passes are made to become violence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: today passes are used to commit violence.

manualTranslations.zh: ”今行者皆稅，本末同流。
manualTranslations.literal: " Now all travelers are taxed—the root and branch flow in one stream.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Now all travelers are taxed, so fundamental and secondary pursuits are treated alike.

manualTranslations.zh: 且如天下諸津，舟航所聚，旁通巴、漢，前指閩、越，七澤十藪，三江五湖，控引河洛，兼包淮海。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, like all the fords under Heaven where boats gather—connecting sideways with Ba and Han, pointing forward to Min and Yue, the seven marshes and ten marshlands, the Three Rivers and Five Lakes, drawing in the Yellow River and Luo, encompassing both Huai and Hai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Consider all the river crossings under Heaven where boats congregate: they connect to Ba and Han in the west and reach Min and Yue in the southeast, threading through the seven marshes and ten marshlands, the Three Rivers and Five Lakes, drawing on the Yellow River and Luo, and spanning the Huai and Hai regions.

manualTranslations.zh: 弘舸巨艦，千軸萬艘，交貿往還，昧旦永日。
manualTranslations.literal: Great vessels and huge ships, thousands of axles and tens of thousands of craft, commerce going and coming—from daybreak until day's end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Great vessels and huge ships—thousands upon tens of thousands of craft—trade back and forth from dawn until nightfall.

manualTranslations.zh: 今若江津河口，置鋪納稅，納稅則檢覆，檢覆則遲留。
manualTranslations.literal: If now at river crossings and estuaries tax stations are set up to collect taxes, collecting taxes then requires inspection and verification, and inspection and verification then causes delay and detention.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If tax stations are placed at river crossings and estuaries, collecting taxes requires inspection, and inspection causes delay.

manualTranslations.zh: 此津才過，彼鋪復止，非唯國家稅錢，更遭主司僦賂。
manualTranslations.literal: Having just passed this ford, one is stopped again at that station—not only does the state take tax money; one further suffers extortion and bribes from the officials in charge.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: No sooner has a vessel cleared one crossing than it is halted at the next station. Merchants pay not only state taxes but also bribes extorted by officials.

manualTranslations.zh: 船有大小，載有少多，量物而稅，觸途淹久。
manualTranslations.literal: Boats have large and small; loads have more and less; measuring goods to tax them—everywhere one touches the road, delays are long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Boats vary in size and cargoes in quantity; taxing goods by measurement means delays at every stop.

manualTranslations.zh: 統論一日之中，未過十分之一，因此壅滯，必致籲嗟。
manualTranslations.literal: Generally speaking, in the course of a day not even one-tenth is passed; because of this obstruction and stagnation, sighs and complaints must result.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On average, in a full day a vessel may not cover even one-tenth of its route. Such congestion inevitably provokes widespread complaint.

manualTranslations.zh: 一朝失利，則萬商廢業，萬商廢業，則人不聊生。
manualTranslations.literal: Once in the morning profit is lost, then ten thousand merchants abandon their occupations; ten thousand merchants abandon their occupations, then people cannot preserve their livelihoods.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once profits are lost, myriad merchants abandon their trades—and when myriad merchants abandon their trades, people cannot make a living.

manualTranslations.zh: 其間或有輕訬任俠之徒，斬龍刺蛟之黨，鄱陽暴謔之客，富平悍壯之夫，居則藏鏹，出便竦劍。
manualTranslations.literal: Among them there may be lightly scornful, chivalrous gallants, dragon-slaying and flood-dragon stabbing partisans, Poyang's brutal revelers, Fuping's fierce stalwarts—at home they hoard money; abroad they brandish swords.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among them are reckless gallants and swashbucklers, dragon-slaying adventurers, brawlers from Poyang, fierce men from Fuping—who hoard silver at home and draw swords abroad.

manualTranslations.zh: 加之以重稅，因之以威脅，一旦獸窮則搏，鳥窮則攫，執事者復何以安之哉？
manualTranslations.literal: Add to them heavy taxes, follow with intimidation—once beasts are cornered they strike, birds cornered they seize; how again can those in charge find peace?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Add heavy taxes and follow with intimidation, and when beasts are cornered they fight and birds cornered they strike. How, then, can officials retain their peace?

manualTranslations.zh: 臣知其不可者四也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject knows the fourth reason why it is inadvisable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I know a fourth reason why this will not work.

manualTranslations.zh: 五帝之初，不可詳已；
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of the Five Emperors, it cannot be examined in detail;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The beginnings of the Five Emperors cannot be examined in detail;

manualTranslations.zh: 三王之後，厥有著雲；
manualTranslations.literal: after the Three Kings, there are clear records;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: after the Three Sage Kings, clear records exist;

manualTranslations.zh: 秦、漢相承，典章大備至如關市之稅，史籍有文。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin and Han succeeded each other; canons and regulations were greatly complete—as for the tax on passes and markets, the historical records contain entries.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Through Qin and Han succession, institutions were fully established, and records of the tax on passes and markets exist in the historical texts.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦政以雄圖武力，舍之而不用也；
manualTranslations.literal: Qin rule, with heroic designs and martial force, set it aside and did not use it;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin, with his grand ambitions and military power, set it aside and did not employ it;

manualTranslations.zh: 漢武以霸略英才，去之而勿取也。
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, with hegemonic strategy and outstanding talent, removed it and did not take it up.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han, with his hegemonic strategy and outstanding talent, abolished it and would not restore it.

manualTranslations.zh: 何則？
manualTranslations.literal: Why?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why?

manualTranslations.zh: 關為禦暴之所，市為聚人之地，稅市則人散，稅關則暴興，暴興則起異圖，人散則懷不軌。
manualTranslations.literal: Passes are places for warding off violence; markets are places for gathering people. Tax markets and people scatter; tax passes and violence arises—violence arises and alien designs are stirred; people scatter and they harbor rebellious intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Passes were meant to keep out violence; markets were meant to gather people. Tax markets and people disperse; tax passes and violence rises. When violence rises, rebellious designs emerge; when people disperse, subversive intent takes hold.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫人心莫不背善而樂禍，易動而難安。
manualTranslations.literal: Now human hearts all turn away from good and delight in calamity—they are easy to move but hard to settle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Human hearts naturally turn from good and delight in calamity; they are easily stirred but hard to pacify.

manualTranslations.zh: 一市不安，則天下之市心搖矣；
manualTranslations.literal: One market unsettled, then the hearts of markets under Heaven are shaken;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one market is unsettled, the confidence of markets throughout the realm is shaken;

manualTranslations.zh: 一關不安，則天下之關心動矣。
manualTranslations.literal: one pass unsettled, then the hearts of passes under Heaven are moved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if one pass is unsettled, anxiety spreads through every pass in the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 況澆風久扇，變法為難，徒欲禁末流、規小利，豈知失玄默、亂大倫。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, dissolute customs have long been fanned; changing laws is difficult—merely wishing to restrain branch streams and scheme for small profit, how could one know one loses dark silence and disrupts the great order?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, decadent customs have long prevailed and changing laws is difficult. Merely seeking to restrain secondary pursuits for small gain, one fails to see that this forfeits tranquil governance and disrupts the fundamental order.

manualTranslations.zh: 魏、晉眇小，齊、隋齷齪，亦所不行斯道者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei and Jin were petty and small; Qi and Sui were sordid and cramped—they too did not carry out this policy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even the petty regimes of Wei and Jin and the sordid dynasties of Qi and Sui did not pursue this policy.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣知其不可者五也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject knows the fifth reason why it is inadvisable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I know a fifth reason why this will not work.

manualTranslations.zh: 今之所以稅關市者，何也？
manualTranslations.literal: Now why tax passes and markets?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why is it, then, that passes and markets are to be taxed?

manualTranslations.zh: 豈不以國用不足，邊寇為虞，一行斯術，冀有殷贍然也！
manualTranslations.literal: Is it not because state expenses are insufficient and border foes are a worry—carry out this method once, hoping for abundance and sufficiency!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Is it not because state revenues are insufficient and border enemies cause concern—a hope that by implementing this measure, funds might become ample!

manualTranslations.zh: 微臣敢借前箸以籌之。
manualTranslations.literal: This lowly subject dares borrow the chopsticks before him to reckon it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your humble subject ventures to use the chopsticks of past sages to calculate the matter.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟陛下當聖期，禦玄籙，沉璧於洛，刻石於嵩，鑄寶鼎以窮奸，坐明堂而布政，神化廣洽，至德潛通。
manualTranslations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty occupies the sage period, holds the dark talisman, sank the jade disc in the Luo, carved stone at Song, cast the precious cauldron to exhaust wickedness, sat in the Bright Hall to distribute government—the divine transformation broadly harmonizes, the utmost virtue secretly pervades.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty occupies a sage age, holds the mandate of Heaven, performed the rite of sinking the jade disc in the Luo River, carved stone at Mount Song, cast the precious cauldron to expose evil, and seated himself in the Bright Hall to govern. Divine influence spreads widely and supreme virtue pervades all.

manualTranslations.zh: 東夷暫驚，應時平殄；
manualTranslations.literal: The eastern Yi were briefly alarmed and promptly extinguished according to the time;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The eastern barbarians were briefly alarmed and promptly subdued;

manualTranslations.zh: 南蠻才動，計日歸降。
manualTranslations.literal: the southern Man had barely stirred when within numbered days they submitted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the southern tribes had barely stirred before they submitted within days.

manualTranslations.zh: 西域五十餘國，廣輸一萬餘里，城堡清夷，亭堠靜謐。
manualTranslations.literal: More than fifty states of the Western Regions, extending over ten thousand li in breadth—fortresses clear and pacified, beacon towers quiet and serene.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: More than fifty states of the Western Regions stretch over ten thousand li, their fortresses tranquil and their beacon towers quiet.

manualTranslations.zh: 比為患者，唯苦二蕃。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who have lately been troublesome are only the two frontier peoples.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The only recent sources of trouble are the two frontier peoples.

manualTranslations.zh: 今吐蕃請命，邊事不起，即目雖尚屯兵，久後疑成馳柝。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Tibet requests orders and border affairs do not arise; at present troops are still stationed, but in time I suspect even the alarm-clapper will cease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now Tibet has submitted and border incidents have ceased. Troops are still stationed for now, but in time even the border alarm may fall silent.

manualTranslations.zh: 獨有默啜，假息孤恩，惡貫禍盈，覆亡不暇。
manualTranslations.literal: Only Mochuo, borrowing a breath on isolated favor—his evil run through, calamities full—has no leisure before overthrow and ruin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only Mochuo, living on borrowed time through Your Majesty's grace, has evil fulfilled and calamity full—his overthrow cannot be long delayed.

manualTranslations.zh: 征役日已省矣，繁費日已稀矣，然猶下明製，遵太樸，愛人力，惜人財，王侯舊封，妃主新禮，所有支料，咸令減削。
manualTranslations.literal: Conscript service daily grows reduced, heavy expenses daily grow scarce—yet still edicts of clear regulation are issued, the great simplicity is followed, human labor is loved, human wealth is cherished—the old enfeoffments of kings and marquises, the new gifts of princesses and consorts, all provisions and supplies are uniformly ordered reduced.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Conscription is already reduced daily and heavy expenditures grow ever rarer. Yet Your Majesty still issues clear edicts, observes great simplicity, cherishes human labor and treasure, and has ordered reductions in the stipends of enfeoffed nobles and the gifts of princesses and consorts alike.

manualTranslations.zh: 此陛下以躬率先，堯、舜之用心也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is Your Majesty taking the lead in person—the mind of Yao and Shun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is Your Majesty leading by personal example—the very spirit of Yao and Shun.

manualTranslations.zh: 且關中、河北，水旱數年，諸處逃亡，今始安輯，倘加重稅，或慮相驚。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, in Guanzhong and Hebei, flood and drought for several years; fugitives in many places have only now been settled—if heavy taxes are added, one fears mutual alarm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, Guanzhong and Hebei have suffered flood and drought for years. Fugitives in many regions have only now been pacified; imposing heavy taxes may provoke widespread alarm.

manualTranslations.zh: 況承平歲積，薄賦日久，俗荷深恩，人知自樂。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, years of peace accumulate; light levies have been long; customs bear deep grace, people know self-contentment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, years of peace have accumulated and light taxation has long prevailed. The people have enjoyed deep grace and know contentment.

manualTranslations.zh: 卒有變法，必多生怨，生怨則驚擾，驚擾則不安，中既不安，外何能禦？
manualTranslations.literal: Suddenly there is change of law, necessarily many grievances arise; grievances arise then alarm and disturbance; alarm and disturbance then unrest—when the interior is already unsettled, how can the exterior be defended?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A sudden change of law will inevitably breed widespread resentment. Resentment breeds alarm, alarm breeds unrest—and when the interior is unsettled, how can the exterior be defended?

manualTranslations.zh: 文王曰：“帝王富其人，霸王富其地，理國若不足，亂國若有餘。
manualTranslations.literal: King Wen said: "Emperors and kings enrich their people; hegemons and lords enrich their lands. A well-ordered state seems insufficient; a disorderly state seems to have surplus.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: King Wen said: "Emperors and kings enrich their people; hegemons enrich their territory. A well-governed state seems to have too little; a chaotic state seems to have too much.

manualTranslations.zh: ”古人有言：“帝王藏於天下，諸侯藏於百姓，農夫藏於庾，商賈藏於篋。
manualTranslations.literal: " The ancients had a saying: "Emperors and kings store [wealth] in the realm under Heaven; feudal lords store it in the common people; farmers store it in granaries; merchants store it in chests.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " The ancients said: "Emperors store wealth throughout the realm; feudal lords store it among the people; farmers store it in granaries; merchants store it in coffers.

manualTranslations.zh: ”惟陛下詳之。
manualTranslations.literal: " May Your Majesty examine this in detail.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " I ask Your Majesty to consider this carefully.

manualTranslations.zh: 必若師興有費，國儲多窘，即請倍算商客，加斂平人。
manualTranslations.literal: If it must be that armies are raised and there are expenses, and state stores are greatly straitened, then please double-assess merchant travelers and add levies on common people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If military campaigns require funds and state reserves are strained, then by all means double the assessments on merchants and add levies on common folk.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此則國保富強，人免憂懼，天下幸甚。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus then the state preserves strength and wealth, people are spared worry and fear—the realm under Heaven is greatly fortunate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That would preserve national wealth and strength, spare the people worry and fear, and bring great fortune to the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣知其不可者六也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject knows the sixth reason why it is inadvisable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I know a sixth reason why this will not work.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下留神係表，屬想政源，冒茲炎熾，早朝晏坐。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty keeps mind on the attached memorial, fixes thought on the source of governance, braves this blazing heat—early court, late sitting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty attends closely to memorials, fixes thought on the source of governance, braves this scorching heat, and holds court early and works late.

manualTranslations.zh: 一日二日，機務不遺，先天後天，虛心密應。
manualTranslations.literal: Day after day, urgent affairs are not omitted; before Heaven, after Heaven—empty of mind, secretly responsive.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Day after day, no urgent business is neglected. With openness before Heaven and responsiveness after Heaven, You respond with careful attention.

manualTranslations.zh: 時政得失，小子何知，率陳瞽辭，伏紙惶懼。
manualTranslations.literal: The gains and losses of present governance—what does this petty fellow know? I frankly present blind words, prostrate on paper in fear and trepidation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What does one such as I know of the merits and faults of present policy? I frankly offer these blind words and submit this memorial in fear and trepidation.

manualTranslations.zh: 疏奏，則天納之，乃寢其事。
manualTranslations.literal: The memorial was submitted; Empress Wu accepted it, and then shelved the matter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Empress Wu accepted it and shelved the proposal.

context.afterSource: 崔融，齊州全節人。

sourceRange.text: 藏用常以俗多拘忌，有乖至理，乃著《析滯論》以暢其事，辭曰：客曰：“天道玄微，神理幽化，聖人所以法象，眾庶由其運行。故大撓造甲子，容成著律曆，黃公裁變，玄女啟謨，八門禦時，六神直事。從之者則兵強國富，違之者則將弱朝危，有同影響，若合符契。先生亦嚐聞之乎？主人曰：“何為其然也？子所謂曲學所習，需昧所守，徒識偏方之詭說，未究亨衢之通論。蓋《易》曰“先天不違”，《傳》稱“人神之主”。範圍不過，三才所以虛中；進退非邪，百王所以無外。故曰：“國之將興聽於人，將亡聽於神。”又曰：“禍福無門，唯人所召。人無釁焉，妖不自作。”由是言之，得喪興亡，並關人事；吉凶悔吝，無涉天時。且皇天無親，唯德是輔，為不善者，天降之殃。高宗修德，桑穀以變；宋君引過，法星退舍，此天道所以從人者也。古之為政者，刑獄不濫則人壽，賦斂蠲省則人富，法令有常則國靜，賞罰得中則兵強。所以禮者，士之所歸，賞者，士之所死，禮賞不倦，則士爭先。苟違此途，雖卜時行刑，擇日出令，必無成功矣。自叔世遷訛，俗多徼幸，競稱怪力，爭誦詭言，屈政教而就孤虛，棄信賞而從推步。附會前史，變易舊經，依托空文，以為征據。覆軍敗將者，則隱秘無聞；偶同幸中者，則共相文飾。豈唯德之增惑，亦乃學人自是。嗚呼，習俗訛謬，一至此焉！昔者，甲子興師，非成功之日；往亡用事，異製勝之辰。人事苟修，何往不濟？至若環城自守，接陣重圍，無闕地形，不乖天道。若兵強將智，粟積城堅，雖復屢轉魁剛，頻移太歲，坐推白虎，行計貪狼，自符難鬥之祥，多貽蟻附之困。故曰，任賢使能，則不時日而事利；明法審令，則不卜筮而事吉；養勞賞功，則不禱祠而得福。此所謂天時不如地利，地利不如人和。太公犯雨，逆天時也，韓信背水，乖地利也，並存人事，俱成大業。削樹而斬龐涓，舉火而屠張郃，未必暗同歲德，冥會日遊，俱運三門，並占四殺。杜郵齒劍，抑唯計沮，垓下悲歌，實階剚印。若以並資厭勝，不事良圖，則長平盡坑，固須恒濟，襄城無噍，亦可常保。是知拘而多忌，終喪大功；百姓與能，必遺小數。金雞玉鶴，方為楚國之殃；《萬畢》、《枕中》，適構淮南之禍。刻符指盜，反更亡身；被髮邀神，翻招夷族。嗟乎，威鬥赭鞭，不禳赤伏之運；築城斷罔，何救素靈之哭！火災不驗，裨灶無力以窺天；超乘階凶，王孫取監於觀德。九征九變，是曰長途；人謀鬼謀，良歸有道。此並經史陳跡，賢聖通規，仁遠乎哉，詎宜滯執？客乃蹙然避席曰：“鄙人困蒙，不階至道，請事斯語，歸於正途。而今而後，焚蓍龜，毀律曆，廢六合，斥五行，浩然清慮，則將奚若？”答曰：“此所謂過猶不及也。夫甲子所以配日月，律曆所以通歲時，金木所以備法象，蓍龜所以筮吉凶。聖人以此神明德行，輔助謀猷，存之則協讚成功，執之則凝滯於物。消息之義，其在茲乎！”客於是循牆匍匐，帖然無氣，口去心醉，不知所以答矣。

manualTranslations.zh: 藏用常以俗多拘忌，有乖至理，乃著《析滯論》以暢其事，辭曰：客曰：“天道玄微，神理幽化，聖人所以法象，眾庶由其運行。
manualTranslations.literal: Zangyong often considered that popular custom was full of taboos contrary to ultimate principle; he therefore composed the "Discourse on Unblocking Stagnation" to set forth his views, saying: The Guest said: "The Way of Heaven is abstruse and subtle; the divine principle is darkly transformative—sages model themselves upon it, and the common multitude act according to its operations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zangyong often felt that popular custom was riddled with taboos at odds with ultimate principle, so he wrote the "Discourse on Unblocking Stagnation" to set forth his views. He wrote: The Guest said, "The Way of Heaven is abstruse and subtle, and the divine principle works in hidden transformation; sages take it as their model, and the common people live by its course.

manualTranslations.zh: 故大撓造甲子，容成著律曆，黃公裁變，玄女啟謨，八門禦時，六神直事。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore Da Rao created the sexagenary cycle, Rong Cheng authored the calendrical system, Huang Gong determined transformations, the Dark Lady opened the plan, the Eight Gates ward off the seasons, and the Six Spirits attend to affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Da Rao devised the sexagenary cycle, Rong Cheng wrote the calendrical system, Huang Gong fixed the transformations, the Dark Lady revealed the design, the Eight Gates govern the seasons, and the Six Spirits oversee affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 從之者則兵強國富，違之者則將弱朝危，有同影響，若合符契。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who follow them have strong armies and wealthy states; those who violate them have weak generals and endangered courts—the effect is like shadow and echo, as if matching tally halves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who follow them grow strong in arms and rich in state; those who defy them find their generals weakened and their court endangered—the effect is immediate, like shadow and echo, as if tally halves were joined.

manualTranslations.zh: 先生亦嚐聞之乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Has the Master also heard of this?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Has the Master heard of this as well?

manualTranslations.zh: 主人曰：“何為其然也？
manualTranslations.literal: The Host said: "Why should this be so?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Host said, "Why should that be so?

manualTranslations.zh: 子所謂曲學所習，需昧所守，徒識偏方之詭說，未究亨衢之通論。
manualTranslations.literal: What you speak of are cramped studies habitually learned and shallow convictions rigidly held—you merely know the eccentric claims of partial schools and have not investigated the comprehensive doctrine of the broad highway.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What you describe are narrow studies learned by rote and dim convictions held blindly—you know only the eccentric claims of partial schools and have not examined the comprehensive doctrine of the open road.

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋《易》曰“先天不違”，《傳》稱“人神之主”。
manualTranslations.literal: For the Changes says "He does not violate what precedes Heaven," and the Commentary calls it "the lord of man and spirit."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "He does not violate what precedes Heaven," and the Commentary calls it "the master of human and divine affairs."

manualTranslations.zh: 範圍不過，三才所以虛中；
manualTranslations.literal: Its scope does not overstep, and therefore the three powers have emptiness at the center;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Its scope does not overreach, and so the three powers hold emptiness at their center;

manualTranslations.zh: 進退非邪，百王所以無外。
manualTranslations.literal: Its advance and retreat are without deviation, and therefore the hundred kings have nothing outside it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Its advance and retreat are without error, and so the hundred kings have nothing beyond it.

manualTranslations.zh: 故曰：“國之將興聽於人，將亡聽於神。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore it is said: "When a state is about to rise, heed people; when it is about to perish, heed spirits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence the saying, "When a state is about to rise, listen to people; when it is about to fall, listen to spirits."

manualTranslations.zh: ”又曰：“禍福無門，唯人所召。
manualTranslations.literal: " It is also said: "Fortune and misfortune have no gate of their own—only people summon them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: And again, "Fortune and misfortune have no fixed gate—only people summon them."

manualTranslations.zh: 人無釁焉，妖不自作。
manualTranslations.literal: When people give no cause, portents do not arise of themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When people give no cause, portents do not arise on their own.

manualTranslations.zh: ”由是言之，得喪興亡，並關人事；
manualTranslations.literal: " From this it follows that gain and loss, rise and fall, all depend on human affairs;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this it follows that gain and loss, rise and fall, all turn on human affairs;

manualTranslations.zh: 吉凶悔吝，無涉天時。
manualTranslations.literal: good fortune, misfortune, regret, and distress have nothing to do with the timing of Heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and good fortune, misfortune, regret, and distress have nothing to do with heavenly timing.

manualTranslations.zh: 且皇天無親，唯德是輔，為不善者，天降之殃。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, High Heaven is without partiality and only assists virtue; for those who do what is not good, Heaven sends down calamity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, High Heaven is impartial and assists only virtue; for those who do wrong, Heaven sends down disaster.

manualTranslations.zh: 高宗修德，桑穀以變；
manualTranslations.literal: When Gaozong cultivated virtue, the mulberry and grain transformed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Gaozong cultivated virtue, the mulberry and grain changed of themselves;

manualTranslations.zh: 宋君引過，法星退舍，此天道所以從人者也。
manualTranslations.literal: when the lord of Song acknowledged his fault, the Punishment Star withdrew from its lodge—this is how the Way of Heaven follows people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when the ruler of Song acknowledged his fault, the Punishment Star withdrew from its station—this is how the Way of Heaven follows human action.

manualTranslations.zh: 古之為政者，刑獄不濫則人壽，賦斂蠲省則人富，法令有常則國靜，賞罰得中則兵強。
manualTranslations.literal: Ancient administrators of government—when punishments and prisons were not abused, people lived long; when levies and taxes were reduced and lightened, people grew wealthy; when laws and commands had constancy, the state was tranquil; when rewards and punishments were balanced, the army was strong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers who governed well found that when punishments and prisons were not abused, people lived long; when levies and taxes were reduced, people grew wealthy; when laws and commands were steady, the state was calm; and when rewards and punishments were fair, the army was strong.

manualTranslations.zh: 所以禮者，士之所歸，賞者，士之所死，禮賞不倦，則士爭先。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore ritual is what gentlemen rally to, and rewards are what gentlemen die for—when ritual and reward never slacken, gentlemen vie to be first.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ritual is what gentlemen rally to, and reward is what they die for; when ritual and reward never flag, gentlemen compete to lead.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟違此途，雖卜時行刑，擇日出令，必無成功矣。
manualTranslations.literal: If one departs from this course, even selecting times to execute punishment and choosing days to issue commands will surely bring no success.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Depart from this path, and even if one chooses auspicious times to punish or issue orders, success is impossible.

manualTranslations.zh: 自叔世遷訛，俗多徼幸，競稱怪力，爭誦詭言，屈政教而就孤虛，棄信賞而從推步。
manualTranslations.literal: From the later ages, as the times shifted into error, custom became full of hoping for luck; people competed to praise occult forces and vied to recite bizarre talk, bending government and education to submit to solitary-void divination, abandoning trust and rewards to follow calendrical calculation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since later ages fell into error, custom has been full of hoping for lucky breaks; people compete to praise occult powers and recite strange doctrines, bending government and education to solitary-void divination and abandoning trust and reward for calendrical reckoning.

manualTranslations.zh: 附會前史，變易舊經，依托空文，以為征據。
manualTranslations.literal: They forced links to past histories, altered old classics, relied on empty texts, and took these as evidence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They forced parallels with past histories, altered old classics, and treated empty texts as proof.

manualTranslations.zh: 覆軍敗將者，則隱秘無聞；
manualTranslations.literal: When armies were destroyed and generals defeated, those cases were concealed and left unheard;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When armies were destroyed and generals defeated, the cases were hushed up and never heard of;

manualTranslations.zh: 偶同幸中者，則共相文飾。
manualTranslations.literal: when outcomes happened by chance to match, they embellished one another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when outcomes happened by lucky coincidence, they embellished one another.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈唯德之增惑，亦乃學人自是。
manualTranslations.literal: Not only did this further confuse virtue—it also made scholars complacent in their own rightness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This not only further confused virtue; it also made scholars smug in their own opinions.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗚呼，習俗訛謬，一至此焉！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas, erroneous custom has reached this pitch!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas, corrupt custom has reached this extreme!

manualTranslations.zh: 昔者，甲子興師，非成功之日；
manualTranslations.literal: In the past, launching troops on a jiazi day was not a day for success;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the past, launching troops on a jiazi day was said to be no day for success;

manualTranslations.zh: 往亡用事，異製勝之辰。
manualTranslations.literal: employing the Day of Past Dissolution differed from the hour for securing victory.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and using the Day of Past Dissolution was unlike the moment for securing victory.

manualTranslations.zh: 人事苟修，何往不濟？
manualTranslations.literal: If human affairs are properly cultivated, where would one go and not succeed?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If human affairs are properly managed, where would one fail to succeed?

manualTranslations.zh: 至若環城自守，接陣重圍，無闕地形，不乖天道。
manualTranslations.literal: As for encircling a city to hold it fast, or meeting the enemy in layered siege—terrain need not be lacking, and the Way of Heaven need not be violated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even when encircling a city in defense or facing layered sieges in battle, one need not lack favorable terrain or violate the Way of Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 若兵強將智，粟積城堅，雖復屢轉魁剛，頻移太歲，坐推白虎，行計貪狼，自符難鬥之祥，多貽蟻附之困。
manualTranslations.literal: If the army is strong and the general wise, grain is stocked and walls are sturdy—even if one repeatedly shifts the Kui and Gang stars, frequently moves the Year Star, sits calculating the White Tiger, and marches planning by the Greedy Wolf, naturally matching inauspicious signs for hard fighting, one mostly invites the trouble of ants clinging on.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the army is strong, the general wise, grain stocked, and walls solid, then even after repeatedly shifting the Kui and Gang stars, moving the Year Star, calculating the White Tiger while seated, and planning marches by the Greedy Wolf—matching every ill omen for hard fighting—one still mostly invites the plight of ants swarming a corpse.

manualTranslations.zh: 故曰，任賢使能，則不時日而事利；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore it is said: employ the worthy and use the capable, and affairs prosper without heeding days and times;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: employ the worthy and use the capable, and affairs succeed without regard to days and times;

manualTranslations.zh: 明法審令，則不卜筮而事吉；
manualTranslations.literal: clarify laws and examine commands, and affairs are auspicious without divination;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: clarify laws and examine commands, and affairs turn out well without divination;

manualTranslations.zh: 養勞賞功，則不禱祠而得福。
manualTranslations.literal: nurture the weary and reward merit, and fortune is gained without prayer and sacrifice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: care for the weary and reward merit, and blessing comes without prayer or sacrifice.

manualTranslations.zh: 此所謂天時不如地利，地利不如人和。
manualTranslations.literal: This is what they call: the timing of Heaven is not as good as the advantage of terrain, and the advantage of terrain is not as good as human harmony.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by saying that heavenly timing is inferior to terrain, and terrain is inferior to human harmony.

manualTranslations.zh: 太公犯雨，逆天時也，韓信背水，乖地利也，並存人事，俱成大業。
manualTranslations.literal: Taigong braved rain—going against the timing of Heaven; Han Xin fought with water at his back—contrary to terrain advantage; yet both relied on human affairs and alike achieved great enterprise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taigong marched in rain, defying heavenly timing; Han Xin fought with water at his back, contrary to terrain advantage—yet both relied on human affairs and alike achieved great success.

manualTranslations.zh: 削樹而斬龐涓，舉火而屠張郃，未必暗同歲德，冥會日遊，俱運三門，並占四殺。
manualTranslations.literal: Felling trees to behead Pang Juan, raising fire to slaughter Zhang He—they need not secretly match the Year Virtue, secretly coincide with the Sun's circuit, jointly deploy the Three Gates, or together occupy the Four Kills.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Felling trees to behead Pang Juan and raising fire to slaughter Zhang He did not require secretly matching the Year Virtue, secretly aligning with the Sun's circuit, jointly deploying the Three Gates, or together occupying the Four Kills.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜郵齒劍，抑唯計沮，垓下悲歌，實階剚印。
manualTranslations.literal: At Duyang biting the sword—truly only Ji Ju schemed; the mournful song at Gaixia—in truth it was the step toward cutting the seal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sword-biting at Duyang came down to Ji Ju's scheming alone; the mournful song at Gaixia was in truth the step toward having one's seal cut off.

manualTranslations.zh: 若以並資厭勝，不事良圖，則長平盡坑，固須恒濟，襄城無噍，亦可常保。
manualTranslations.literal: If one relied equally on occult suppression and did not pursue sound planning, then the total slaughter at Changping would surely require the Eternal Ford, and the annihilation at Xiangcheng could also be permanently preserved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one relied equally on occult suppression instead of sound planning, then the total slaughter at Changping would surely have needed the Eternal Ford, and the annihilation at Xiangcheng could also have been permanently avoided.

manualTranslations.zh: 是知拘而多忌，終喪大功；
manualTranslations.literal: From this one knows that being constrained and full of taboos ultimately loses great achievement;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this one knows that constraint and excessive taboos ultimately destroy great achievement;

manualTranslations.zh: 百姓與能，必遺小數。
manualTranslations.literal: when the common people contribute their abilities, one must set aside petty reckonings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when the people contribute their abilities, one must leave petty reckonings aside.

manualTranslations.zh: 金雞玉鶴，方為楚國之殃；
manualTranslations.literal: The golden rooster and jade crane proved to be the calamity of the state of Chu;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The golden rooster and jade crane became the disaster of the state of Chu;

manualTranslations.zh: 《萬畢》、《枕中》，適構淮南之禍。
manualTranslations.literal: The "Ten Thousand Completions" and "Pillow Book" just brought about the disaster of Huainan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Ten Thousand Completions and Pillow Book brought about the disaster of Huainan.

manualTranslations.zh: 刻符指盜，反更亡身；
manualTranslations.literal: Carving talismans to identify thieves yet instead brought about one's own death;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Carving talismans to catch thieves instead brought about one's own death;

manualTranslations.zh: 被髮邀神，翻招夷族。
manualTranslations.literal: Disheveling hair to invite spirits instead invited extermination of one's clan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Disheveling one's hair to summon spirits instead brought extermination upon one's clan.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗟乎，威鬥赭鞭，不禳赤伏之運；
manualTranslations.literal: Alas—the war-drum and ruddy whip could not avert the rise of the Red symbol;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas, the war-drum and ruddy whip could not avert the rise of the Red symbol;

manualTranslations.zh: 築城斷罔，何救素靈之哭！
manualTranslations.literal: Building walls and cutting dikes—how could they save the weeping of Su Ling!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Building walls and cutting dikes—how could they save the weeping of Su Ling!

manualTranslations.zh: 火災不驗，裨灶無力以窺天；
manualTranslations.literal: The fire disaster went unfulfilled, and Pixie Zao lacked strength to peer into Heaven;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The predicted fire disaster did not come to pass, and Pixie Zao lacked the power to read Heaven;

manualTranslations.zh: 超乘階凶，王孫取監於觀德。
manualTranslations.literal: Leaping onto the chariot step brought misfortune—the king's grandson took warning from observing virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Leaping onto the chariot step brought disaster; the king's grandson took his lesson from observing virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 九征九變，是曰長途；
manualTranslations.literal: Nine probes and nine transformations—this is called the long journey;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Nine probes and nine transformations—this is called the long road;

manualTranslations.zh: 人謀鬼謀，良歸有道。
manualTranslations.literal: Human planning and ghostly planning alike ultimately return to the proper Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Human planning and ghostly planning alike ultimately return to the proper Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 此並經史陳跡，賢聖通規，仁遠乎哉，詎宜滯執？
manualTranslations.literal: These are all tracks laid out in the classics and histories, the universal norms of the sage and worthy—is humanity far away? How could one cling rigidly?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: These are all precedents set forth in the classics and histories, the universal norms of sages and worthies—is humanity really so far away? Why cling so rigidly?

manualTranslations.zh: 客乃蹙然避席曰：“鄙人困蒙，不階至道，請事斯語，歸於正途。
manualTranslations.literal: The Guest then, looking abashed, withdrew from his mat and said: "This rustic is benumbed and ignorant, not having reached the supreme Way—allow me to take these words and return to the proper path.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Guest then, abashed, withdrew from his mat and said, "I am a dull and ignorant man who has not reached the supreme Way. Allow me to follow these words and return to the proper path.

manualTranslations.zh: 而今而後，焚蓍龜，毀律曆，廢六合，斥五行，浩然清慮，則將奚若？
manualTranslations.literal: From now on, burning the yarrow and tortoise, destroying calendars, abolishing the six harmonies, rejecting the five phases, with vast clear-mindedness—what then shall I be like?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From now on, if I burn the yarrow and tortoise, destroy calendars, abolish the six harmonies, and reject the five phases, and with vast clarity of mind—what then shall I become?

manualTranslations.zh: ”答曰：“此所謂過猶不及也。
manualTranslations.literal: " The reply said: "This is what they call going too far is as bad as not going far enough.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The reply said, "This is what is meant by going too far is no better than falling short.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫甲子所以配日月，律曆所以通歲時，金木所以備法象，蓍龜所以筮吉凶。
manualTranslations.literal: The sexagenary cycle matches sun and moon; calendars connect with the seasons; metal and wood complete the modeled images; yarrow and tortoise divination determine fortune and misfortune.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sexagenary cycle matches sun and moon; calendars align with the seasons; metal and wood complete the modeled images; yarrow and tortoise are used to divine fortune and misfortune.

manualTranslations.zh: 聖人以此神明德行，輔助謀猷，存之則協讚成功，執之則凝滯於物。
manualTranslations.literal: The sage uses these to illuminate virtue and conduct and assist in deliberation—preserved, they harmoniously help success; rigidly held, they stagnate and bind one to things.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sages use these to illuminate virtue and conduct and to assist deliberation; kept in their place, they harmoniously aid success; clung to rigidly, they freeze one in attachment to things.

manualTranslations.zh: 消息之義，其在茲乎！
manualTranslations.literal: The meaning of waxing and waning—is it not here!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The meaning of waxing and waning—is it not found here!

manualTranslations.zh: ”客於是循牆匍匐，帖然無氣，口去心醉，不知所以答矣。
manualTranslations.literal: " The Guest then crawled along the wall in prostration, utterly subdued and breathless, mouth agape and heart intoxicated, not knowing how to reply.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Guest then crawled along the wall in prostration, utterly subdued and breathless, mouth agape and heart overwhelmed, not knowing how to answer.

sourceRange.text: 時則天將營興泰宮於萬安山，藏用上疏諫曰：臣愚雖不達時變，竊嚐讀書，見自古帝王之跡眾矣。臣聞土階三尺，茅茨不翦，采椽不斫者，唐堯之德也；卑宮室，菲飲食，盡力於溝洫者，大禹之行也；惜中人十家之產，而罷露台之製者，漢文之明也。並能垂名無窮，為帝皇之烈。豈不以克念徇物，博施濟眾，以臻於仁恕哉！今陛下崇台邃宇，離宮別館，亦已多矣。更窮人之力以事土木，臣恐議者以陛下為不憂人、務奉已也。且頃歲已來，雖年穀頗登，而百姓未有儲蓄。陛下西幸東巡，人未休息，土木之役，歲月不空。陛下不因此時施德布化，復廣造宮苑，臣恐人未易堪。今左右近臣，多以順意為忠；朝廷具僚，皆以犯忤為患。至今陛下不知百姓失業，亦不知左右傷陛下之仁也。臣聞忠臣不避死亡之患，以納君於仁；明主不惡切直之言，以垂名千載。陛下誠能發明恕之製，以勞人為辭，則天下必以陛下為惜人力而苦己也。小臣固陋，不識忌諱，敢冒死上聞。乞下臣此章，與執事者議其可否，則天下幸甚。

manualTranslations.zh: 時則天將營興泰宮於萬安山，藏用上疏諫曰：臣愚雖不達時變，竊嚐讀書，見自古帝王之跡眾矣。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Empress Wu was about to build Xingtai Palace at Mount Wan'an. Zangyong submitted a memorial to remonstrate, saying: "This subject is foolish and, though I do not comprehend the changes of the times, I have privately read books and seen that the traces of emperors and kings since antiquity are many."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Wu was planning to construct Xingtai Palace on Mount Wan'an. Zangyong submitted a memorial in protest, saying: "Though I am but a foolish subject who does not grasp the changing times, in my private reading I have encountered countless examples of emperors and kings of old."

manualTranslations.zh: 臣聞土階三尺，茅茨不翦，采椽不斫者，唐堯之德也；
manualTranslations.literal: I have heard that earthen steps three feet high, thatched roofs left untrimmed, and unhewn rafters of plain wood—these were the virtue of Tang Yao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have read that Tang Yao's virtue lay in earthen steps three feet high, unshorn thatch, and unadorned wooden rafters.

manualTranslations.zh: 卑宮室，菲飲食，盡力於溝洫者，大禹之行也；
manualTranslations.literal: Humbling the palace chambers, making food and drink frugal, and exerting all strength on ditches and canals—this was the conduct of Yu the Great.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu the Great's way was to keep his dwellings modest, his fare simple, and to devote all his strength to digging canals and irrigation works.

manualTranslations.zh: 惜中人十家之產，而罷露台之製者，漢文之明也。
manualTranslations.literal: Cherishing the property of ten middling households and abolishing the terrace-pavilion project—this was the wisdom of Emperor Wen of Han.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han showed his wisdom when he spared the wealth of ten ordinary households and canceled plans for a terrace pavilion.

manualTranslations.zh: 並能垂名無窮，為帝皇之烈。
manualTranslations.literal: All alike were able to leave their names to endure without end, becoming exemplars among emperors and sovereigns.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All of them won lasting renown and stand as great models among emperors and kings.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈不以克念徇物，博施濟眾，以臻於仁恕哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Was it not because they restrained their thoughts and yielded to material things, broadly dispensing benefits to relieve the multitude, thereby attaining benevolence and forbearance!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Surely this was because they mastered their desires, set aside personal indulgence, and broadly gave aid to the people until they reached true benevolence and forbearance!

manualTranslations.zh: 今陛下崇台邃宇，離宮別館，亦已多矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Your Majesty's lofty terraces and deep halls, detached palaces and separate lodges, are already many.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already has no lack of lofty towers, deep halls, detached palaces, and separate lodges.

manualTranslations.zh: 更窮人之力以事土木，臣恐議者以陛下為不憂人、務奉已也。
manualTranslations.literal: Further exhausting people's strength to serve earthworks and timber construction—I fear critics will regard Your Majesty as not caring for the people and devoted to serving yourself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you further drain the people's strength for construction, I fear observers will take Your Majesty to be indifferent to the people's welfare and intent only on gratifying yourself.

manualTranslations.zh: 且頃歲已來，雖年穀頗登，而百姓未有儲蓄。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, in recent years, though the annual grain harvest has been fairly abundant, the common people still have no savings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, in recent years, though harvests have been fairly good, the common people still have nothing put by.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下西幸東巡，人未休息，土木之役，歲月不空。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty's journeys west and tours east—the people have not yet rested, and labors of earth and wood leave no month empty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's journeys west and tours east, the people have had no respite, and construction work has left scarcely a month free.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下不因此時施德布化，復廣造宮苑，臣恐人未易堪。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty, instead of using this time to spread virtue and disseminate transforming influence, again broadly builds palaces and gardens—I fear the people will not easily bear it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Instead of using this moment to spread virtue and benevolent rule, Your Majesty would again expand palaces and gardens on a grand scale—I fear the people will find it hard to endure.

manualTranslations.zh: 今左右近臣，多以順意為忠；
manualTranslations.literal: Now the close attendants at Your Majesty's side mostly take complying with your wishes to be loyalty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today those nearest Your Majesty mostly treat agreement with your wishes as loyalty.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷具僚，皆以犯忤為患。
manualTranslations.literal: All officials of the court alike regard giving offense and contradiction as a calamity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the court all treat speaking against Your Majesty as something to be dreaded.

manualTranslations.zh: 至今陛下不知百姓失業，亦不知左右傷陛下之仁也。
manualTranslations.literal: To this day Your Majesty does not know the people's loss of livelihood, nor does Your Majesty know that those around you are harming Your Majesty's benevolence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even now Your Majesty remains unaware that the people have lost their livelihoods, and unaware that those around you are damaging Your Majesty's reputation for benevolence.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣聞忠臣不避死亡之患，以納君於仁；
manualTranslations.literal: I have heard that loyal ministers do not avoid the peril of death, in order to lead the ruler into benevolence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard that loyal ministers do not shrink from the risk of death if by doing so they can guide their ruler toward benevolent rule.

manualTranslations.zh: 明主不惡切直之言，以垂名千載。
manualTranslations.literal: A wise ruler does not detest blunt and straight speech, in order to leave his name for a thousand years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A wise ruler does not resent frank and forthright counsel, for by accepting it he wins a name that endures for a thousand years.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下誠能發明恕之製，以勞人為辭，則天下必以陛下為惜人力而苦己也。
manualTranslations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly enact measures of enlightened forbearance, taking the burden on the people as your reason, then all under Heaven will surely regard Your Majesty as cherishing human labor and imposing hardship on yourself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would truly proclaim a policy of enlightened forbearance and decline further work on the grounds that it would overtax the people, all under Heaven would surely see Your Majesty as one who spares human labor and willingly burdens himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 小臣固陋，不識忌諱，敢冒死上聞。
manualTranslations.literal: This petty official is indeed crude and ignorant, does not know taboos, and dares to risk death to report upward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I am but a humble and ignorant official, unversed in what may not be said, yet I dare risk my life to bring this before Your Majesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 乞下臣此章，與執事者議其可否，則天下幸甚。
manualTranslations.literal: I beg that you transmit this memorial of mine to the responsible officials to discuss its advisability, then all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that this memorial be forwarded to the responsible officials for deliberation on its merits, for then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed.

sourceRange.text: 彥伯聖曆中累除給事中，時王公卿士多以言語不慎，密為酷吏周興、來俊臣等所陷，彥伯乃著《樞機論》以誡於代，其辭曰：《書》曰：“唯口起羞，惟甲胃起戎。”又云：“齊乃位，度乃口。”《易》曰：“慎言語，節飲食。”又云：“出其言善，千里應之；出其言不善，千里違之。”《禮》亦云：“可言也，不可行也，君子不言也；可行也，不可言也，君子不行也。”嗚呼！先聖知言之為大也，知言之為急也，精微以勸之，典謨以告之，禮經以防之。守名教者，何可不修其詁訓而服其糟粕乎？故曰：“言語者，君子之樞機，動則物應，物應則得失之兆見也。得之者江海比鄰，失之者肝膽楚、越，然後知否泰榮辱，係於言乎！夫言者，德之柄也，行之主也，誌之端也，身之文也，既可以濟身，亦可以覆身。故中庸鏤其心，右階銘其背，南容復於白圭，箕子疇於《洪範》，良有以也。是以掎摭瑕玷，參詳躁競，審無常以階亂，將不密以致危。利生於口，森然覆邦之說；道不由衷，變彼如簧之刺。可不懼之哉！其有識暗邪正，慮微形朕，破金湯之龠，封禍亂之根，用詀讘為全計，以號詉為令德。至若梧宮問答，荊、齊所以奔命；韓、魏加肘，智伯所以危殘。蔡侯繩息媯也，亟招甲兵之罰；鄭曼圖宗卿也，而受鼎鑊之誅。史遷輕議，終下蠶室；張紘說，更齒龍淵。凡此過言，其流匪一。或穢猶糞土，或動成刀劍，或苟且其心，或脂膏其吻。挾邪作蠱，守之而不懈；往輒破的，去之而彌遠。亦可異韓廬聚音，釐也群吠，得死為幸，何循名之立乎？雖復伯玉沮顏，追謝於元凱，蔣濟貽恨，失譽於王陵，犀首沒齒於季章，曹瞞齚舌於劉主，當何及哉！孔子曰：“予欲無言。”又云：“終身為善一言敗之，惜也。”老子亦云：“多言數窮。”又雲“聰明深察而近於死者，議人者也。”何聖人之深思偉慮，杜漸防萌之至乎！夫不可言而言者曰狂，可言而不言者曰隱。鉗舌拱默，曷通彼此之懷；括囊而處，孰啟謨明之訓？則上言者，下聽也；下言者，上用也。睿哲之言，猶天地也，人覆燾而生焉；大雅之言，猶鍾鼓也，人考擊而樂焉。作以龜鏡，姬公之言也；出為金石，曾子之言也；存其家邦，國僑之言也；立而不朽，臧孫之言也。是謂德音，詣我宗極，滿於天下，貽厥後昆。殷宗甘之於酒醴，孫卿諭之以琴瑟，闕里重於四時，郢都輕其千乘。豈不韙哉，豈不休哉！但楙探世猷，克念丕訓，審思而應，精慮而動。謀其心以後發，擇其交以後談，不蹙趨於非黨，不屏營於詭遇。非先王之至德不敢行，非先王之法言不敢道，翦其諜諜之緒，撲其炎炎之勢。自然介爾景福，錫茲純嘏，則悔吝何由而生，怨惡何由而至哉？孔子曰：“終日行，不遺已患；終日言，不遺已憂。”如此乃可以言也。戒之哉，戒之哉！
