sourceRange.text: 玄宗三十子：元獻楊皇后生肅宗，劉華妃生奉天皇帝琮、靖恭太子琬、儀王璲，趙麗妃生廢太子瑛，錢妃生棣王琰，皇甫德儀生鄂王瑤，劉才人生光王琚，貞順武皇后生夏悼王一、懷哀王敏、壽王瑁、盛王琦，高婕妤生潁王璬、郭順儀生永王璘，柳婕妤生延王玢，鐘美人生濟王環，盧美人生信王瑝，閻才人生義王玭，王美人生陳王珪，陳美人生豐王珙，鄭才人生恆王瑱，武賢儀生涼王璿，汴哀王璥，餘七王早夭。奉天皇帝琮，玄宗長子也，本名嗣直。景雲元年九月，封許昌郡王。先天元年八月，進封郯王。開元四年正月，遙領安西大都護，仍充安撫河東、關內、隴右諸蕃大使。十三年，改封慶王，仍改名潭。十五年，遙領涼州都督，兼河西諸軍節度大使。二十一年，加太子太師，改名琮。二十四年，拜司徒。天寶元年，兼太原牧。十一載薨，贈靖德太子，葬於渭水之南細柳原，仍於啟夏門內置廟祔享焉。肅宗元年建寅月九日，詔追冊為奉天皇帝，妃竇氏為恭應皇后，備禮改葬於華清宮北齊陵，以尚書右僕射、冀國公裴冕為其使。初，開元二十五年，太子瑛得罪廢，令琮養其子，及天寶十一載琮薨，以瑛子俅為嗣慶王，除秘書監同正員。

sourceRange.text: 貞元元年，親祠南郊，為大禮使。屬兵旱之後，賦入尚少，縱裁定文物，儉而中禮。無何，萬年丞源邃為京兆尹李齊運所抑捽至死，縱劾奏不行。數月，除吏部侍郎，尋檢校禮部尚書、東畿唐汝鄧都觀察使、河南尹。是時兵革甫定，民耗六七，縱悉心求瘼，為理簡易。先是，戍邊之師由洛陽者，儲餼取辦於編戶。縱始官備，不征於人，令五家相保，俾自占告發斂，以絕胥吏之私。又引伊、洛水以通里閈，都中灌溉濟不逮為十一二，人甚安之。徵拜太常卿。貞元七年六月卒官，年六十二，謚曰忠，贈吏部尚書。

context.beforeSource: 嘗議其大體，不親細事，獄訴儀制，皆付之僚吏。
context.afterSource: 縱孝悌，修飭自立，以父為元載排抑，居退十餘年，左宦外府，訖載得罪，不求聞達。

manualTranslations.zh: 貞元元年，親祠南郊，為大禮使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, he personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburbs and served as commissioner for the grand rites.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan (785) he personally performed the Southern Suburbs sacrifice and served as commissioner for the grand rites.

manualTranslations.zh: 屬兵旱之後，賦入尚少，縱裁定文物，儉而中禮。
manualTranslations.literal: It followed war and drought, when tax receipts were still scant; Zong fixed the ritual regalia, frugal yet conforming to the rites.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After years of war and drought, when revenue was still scarce, Zong set the ritual regalia, keeping it frugal yet within proper bounds.

manualTranslations.zh: 無何，萬年丞源邃為京兆尹李齊運所抑捽至死，縱劾奏不行。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long, Yuan Sui, assistant magistrate of Wannian, was crushed to death by oppression from Jingzhao Intendant Li Qiyun; Zong's impeachment memorial was not acted upon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuan Sui, assistant magistrate of Wannian, was crushed to death under oppression by Jingzhao Intendant Li Qiyun; Zong submitted an impeachment, but no action was taken.

manualTranslations.zh: 數月，除吏部侍郎，尋檢校禮部尚書、東畿唐汝鄧都觀察使、河南尹。
manualTranslations.literal: Several months later he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel; soon he was made acting Minister of Rites, metropolitan observer of the Tang-Ru-Deng circuit in the eastern capital region, and Prefect of Henan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Several months later he was made vice minister of personnel; soon he was also acting minister of rites, metropolitan observer of the Tang-Ru-Deng circuit in the eastern capital region, and prefect of Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時兵革甫定，民耗六七，縱悉心求瘼，為理簡易。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time warfare had only just ended and the people were depleted by six or seven tenths; Zong devoted himself to seeking out their hardships and governed with simple, straightforward methods.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Warfare had only just ended and the people were depleted by six or seven tenths; Zong devoted himself to finding their hardships and governed with simple, straightforward methods.

manualTranslations.zh: 先是，戍邊之師由洛陽者，儲餼取辦於編戶。
manualTranslations.literal: Previously, frontier garrison troops passing through Luoyang had their provisions supplied by levies on registered households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Previously, troops garrisoning the frontiers who passed through Luoyang had their provisions supplied by levies on registered households.

manualTranslations.zh: 縱始官備，不征於人，令五家相保，俾自占告發斂，以絕胥吏之私。
manualTranslations.literal: Zong first made official provisioning complete and levied nothing from the people; he ordered households to form groups of five for mutual guarantee and to declare and collect among themselves, thereby cutting off private exactions by clerks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zong established full official provisioning and levied nothing from the people; he required households to form groups of five for mutual guarantee and to declare and collect among themselves, cutting off private exactions by clerks.

manualTranslations.zh: 又引伊、洛水以通里閈，都中灌溉濟不逮為十一二，人甚安之。
manualTranslations.literal: He also drew the Yi and Luo rivers to connect the lanes and alleys; irrigation within the capital helped those unable to reach water in eleven or twelve cases out of ten, and the people were greatly put at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also diverted the Yi and Luo rivers to reach the lanes and alleys; irrigation within the capital helped those who could not otherwise reach water in eleven or twelve cases out of ten, and the people were greatly reassured.

manualTranslations.zh: 徵拜太常卿。
manualTranslations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed minister of ceremonies.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞元七年六月卒官，年六十二，謚曰忠，贈吏部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Zhenyuan he died in office at age sixty-two; his posthumous title was Zhong, and he was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Zhenyuan (791) he died in office at age sixty-two; his posthumous title was Zhong (Loyal), and he was posthumously made minister of personnel.

sourceRange.text: 襄州將士康楚元、張嘉延率眾為亂，陷荊、襄、澧、朗等州，以光遠兼御史大夫，持節荊襄招討，仍充山南東道處置兵馬都使。三年，除鳳翔尹，充本府及秦隴觀察使。先是，岐、隴吏人郭愔等為土賊，掠州縣，為五堡，光遠使判官、監察御史嚴侁召而降之。光遠在官好蒱酒，晚年不親戎事。上元元年冬，愔等潛連黨項及奴剌、突厥敗韋倫於秦、隴，殺監軍使，擊黃戍。肅宗追還，以李鼎代之。二年，兼成都尹，充劍南節度營田觀察處置使，仍兼御史大夫。及段子璋反，東川節度使李奐敗走，投光遠，率將花驚定等討平之。將士肆其剽劫，婦女有金銀臂釧，兵士皆斷其腕以取之，亂殺數千人，光遠不能禁。肅宗遣監軍官使按其罪，光遠憂恚成疾，上元二年十月卒。

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ruoshui was Qi Wu's clansman cousin. He rose through repeated promotions to General of the Left Golden Guards and was concurrently Attendant for Diplomatic Correspondence.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: His appearance was very imposing. He spent thirty years in the hostel, knew many old protocols, and whenever he announced congratulations and guided ceremonies, his turning and bowing were something worth watching.

sourceRange.text: 廣德初，吐蕃寇長安。晉卿時病臥於私第，蕃聞之，輿入逼脅，晉卿閉口不言，賊不敢害。及上自陜至，冊為太保，罷知政事，又詔以太保致仕。永泰元年四月薨。輟朝三日，令京兆少尹一員護喪事，緣葬諸物並官給，賻絹布五百段、米粟五百石。太常議謚曰「懿獻」。初，晉卿東都留守，引用大理評事元載為推官。至是載為中書侍郎、平章事，懷舊恩，諷有司改謚曰文貞。大歷七年，令配享肅宗廟庭。

context.beforeSource: 歷三朝，皆以謹密見稱。
context.afterSource: 裴冕，河東人也，為河東冠族。

manualTranslations.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃寇長安。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde, the Tibetans raided Chang'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangde era the Tibetans attacked Chang'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉卿時病臥於私第，蕃聞之，輿入逼脅，晉卿閉口不言，賊不敢害。
manualTranslations.literal: Jinqing at the time lay ill in his private residence; the Tibetans heard of it, entered by litter to coerce him, Jinqing closed his mouth and did not speak, and the bandits did not dare harm him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jinqing lay ill at home; the Tibetans heard of him, came in a litter to coerce him, but he kept silent and they did not dare harm him.

manualTranslations.zh: 及上自陜至，冊為太保，罷知政事，又詔以太保致仕。
manualTranslations.literal: When the Emperor came from Shaan, Jinqing was enfeoffed as Grand Guardian, ceased knowing administration, and was again ordered to retire as Grand Guardian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Shaan, Jinqing was made grand guardian, relieved of government, and again ordered to retire with that title.

manualTranslations.zh: 永泰元年四月薨。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongtai he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Yongtai 1 (765).

manualTranslations.zh: 輟朝三日，令京兆少尹一員護喪事，緣葬諸物並官給，賻絹布五百段、米粟五百石。
manualTranslations.literal: Court was suspended three days; one Junior Administrator of the Capital was ordered to oversee funeral affairs; all items connected with burial were supplied by the state; condolence gifts were five hundred lengths of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Court mourning lasted three days; a junior capital official was assigned to oversee the funeral; all burial expenses were paid by the state, with five hundred lengths of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain as condolence gifts.

manualTranslations.zh: 太常議謚曰「懿獻」。
manualTranslations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated and gave the posthumous title "Yi-xian."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous name Yi-xian ("Reverent and Dedicated").

manualTranslations.zh: 初，晉卿東都留守，引用大理評事元載為推官。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, when Jinqing was Eastern Capital Retention Officer, he brought in Yuan Zai, Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as investigating officer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jinqing was eastern capital guardian, he had appointed Yuan Zai, an assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as his investigating officer.

manualTranslations.zh: 至是載為中書侍郎、平章事，懷舊恩，諷有司改謚曰文貞。
manualTranslations.literal: By this time Zai was Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-ordinating Minister; cherishing old grace, he hinted to the responsible offices to change the posthumous title to Wen-zhen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By then Yuan Zai was vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister; remembering old kindness, he prompted the authorities to change the posthumous name to Wen-zhen ("Cultured and Upright").

manualTranslations.zh: 大歷七年，令配享肅宗廟庭。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali, he was ordered to share sacrifice in Suzong's temple court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Dali 7 (772) he was ordered to share sacrifices in Suzong's temple.

sourceRange.text: 衛伯玉，有膂力，幼習藝。天寶中杖劍之安西，以邊功累遷至員外諸衛將軍。肅宗即位，興師靖難，伯玉激憤，思立功名，自安西歸長安。初為神策軍兵馬使出鎮。乾元二年十月，逆賊史思明遣偽將李歸仁鐵騎三千來犯，伯玉以數百騎於疆子阪擊破之，積屍滿野，虜馬六百匹，歸仁與其黨東走。以功遷右羽林軍大將軍，知軍事。轉四鎮、北庭行營節度使。獻俘百余人至闕下，詔解縛而赦之，遷伯玉神策軍節度。上元二年二月，史思明領眾西下圖長安，史朝義率其黨夜襲陜州。伯玉以兵逆擊，大破賊於永寧。賊退，進位特進，封河東郡公。

manualTranslations.zh: 衛伯玉，有膂力，幼習藝。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei Boyu had great physical strength and from childhood practiced martial arts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei Boyu was powerfully built and had practiced martial arts since childhood.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寶中杖劍之安西，以邊功累遷至員外諸衛將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: During the Tianbao era he went armed to Anxi and, through frontier achievements, was repeatedly promoted until he reached Honorary General of the Imperial Guards.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he went armed to Anxi and, through frontier achievements, was repeatedly promoted until he reached honorary general of the imperial guards.

manualTranslations.zh: 肅宗即位，興師靖難，伯玉激憤，思立功名，自安西歸長安。
manualTranslations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne and raised an army to quell the rebellion, Boyu was stirred with indignation, eager to achieve merit and fame, and returned from Anxi to Chang'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Suzong ascended the throne and raised an army to quell the rebellion, Boyu burned with indignation, eager to win merit and fame, and returned from Anxi to Chang'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 初為神策軍兵馬使出鎮。
manualTranslations.literal: At first he served as army commissioner of the Shence Army and went out to garrison command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first he served as army commissioner of the Shence Army and took up a garrison command.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾元二年十月，逆賊史思明遣偽將李歸仁鐵騎三千來犯，伯玉以數百騎於疆子阪擊破之，積屍滿野，虜馬六百匹，歸仁與其黨東走。
manualTranslations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Qianyuan, the rebel Shi Siming dispatched the false general Li Guiren with three thousand iron cavalry to attack; Boyu with several hundred horsemen defeated them at Jiangzi Slope. Corpses piled the fields, six hundred enemy horses were captured, and Guiren fled east with his followers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 759 the rebel Shi Siming sent the false general Li Guiren with three thousand armored cavalry to attack. Boyu met them with several hundred horsemen at Jiangzi Slope and routed them. Corpses covered the ground, six hundred horses were captured, and Guiren fled east with his followers.

manualTranslations.zh: 以功遷右羽林軍大將軍，知軍事。
manualTranslations.literal: For this merit he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Pulin Army, overseeing military affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For this merit he was made grand general of the Right Pulin Army, overseeing military affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 轉四鎮、北庭行營節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: He was then made Military Governor of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign headquarters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was then made military governor of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign headquarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 獻俘百余人至闕下，詔解縛而赦之，遷伯玉神策軍節度。
manualTranslations.literal: He presented more than a hundred captives at the palace gates; an edict ordered their bonds removed and pardoned them, and Boyu was transferred to military commissioner of the Shence Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He presented more than a hundred captives at court; an edict ordered their bonds removed and granted them pardon, and Boyu was made military commissioner of the Shence Army.

manualTranslations.zh: 上元二年二月，史思明領眾西下圖長安，史朝義率其黨夜襲陜州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shangyuan, Shi Siming led his masses west to strike at Chang'an; Shi Chaoyi led his followers in a night raid on Shan prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second month of 761 Shi Siming led his forces west to threaten Chang'an, and Shi Chaoyi led his followers in a night raid on Shan prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 伯玉以兵逆擊，大破賊於永寧。
manualTranslations.literal: Boyu met the attack with troops and utterly defeated the rebels at Yongning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Boyu met the attack with troops and routed the rebels at Yongning.

manualTranslations.zh: 賊退，進位特進，封河東郡公。
manualTranslations.literal: When the rebels withdrew, he was advanced to Special Grand Master and enfeoffed Duke of Hedong commandery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew, he was advanced to special grand master and enfeoffed duke of Hedong commandery.

sourceRange.text: 既退，復上封論備吐蕃利害，曰：朔方，國之北門，西禦犬戎，北虞獫狁，五城相去三千餘里。開元、天寶中，戰士十萬，戰馬三萬，才敵一隅。自先皇帝龍飛靈武，戰士從陛下收復兩京，東西南北，曾無寧歲。中年以僕固之役，又經耗散，人亡三分之二，比於天寶中有十分之一。今吐蕃充斥，勢強十倍，兼河、隴之地，雜羌、渾之眾，每歲來窺近郊。以朔方減十倍之軍，當吐蕃加十倍之騎，欲求制勝，豈易為力！入近內地，稱四節度，每將盈萬，每賊兼乘數四。臣所統將士，不當賊四分之一，所有征馬，不當賊百分之二，誠合固守，不宜與戰。又得馬璘牒，賊擬涉渭而南。臣若堅壁，恐犯畿甸；若過畿內，則國人大恐，諸道易搖。外有吐蕃之強，中有易搖之眾，外畏內懼，將何以安？臣伏以陛下橫制勝之術，力非不足，但慮簡練未精，進退未一，時淹師老，地闊勢分。願陛下更詢讜議，慎擇名將，俾之統軍，於諸道各抽精卒，成四五萬，則制勝之道必矣，未可失時。臣又料河南、河北、山南、江淮小鎮數千，大鎮數萬，空耗月餼，曾不習戰。臣請抽赴關中，教之戰陣，則軍聲益振，攻守必全，亦長久之計也。臣猥蒙任遇，垂二十年，今齒發已衰，願避賢路，止足不誡，神明所鑒。詔曰：「卿憂深虛遠，殊沃朕心，始終倚賴，未可執辭也。

sourceRange.text: 六月十四日薨，時年八十五，德宗聞之震悼，廢朝五日，詔曰：天地以四時成物，元首以股肱作輔，公臺之任，鼎足相承，上以調三光，下以蒙五嶽。允釐庶績，鎮撫四夷，體元和之氣，根貞一之德，功至大而不伐，身處高而更安。尚父比呂望之名，為師增周公之位，盛業可久，歿而彌光。故太尉、兼中書令、上柱國、汾陽郡王、尚父子儀，天降人傑，生知王佐，訓師如子，料敵若神。昔天寶多難，羯胡作禍，咸秦失險，河洛為戎。公能扶翼肅宗，載造區夏。於國有患，勞其戡定；於邊有寇，藉其驅除。安社稷必在於絳侯，定羌戎無逾於充國。絳臺綏四散之眾，涇陽降十萬之虜。勛高今古，名璟夷狄，而勞乎征鎮，二紀於茲。

sourceRange.text: 子儀聞之，因兵部侍郎張重光宣慰回，附章論奏曰：臣聞雍州之地，古稱天府，右探隴、蜀，左扼崤、函，前有終南、太華之險，後有清渭、濁河之固，神明之奧，王者所都。地方數千里，帶甲十餘萬，兵強士勇，雄視八方，有利則出攻，無利則入守。此用武之國，非諸夏所同，秦、漢因之，卒成帝業。其後或處之而泰，去之而亡，前史所書，不唯一姓。及隋氏季末，煬帝南遷，河、洛丘墟，兵戈亂起。高祖唱義，亦先入關，惟能翦滅奸雄，底定區宇。以至於太宗、高宗之盛，中宗、玄宗之明，多在秦川，鮮居東洛。間者羯胡構亂，九服分崩，河北、河南，盡從逆命。然而先帝仗朔方之眾，慶緒奔亡；陛下藉西土之師，朝義就戮。豈唯天道助順，抑亦地形使然，此陛下所知，非臣飾說。近因吐蕃淩逼，鑾駕東巡。蓋以六軍之兵，素非精練，皆市肆屠沽之人，務掛虛名，茍避征賦，及驅以就戰，百無一堪。亦有潛輸貨財，因以求免。又中官掩蔽，庶政多荒。遂令陛下振蕩不安，退居陜服。斯蓋關於委任失所，豈可謂秦地非良者哉！今道路云云，不知信否，咸謂陛下已有成命，將幸洛都。臣熟思其端，未見其利。夫以東周之地，久陷賊中，宮室焚燒，十不存一。百曹荒廢，曾無尺椽，中間畿內，不滿千戶。井邑榛荊，豺狼站嗥，既乏軍儲，又鮮人力，東至鄭、汴，達於徐方，北自覃懷，經於相土，人煙斷絕，千里蕭條。將何以奉萬乘之牲餼，供百官之次舍？矧其土地狹厄，才數百里間，東有成臯，南有二室，險不足恃，適為戰場。陛下奈何棄久安之勢，從至危之策，忽社稷之計，生天下之心。臣雖至愚，竊為陛下不取。且聖旨所慮，豈不以京畿新遭剽掠，田野空虛，恐糧食不充，國用有闕，以臣所見，深謂不然。昔衛文小國之君，諸侯之主耳，遭懿公為狄所滅，始廬於曹，衣大布之衣，冠大帛之冠，元年革車三十乘，季年三百乘，卒能恢復舊業，享無疆之休。況明明天子，躬儉節用，茍能黜素餐之吏，去冗食之官，抑豎刁、易牙之權，任蘧瑗、史䲡之直，薄征馳力，恤隱迨鰥，委諸相以簡賢任能，付老臣以練兵禦侮，則黎元自理，寇盜自平，中興之功，旬月可冀，卜年之期，永永無極矣。願時邁順動，回鑾上都，再造邦家，唯新庶政，奉宗廟以修薦享，謁陵寢以崇孝思，臣雖隕越，死無所恨。

sourceRange.text: 元和十五年，穆宗即位，尊郭妃為皇太后，詔曰：「追遠飾終，先王令典。況積仁累義，事已顯於身前；祥會慶傳，福遂流於天下。式光盛德，爰舉徽章，尊尊親親，於是乎在。皇太后父贈尚書左僕射曖，克荷崇構，有勞王家，孝友本於生知，英華發於事任，實修一德，歷仕三朝。建中末年，屬有大難，畢力扈駕，忘軀即戎，忠貞之節，國史明備。才高望洽，是膺沁水之祥；德厚流光，乃啟塗山之祚。肆予小子，獲纘大業，未展定申之命，敢緣褒紀之恩，俾繼維師，用不縟禮。可贈太傅。」曖子釗、鏦、銛。

sourceRange.text: 子儀不受，復上表曰：臣伏以尚書令，武德之際，太宗為之，昨瀝懇上陳，請罷斯職；而陛下未垂亮察，務欲褒崇，區區微誠，益用惶懼。何則？太宗立極之主，聖德在人，自後因廢此官，永代作則。陛下守文繼體，固當奉而行之，豈可猥私老臣，隳厥成式，上掩陛下之德，下貽萬方之非。臣雖至愚，安敢輕受？況久經兵亂，僭賞者多，一人之身，兼官數四，朱紫同色，清濁不分，「爛羊」之謠，復聞聖代。臣頃觀其弊，思革其源，以逆寇猶存，未敢輕議。今元兇沮敗，計日成擒，中外無虞，妖氛漸息。此陛下作法之際，審官之時，固合始於老臣，化及班列。豈可輕為此舉，以亂國章？國章亂於上，則庶政隳於下，海內之政皆亂，則國家又安得永代而無患哉！陛下茍能從臣之言，俯察誠請，彼貪榮冒進者，亦將各讓其所兼之官，自然天下文明，百工式敘，太平之業，可得而復也。臣誠蒙鄙，識昧古今，志之所切，實在於此。手詔答曰：「優崇之命，所以報功；總領之司，期於賦政。卿入居臺鉉，出統戎旃，爰自先朝，累匡多難，靖群氛於海表，凝庶績於天階。敏事而寡言，居敬而行簡，人難其易，爾易其難。所以命掌六聯，首茲百辟，顧循時議，僉謂允諧。而屢拜封章，懇懷讓揖，守淳素之道，語政理之源，無待禮成，曲從德讓。宜宣示於外，編之史冊。」遣內侍魚朝恩傳詔，賜美人盧氏等六人、從者八人，並車服、帷帳、床蓐、珍玩之具。

sourceRange.text: 子儀既謝恩，上表進肅宗所賜前後詔敕，因自陳訴曰：臣德薄蟬翼，命輕鴻毛，累蒙國恩，猥廁朝列。會天地震蕩，中原血戰，臣北自靈武，冊先皇帝，乃舉兵而南，大搜於岐陽。先帝憂勤宗社，托臣以家國，俾副陛下掃兩京之妖昆。陛下雄圖丕斷，再造區宇，自後不以臣寡劣，委文武之二柄，外敷邦教，內調鼎飪，是以常許國家之死，實荷日月之明。臣本愚淺，言多詆直，慮此招謗，上瀆冕旒。陛下居高聽卑，察臣不貳，皇天後土，察臣無私。伏以器忌滿盈，日增兢惕，焉敢偷全，久妨賢路？自受恩塞下，制敵行間，東西十年，前後百戰。天寒劍折，濺血沾衣；野宿魂驚，飲冰傷骨。跋涉難阻，出沒死生，所仗唯天，以至今日。陛下曲申惠獎，念及勤勞，貽臣詔書一千餘首，聖旨微婉，慰諭綢繆，彰微臣一時之功，成子孫萬代之寶。自靈武、河北、河南、彭原、鄜坊、河東、鳳翔、兩京、絳州，臣所經行，賜手詔敕書凡二十卷，昧死上進，庶煩聽覽。詔答曰：「朕不德不明，俾大臣憂疑，朕之過也。朕甚自愧，公勿以為慮。」代宗以子儀頃同患難，收復兩京，禮之逾厚。

sourceRange.text: 永泰元年五月，嚴武卒，杜濟為西川行軍司馬，權知軍府事。時郭英幹為都知兵馬使，郭嘉琳為都虞候，皆請英幹兄英乂為節度使。旰時為西山都知兵馬使，與軍眾共請大將王崇俊為節度使。二奏俱至京師，會朝廷已除英乂，旰使因見英乂陳其事。英乂至成都，數日，誣殺王崇俊，又召旰還成都。英乂減將健糧賜，人心怨怒。旰在西山聞之，大恐，乃托備吐蕃，未赴成都。英乂怒，出兵聲言助旰討吐蕃，其實襲之也。旰家在漢州，英乂遷之成都，通其妾媵。旰知之，轉入深山。英乂自率師攻旰，值天大寒，雪深數尺，英乂士馬凍死者數百人，眾心離叛。旰遂出兵拒敵，英乂與之接戰，英乂軍大敗而還，收余兵才千人，歸成都，將卒因多逃散。

sourceRange.text: 王昂者，出自戎旅，以軍功累遷河中尹，充河中節度使。貪縱不法，務於聚斂，以貨籓身。永泰元年正月，檢校刑部尚書知省事，改殿中少監。元載秉政，與載深相結托。大曆五年六月，為江陵尹、兼御史大夫，充荊南節度觀察使，代衛伯玉。昂既行，伯玉諷大將楊𨨫等拒昂，乞留伯玉，詔許之。昂復檢校刑部尚書，知省事。專事奢靡，廣修第宅，多畜妓妾，以逞其誌。在刑部，雖公務有程，昂耽徇私宴，連日不視曹事。性貪吝，無愧茍得，乃鬻公廨園菜，收其錢以潤屋，甚為時論所醜。元載誅，貶連州刺史，遣中使監至萬州，過硤江，墜江而卒。

context.beforeSource: 以載籍沒鐘乳五百兩分賜中書門下御史臺五品已上、尚書省四品已上。
context.afterSource: 李少良者，以吏用，早從使幕，因職遷殿中侍御史。

manualTranslations.zh: 王昂者，出自戎旅，以軍功累遷河中尹，充河中節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Ang came from the military ranks; through military merit he was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Hezhong and served as military commissioner of Hezhong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ang came from the military ranks; through military merit he rose to prefect of Hezhong and military commissioner of Hezhong.

manualTranslations.zh: 貪縱不法，務於聚斂，以貨籓身。
manualTranslations.literal: Greedy and unrestrained in lawlessness, he devoted himself to amassing wealth and used goods to secure his post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Greedy and lawless, he devoted himself to amassing wealth and used bribes to secure his post.

manualTranslations.zh: 永泰元年正月，檢校刑部尚書知省事，改殿中少監。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yongtai he was acting minister of justice directing office affairs, then changed to vice director of the Palace Domestic Service.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongtai 1 (765) he was acting minister of justice directing office affairs, then became vice director of the Palace Domestic Service.

manualTranslations.zh: 元載秉政，與載深相結托。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yuan Zai held power, Ang formed a deep bond with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai held power, Ang formed a deep alliance with him.

manualTranslations.zh: 大曆五年六月，為江陵尹、兼御史大夫，充荊南節度觀察使，代衛伯玉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Dali he became prefect of Jiangling, concurrent censor-in-chief, and Jingnan military commissioner and investigating commissioner, replacing Wei Boyu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Dali 5 (770) he became prefect of Jiangling, concurrent censor-in-chief, and Jingnan military commissioner and investigating commissioner, replacing Wei Boyu.

manualTranslations.zh: 昂既行，伯玉諷大將楊𨨫等拒昂，乞留伯玉，詔許之。
manualTranslations.literal: After Ang had set out, Boyu prompted the great generals Yang Kui and others to resist Ang and beg that Boyu be kept; an edict approved this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Ang had set out, Boyu prompted the great generals Yang Kui and others to resist him and petitioned that Boyu be retained; the emperor approved.

manualTranslations.zh: 昂復檢校刑部尚書，知省事。
manualTranslations.literal: Ang again became acting minister of justice directing office affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ang again became acting minister of justice directing office affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 專事奢靡，廣修第宅，多畜妓妾，以逞其誌。
manualTranslations.literal: He devoted himself to luxury, built mansions on a grand scale, and kept many courtesans and concubines to indulge his desires.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to luxury, built mansions on a grand scale, and kept many courtesans to indulge his desires.

manualTranslations.zh: 在刑部，雖公務有程，昂耽徇私宴，連日不視曹事。
manualTranslations.literal: While in the Ministry of Justice, though public business had its schedule, Ang indulged in private feasts and for days on end did not attend to bureau affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While in the Ministry of Justice, though public business had its schedule, Ang indulged in private feasts and for days on end ignored bureau affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 性貪吝，無愧茍得，乃鬻公廨園菜，收其錢以潤屋，甚為時論所醜。
manualTranslations.literal: By nature greedy and stingy, he felt no shame in grasping what he could; he even sold the vegetables from the government office garden and took the money to enrich his house—a thing much despised in public opinion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By nature greedy and stingy, he felt no shame in grasping what he could; he even sold vegetables from the government office garden and used the money to enrich his house—a thing much despised in public opinion.

manualTranslations.zh: 元載誅，貶連州刺史，遣中使監至萬州，過硤江，墜江而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: When Yuan Zai was executed, Ang was demoted to prefect of Lian Prefecture; a palace envoy was sent to escort him under supervision to Wan Prefecture. Crossing the Xia River, he fell into the river and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai was executed, Ang was demoted to prefect of Lian Prefecture; a palace envoy was sent to escort him under supervision to Wan Prefecture. Crossing the Xia River, he fell into the river and drowned.

sourceRange.text: 貓能致功，鼠不爲害。

localRange.text: 貓能致功，鼠不為害。

context.beforeSource: 若以劉向《五行傳》論之，恐須申命憲司，察聽貪吏，誡諸邊候，無失僥巡。
context.afterSource: 代宗深嘉之。

sourceRange.text: 常袞，京兆人也。父無爲，三原縣丞，以袞累贈僕射。袞，天寶末舉進士，歴太子正字，累授補闕、起居郎。寶應二年，選爲翰林學士、考功員外郎中、知制誥，依前翰林學士。永泰元年，遷中書舍人。袞文章俊拔，當時推重，與楊炎同爲舍人，時稱爲常、楊。性淸直孤潔，不妄交遊。内侍魚朝恩恃權寵，兼領國子監事，袞上疎以爲不可。時朝廷多事，西北邊虜，連爲寇盜，袞累上章陳其利害，代宗甚顧遇之，加集賢院學士。大歴元年，遷禮部侍郎，仍爲學士。時中官劉忠翼權傾内外，涇原節度馬璘又累著功勛，恩寵莫二，各有親戚干貢部及求爲兩館生，袞皆執理，人皆畏之。

context.beforeSource: 子巖，登進士第，辟襄陽掌書記、監察御史，方雅有父風。
context.afterSource: 元載之得罪，令袞與劉晏、李涵等鞫之，獄竟，拜袞門下侍郎、同平章事，太淸、太微宮使，崇文、弘文館大學士，與楊綰同掌樞務。

manualTranslations.zh: 常袞，京兆人也。
manualTranslations.literal: Chang Gun was a native of Jingzhao.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chang Gun was a native of Jingzhao.

manualTranslations.zh: 父無爲，三原縣丞，以袞累贈僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Wuwei was assistant magistrate of Sanyuan county; because of Gun he was posthumously granted Vice Director.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Wuwei was assistant magistrate of Sanyuan county; because of Gun he was posthumously granted the title of vice director.

manualTranslations.zh: 袞，天寶末舉進士，歴太子正字，累授補闕、起居郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Gun, at the end of Tianbao passed the jinshi examination, served as Rectifier of Texts for the Heir Apparent, and was successively appointed remonstrance official and Attendant of the Imperial Diary.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gun passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Tianbao era, served as Rectifier of Texts for the Heir Apparent, and was successively appointed remonstrance official and Attendant of the Imperial Diary.

manualTranslations.zh: 寶應二年，選爲翰林學士、考功員外郎中、知制誥，依前翰林學士。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Baoying he was selected as Hanlin academician, acting external vacancy director in the Bureau of Appointments, and charged with drafting edicts, retaining his prior Hanlin status.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Baoying 2 he was selected as Hanlin academician, acting external vacancy director in the Bureau of Appointments, and charged with drafting edicts, retaining his Hanlin status.

manualTranslations.zh: 永泰元年，遷中書舍人。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was transferred to drafter of the Central Secretariat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 he was transferred to drafter of the Central Secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 袞文章俊拔，當時推重，與楊炎同爲舍人，時稱爲常、楊。
manualTranslations.literal: Gun's literary compositions were brilliant and outstanding; at the time he was highly esteemed; together with Yang Yan he served as drafters, and they were called Chang and Yang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gun's writings were brilliant and outstanding, and he was highly esteemed at court; serving as drafters together with Yang Yan, they were known as Chang and Yang.

manualTranslations.zh: 性淸直孤潔，不妄交遊。
manualTranslations.literal: By nature he was pure, upright, aloof, and fastidious, not making acquaintances lightly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By nature he was pure, upright, aloof, and fastidious, and did not make acquaintances lightly.

manualTranslations.zh: 内侍魚朝恩恃權寵，兼領國子監事，袞上疎以爲不可。
manualTranslations.literal: Palace eunuch Yu Cha'en relied on power and favor and also superintended the Directorate of Education; Gun submitted a memorial saying this was not permissible.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Yu Cha'en relied on power and favor and also headed the Directorate of Education; Gun submitted a memorial arguing that this was improper.

manualTranslations.zh: 時朝廷多事，西北邊虜，連爲寇盜，袞累上章陳其利害，代宗甚顧遇之，加集賢院學士。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the court faced many affairs; on the northwestern borders the barbarians repeatedly raided as bandits; Gun repeatedly submitted memorials setting forth the advantages and harms, and Emperor Daizong greatly favored him, adding him as academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court then faced many pressing affairs, and on the northwestern frontier the barbarians repeatedly raided; Gun repeatedly submitted memorials on the advantages and harms involved, and Emperor Daizong greatly favored him, adding him as academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

manualTranslations.zh: 大歴元年，遷禮部侍郎，仍爲學士。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Dali he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Rites, retaining his academician status.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Dali 1 he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Rites while retaining his academician status.

manualTranslations.zh: 時中官劉忠翼權傾内外，涇原節度馬璘又累著功勛，恩寵莫二，各有親戚干貢部及求爲兩館生，袞皆執理，人皆畏之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the palace eunuch Liu Zhongyi's power dominated court and countryside, and Jingyuan military commissioner Ma Lin had also repeatedly achieved merit—no two shared equal favor; each had relatives who pressed the examination bureau and sought to become students of the two academies; Gun in every case upheld principle, and all feared him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time the palace eunuch Liu Zhongyi's power dominated court and countryside, and Jingyuan military commissioner Ma Lin had also repeatedly won distinction—no two enjoyed equal favor. Each had relatives who pressed the examination bureau and sought places as students of the two academies; Gun in every case upheld principle, and everyone feared him.

sourceRange.text: 至冬被疾，肩輿入中書，臥而承旨。或休假在第，大事必令中使咨決。薨時年六十，上甚悼惜之，廢朝三日，冊贈太傅，賻布帛米粟有差，諡曰文貞。無子，遺命猶子植爲嗣。有文集三十巻。故事，門下侍郎未嘗有贈三師者，德宗以祐甫謇謇有大臣節，故特寵異之。硃泚之亂，祐甫妻王氏陷于賊中，泚以嘗與祐甫同列，雅重其爲人，乃遺王氏繒帛菽粟，王氏受而緘封之，及德宗還京，具陳其狀以獻。士君子益重祐甫家法，宜其享令名也。

context.beforeSource: 祐甫謀猷啓沃，多所弘益，天下以爲可復貞觀、開元之太平也。
context.afterSource: 植字公修，祐甫弟廬江令嬰甫子。

manualTranslations.zh: 至冬被疾，肩輿入中書，臥而承旨。
manualTranslations.literal: By winter he fell ill; carried in a sedan chair into the Chancellery, he lay ill while receiving imperial instructions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By winter he fell ill; carried in a sedan chair into the Chancellery, he received imperial instructions while lying ill.

manualTranslations.zh: 或休假在第，大事必令中使咨決。
manualTranslations.literal: When he took leave at his residence, on major affairs the emperor always sent a palace envoy to consult him for decisions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he took leave at home, the emperor always sent a palace envoy to consult him on major affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 薨時年六十，上甚悼惜之，廢朝三日，冊贈太傅，賻布帛米粟有差，諡曰文貞。
manualTranslations.literal: He died at age sixty; the emperor greatly mourned and regretted it, suspended court three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor, granted funeral gifts of cloth, silks, rice, and grain in graded amounts, and gave the posthumous name Cultured and Upright.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died at age sixty. The emperor deeply mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor, granted funeral gifts of cloth, silks, rice, and grain in graded amounts, and gave him the posthumous name Cultured and Upright.

manualTranslations.zh: 無子，遺命猶子植爲嗣。
manualTranslations.literal: He had no sons and in his final wishes named his nephew-adopted son Zhi as heir.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had no sons and in his final wishes named his nephew Zhi as heir.

manualTranslations.zh: 有文集三十巻。
manualTranslations.literal: He left a collected works in thirty juan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He left collected works in thirty juan.

manualTranslations.zh: 故事，門下侍郎未嘗有贈三師者，德宗以祐甫謇謇有大臣節，故特寵異之。
manualTranslations.literal: By precedent, vice directors of the Chancellery had never been posthumously granted the Three Preceptor titles; Dezong, because Youfu was forthright and possessed a chief minister's integrity, therefore especially favored and distinguished him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By precedent, vice directors of the Chancellery had never been posthumously granted the Three Preceptor titles; Dezong, because Youfu was forthright and possessed a chief minister's integrity, therefore especially honored him.

manualTranslations.zh: 硃泚之亂，祐甫妻王氏陷于賊中，泚以嘗與祐甫同列，雅重其爲人，乃遺王氏繒帛菽粟，王氏受而緘封之，及德宗還京，具陳其狀以獻。
manualTranslations.literal: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Youfu's wife Lady Wang was trapped among the rebels; Ci, because he had once served on the same council with Youfu and greatly respected his character, sent Lady Wang silks, cloth, beans, and grain; Lady Wang accepted them and sealed them away, and when Dezong returned to the capital she fully set forth the circumstances and presented them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Youfu's wife Lady Wang was trapped among the rebels. Ci, who had once served with Youfu on the council and greatly respected his character, sent Lady Wang silks, cloth, beans, and grain. Lady Wang accepted them and sealed them away, and when Dezong returned to the capital she fully reported what had happened and presented the gifts.

manualTranslations.zh: 士君子益重祐甫家法，宜其享令名也。
manualTranslations.literal: Gentlemen of worth all the more esteemed Youfu's household discipline; it is fitting that he enjoyed a fine reputation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men of worth all the more esteemed Youfu's household discipline; it is fitting that he enjoyed a fine reputation.

sourceRange.text: 鏦，母升平長公主，大歷、貞元之間，恩禮冠諸主。順宗在東宮，以女德陽郡主尚鏦，時鏦與公主年未及冠，郡主尤為德宗之所鐘愛，故鏦之貴寵，焜燿一時。順宗即位，改封德陽為漢陽公主。鏦累官至衛尉卿、駙馬都尉，改殿中監。穆宗即位，鏦為叔舅，改右金吾衛大將軍、兼御史大夫，充左街使。城南有汾陽王別墅，林泉之致，莫之與比，穆宗常遊幸之，置酒極歡而罷，賜钅從甚厚。俄加檢校工部尚書，兼太子詹事，充閑廄宮苑使。從容貴位三十餘年，而椒房之寵，國舅之恩，近代已來，無有其比。而鏦恭遜虔恪，不以富貴驕人，士無賢不肖，接之以禮，由是中外稱之。長慶二年十月卒，贈尚書左僕射，仍以其弟銛代鏦為太子詹事，充閑廄宮苑使。

sourceRange.text: 又嘗撰《誕聖樂曲》以進，其表曰：臣聞於師，夫君子為能知樂，是故審音以知聲，審樂以知政，則理道備矣。清明廣大，終始周旋，與天地同其和，與四時合其序，豈止於鐘鼓管磬雲乎哉！臣伏見開元中天長節著於甲令，每於是日海縣歡娛，稱萬壽之無疆，樂一人之有慶，故能追堯接舜，邁禹逾湯，自周已後，不能議矣。臣竊以陛下降誕之辰，未有惟新之曲。雖太和已佈於六氣，而大樂未宣於八音，無乃臣子之分，或有所闕。愚臣不揆頑昧，敢思祖述，每思歌竊抃，忘寢與食久矣。適遇有知音者，與臣論及樂章，探微賾奧，窮理盡性，臣乃遣造《繼天誕聖樂》一曲。大抵以宮為調，表五音之奉君也；以土為德，知五運之居中也。凡二十五遍，法二十四氣而足成一歲也。每遍一十六拍，象八元、八凱登庸於朝也。所冀《雲門》、《咸池》，永傳於律呂，空桑、孤竹，合薦於宮懸，不聞沾滯之聲，長作中和之樂。可使九域之人，頓忘於肉味；四夷之俗，皆播於薰風。與唐惟休，終古盡善。臣不勝懇款屏營之至，謹昧死陳獻以聞。其所造譜，謹同封進。

sourceRange.text: 元和五年四月，制曰：邪以蓄眾，自致覆車；奸以事君，所宜用鉞。故楚人告變，韓信患釋於事先；蜀土征災，鐘會禍生於部下。況害深楚、蜀，功匪鐘、韓，構此厲階，佈於公議。懷私負德，合置於嚴科；屈法申恩，尚從於寬典。前昭義軍節度副大使、知節度事盧從史，擢自裨將，居於大籓，不思報國之誠，每設徇身之計。比丁家禍，曾無戚容，行棄人倫，孝虧大性。屬常山稱亂，朝制未行，固願興師，苟求復位。刻期效用，請以身先；指日投誠，誓雲獨致。示於懷撫，推以信誠。排眾論以釋其苴麻，決中心而授之鈇鉞，委以重任，命之專征。章奏所陳，事無違者；恩光是貸，予何愛焉。而乃冒利蓄奸，隳政敗度，成師既出，保敵而交通；邪計以行，臨戎而向背。諸侯盡力而不應，遺寇遊魂而是托。臣節既喪，恩豈念於生成；台位於求，禮頓虧於忠敬。肆其醜行，熾以凶威，至於逼脅軍中，潛施賊號；陵污麾下，實玷皇風。貨以籓身，虐而用眾，士庶怨而罔恤，將校勞而不圖。稟於陶鈞，行事至此，視於天地，負我何多，且辜覆載之仁，寧逭神鬼之責。況頃年上請，就食山東，及遣旋師，不時恭命，致動其眾，覬生其心，賴劉濟抗忠正之辭，使邪豎絕遲回之計。加以遍毀鄰境，密疏事情，反覆百端，高下萬變，心無恥愧，事至滿盈。朕念以始終，務於含貸，所期悔過，豈謂逾凶。而昭義軍忠節夙彰，義聲昭著，發其眾怒，葉以一心，顧大惡而不容，幸全軀而自免，宜從大戮，以正彝章。尚以曾列方隅，嘗經任使，惜君臣之體，抑中外之情，俾投魑魅之鄉，以解人神之憤。可貶驩州司馬。嗚呼！奸由事驗，自開棄絕之門；禍實己招，豈漏恢疏之網。凡百多士，宜諒朕懷。

sourceRange.text: 數年，代宗即位，召爲翰林學士，頗承恩遇。及元載輔政，惡其異己，因江南道觀察都團練使魏少游奏求參佐，稱泌有才，拜檢校秘書少監，充江南西道判官，幸其出也。尋改爲檢校郎中，依前判官。元載誅，乃馳傳入謁，上見悅之。又爲宰相常袞所忌，出爲楚州刺史。及謝恩，具陳戀闕，上素重之，留京數月。會澧州刺史闕，袞盛陳泌理行，以荊南凋瘵，遂輟泌理之。詔曰：「荊南都會，粵在澧陽，俾人歸厚，惟賢是牧。以泌文可以代成風俗，政可以全活惸嫠。爰命頒條，期乎共理，地薄淮陽之守，勉思渤海之功。可檢校御史中丞，充澧朗硤團練使。」重其禮而遣之。無幾，改杭州刺史，以理稱。

sourceRange.text: 使還，贄奏事曰：賊泚稽誅，保聚宮苑，勢窮援絕，引日偷生。懷光總仗順之軍，乘制勝之氣，鼓行芟翦，易若摧枯。而乃寇奔不追，師老不用，諸帥每欲進取，懷光輒沮其謀。據茲事情，殊不可解。陛下意在全護，委曲聽從，觀其所為，亦未知感。若不別為規略，漸相制持，唯以姑息求安，終恐變故難測。此誠事機危迫之秋也，故不可以尋常容易處之。今李晟奏請移軍，適遇臣銜命宣慰，懷光偶論此事，臣遂泛問所宜，懷光乃云：「李晟既欲別行，某亦都不要藉。」臣猶慮有翻覆，因美其軍強盛。懷光大自矜誇，轉有輕晟之意。臣又從容問云：「昨發離行在之日，未知有此商量；今日從此卻回，或恐聖旨顧問，事之可否，決定何如？」懷光已肆輕言，不可中變，遂云：「恩命許去，事亦無妨。」要約再三，非不詳審，雖欲追悔，固難為詞。伏望即以李晟表出付中書，敕下依奏，別賜懷光手詔，示以移軍事由。其手詔大意云：「昨得李晟奏，請移軍城東以分賊勢。朕緣未知利害，本欲委卿商量，適會陸贄從彼宣慰回，雲見卿論敘軍情，語及於此，仍言許去，事亦無妨，遂敕本軍允其所請。卿宜授以謀略，分路夾攻，務使葉齊，克平寇孽。」如此詞婉而直，理當而明，雖蓄異端，何由起怨？臣初奉使諭旨，本緣糧料不均，偶屬移軍，事相諧會。又幸懷光詭對，且無阻絕之言，機宜合並。若有幽贊，一失其便，後何可追，幸垂裁察！

manualTranslations.zh: 使還，贄奏事曰：賊泚稽誅，保聚宮苑，勢窮援絕，引日偷生。
manualTranslations.literal: When the envoy returned, Zhi reported on affairs, saying:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On his return Zhi reported to the throne:

manualTranslations.zh: 懷光總仗順之軍，乘制勝之氣，鼓行芟翦，易若摧枯。
manualTranslations.literal: Huai'guang commands armies that rely on righteousness, rides the breath of assured victory—drumming forward to mow and cut, easy as snapping dry wood.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huai'guang commands armies loyal to the throne and holds the advantage. He need only march forward to cut Zhu Ci down as easily as breaking dry wood.

manualTranslations.zh: 而乃寇奔不追，師老不用，諸帥每欲進取，懷光輒沮其謀。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet he does not pursue when the bandit flees; the army grows old and is not used; whenever the various commanders wish to advance, Huai'guang always thwarts their plans.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet he does not pursue the fleeing enemy. His army grows idle. Whenever the other commanders wish to advance, Huai'guang blocks them.

manualTranslations.zh: 據茲事情，殊不可解。
manualTranslations.literal: According to these circumstances, especially incomprehensible.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On these grounds his conduct is utterly inexplicable.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下意在全護，委曲聽從，觀其所為，亦未知感。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty's intent is to protect him wholly, following him with accommodation—observing his conduct, he also does not seem to know gratitude.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has sought to protect him and indulged his wishes, yet he shows no gratitude.

manualTranslations.zh: 若不別為規略，漸相制持，唯以姑息求安，終恐變故難測。
manualTranslations.literal: If you do not separately devise strategy and gradually restrain one another, seeking only ease through indulgence, in the end I fear unforeseen change will be hard to measure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Unless you adopt another strategy and gradually restrain him, seeking only temporary peace through indulgence, I fear an unforeseen crisis will arise.

manualTranslations.zh: 此誠事機危迫之秋也，故不可以尋常容易處之。
manualTranslations.literal: This is truly the season when the moment's opportunity is perilously pressing—therefore one cannot treat it with the ordinary and easy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is a moment of grave urgency and cannot be handled with ordinary ease.

manualTranslations.zh: 今李晟奏請移軍，適遇臣銜命宣慰，懷光偶論此事，臣遂泛問所宜，懷光乃云：「李晟既欲別行，某亦都不要藉。」
manualTranslations.literal: Now Li Sheng memorializes requesting to move the army; it happened to meet your servant bearing orders to proclaim comfort. Huai'guang chanced to discuss this matter; your servant then broadly asked what was fitting. Huai'guang then said: "Since Li Sheng wishes to march separately, I also need no support at all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Sheng has now asked to move his army. It happened that I was on mission to comfort the troops when Huai'guang raised the matter. I asked his view, and he said, "If Li Sheng wishes to march separately, I need no support from him at all.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣猶慮有翻覆，因美其軍強盛。
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant still feared reversal and therefore praised his army as strong and flourishing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fearing he might change his mind, I praised the strength of his army.

manualTranslations.zh: 懷光大自矜誇，轉有輕晟之意。
manualTranslations.literal: Huai'guang greatly prided himself and boasted, turning to have mind to slight Sheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huai'guang swelled with pride and showed contempt for Li Sheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣又從容問云：「昨發離行在之日，未知有此商量；
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant again calmly asked, saying: "When I set out leaving the mobile court yesterday, I did not know of this consultation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I then asked calmly, "When I left the imperial camp yesterday, this matter had not been discussed.

manualTranslations.zh: 今日從此卻回，或恐聖旨顧問，事之可否，決定何如？」
manualTranslations.literal: Today returning from here, I fear the sacred edict may inquire—whether the affair can be done or not, how is it decided?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If I return now, the emperor may inquire. Has the matter been decided, or not?

manualTranslations.zh: 懷光已肆輕言，不可中變，遂云：「恩命許去，事亦無妨。」
manualTranslations.literal: Huai'guang had already let loose light words and could not change midway; he then said: "If grace and command permit departure, the affair also has no obstacle."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huai'guang had spoken rashly and could not take it back. He said, "If the emperor permits it, there is no objection."

manualTranslations.zh: 要約再三，非不詳審，雖欲追悔，固難為詞。
manualTranslations.literal: The essential agreement was repeated three times—not inattentive or uncareful; though he wishes to regret and turn back, solidly it is hard to find words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He repeated his assent several times, clearly and deliberately. Though he may wish to retract it, he can hardly find words to do so.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏望即以李晟表出付中書，敕下依奏，別賜懷光手詔，示以移軍事由。
manualTranslations.literal: I humbly hope you will immediately take Li Sheng's memorial out and deliver it to the Secretariat, issue an edict down according to the memorial, and separately bestow on Huai'guang a handwritten edict showing the reasons for moving the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to send Li Sheng's memorial to the Secretariat, issue an edict approving it, and separately send Huai'guang a handwritten edict explaining the reasons for the troop movement.

manualTranslations.zh: 其手詔大意云：「昨得李晟奏，請移軍城東以分賊勢。
manualTranslations.literal: The handwritten edict's general sense would say: "Yesterday I received Li Sheng's memorial requesting to move the army east of the city to divide the bandits' power.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The handwritten edict might read in substance: "Yesterday I received Li Sheng's memorial asking to move his army east of the city to divide the rebel force.

manualTranslations.zh: 朕緣未知利害，本欲委卿商量，適會陸贄從彼宣慰回，雲見卿論敘軍情，語及於此，仍言許去，事亦無妨，遂敕本軍允其所請。
manualTranslations.literal: We, not yet knowing advantage and harm, originally wished to entrust this to you for consultation; it happened to meet Lu Zhi returning from proclaiming comfort there, who said he saw you discuss and narrate army sentiment, words reaching this point, still saying permission to go—the affair also has no obstacle—thereupon We ordered your original army to grant his request.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Not knowing the full implications, I meant to consult you. Lu Zhi has just returned from your camp and reports that in discussing the army's situation you agreed that Li Sheng's move would be acceptable. I have therefore ordered Li Sheng's request granted.

manualTranslations.zh: 卿宜授以謀略，分路夾攻，務使葉齊，克平寇孽。」
manualTranslations.literal: You should grant him strategy, divide routes and attack from both sides, strive to make efforts together, conquer and level the bandit spawn.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You should give him your counsel, attack by separate routes, and together destroy the rebels.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此詞婉而直，理當而明，雖蓄異端，何由起怨？
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the words are tactful yet direct, principle fitting yet clear—even if he harbors divergent intent, whence would resentment arise?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such words would be tactful yet direct, reasonable and clear. Even if he harbors disloyalty, how could he take offense?

manualTranslations.zh: 臣初奉使諭旨，本緣糧料不均，偶屬移軍，事相諧會。
manualTranslations.literal: When your servant first received mission to proclaim the intent, it was originally because of uneven grain rations; it happened to coincide with moving the army—the affairs harmoniously met.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My original mission concerned unequal rations. The question of moving troops arose by chance, and the two matters fell conveniently together.

manualTranslations.zh: 又幸懷光詭對，且無阻絕之言，機宜合並。
manualTranslations.literal: Also fortunately Huai'guang's crafty reply had no words of obstruction—the opportune moment should be joined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fortunately Huai'guang answered evasively and did not refuse outright. The opportunity should be seized at once.

manualTranslations.zh: 若有幽贊，一失其便，後何可追，幸垂裁察！
manualTranslations.literal: If there is hidden approval and one loses this convenience, afterward how can it be pursued? I hope you will deign to judge and examine!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Heaven favors us and we miss this chance, it cannot be recovered. I beg Your Majesty to decide!

sourceRange.text: 」贄論奏曰：臣實頑鄙，一無所堪，猥蒙任使，待罪宰相。雖懷竊位之懼，且乏知人之明，自揣庸虛，終難上報。唯知廣求才之路，使賢者各以匯征；啟至公之門，令職司皆得自達。既蒙允許，即宜宣行。南宮舉人，才至十數，或非臺省舊吏，則是使府佐僚，累經薦延，多歷事任。論其資望，既不愧於班行；考其行能，又未聞於闕敗。遽以騰口，上煩聖聰，道之難行，亦可知矣！陛下勤求理道，務徇物情，因謂舉薦非宜，復委宰臣揀擇。其為崇任輔弼，博采輿詞，可謂聖德之盛者。然於委任責成之道，聽言考實之方，閑邪存誠，猶恐有闕。陛下既納臣言而用之，旋聞橫議而止之，於臣謀不責成，於橫議不考實，此乃謀失者得以辭其罪，議曲者得以肆其誣。率是而行，觸類而長，固無必定之計，亦無必實之言。計不定則理道難成，言不實則小人得誌。國家之病，常必由之。昔齊桓公問管仲害霸之事，對曰：「得賢不能任，害霸也；用而不能終，害霸也；與賢人謀事，而與小人議之，害霸也。」為小人者，不必悉懷險诐，故覆邦家。蓋以其意性回邪，趣向狹促，以沮議為出眾，以自異為不群，趨近利而昧遠圖，效小信而傷大道，況又言行難保，恣其非心者乎！伏以宰輔，常制不過數人，人之所知，固有限極，不有遍諳諸士，備閱群才。若令悉命群官，理須展轉詢訪，是則變公舉為私薦，易明易攵為暗投。儻如議者之言，所舉多有情故，舉於君上，且未絕私；薦於宰臣，安肯無詐！失人之弊，必又甚焉。所以承前命官，罕有不涉私謗，雖則秉鈞不一，或自行情，亦由私訪所親，轉為所賣。其弊非遠，聖鑒明知。今又將徇浮言，專任宰臣除吏，宰臣不遍諳識，踵前須訪於人。若訪親朋，則是悔其覆車，不易故轍；若訪於朝列，則是求其私薦，不如公舉之愈也。二者利害，惟陛下更詳擇焉。恐不如委任長官，慎揀僚屬，所揀既少，所求亦精，得賢有鑒識之名，失實當暗謬之責。人之常性，莫不愛身，況於臺省長官，皆是當朝華選，孰肯徇私妄舉，以傷名取責者耶！所謂臺省長官，即僕射、尚書、左右丞、侍郎及御史大夫、中丞是也。陛下比擇輔相，多亦出於其中。今之宰臣，則往日臺省長官也；今之臺省長官，乃將來之宰臣也，但是職名暫異，固非行業頓殊。豈有為長官之時不能舉一二屬吏，居宰臣之位則可擇千百具僚，物議悠悠，其惑斯甚。夫求才貴廣，考課貴精。求廣在於各舉所知，長吏之薦擇是也；貴精在於按名責實，宰臣之序進是也。往者則天太后踐祚臨朝，欲收人心，尤務拔擢，弘委任之意，開汲引之門，進用不疑，求訪無倦，非但人得薦士，亦許自舉其才。所薦必行，所舉輒試，其於選士之道，豈不傷於容易哉！而課責既嚴，進退皆速，不肖者旋黜，才能者驟升，是以當代謂知人之明，累朝賴多士之用。此乃近於求才貴廣，考課貴精之效也。陛下誕膺寶歷，思致理平，雖好賢之心，有逾於前哲，而得人之盛，未迨於往時。蓋由賞鑒獨任於聖聰，搜擇頗難於公舉，仍啟登延之路，罕施練核之方。遂使先進者漸益雕訛，後來者不相接續，施一令則謗沮互起，用一人則瘡磐立成。此乃失於選才太精，制法不一之患也。則天舉用之法，傷易而得人；陛下慎揀之規，太精而失士。陛下選任宰相，必異於庶官；精擇長官，必愈於末品。及至宰相獻規，長吏薦士，陛下即但納橫議，不稽始謀。是乃任以重者輕其言，待以輕者重其事，且又不辨所毀之虛實，不校所試之短長。人之多言，何所不至，是將使人無所措其手足，豈獨選任之道失其端而已乎！

manualTranslations.zh: 」贄論奏曰：臣實頑鄙，一無所堪，猥蒙任使，待罪宰相。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi argued in memorial, saying: Your servant is truly obstinate and base, capable in nothing, undeservedly receiving appointment, awaiting punishment as chief minister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi submitted a reasoned memorial, saying: Your servant is truly dull and unworthy, fit for nothing, yet undeservedly raised to the chancellorship to serve at risk of fault.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖懷竊位之懼，且乏知人之明，自揣庸虛，終難上報。
manualTranslations.literal: Though harboring fear of usurping the post, and moreover lacking the clarity to know men, measuring myself common and empty, in the end I can hardly repay above.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though I fear I hold a post beyond my desert, and though I lack the discernment to know men well, I know myself to be mediocre and can scarcely hope to repay Your Majesty's grace.

manualTranslations.zh: 唯知廣求才之路，使賢者各以匯征；
manualTranslations.literal: I know only to broaden the road of seeking talent, causing worthy men each to be gathered in summons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I know only that the path to talent must be widened so that the worthy may each be summoned forth together.

manualTranslations.zh: 啟至公之門，令職司皆得自達。
manualTranslations.literal: Open the gate of utmost fairness, causing every office to be able to reach self-expression.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Open the gate of perfect fairness so that every office may make itself known.

manualTranslations.zh: 既蒙允許，即宜宣行。
manualTranslations.literal: Having received permission, it then ought to be proclaimed and carried out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Having received Your Majesty's approval, the policy ought at once to be proclaimed and put into effect.

manualTranslations.zh: 南宮舉人，才至十數，或非臺省舊吏，則是使府佐僚，累經薦延，多歷事任。
manualTranslations.literal: Southern Palace examination candidates were only ten-odd in number; some were not old clerks of the Boards and Departments, then they were staff of commissioner offices, repeatedly recommended and extended, many having passed through duties and posts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The recent examination passers numbered only a dozen or so. Some were not former clerks of the central boards and departments but staff of commissioner offices, repeatedly recommended and long experienced in office.

manualTranslations.zh: 論其資望，既不愧於班行；
manualTranslations.literal: Speaking of their qualifications and standing, they already did not fail to match their ranks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In seniority and reputation they were fit for their ranks.

manualTranslations.zh: 考其行能，又未聞於闕敗。
manualTranslations.literal: Examining their conduct and ability, again none were heard of in neglect and failure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In conduct and ability none had yet been found deficient.

manualTranslations.zh: 遽以騰口，上煩聖聰，道之難行，亦可知矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Abruptly because of clamoring mouths, above troubling sage hearing—the Way's difficulty in practice also can be known!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet at once the mouths of rumor stir, troubling Your Majesty's ear. How difficult it is to put sound policy into practice is plain enough!

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下勤求理道，務徇物情，因謂舉薦非宜，復委宰臣揀擇。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty diligently seeks the Way of order, striving to follow the people's sentiment; therefore you say recommendation is not fitting and again entrust chief ministers to select and choose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty earnestly seeks good government and attends to public feeling, and for that reason you hold that recommendation is unsuitable and again leave selection to the chief ministers.

manualTranslations.zh: 其為崇任輔弼，博采輿詞，可謂聖德之盛者。
manualTranslations.literal: This in reverencing and trusting chief ministers and broadly gathering public discourse can be called overflowing sage virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In honoring your ministers and heeding public opinion, this shows the greatness of your sage virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 然於委任責成之道，聽言考實之方，閑邪存誠，猶恐有闕。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet in the Way of entrusting responsibility and demanding fulfillment, the method of listening to words and examining reality, restraining evil and preserving sincerity—still I fear there are gaps.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet in entrusting responsibility, testing speech against fact, and keeping out evil while holding to sincerity, I fear something is still lacking.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下既納臣言而用之，旋聞橫議而止之，於臣謀不責成，於橫議不考實，此乃謀失者得以辭其罪，議曲者得以肆其誣。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty having accepted your servant's words and used them, soon hearing perverse discussion and stopping them—toward your servant's plans not demanding fulfillment, toward perverse discussion not examining reality—this is whereby those whose plans fail can use words to excuse their guilt, and those whose discussion is crooked can freely spread their slander.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty accepted my proposal and put it into effect, then at once halted it on hearing reckless criticism. You hold me to no account for the plan's failure, yet you do not test the reckless critics' claims. Thus those whose counsel fails may excuse their fault, and those who speak crookedly may slander at will.

manualTranslations.zh: 率是而行，觸類而長，固無必定之計，亦無必實之言。
manualTranslations.literal: Following this as model and acting, touching each category it grows—indeed no fixed and certain plans, also no necessarily true words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If this pattern continues and spreads by analogy, there will be no settled policy and no speech that can be trusted as true.

manualTranslations.zh: 計不定則理道難成，言不實則小人得誌。
manualTranslations.literal: Plans not fixed then the Way of order is hard to complete; words not true then petty men obtain their wish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without settled plans good government cannot be achieved; without truthful speech petty men get their way.

manualTranslations.zh: 國家之病，常必由之。
manualTranslations.literal: The state's illness constantly must proceed from this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The state's afflictions commonly spring from this.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔齊桓公問管仲害霸之事，對曰：「得賢不能任，害霸也；
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong what harmed hegemony; he answered: "Getting worthy men yet unable to employ them—harms hegemony;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong what harmed hegemony. He answered: "To gain worthy men yet fail to employ them harms hegemony;

manualTranslations.zh: 用而不能終，害霸也；
manualTranslations.literal: To employ them yet be unable to see them through—harms hegemony;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To employ them yet fail to see the appointment through harms hegemony;

manualTranslations.zh: 與賢人謀事，而與小人議之，害霸也。」
manualTranslations.literal: To consult with worthy men on affairs yet discuss them with petty men—harms hegemony."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To plan with worthy men yet debate the plan with petty men harms hegemony."

manualTranslations.zh: 為小人者，不必悉懷險诐，故覆邦家。
manualTranslations.literal: Petty men do not necessarily all harbor treacherous deceit, thus overturning state and family.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Petty men need not all harbor treacherous intent in order to ruin state and family.

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋以其意性回邪，趣向狹促，以沮議為出眾，以自異為不群，趨近利而昧遠圖，效小信而傷大道，況又言行難保，恣其非心者乎！
manualTranslations.literal: For their minds and natures are twisted and perverse, their bent narrow and cramped—they take obstructing deliberation as standing out, taking themselves as different as not joining the group, rushing toward near profit while blind to far design, imitating small trustworthiness while harming the great Way—how much more when words and conduct are hard to guarantee and they indulge their wicked hearts!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Their minds are crooked and their outlook cramped. They treat obstruction as distinction, eccentricity as independence, near gain as wisdom and far design as folly, small shows of trustworthiness as virtue and the great Way as expendable—and all the more so when their words and deeds cannot be trusted and they indulge their private malice!

manualTranslations.zh: 伏以宰輔，常制不過數人，人之所知，固有限極，不有遍諳諸士，備閱群才。
manualTranslations.literal: I submit that chief ministers, by regular rule no more than several men—what men know indeed has a bounded limit; they do not everywhere know all scholars or completely review all talent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chief ministers, by custom, number only a few. What any man can know is necessarily limited; they cannot know every scholar or review every talent in the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 若令悉命群官，理須展轉詢訪，是則變公舉為私薦，易明易攵為暗投。
manualTranslations.literal: If ordered to command all officials, by principle they must extend and turn in inquiry and investigation—then this changes public recommendation to private recommendation, open recommendation to secret recommendation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the chief ministers must appoint every official themselves, they can only do so by making round after round of private inquiry—turning public recommendation into private patronage and open selection into back-room nomination.

manualTranslations.zh: 儻如議者之言，所舉多有情故，舉於君上，且未絕私；
manualTranslations.literal: If like the discussants' words, what is recommended mostly has personal ties; recommending to the lord above, still private favor is not ended;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the critics are right that recommendations are mostly made through personal ties, then even when names are sent to Your Majesty private favor is not eliminated;

manualTranslations.zh: 薦於宰臣，安肯無詐！
manualTranslations.literal: Recommending to chief ministers—how can there fail to be fraud!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when names are sent to the chief ministers, how can fraud be avoided!

manualTranslations.zh: 失人之弊，必又甚焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The harm of losing good men must again be even greater.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The loss of capable men will be even worse.

manualTranslations.zh: 所以承前命官，罕有不涉私謗，雖則秉鈞不一，或自行情，亦由私訪所親，轉為所賣。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore formerly in appointing officials, rarely were there not entanglements of private slander; though holding the scale not uniform, some acted by personal feeling—also because private inquiries to kin were in turn sold out by them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is why past appointments were rarely free of private complaint. Even when chief ministers differed in judgment and some acted from personal inclination, they still relied on private inquiries among their intimates—and were in turn betrayed by them.

manualTranslations.zh: 其弊非遠，聖鑒明知。
manualTranslations.literal: This harm is not distant; sage discernment clearly knows it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This evil is not remote; Your Majesty knows it well.

manualTranslations.zh: 今又將徇浮言，專任宰臣除吏，宰臣不遍諳識，踵前須訪於人。
manualTranslations.literal: Now again about to follow floating words, exclusively entrusting chief ministers to remove and appoint officials—chief ministers do not everywhere know and recognize, and following precedent must inquire of others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now, yielding again to loose talk, you would leave appointment entirely to the chief ministers. They cannot know everyone themselves and, as before, must ask others.

manualTranslations.zh: 若訪親朋，則是悔其覆車，不易故轍；
manualTranslations.literal: If inquiring of kin and friends, then this regrets the overturned cart and does not change the old rut;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they ask kin and friends, they repeat the old mistake and change nothing;

manualTranslations.zh: 若訪於朝列，則是求其私薦，不如公舉之愈也。
manualTranslations.literal: If inquiring among the court ranks, then this seeks their private recommendations—not as good as public recommendation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if they ask colleagues at court, they solicit private recommendations—which is no better than open recommendation.

manualTranslations.zh: 二者利害，惟陛下更詳擇焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Of the two, benefit and harm—may Your Majesty further examine and choose.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Between the two courses, may Your Majesty weigh the benefit and harm.

manualTranslations.zh: 恐不如委任長官，慎揀僚屬，所揀既少，所求亦精，得賢有鑒識之名，失實當暗謬之責。
manualTranslations.literal: I fear it is not as good as entrusting department chiefs, carefully selecting subordinates—those selected being few, what is sought also refined; gaining worthy men brings a name for discernment, losing on reality ought to bear the blame of hidden error.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Better, I fear, to entrust department chiefs to choose their subordinates carefully. Fewer men would be chosen, but the search would be sharper. Success would bring them credit for discernment; failure would bring blame for error.

manualTranslations.zh: 人之常性，莫不愛身，況於臺省長官，皆是當朝華選，孰肯徇私妄舉，以傷名取責者耶！
manualTranslations.literal: Men's constant nature—none do not love their bodies; how much more for Board and Department chiefs, all being the dynasty's splendid selections—who would willingly favor private ties and rashly recommend, to harm their name and invite blame!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Human nature being what it is, every man protects his own reputation—how much more the heads of the central boards and departments, all chosen from the finest of the court. Who among them would risk his name by recommending unworthy men for private reasons!

manualTranslations.zh: 所謂臺省長官，即僕射、尚書、左右丞、侍郎及御史大夫、中丞是也。
manualTranslations.literal: What are called Board and Department chiefs are precisely the Grand Masters, Ministers, Left and Right Vice Directors, Vice Ministers, and the Censor-in-Chief and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By Board and Department chiefs I mean the Grandees, Ministers, Left and Right Vice Directors, Vice Ministers, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Censor-in-Chief.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下比擇輔相，多亦出於其中。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty in recent selection of chief ministers—many also came from among them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Many of the chief ministers Your Majesty has lately chosen came from among them.

manualTranslations.zh: 今之宰臣，則往日臺省長官也；
manualTranslations.literal: Today's chief ministers are then the former Board and Department chiefs;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today's chief ministers were yesterday's board and department heads;

manualTranslations.zh: 今之臺省長官，乃將來之宰臣也，但是職名暫異，固非行業頓殊。
manualTranslations.literal: Today's Board and Department chiefs are the future chief ministers; only the office names are temporarily different—not at all that conduct and calling are suddenly separate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and today's board and department heads are tomorrow's chief ministers. Only the titles differ for a time; their character and capacity are not suddenly transformed.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈有為長官之時不能舉一二屬吏，居宰臣之位則可擇千百具僚，物議悠悠，其惑斯甚。
manualTranslations.literal: How can it be that when serving as department chief one cannot recommend one or two subordinate clerks, yet occupying the chief minister's place one can choose hundreds and thousands of officials—public discussion endless, how very confusing!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How can the same men who, as department heads, could not be trusted to recommend one or two subordinates suddenly, as chief ministers, be expected to choose hundreds and thousands of officials? Public opinion is baffled indeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫求才貴廣，考課貴精。
manualTranslations.literal: Seeking talent values breadth; examining performance values precision.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In seeking talent breadth matters; in judging performance precision matters.

manualTranslations.zh: 求廣在於各舉所知，長吏之薦擇是也；
manualTranslations.literal: Breadth in seeking lies in each recommending what one knows—the department chiefs' recommendations and selections are this;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Breadth lies in each man recommending those he knows—the department chiefs' selections serve this purpose;

manualTranslations.zh: 貴精在於按名責實，宰臣之序進是也。
manualTranslations.literal: Precision in valuation lies in matching names to reality and demanding results—the chief ministers' ordered advancement is this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: precision lies in matching names to reality and holding men accountable—the chief ministers' review serves this purpose.

manualTranslations.zh: 往者則天太后踐祚臨朝，欲收人心，尤務拔擢，弘委任之意，開汲引之門，進用不疑，求訪無倦，非但人得薦士，亦許自舉其才。
manualTranslations.literal: Formerly Empress Wu Zetian ascended the throne and presided over court, wishing to win hearts, especially striving at promotion, broadening the intent of entrustment, opening the gate of drawing up—advancing employments without doubt, seeking and inquiring without weariness—not only could people recommend scholars, they were also permitted to recommend their own talent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu Zetian came to the throne she sought to win hearts and made promotion her chief task. She opened wide the gate of appointment, advanced men without hesitation, and searched tirelessly. Not only could officials recommend others; they might even recommend themselves.

manualTranslations.zh: 所薦必行，所舉輒試，其於選士之道，豈不傷於容易哉！
manualTranslations.literal: What was recommended must be carried out, what was nominated was immediately tested—in the Way of selecting scholars, was this not harmed by being too easy!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Every recommendation was acted on and every nominee promptly tested. By the standards of selecting scholars, was this not dangerously easy!

manualTranslations.zh: 而課責既嚴，進退皆速，不肖者旋黜，才能者驟升，是以當代謂知人之明，累朝賴多士之用。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet examination and responsibility being strict, advancement and removal all swift—the unworthy were quickly dismissed, the capable suddenly promoted; therefore the age was called to have clarity in knowing men, and successive courts relied on many scholars' employment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet because examination was strict and promotion and dismissal swift, the unworthy were quickly removed and the capable rapidly advanced. The age was praised for knowing men, and later reigns benefited from the abundance of talent.

manualTranslations.zh: 此乃近於求才貴廣，考課貴精之效也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is nearly the effect of seeking talent valuing breadth and examining performance valuing precision.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This was nearly the perfect balance of breadth in seeking talent and precision in judging performance.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下誕膺寶歷，思致理平，雖好賢之心，有逾於前哲，而得人之盛，未迨於往時。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty born to receive the precious succession, thinking to achieve order and peace—though the heart loving the worthy exceeds former sages, the flourishing of obtaining men has not reached past times.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, born to the throne and intent on bringing order, loves worthy men even more than the sages of old—yet the harvest of talent has not matched earlier times.

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋由賞鑒獨任於聖聰，搜擇頗難於公舉，仍啟登延之路，罕施練核之方。
manualTranslations.literal: Covering because appraisal rested solely in sage discernment, searching and selection quite difficult through public recommendation, still opening the road of summoning and extending, rarely applying the method of thorough examination.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is because judgment rests solely with Your Majesty, open recommendation is difficult, the gate of appointment remains open, and rigorous testing is rarely applied.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂使先進者漸益雕訛，後來者不相接續，施一令則謗沮互起，用一人則瘡磐立成。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore causing the advanced gradually to grow more corroded and erroneous, the later comers not connecting in succession—issuing one decree then slander and obstruction rise together, employing one man then scars immediately form.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The result is that senior men grow ever more compromised, successors fail to follow them, every decree provokes a chorus of slander, and every appointment leaves fresh scars.

manualTranslations.zh: 此乃失於選才太精，制法不一之患也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is the affliction of failing through selecting talent too precisely and making law not uniform.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is the harm of selecting talent too narrowly and keeping policy unsettled.

manualTranslations.zh: 則天舉用之法，傷易而得人；
manualTranslations.literal: Empress Wu's method of recommending and employing harmed by ease yet obtained men;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Empress Wu's method erred on the side of ease, yet she obtained men;

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下慎揀之規，太精而失士。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty's rule of careful selection—too precise and losing scholars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's rule errs on the side of strictness, and scholars are lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下選任宰相，必異於庶官；
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty in selecting and appointing chief ministers must differ from common officials;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rightly treats the choice of chief ministers differently from lesser appointments;

manualTranslations.zh: 精擇長官，必愈於末品。
manualTranslations.literal: Carefully selecting department chiefs must exceed low ranks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and rightly applies stricter scrutiny to department heads than to low ranks.

manualTranslations.zh: 及至宰相獻規，長吏薦士，陛下即但納橫議，不稽始謀。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet when chief ministers present regulations and department chiefs recommend scholars, Your Majesty then only accepts perverse discussion, not examining the original deliberation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet when chief ministers offer policy and department heads recommend talent, Your Majesty hears only reckless criticism and does not examine the original proposal.

manualTranslations.zh: 是乃任以重者輕其言，待以輕者重其事，且又不辨所毀之虛實，不校所試之短長。
manualTranslations.literal: This is entrusting with heavy matters yet treating their words lightly, treating with light matters yet weighing the affair heavily—and moreover not distinguishing the truth and falsehood of what is slandered, not comparing the strengths and weaknesses of what is tested.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is to treat grave counsel lightly and petty rumor seriously—not to test what is slandered for truth or falsehood, nor to judge nominees by their actual merits and faults.

manualTranslations.zh: 人之多言，何所不至，是將使人無所措其手足，豈獨選任之道失其端而已乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Men's much speaking—what would not they reach! This will cause people nowhere to place their hands and feet—not only that the Way of selection and appointment loses its beginning!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When men talk freely, nothing is spared. People will no longer know where to turn—not in selection alone, but in every affair of state!

sourceRange.text: 而鄜坊節度李建徽、神策行營陽惠元猶在咸陽，贄慮懷光並建徽等軍，又奏曰：懷光當管師徒，足以獨制兇寇，逗留未進，抑有他由。所患太強，不資傍助。比者又遣李晟、李建徽、陽惠元三節度之眾附麗其營，無益成功，只憂生事。何則？四軍懸壘，群帥異心，論勢力則懸絕高卑，據職名則不相統屬。懷光輕晟等兵微位下，而忿其制不從心。晟等疑懷光養寇蓄奸，而怨其事多陵己。端居則互防飛謗，欲戰則遞恐分功，齟齬不和，嫌釁遂構，俾之同處，必不兩全。強者惡積而後亡，弱者勢危而先覆，覆亡之禍，翹足可期。舊寇未平，新患方起，憂嘆所切，實堪疚心。太上消慝於未萌，其次救失於始兆，況乎事情已露，禍難垂成，委而不謀，何以制亂？李晟見機慮變，先請移軍就東，建徽、惠元，勢轉孤弱，為其吞噬，理在必然。他日雖有良圖，亦恐不能自拔，拯其危急，唯在此時。今因李晟願行，便遣合軍同往，托言晟兵素少，慮為賊泚所邀，藉此兩軍，叠為掎角。仍先諭旨，密使促裝，詔書至營，即日進路。懷光意雖不欲，然亦計無所施。是謂先人有奪人之心，疾雷不及掩耳者也。夫制軍馭將，所貴見情，離合疾徐，各有宜適。當離者合之則召亂，當合者離之則寡功；當疾而徐則失機，當徐而疾則漏策。得其要，契其時，然後舉無敗謀，措無危勢。而今者屯兵而不肯為用，聚將而罔能葉心，自為鯨鯢，變在朝夕。留之不足以相制，徒長歷階；析之各競於擅能，或成勛績。事有必應，斷無可疑。
