manualTranslations.zh: 而鄜坊節度李建徽、神策行營陽惠元猶在咸陽，贄慮懷光並建徽等軍，又奏曰：懷光當管師徒，足以獨制兇寇，逗留未進，抑有他由。
manualTranslations.literal: Meanwhile Fufang Military Governor Li Jianhui and Shence Mobile Camp Commander Yang Huiyuan were still at Xianyang; Zhi, fearing Huai'guang would absorb Jianhui's and the other armies, again memorialized, saying:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Jianhui, military governor of Fufang, and Yang Huiyuan of the Shence mobile camp were still at Xianyang. Fearing that Huai'guang would absorb their armies, Lu Zhi memorialized again:

manualTranslations.zh: 所患太強，不資傍助。
manualTranslations.literal: What one worries about is that he is too strong, not that he lacks help from others.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The concern is not that he lacks support, but that he is too strong.

manualTranslations.zh: 比者又遣李晟、李建徽、陽惠元三節度之眾附麗其營，無益成功，只憂生事。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently Li Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan—the armies of three military governors—were again sent to attach to his camp; it does no good for success, only raises worry of stirring trouble.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently Li Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan—the forces of three military governors—were attached to his camp. This will not help achieve victory; it will only provoke trouble.

manualTranslations.zh: 何則？
manualTranslations.literal: Why is this so?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why?

manualTranslations.zh: 四軍懸壘，群帥異心，論勢力則懸絕高卑，據職名則不相統屬。
manualTranslations.literal: Four armies stand in separate camps, their commanders of different minds; in strength they are vastly unequal, and by office and title they do not belong to one chain of command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Four armies camp apart, and their commanders are at odds. In strength they are vastly unequal, and in rank none is subordinate to another.

manualTranslations.zh: 懷光輕晟等兵微位下，而忿其制不從心。
manualTranslations.literal: Huai'guang disdains Sheng and the others for their small armies and low rank, and resents that he cannot fully command them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huai'guang looks down on Li Sheng and the others for their weaker forces and lower rank, and resents that he cannot fully command them.

manualTranslations.zh: 晟等疑懷光養寇蓄奸，而怨其事多陵己。
manualTranslations.literal: Sheng and the others suspect Huai'guang of harboring bandits and hoarding treachery, and resent that his affairs often encroach on themselves.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Sheng and the others suspect Huai'guang of deliberately sparing the enemy and harboring treachery, and resent his habit of riding roughshod over them.

manualTranslations.zh: 端居則互防飛謗，欲戰則遞恐分功，齟齬不和，嫌釁遂構，俾之同處，必不兩全。
manualTranslations.literal: At rest they mutually guard against slander; wishing to fight, they each fear sharing merit. Discord and ill will build; placed together, both cannot be preserved intact.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In camp they trade slander; in battle each fears the other will steal credit. Mutual distrust breeds conflict, and if they remain together, neither side can survive intact.

manualTranslations.zh: 強者惡積而後亡，弱者勢危而先覆，覆亡之禍，翹足可期。
manualTranslations.literal: The strong, hatred accumulated, perish afterward; the weak, position perilous, are overturned first; the calamity of ruin can be awaited with heels raised.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The stronger will be destroyed only after hatred has built up; the weaker, more endangered, will fall first. Their ruin is only a matter of time.

manualTranslations.zh: 舊寇未平，新患方起，憂嘆所切，實堪疚心。
manualTranslations.literal: The old bandits are not yet pacified, new trouble is just rising; the worry and sigh of what cuts close truly can afflict the heart.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The old enemy is not yet subdued and a new threat is already rising. The anguish of this situation is truly hard to bear.

manualTranslations.zh: 太上消慝於未萌，其次救失於始兆，況乎事情已露，禍難垂成，委而不謀，何以制亂？
manualTranslations.literal: The highest removes blight before it sprouts; next saves mistakes at the first sign; how much more when the matter is already exposed and calamity about to be complete—entrust without planning, how govern disorder?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The wise eliminate evil before it takes root; the next best remedy is at the first sign of trouble. When the danger is already exposed and disaster imminent, how can we refuse to act and still hope to control the chaos?

manualTranslations.zh: 李晟見機慮變，先請移軍就東，建徽、惠元，勢轉孤弱，為其吞噬，理在必然。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Sheng, seeing the moment and considering change, first requested to move the army east; Jianhui and Huiyuan, power turning isolated and weak, will be swallowed by him—reason lies in inevitability.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Sheng saw what was coming and asked to move his army east. Jianhui and Huiyuan, left isolated and weak, will inevitably be swallowed up by Huai'guang.

manualTranslations.zh: 他日雖有良圖，亦恐不能自拔，拯其危急，唯在此時。
manualTranslations.literal: Another day though there be good plans, I fear he still cannot extract himself; saving their urgent peril lies only in this moment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if they devise a better plan later, they may not escape in time. To save them, we must act now.

manualTranslations.zh: 今因李晟願行，便遣合軍同往，托言晟兵素少，慮為賊泚所邀，藉此兩軍，叠為掎角。
manualTranslations.literal: Now, taking Li Sheng's wish to go, send the combined armies to go together; under pretext that Sheng's troops are always few, fearing interception by the bandit Zhu Ci, by means of these two armies, layered as pincers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Use Li Sheng's request as pretext to send all three armies east together. Say that Li Sheng's force is too small and might be intercepted by Zhu Ci's rebels, and that the other two armies will support him in a coordinated pincer.

manualTranslations.zh: 仍先諭旨，密使促裝，詔書至營，即日進路。
manualTranslations.literal: Still first proclaim the intent, secretly send orders to hasten packing; when the edict reaches camp, that same day march the route.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: First send secret orders to prepare to march; when the edict reaches camp, they should move that same day.

manualTranslations.zh: 懷光意雖不欲，然亦計無所施。
manualTranslations.literal: Huai'guang in mind though unwilling, yet also finds no measure to apply.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Huai'guang will dislike it, but will have no way to stop it.

manualTranslations.zh: 是謂先人有奪人之心，疾雷不及掩耳者也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is what is called the first striker having a heart to seize from others—swift thunder does not reach before covering the ears.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is what the ancients meant by striking first: thunder before one can cover one's ears.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫制軍馭將，所貴見情，離合疾徐，各有宜適。
manualTranslations.literal: As for controlling armies and driving generals, what is prized is seeing the circumstances; separation and union, haste and delay, each has its fitting place.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In commanding armies and managing generals, what matters is reading the situation. Whether to unite or divide, to act quickly or slowly—each has its proper moment.

manualTranslations.zh: 當離者合之則召亂，當合者離之則寡功；
manualTranslations.literal: Those who should be separated, if joined will summon disorder; those who should be joined, if separated will have scant achievement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Joining those who should be kept apart invites chaos; separating those who should act together diminishes their effectiveness.

manualTranslations.zh: 當疾而徐則失機，當徐而疾則漏策。
manualTranslations.literal: When haste is called for, if slow then lose the moment; when delay is called for, if hasty then leak the plan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moving too slowly when speed is needed loses the opportunity; acting too quickly when caution is needed ruins the plan.

manualTranslations.zh: 得其要，契其時，然後舉無敗謀，措無危勢。
manualTranslations.literal: Obtaining its essentials, matching its time, then raising plans none fail, placing measures none perilous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seize the essential point and act at the right moment, and no plan will fail and no move will create danger.

manualTranslations.zh: 而今者屯兵而不肯為用，聚將而罔能葉心，自為鯨鯢，變在朝夕。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet now armies are encamped yet unwilling to be used, generals gathered yet unable to unite in heart—they make themselves whales and narwhals; change lies within morning and evening.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now troops are assembled but will not cooperate, and generals are gathered but cannot unite. They are turning into mortal enemies, and disaster may strike at any moment.

manualTranslations.zh: 留之不足以相制，徒長歷階；
manualTranslations.literal: Keeping them is insufficient to restrain each other, only vainly lengthening step-by-step ascent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Keeping them together will not allow them to check one another; it will only escalate the danger.

manualTranslations.zh: 析之各競於擅能，或成勛績。
manualTranslations.literal: Dividing them, each competes in exclusive ability, perhaps achieving merit and achievement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Separating them, each may strive to prove himself and perhaps achieve merit.

manualTranslations.zh: 事有必應，斷無可疑。
manualTranslations.literal: The matter has what must be answered; decisively nothing doubtful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This must be done; there is no room for doubt.

sourceRange.text: 贄以中原之兵，不習邊事，及扞虜戰賊，多有敗衄，又苦邊將名目太多，諸軍統制不一，緩急無以應敵，乃上疏論其事曰：臣歷觀前代書史，皆謂鎮撫四夷，宰相之任，不揆闇劣，屢敢上言。誠以備邊禦戎，國家之重事；理兵足食，備禦之大經。兵不治則無可用之師，食不足則無可固之地。理兵在制置得所，足食在斂導有方。陛下幸聽愚言，先務積谷，人無加賦，官不費財，坐致邊儲，數逾百萬。諸鎮收糴，今已向終，分貯軍城，用防艱急，縱有寇戎之患，必無乏絕之憂。守此成規，以為永制，常收冗費，益贍邊農，則更經二年，可積十萬人三歲之糧矣。足食之原粗立，理兵之術未精，敢議籌量，庶備采擇。伏以戎狄為患，自古有之，其於制禦之方，得失之論，備存史籍，可得而言。大抵尊即序者，則曰「非德無以化要荒」，曾莫知威不立，則德不能馴也。樂武威者，則曰「非兵無以服兇獷」，曾莫知德不修，則兵不可恃也。務和親者，則曰「要結可以睦鄰好」，曾莫知我結之而彼復解也。美長城者，則曰「設險可以固邦國而扞寇仇」，曾莫知力不足，兵不堪，則險之不能有也。尚薄伐者，則曰「驅遏可以禁侵暴而省征徭，」曾莫知兵不銳，壘不完，則遏之不能勝，驅之不能去也。議邊之要，略盡於斯，雖互相譏評，然各有偏駁。聽一家之說，則例理可征；考歷代所行，則成敗異效。是由執常理以禦其不常之勢，徇所見而昧於所遇之時。夫中夏有盛衰，夷狄有強弱，事機有利害，措置有安危，故無必定之規，亦無長勝之法。夏後以序戎而聖化茂，古公以避狄而王業興；周城朔方而獫狁攘，秦築臨洮而宗社覆；漢武討匈奴而貽悔，太宗征突厥而致安；文、景約和親而不能弭患於當年，宣、元弘撫納而足以保寧於累葉。蓋以中夏之盛衰異勢，夷狄之強弱異時，事機之利害異情，措置之安危異便。知其事而不度其時則敗，附其時而不失其稱則成。形變不同，胡可專一！夫以中國強盛，夷狄衰微，而能屈膝稱臣，歸心受制，拒之則阻其向化，威之則類於殺降，安得不存而撫之，即而序之也？又如中國強盛，夷狄衰微，而尚棄信奸盟，蔑恩肆毒，諭之不變，責之不懲，安得不取亂推亡，息人固境也？其有遇中國喪亡之弊，當夷狄強盛之時，圖之則彼釁未萌，禦之則我力不足，安得不卑詞降禮，約好通和，啖之以親，紓其交禍？縱不必信，且無大侵，雖非禦戎之善經，蓋時事亦有不得已也。儻或夷夏之勢，強弱適同，撫之不寧，威之不靖；力足以自保，不足以出攻，得不設險以固軍，訓師以待寇，來則薄伐以遏其深入，去則攘斥而戒於遠追？雖為安邊之令圖，蓋勢力亦有不得不然也。故夏之即序，周之於攘，太宗之翦亂，皆乘其時而善用其勢也。古公之避狄，文、景之和親，神堯之降禮，皆順其時而不失其稱也。秦皇之長城，漢武之窮討，皆知其事而不度其時者也。向若遇孔熾之勢，行即序之方，則見侮而不從矣！乘可取之資，懷畏避之誌，則失機而養寇矣！有攘卻之力，用和親之謀，則示弱而勞費矣！當降屈之時，務翦伐之略，則召禍而危殆矣！故曰：知其事而不度其時則敗，附其時而不失其稱則成。是無必定之規，亦無長勝之法，得失著效，不其然歟！至於察安危之大情，計成敗之大數，百代之不變易者，蓋有之矣。其要在於失人肆欲則必蹶，任人從眾則必全，此乃古今所同，而物理之所壹也。國家自祿山構亂、河隴用兵以來，肅宗中興，撤邊備以靖中邦，借外威以寧內難。於是吐蕃乘釁，吞噬無厭；回紇矜功，憑陵亦甚。中國不遑振旅，四十余年。使傷耗遺氓，竭力蠶織，西輸賄幣，北償馬資，尚不足塞其煩言，滿其驕誌。復乃遠征士馬，列戍疆陲，猶不能遏其奔沖，止其侵侮。小入則驅略黎庶，深入則震驚邦畿。時有議安邊策者，多務於所難而忽於所易，勉於所短而略於所長。遂使所易所長者，行之而其要不精；所難所短者，圖之而其功靡就。憂患未弭，職斯之由。夫制敵行師，必量事勢，勢有難易，事有先後。力大而敵脆，則先其所難，是謂奪人之心，暫勞而永逸者也；力寡而敵堅，則先其所易，是謂固國之本，觀釁而後動者也。頃屬多故，人勞未瘳，而欲廣發師徒，深踐寇境，復其侵地，攻其堅城，前有勝負未必之虞，後有饋運不繼之患。儻或撓敗，適所以啟戎心而挫國威，以此為安邊之謀，可謂不量事勢而務於所難矣！天之授者，有分事，無全功；地之產者，有物宜，無兼利。是以五方之俗，長短各殊。長者不可逾，短者不可企；勉所短而敵其所長必殆，用所長而乘其所短必安。強者，乃以水草為邑居，以射獵供飲茹，多馬而尤便馳突，輕生而不恥敗亡，此戎狄之所長也。戎狄之所長，乃中國之所短；而欲益兵蒐乘，角力爭驅，交鋒原野之間，決命尋常之內，以此為禦寇之術，可謂勉所短而校其所長矣！務所難，勉所短，勞費百倍，終於無成。雖果成之，不挫則廢，豈不以越天授而違地產，虧時勢以反物宜者哉！將欲去危就安，息費從省，在慎守所易，精用所長而已。若乃擇將吏以撫寧眾庶，修紀律以訓齊師徒，耀德以佐威，能邇以柔遠；禁侵抄之暴以彰吾信，抑攻取之議以安戎心；彼求和則善待而勿與結盟，彼為寇則嚴備而不務報復，此當今之所易也。賤力而貴智，惡殺而好生，輕利而重人，忍小以全大，安其居而後動，俟其時而後行。是以修封疆，守要害，塹蹊隧，壘軍營，謹禁防，明斥候，務農以足食，練卒以蓄威，非萬全不謀，非百克不鬥。寇小至則張聲勢以遏其入，寇大至則謀其人以邀其歸；據險以乘之，多方以誤之。使其勇無所加，眾無所用；掠則靡獲，攻則不能；進有腹背受敵之虞，退有首尾難救之患，所謂乘其弊，不戰而屈人之兵，此中國之所長也。我之所長，乃戎狄之所短；我之所易，乃戎狄之所難。以長制短，則用力寡而見功多；以易敵難，則財不匱而事速就。舍此不務，而反為所乘，斯謂倒持戈矛，以钅尊授寇者也！今則皆務之矣，猶且守封未固，寇戎未懲者，其病在於謀無定用，眾無適從。所任不必才，才者不必任；所聞不必實，實者不必聞；所信不必誠，誠者不必信；所行不必當，當者未必行。故令措置乖方，課責虧度；財匱於兵眾，力分於將多，怨生於不均，機失於遙制。臣請為陛下粗陳六者之失，惟明主慎聽而熟察之：臣聞工欲善其事，必先利其器；武欲勝其敵，必先練其兵。練兵之中，所用復異。用之於救急，則權以紓難；用之於暫敵，則緩以應機。故事有便宜，而不拘常制；謀有奇詭，而不徇眾情。進退死生，唯將所命，此所謂攻討之兵也！用之於屯戍，則事資可久；勢異從權，非物理所愜不寧，非人情所欲不固。夫人情者，利焉則勸，習焉則安，保親戚則樂生，顧家業則忘死，故可以理術馭，不可以法制驅，此所謂鎮守之兵也。夫欲備封疆，禦戎狄，非一朝一夕之事，固當選鎮守之兵以置焉。古之善選置者，必量其性習，辨其土宜，察其伎能，知其欲惡。用其力而不違其性，齊其俗而不易其宜；引其善而不責其所不能，禁其非而不處其所不欲。而又類其紀伍，安其室家，然後能使之樂其居，定其誌，奮其氣勢，結其恩情。撫之以惠，則感而不驕；臨之以威，則肅而不怨。靡督課而人自為用，弛禁防而眾自不攜。故出則足兵，居則足食，守則固，戰則強。其術無他，便於人情而已矣！今者散征士卒，分戍邊陲，更代往來，以為守備。是則不量性習，不辨土宜，邀其所不能，強其所不欲。求廣其數而不考其用，將致其力而不察其情，斯可以為羽衛之儀，而無益於備禦之實也。何者？窮邊之地，千里蕭條，寒風裂膚，驚沙慘目；與豺狼為鄰伍，以戰鬥為嬉遊；晝則荷戈而耕，夜則倚烽而覘；日有剽害之慮，永無休暇之娛，地惡人勤，於斯為甚！自非生於其域，習於其風，幼而睹焉，長而安焉，不見樂土而遷焉，則罕能寧其居而狎其敵也。關東之地，百物阜殷，從軍之徒，尤被優養。慣於溫飽，狎於歡康，比諸邊隅，若異天地。聞絕塞荒陬之苦，則辛酸動容；聆強蕃勁虜之名，則懾駭奪氣。而乃使之去親族，舍園廬，甘其所辛酸，抗其所懾駭，將冀為用，不亦疏乎！矧又有休代之期，無統帥之馭，資奉若驕子，姑息如倩人，進不邀之以成功，退不處之以嚴憲。其來也鹹負得色，其止也莫有固心，屈指計歸，張頤待飼。僥倖者猶患還期之賒緩，常念戎醜之充斥；王師挫傷，則將乘其亂離，布路東潰，情誌且爾，得之奚為？平居則殫耗資儲以奉浮冗之眾，臨難則拔棄城鎮以搖遠近之心，其弊豈惟無益哉！固亦將有所撓也。復有抵犯刑禁，謫徙軍城，意欲增戶實邊，兼令展效自贖。既是無良之類，且加懷土之情，思亂幸災，又甚戍卒。適足煩於防衛，諒無望於功庸，雖前代時或行之，固非良算之可遵者也。復有擁旄之帥，身不臨邊，但分偏師，俾守疆場。大抵軍中壯銳，元戎例選自隨，委其疲羸，乃配諸鎮。節將既居內地，精兵祗備紀綱，遂令守要禦沖，常在寡弱之輩。寇戎每至，乃勢不支，入壘者才足閉關，在野者悉遭劫執，恣其芟蹂，盡其搜驅。比及都府聞知，虜已克獲旋返。且安邊之本，所切在兵，理兵若斯，可謂措置乖方矣！夫賞以存勸，罰以示懲，勸以懋有庸，懲以威不恪。故賞罰之於馭眾也，猶繩墨之於曲直，權衡之揣重輕，輗軏之所以行車，銜勒之所以服馬也。馭眾而不用賞罰，則善惡相混而能否莫殊；用之而不當功過，則奸妄寵榮而忠實擯抑。夫如是，若聰明可衒，律度無章，則用與不用，其弊一也。自頃權移於下，柄失於朝，將之號令，既鮮克行之於軍，國之典章，又不能施之於將，務相遵養，茍度歲時。欲賞一有功，翻慮無功者反側；欲罰一有罪，復慮同惡者憂虞。罪以隱忍而不彰，功以嫌疑而不賞，姑息之道，乃至於斯。故使忘身效節者，獲誚於等夷；率眾先登者，取怨於士卒；僨軍蹙國者，不懷於愧畏；緩救失期者，自以為智能。褒貶既闕而不行，稱毀復紛然相亂，人雖欲善，誰為言之？況又公忠者，直己而不求於人，反罹困厄；敗撓者，行私而茍媚於眾，例獲優崇。此義士所以痛心，勇夫所以解體也。又有遇敵而所守不固，陳謀而其效靡成；將帥則以資糧不足為詞，有司復以供給無闕為解。既相執證，理合辨明，朝廷每為含糊，未嘗窮究曲直。措理者吞聲而靡訴，誣善者罔上而不慚。馭眾若斯，可謂課責虧度矣！課責虧度，措置乖方，將不得竭其材，卒不得盡其力，屯集雖眾，戰陣莫前。虜每越境橫行，若涉無人之地；遞相推倚，無敢誰何，虛張賊勢上聞，則曰兵少不敵。朝廷莫之省察，惟務征發益師，無裨備禦之功，重增供億之弊。閭井日耗，征求日繁，以編戶傾家破產之資，兼有司榷鹽稅酒之利，總其所入，半以事邊，制用若斯，可謂財匱於兵眾矣！今四夷之最強盛為中國甚患者，莫大於吐蕃，舉國勝兵之徒，才當中國十數大郡而已。其於內虞外備，亦與中國不殊，所能寇邊，數則蓋寡。且又器非犀利，甲不堅完，識迷韜鈐，藝乏趫敏。動則中國畏其眾而不敢抗，靜則中國憚其強而不敢侵，厥理何哉？良以中國之節制多門，蕃醜之統帥專一故也。夫統帥專則人心不分，人心不分則號令不貳，號令不貳則進退可齊，進退可齊則疾徐如意，疾徐如意則機會靡愆，機會靡愆則氣勢自壯！斯乃以少為眾，以弱為強，變化翕辟，在於反掌之內。是猶臂之使指，心之制形，若所任得人，則何敵之有！夫節制多門則人心不一，人心不一則號令不行，號令不行則進退難必，進退難必則疾徐失宜，疾徐失宜則機會不及，機會不及則氣勢自衰！斯乃勇廢為尪，眾散為弱，逗撓離析，兆乎戰陣之前。是猶一國三公，十羊九牧，欲令齊肅，其可得乎？開元、天寶之間，控禦西北兩蕃，唯朔方、河西、隴右三節度而已，猶慮權分勢散，或使兼而領之。中興已來，未遑外討，僑隸四鎮於安定，權附隴右於扶風，所當西北兩蕃，亦朔方、涇原、隴右、河東節度而已，關東戍卒，至則屬焉。雖委任未盡得人，而措置尚存典制。自頃逆泚誘涇、隴之眾叛，懷光汙朔方之軍，割裂誅鋤，所余無幾。而又分朔方之地，建牙擁節者，凡三使焉。其余鎮軍，數且四十，皆承特詔委寄，各降中貴監臨，人得抗衡，莫相稟屬。每俟邊書告急，方令計會用兵，既無軍法下臨，唯以客禮相待。是乃從容拯溺，揖讓救焚，冀無阽危，固亦難矣！夫兵，以氣勢為用者也，氣聚則盛，散則消；勢合則威，析則弱。今之邊備，勢弱氣消，建軍若斯，可謂力分於將多矣。理戎之要，最在均齊，故軍法無貴賤之差，軍實無多少之異，是將所以同其誌而盡其力也。如或誘其誌意，勉其藝能，則當閱其材，程其勇，校其勞逸，度其安危，明申練覆優劣之科，以為衣食等級之制。使能者企及，否者息心，雖有薄厚之殊，而無觖望之釁。蓋所謂日省月試，餼稟均事，如權量之無情於物，萬人莫不安其分而服其平也。今者窮邊之地，長鎮之兵，皆百戰傷夷之余，終年勤苦之劇，角其所能則練習，度其所處則孤危，考其服役則勞，察其臨敵則勇。然衣糧所給，唯止當身，例為妻子所分，常有凍餒之色。而關東戍卒，歲月踐更，不安危城，不習戎備，怯於應敵，懈於服勞。然衣糧所頒，厚逾數等，繼以茶藥之饋，益以蔬醬之資。豐約相形，懸絕斯甚。又有素非禁旅，本是邊軍，將校詭為媚詞，因請遙隸神策，不離舊所，唯改虛名，其於稟賜之饒，遂有三倍之益。此儔類所以忿恨，忠良所以憂嗟，疲人所以流亡，經費所以褊匱。夫事業未異，而給養有殊，人情之所不能甘也，況乎矯佞行而稟賜厚，績藝劣而衣食優，茍未忘懷，能無慍怒！不為戎首，則已可嘉，而欲使其協力同心，以攘寇難，雖有韓、白、孫、吳之將，臣知其必不能焉。養士若斯，可謂怨生於不均矣！凡欲選任將帥，必先考察行能，然後指以所授之方，語以所委之事，令其自揣可否，自陳規模。須某色甲兵，藉某人參佐，要若干士馬，用若干資糧，某處置軍，某時成績，始終要領，悉俾經綸，於是觀其計謀，校其聲實。若謂材無足取，言不可行，則當退之於初，不宜貽慮於其後也。若謂志氣足任，方略可施，則當要之於終，不宜掣肘於其間也。夫如是，則疑者不使，使者不疑；勞神於選才，端拱於委任。既委其事，既足其求，然後可以核其否臧，行其賞罰。受賞者不以為濫，當罰者無得而辭，付授之柄既專，茍且之心自息。是以古之遣將帥者，君親推轂而命之曰：「自閫以外，將軍裁之。」又賜鈇鉞，示令專斷。故軍容不入國，國容不入軍，將在軍，君命有所不受。誠謂機宜不可以遠決，號令不可以兩從，未有委任不專，而望其克敵成功者也。自頃邊軍去就，裁斷多出宸衷，選置戎臣，先求易制，多其部以分其力，輕其任以弱其心，雖有所懲，亦有所失。遂令分閫責成之義廢，死綏任咎之誌衰，一則聽命，二亦聽命，爽於軍情亦聽命，乖於事宜亦聽命。若所置將帥，必取於承順無違，則如斯可矣；若有意平兇靖難，則不可。夫兩境相接，兩軍相持，事機之來，間不容息，蓄謀而俟，猶恐失之，臨時始謀，固已疏矣。況乎千里之遠，九重之深，陳述之難明，聽覽之不一，欲其事無遺策，雖聖者亦有所不能焉。設使謀慮能周，其如權變無及！戎虜馳突，迅如風飈，驛書上聞，旬月方報。守土者以兵寡不敢抗敵，分鎮者以無詔不肯出師，逗留之間，寇已奔逼，托於救援未至，各且閉壘自全。牧馬屯牛，鞠為椎剽；穡夫樵婦，罄作俘囚。雖詔諸鎮發兵，唯以虛聲應援，互相瞻顧，莫敢遮邀，賊既縱掠退歸，此乃陳功告捷。其敗喪則減百而為一，其捃獲則張百而成千。將帥既幸於總制在朝，不憂於罪累；陛下又以為大權由己，不究事情。用師若斯，可謂機失於遙制矣！理兵而措置乖方，馭將而賞罰虧度，制用而財匱，建兵而力分，養士而怨生，用師而機失，此六者，疆場之蟊賊，軍旅之膏肓也。蟊賊不除，而但滋之以糞溉，膏肓不療，而唯啖之以滑甘，適足以養其害，速其災，欲求稼穡豐登，膚革充美，固不可得也。臣愚謂宜罷諸道將士番替防秋之制，率因舊數而三分之：其一分委本道節度使募少壯願住邊城者以徙焉；其一分則本道但供衣糧，委關內、河東諸軍州募蕃、漢子弟願傅邊軍者以給焉；又一分亦令本道但出衣糧，加給應募之人，以資新徙之業。又令度支散於諸道和市耕牛，兼雇召工人，就諸軍城繕造器具。募人至者，每家給耕牛一頭，又給田農水火之器，皆令充備。初到之歲，與家口二人糧，並賜種子，勸之播植，待經一稔，俾自給家。若有余糧，官為收糴，各酬倍價，務獎營田。既息踐更征發之煩，且無幸災茍免之弊。寇至則人自為戰，時至則家自力農。是乃兵不得不強，食不得不足，與夫倏來忽往，豈可同等而論哉！臣又謂宜擇文武能臣一人為隴右元帥，應涇、隴、鳳翔、長武城、山南西道等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉；又擇一人為朔方元帥，應鄜坊、邠寧、靈夏等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉；又擇一人為河東元帥，河東、振武等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉。三帥各選臨邊要會之州以為理所，見置節度，有非要者，隨所便近而並之。唯元帥得置統軍，余並停罷。其三帥部內太原、鳳翔等府及諸郡戶口稍多者，慎揀良吏以為尹守，外奉師律，內課農桑，俾為軍糧，以壯戎府。理兵之宜既得，選帥之授既明，然後減奸濫虛浮之費以豐財，定衣糧等級之制以和眾，弘委任之道以宣其用，懸賞罰之典以考其成。而又慎守中國之所長，謹行當今之所易，則八利可致，六失可除。如是而戎狄不威懷，疆場不寧謐者，未之有也。諸侯軌道，庶類服從。如是而教令不行，天下不理者，亦未之有也。以陛下之英鑒，民心之思安，四方之小休，兩寇之方靜，加以頻年豐稔，所在積糧，此皆天贊國家，可以立制垂統之時也。時不久居，事不常兼，已過而追，雖悔無及。明主者，不以言為罪，不以人廢言，罄陳狂愚，惟所省擇。

manualTranslations.zh: 贄以中原之兵，不習邊事，及扞虜戰賊，多有敗衄，又苦邊將名目太多，諸軍統制不一，緩急無以應敵，乃上疏論其事曰：臣歷觀前代書史，皆謂鎮撫四夷，宰相之任，不揆闇劣，屢敢上言。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi because Central Plains troops did not practice frontier affairs, and in resisting barbarians and fighting bandits many suffered defeat, also suffering from too many frontier generals' titles, the various armies' unified command not one—in urgency and ease having no means to respond to the enemy—then submitted a memorial discussing the matter, saying:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi held that the armies of the central plains were unused to frontier warfare and suffered many defeats against barbarians and rebels; that there were too many frontier commanders and no unified command; and that in crisis the forces could not respond effectively. He therefore submitted a memorial on the matter, saying:

manualTranslations.zh: 誠以備邊禦戎，國家之重事；
manualTranslations.literal: Truly because preparing the frontier and defending against barbarians is the state's weighty affair;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For frontier defense is a weighty affair of state;

manualTranslations.zh: 理兵足食，備禦之大經。
manualTranslations.literal: ordering troops and filling granaries is the great constant of defense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and ordering the armies and filling the granaries is the great foundation of defense.

manualTranslations.zh: 兵不治則無可用之師，食不足則無可固之地。
manualTranslations.literal: Troops not ordered then no usable army; food insufficient then no place that can be held firm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without well-ordered troops there is no army fit for use; without sufficient grain no land can be held.

manualTranslations.zh: 理兵在制置得所，足食在斂導有方。
manualTranslations.literal: Ordering troops lies in disposition being appropriate; filling granaries lies in collection and guidance having method.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ordering troops depends on proper disposition; filling granaries depends on sound collection and distribution.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下幸聽愚言，先務積谷，人無加賦，官不費財，坐致邊儲，數逾百萬。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty fortunately listening to my foolish words, first task accumulating grain—people without added tax, offices without expending funds, sitting to achieve frontier stores, numbering exceeding a million.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has graciously heeded my counsel and made grain accumulation the first task. Without adding to the people's taxes or wasting public funds, frontier stores now exceed a million.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸鎮收糴，今已向終，分貯軍城，用防艱急，縱有寇戎之患，必無乏絕之憂。
manualTranslations.literal: The various commands' grain purchases—now already nearing completion—divided and stored in military cities, used to guard against hardship and urgency; even if there are bandit and barbarian troubles, certainly no fear of exhaustion and cutoff.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The commands' grain purchases are nearly complete, stored in garrison cities against emergency. Even if bandits or barbarians strike, there need be no fear of shortage.

manualTranslations.zh: 守此成規，以為永制，常收冗費，益贍邊農，則更經二年，可積十萬人三歲之糧矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Guarding this established rule as perpetual system, constantly gathering surplus expenses, increasing support for frontier farmers—then after two more years, one could accumulate three years' grain for a hundred thousand men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If this rule is kept as a permanent system, surplus funds redirected to support frontier farming, then in two more years there could be three years' grain for a hundred thousand men.

manualTranslations.zh: 足食之原粗立，理兵之術未精，敢議籌量，庶備采擇。
manualTranslations.literal: The source of sufficient food roughly established, the art of ordering troops not yet refined—I dare discuss planning and reckoning, hoping to prepare for selection and adoption.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The foundation of adequate supply is roughly in place; the art of ordering troops is not yet perfected. I venture to offer further plans for Your Majesty's consideration.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏以戎狄為患，自古有之，其於制禦之方，得失之論，備存史籍，可得而言。
manualTranslations.literal: I respectfully submit that the Rong and Di as a menace has existed since antiquity; regarding methods of control and defense, and discussions of success and failure, these are fully preserved in historical records and may be expounded upon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Respectfully, the threat posed by the Rong and Di is as old as history itself. The methods for controlling and defending against them, and the debates over what succeeded and what failed, are all fully recorded in the chronicles—and can be examined at length.

manualTranslations.zh: 大抵尊即序者，則曰「非德無以化要荒」，曾莫知威不立，則德不能馴也。
manualTranslations.literal: Generally those who honor bringing into ritual order say, "Without virtue there is no means to transform the remote wilds," yet they never understand that unless authority is established, virtue cannot tame them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who prize the approach of bringing the frontier peoples into ritual order declare that "only virtue can transform the remote borderlands"—yet they never grasp that unless authority is first established, virtue alone cannot make them submit.

manualTranslations.zh: 樂武威者，則曰「非兵無以服兇獷」，曾莫知德不修，則兵不可恃也。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who delight in martial prestige say, "Without arms there is no means to subdue the fierce and unruly," yet they never understand that if virtue is not cultivated, arms cannot be relied upon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who delight in martial power insist that "only force can tame the violent and intractable"—yet they never see that without moral cultivation, military might is not something one can trust.

manualTranslations.zh: 務和親者，則曰「要結可以睦鄰好」，曾莫知我結之而彼復解也。
manualTranslations.literal: Those devoted to heqin alliance say, "Binding ties can foster neighborly goodwill," yet they never understand that when we bind them, they again unravel the ties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those devoted to alliance through marriage say that "binding ties can preserve neighborly goodwill"—yet they never see that the moment we forge such bonds, our counterparts may break them again.

manualTranslations.zh: 美長城者，則曰「設險可以固邦國而扞寇仇」，曾莫知力不足，兵不堪，則險之不能有也。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who praise the Great Wall say, "Establishing defenses can fortify the state and repel enemy invaders," yet they never understand that when strength is insufficient and troops inadequate, defenses cannot be held.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who praise the Great Wall claim that "fortifying strategic passes can secure the realm and ward off enemy raids"—yet they never see that when one's strength is inadequate and one's armies insufficient, no fortification can be held.

manualTranslations.zh: 尚薄伐者，則曰「驅遏可以禁侵暴而省征徭，」曾莫知兵不銳，壘不完，則遏之不能勝，驅之不能去也。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who favor limited punitive expeditions say, "Driving back and blocking can forbid aggression and reduce corvée and levies," yet they never understand that when troops are not sharp and fortifications incomplete, blocking cannot prevail and driving cannot remove them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who favor limited border campaigns argue that "driving the enemy back and blocking incursions can end pillaging and lighten the burden of corvée and levies"—yet they never see that when troops are dull and defenses incomplete, blocking cannot win and driving cannot dislodge the foe.

manualTranslations.zh: 議邊之要，略盡於斯，雖互相譏評，然各有偏駁。
manualTranslations.literal: The essentials of discussing border affairs are largely exhausted in these points; though they mutually ridicule and criticize one another, each has its partialities and defects.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The main points debated in discussions of border policy are largely covered by these positions. Though advocates mock one another, each approach is one-sided and flawed in its own way.

manualTranslations.zh: 聽一家之說，則例理可征；
manualTranslations.literal: Listening to one school's doctrine, then its principles and reasoning can be verified;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heed any single school of thought alone, and its logic seems persuasive enough;

manualTranslations.zh: 考歷代所行，則成敗異效。
manualTranslations.literal: Examining what was practiced through successive dynasties, then success and failure yield different results.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: but examine what successive dynasties actually put into practice, and the outcomes vary from success to failure.

manualTranslations.zh: 是由執常理以禦其不常之勢，徇所見而昧於所遇之時。
manualTranslations.literal: This comes from holding to constant principles to defend against inconstant circumstances, and following one's own view while being blind to the times one encounters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is what happens when one clings to fixed principles to meet ever-changing circumstances, and pursues one's own preconceptions while failing to read the times.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫中夏有盛衰，夷狄有強弱，事機有利害，措置有安危，故無必定之規，亦無長勝之法。
manualTranslations.literal: Now, the Central Realm has its rise and decline, the barbarians have their strength and weakness, opportunities have their benefits and harms, and arrangements have their safety and peril—therefore there is no fixed rule, nor any permanently victorious method.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Central Realm waxes and wanes; the frontier peoples grow strong and grow weak; circumstances offer both advantage and harm; and any given policy may bring safety or peril. Thus there is no fixed formula, and no strategy that always wins.

manualTranslations.zh: 夏後以序戎而聖化茂，古公以避狄而王業興；
manualTranslations.literal: Xia Hou brought the Rong into order and sagely transformation flourished; Lord Ancient avoided the Di and royal enterprise arose;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia brought the Rong into order, and sage rule flourished; Lord Danfu fled the Di, and a royal dynasty was born;

manualTranslations.zh: 周城朔方而獫狁攘，秦築臨洮而宗社覆；
manualTranslations.literal: Zhou fortified Shuofang yet the Xianyun raided; Qin built at Lintao yet the ancestral altars fell;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the Zhou fortified Shuofang, yet the Xianyun raided all the more; Qin built fortifications at Lintao, yet the dynasty itself was destroyed;

manualTranslations.zh: 漢武討匈奴而貽悔，太宗征突厥而致安；
manualTranslations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han campaigned against the Xiongnu and bequeathed regret; Emperor Taizong campaigned against the Turks and achieved peace;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han campaigned against the Xiongnu and left posterity with regret; Emperor Taizong campaigned against the Turks and brought peace;

manualTranslations.zh: 文、景約和親而不能弭患於當年，宣、元弘撫納而足以保寧於累葉。
manualTranslations.literal: Wen and Jing made heqin treaties yet could not quell the trouble in their own age; Xuan and Yuan broadly embraced and received them and were sufficient to preserve tranquility for successive generations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Jing negotiated marriage alliances but could not end the troubles of their day; Emperors Xuan and Yuan pursued a policy of conciliation and were able to secure peace for generation after generation.

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋以中夏之盛衰異勢，夷狄之強弱異時，事機之利害異情，措置之安危異便。
manualTranslations.literal: This is because the Central Realm's rise and decline differ in circumstance, the barbarians' strength and weakness differ in time, opportunities' benefits and harms differ in nature, and arrangements' safety and peril differ in suitability.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For the rise and fall of the Central Realm follows one set of circumstances, the strength and weakness of the frontier peoples another; the benefits and harms of any given situation another still; and the safety or peril of any given policy depends on what the moment requires.

manualTranslations.zh: 知其事而不度其時則敗，附其時而不失其稱則成。
manualTranslations.literal: Knowing the matter but not gauging the times leads to failure; adhering to the times without losing what is fitting leads to success.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To understand the problem but misread the times is to fail; to follow the demands of the moment without abandoning what is appropriate is to succeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 形變不同，胡可專一！
manualTranslations.literal: Forms and changes are not the same—how can one be devoted to a single approach!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Circumstances change—how can one cling to a single method!

manualTranslations.zh: 夫以中國強盛，夷狄衰微，而能屈膝稱臣，歸心受制，拒之則阻其向化，威之則類於殺降，安得不存而撫之，即而序之也？
manualTranslations.literal: Now, when China is strong and flourishing and the barbarians are weak and declining, and they are able to bend the knee as subjects and turn their hearts to submission—if one rejects them one obstructs their turning toward civilization; if one threatens them it is like killing those who surrender—how can one not preserve and soothe them, approach them and bring them into order?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When China is strong and the frontier peoples weak, and they come kneeling as subjects, their hearts turned toward obedience—to reject them would block their turning toward civilization; to threaten them would be little better than slaughtering men who have surrendered. How can the court do anything but protect and conciliate them, draw them close, and bring them into proper order?

manualTranslations.zh: 又如中國強盛，夷狄衰微，而尚棄信奸盟，蔑恩肆毒，諭之不變，責之不懲，安得不取亂推亡，息人固境也？
manualTranslations.literal: Again, if China is strong and flourishing and the barbarians are weak and declining, yet they still abandon faith, break alliances treacherously, scorn kindness and unleash cruelty, and instruction does not change them nor censure chastise them—how can one not take their disorder to push them to destruction, give rest to the people and fortify the borders?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Or again: when China is strong and the frontier peoples weak, yet they betray their oaths, break alliances in bad faith, spurn kindness and unleash violence, and neither persuasion nor reproach can move them—how can the court do anything but seize on their disorder to bring about their downfall, spare its own people, and secure the borders?

manualTranslations.zh: 其有遇中國喪亡之弊，當夷狄強盛之時，圖之則彼釁未萌，禦之則我力不足，安得不卑詞降禮，約好通和，啖之以親，紓其交禍？
manualTranslations.literal: When one encounters China's decline and ruin, at a time when the barbarians are strong and flourishing—if one plots against them their provocation has not yet emerged; if one defends against them our strength is insufficient—how can one not use humble words and lowered ceremony, covenant for friendship and open harmony, appease them with intimacy, and relieve the mutual calamity of conflict?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When China is in decline and the frontier peoples are ascendant—plot against them and no provocation has yet arisen; try to resist and one's strength is not enough—how can the court do anything but speak humbly, lower its ceremonial demeanor, seek treaties of friendship, appease them with conciliatory overtures, and avert the disaster of open conflict?

manualTranslations.zh: 縱不必信，且無大侵，雖非禦戎之善經，蓋時事亦有不得已也。
manualTranslations.literal: Even if one need not fully trust them, and there are no major incursions, though this is not the best constant practice for controlling the Rong, yet in the circumstances of the times there are also things one cannot avoid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if such agreements cannot be fully trusted, and even if no major invasion follows, this may not be the ideal long-term policy for managing the frontier—yet there are times when circumstances leave no alternative.

manualTranslations.zh: 儻或夷夏之勢，強弱適同，撫之不寧，威之不靖；
manualTranslations.literal: If perhaps the strength of barbarians and Chinese are equally matched, soothing does not bring peace and threatening does not bring tranquility;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Should the power of the frontier peoples and the Central Realm be evenly matched—so that conciliation cannot secure peace and intimidation cannot restore calm—

manualTranslations.zh: 力足以自保，不足以出攻，得不設險以固軍，訓師以待寇，來則薄伐以遏其深入，去則攘斥而戒於遠追？
manualTranslations.literal: Strength sufficient to protect oneself but insufficient to sally forth in attack—must one not establish defenses to fortify the army, train troops to await raiders, when they come conduct limited campaigns to block their deep penetration, and when they depart drive them off yet refrain from distant pursuit?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and one's strength is enough to defend but not enough to take the offensive—must one not fortify strategic positions, drill the army to await attack, meet incursions with limited counter-raids to check deep penetration, and when the enemy withdraws, drive them off without pursuing too far?

manualTranslations.zh: 雖為安邊之令圖，蓋勢力亦有不得不然也。
manualTranslations.literal: Though this is the excellent plan for securing the borders, it is also that circumstances of power leave no alternative.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though this is the soundest plan for securing the borders, the balance of power may also leave no other choice.

manualTranslations.zh: 故夏之即序，周之於攘，太宗之翦亂，皆乘其時而善用其勢也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore Xia's bringing into order, Zhou's repelling, Taizong's cutting down disorder—all seized their times and well employed their circumstances of power.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus Yu's bringing the Rong into order, the Zhou's repelling of invaders, and Taizong's suppression of rebellion—all seized the moment and made the best use of prevailing conditions.

manualTranslations.zh: 古公之避狄，文、景之和親，神堯之降禮，皆順其時而不失其稱也。
manualTranslations.literal: Lord Ancient's avoiding the Di, Wen and Jing's heqin, Emperor Shenyao's lowered ceremony—all followed the times without losing what was fitting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lord Danfu's flight from the Di, the heqin policies of Emperors Wen and Jing, and Emperor Gaozu's lowered ceremonial demeanor—all conformed to the times without sacrificing what was appropriate.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦皇之長城，漢武之窮討，皆知其事而不度其時者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Qin Shihuang's Great Wall and Emperor Wu of Han's exhaustive campaigns—both knew the matter but did not gauge the times.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang's Great Wall and Emperor Wu's endless campaigns both understood the problem but failed to read the times.

manualTranslations.zh: 向若遇孔熾之勢，行即序之方，則見侮而不從矣！
manualTranslations.literal: If one had encountered overwhelmingly fierce circumstances and pursued the method of bringing into order, then one would be insulted and they would not obey!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Had one pursued a policy of orderly submission in a moment of overwhelming enemy strength, one would only be mocked—and they would refuse to obey!

manualTranslations.zh: 乘可取之資，懷畏避之誌，則失機而養寇矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Seizing resources that could be taken, yet harboring a will of fear and avoidance, one loses opportunity and nourishes the raiders!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To hold the advantage for decisive action yet shrink back in fear is to miss one's chance and feed the enemy's strength!

manualTranslations.zh: 有攘卻之力，用和親之謀，則示弱而勞費矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Having the power to repel and drive back, yet employing heqin strategy, one shows weakness and wastes resources!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To have the power to drive the enemy back yet resort to marriage alliances is to show weakness and squander resources!

manualTranslations.zh: 當降屈之時，務翦伐之略，則召禍而危殆矣！
manualTranslations.literal: When one should submit and yield, yet devoting oneself to aggressive campaigns, one invites calamity and peril!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To pursue aggressive campaigns when one ought to submit is to invite disaster and court destruction!

manualTranslations.zh: 故曰：知其事而不度其時則敗，附其時而不失其稱則成。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus it is said: knowing the matter but not gauging the times leads to failure; adhering to the times without losing what is fitting leads to success.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus it is said: to understand the problem but misread the times is to fail; to follow the demands of the moment without abandoning what is appropriate is to succeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 是無必定之規，亦無長勝之法，得失著效，不其然歟！
manualTranslations.literal: Thus there is no fixed rule, nor any permanently victorious method—the gains and losses prove themselves. Is it not so!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There is no fixed formula and no strategy that always wins—the gains and losses speak for themselves. Is it not so?

manualTranslations.zh: 至於察安危之大情，計成敗之大數，百代之不變易者，蓋有之矣。
manualTranslations.literal: As for discerning the great principle of safety and peril, calculating the great pattern of success and failure—among things unchanged for a hundred generations, these exist.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet in discerning the great principle of safety and peril, and calculating the great pattern of success and failure, there are truths that hold across a hundred generations.

manualTranslations.zh: 其要在於失人肆欲則必蹶，任人從眾則必全，此乃古今所同，而物理之所壹也。
manualTranslations.literal: The crux lies in this: lose the support of people through indulgence of desires and one must stumble; employ people and follow the consensus and one must be preserved. This is the same in ancient and modern times—the single principle of natural order.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The crux is this: to alienate the people through indulgence of one's desires is to invite collapse; to employ the worthy and heed the consensus is to preserve the state. This has been true in every age—it is the one constant principle of nature.

manualTranslations.zh: 國家自祿山構亂、河隴用兵以來，肅宗中興，撤邊備以靖中邦，借外威以寧內難。
manualTranslations.literal: Since the state, from An Lushan's rebellion and campaigns in Hexi and Longyou, when Emperor Suzong restored the dynasty, withdrew border defenses to pacify the Central Plain, and borrowed foreign military might to quell internal troubles.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since An Lushan's rebellion and the campaigns in Hexi and Longyou, the dynasty—when Emperor Suzong restored order—withdrew frontier defenses to pacify the Central Plain and borrowed foreign military power to quell internal strife.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是吐蕃乘釁，吞噬無厭；
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon Tibet seized the opportunity, swallowing territory insatiably;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereupon Tibet seized the opportunity and swallowed territory without end;

manualTranslations.zh: 回紇矜功，憑陵亦甚。
manualTranslations.literal: The Uyghurs flaunted their merits and were also extremely overbearing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the Uyghurs flaunted their contributions and grew ever more overbearing.

manualTranslations.zh: 中國不遑振旅，四十余年。
manualTranslations.literal: China had no leisure to restore its armies—for more than forty years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For more than forty years China had no leisure to rebuild its armies.

manualTranslations.zh: 使傷耗遺氓，竭力蠶織，西輸賄幣，北償馬資，尚不足塞其煩言，滿其驕誌。
manualTranslations.literal: This caused the surviving populace to be depleted, straining themselves at sericulture and weaving, sending tribute westward and paying for horses northward—yet still insufficient to stop their vexatious demands and satisfy their proud ambitions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The surviving populace was worn down, straining at sericulture and weaving to send tribute westward and pay for horses northward—yet still could not satisfy their endless demands or their proud ambitions.

manualTranslations.zh: 復乃遠征士馬，列戍疆陲，猶不能遏其奔沖，止其侵侮。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover they dispatched troops on distant campaigns and stationed garrisons along the borders, yet still could not check their wild charges or stop their raids.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even when troops were sent on distant campaigns and garrisons lined the frontiers, their wild charges could not be checked nor their raids stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 小入則驅略黎庶，深入則震驚邦畿。
manualTranslations.literal: Small incursions meant plundering the common people; deep penetration shook the capital region.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Small raids plundered the common people; deep incursions shook the capital itself.

manualTranslations.zh: 時有議安邊策者，多務於所難而忽於所易，勉於所短而略於所長。
manualTranslations.literal: When border pacification policies were debated, most devoted themselves to what was difficult and neglected what was easy, strained at what was their weakness and overlooked what was their strength.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When border policies were debated, most devoted themselves to what was difficult and neglected what was easy, strained at their weaknesses and overlooked their strengths.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂使所易所長者，行之而其要不精；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus what was easy and their strength—when implemented, its essentials were not refined;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus what was easy and within their strength was pursued without mastering its essentials;

manualTranslations.zh: 所難所短者，圖之而其功靡就。
manualTranslations.literal: What was difficult and their weakness—when plotted, the achievement was never accomplished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: while what was difficult and beyond their strength was attempted without ever achieving success.

manualTranslations.zh: 憂患未弭，職斯之由。
manualTranslations.literal: Calamities not yet settled—this is precisely the reason.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That calamities remain unabated is precisely for this reason.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫制敵行師，必量事勢，勢有難易，事有先後。
manualTranslations.literal: In controlling enemies and deploying armies, one must measure circumstances of affairs; circumstances have easy and difficult aspects, affairs have prior and posterior order.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In controlling enemies and deploying armies, one must weigh the circumstances; circumstances differ in difficulty, and affairs have their proper sequence.

manualTranslations.zh: 力大而敵脆，則先其所難，是謂奪人之心，暫勞而永逸者也；
manualTranslations.literal: When strength is great and the enemy fragile, then strike first at what is difficult—this is called seizing the enemy's heart, temporary toil for permanent ease;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When one's strength is great and the enemy weak, strike first at what is difficult—this is called seizing the enemy's will: temporary hardship for lasting peace;

manualTranslations.zh: 力寡而敵堅，則先其所易，是謂固國之本，觀釁而後動者也。
manualTranslations.literal: When strength is slight and the enemy firm, then strike first at what is easy—this is called securing the foundation of the state, observing provocation before acting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When one's strength is slight and the enemy strong, strike first at what is easy—this is called securing the foundation of the state: watch for provocation before acting.

manualTranslations.zh: 頃屬多故，人勞未瘳，而欲廣發師徒，深踐寇境，復其侵地，攻其堅城，前有勝負未必之虞，後有饋運不繼之患。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently, amid many troubles, the people's exhaustion not yet healed, yet wishing to broadly dispatch armies, deeply penetrate enemy territory, recover invaded lands, attack fortified cities—ahead lies uncertainty of victory or defeat, behind lies the peril of supply lines not continuing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently, amid many troubles, with the people's exhaustion not yet healed, some wish to dispatch armies in force, penetrate deep into enemy territory, recover lost lands, and assault fortified cities—facing uncertainty of victory ahead and the peril of broken supply lines behind.

manualTranslations.zh: 儻或撓敗，適所以啟戎心而挫國威，以此為安邊之謀，可謂不量事勢而務於所難矣！
manualTranslations.literal: If perchance defeated, this would precisely awaken the barbarians' boldness and damage national prestige—to take this as border pacification strategy is truly not measuring circumstances of affairs and devoting oneself to what is difficult!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If defeated, this would only embolden the barbarians and damage national prestige. To take such a course as a border policy is truly to ignore the circumstances and devote oneself to what is hardest!

manualTranslations.zh: 天之授者，有分事，無全功；
manualTranslations.literal: What Heaven bestows: there is division of tasks, no complete achievement in all;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What Heaven bestows comes with divided tasks, not complete mastery of all;

manualTranslations.zh: 地之產者，有物宜，無兼利。
manualTranslations.literal: What Earth produces: each thing has its proper suitability, no combined benefit in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: what Earth produces suits each thing in its own way, not every advantage at once.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以五方之俗，長短各殊。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the customs of the five directions each have their own strengths and weaknesses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the customs of the five directions each have their own strengths and weaknesses.

manualTranslations.zh: 長者不可逾，短者不可企；
manualTranslations.literal: What is long cannot be exceeded; what is short cannot be reached for;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Strengths cannot be surpassed by force of will; weaknesses cannot be wished away;

manualTranslations.zh: 勉所短而敵其所長必殆，用所長而乘其所短必安。
manualTranslations.literal: Straining at what is short and matching against what is long leads to peril; using what is long and exploiting what is short leads to safety.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: to strain at one's weaknesses and contest the enemy's strengths is to court disaster; to employ one's strengths and exploit the enemy's weaknesses is to secure safety.

manualTranslations.zh: 強者，乃以水草為邑居，以射獵供飲茹，多馬而尤便馳突，輕生而不恥敗亡，此戎狄之所長也。
manualTranslations.literal: The strong ones dwell by water and grass as their settlements, sustain themselves by hunting for food and drink, have many horses and are especially adept at swift cavalry charges, hold life lightly and do not shame defeat and death—this is what the Rong and Di excel at.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The strong dwell by water and grass, live by hunting, keep many horses and excel at swift cavalry charges, hold life lightly and do not fear defeat or death—this is what the Rong and Di do best.

manualTranslations.zh: 戎狄之所長，乃中國之所短；
manualTranslations.literal: What the Rong and Di excel at is precisely what China is deficient in;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What the Rong and Di do best is precisely what China does worst;

manualTranslations.zh: 而欲益兵蒐乘，角力爭驅，交鋒原野之間，決命尋常之內，以此為禦寇之術，可謂勉所短而校其所長矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet wishing to increase troops and gather chariots, contending in strength and racing in driving, clashing on open plains and deciding life and death within ordinary range—to take this as the method of repelling raiders is truly straining at what is short and comparing against what is long!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: yet to mass troops and chariots, contest strength in open pursuit, and decide life and death on the plain—to take this as the method of repelling raiders is truly to strain at one's weaknesses and measure oneself against the enemy's strengths!

manualTranslations.zh: 務所難，勉所短，勞費百倍，終於無成。
manualTranslations.literal: Devoting oneself to what is difficult, straining at what is short—labor and expense a hundredfold, ending in no achievement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To devote oneself to what is difficult and strain at what is weak costs a hundredfold in labor and expense, and ends in failure.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖果成之，不挫則廢，豈不以越天授而違地產，虧時勢以反物宜者哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Even if one truly succeeded, without setback it would be abandoned—is this not because one transgresses Heaven's bestowal and violates Earth's products, damages circumstances of the times and reverses each thing's proper suitability!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if one succeeded, the effort could not be sustained without ruin—is this not because one transgresses Heaven's allotment, violates Earth's natural suitability, and works against the demands of the times!

manualTranslations.zh: 將欲去危就安，息費從省，在慎守所易，精用所長而已。
manualTranslations.literal: If one wishes to leave peril and attain safety, cease waste and follow economy, it lies in carefully guarding what is easy and skillfully employing what is long—nothing more.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To leave peril for safety, and end waste through economy, one need only carefully hold to what is easy and skillfully employ what one does best.

manualTranslations.zh: 若乃擇將吏以撫寧眾庶，修紀律以訓齊師徒，耀德以佐威，能邇以柔遠；
manualTranslations.literal: As for selecting generals and officials to pacify and settle the populace, refining discipline to train and align troops, displaying virtue to assist authority, being able with what is near to soften what is far;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Select capable generals and officials to pacify the people; refine discipline to train the troops; let displayed virtue support authority, and let competence at home soften those abroad;

manualTranslations.zh: 禁侵抄之暴以彰吾信，抑攻取之議以安戎心；
manualTranslations.literal: Forbidding the violence of raids and pillaging to manifest our trustworthiness, suppressing proposals for offensive seizure to settle the barbarians' hearts;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: forbid the violence of border raids to demonstrate good faith, and suppress proposals for offensive seizure to reassure the barbarians;

manualTranslations.zh: 彼求和則善待而勿與結盟，彼為寇則嚴備而不務報復，此當今之所易也。
manualTranslations.literal: When they seek peace, treat them well but do not enter alliances with them; when they raid, prepare strictly but do not pursue retaliation—this is what is easy in the present age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When they seek peace, treat them well but do not bind them in formal alliance; when they raid, prepare strictly but do not pursue revenge—this is what is easy in the present age.

manualTranslations.zh: 賤力而貴智，惡殺而好生，輕利而重人，忍小以全大，安其居而後動，俟其時而後行。
manualTranslations.literal: Valuing wisdom over brute force, hating killing and loving life, holding profit lightly and people heavily, enduring small losses to preserve the great, settling one's position before acting, awaiting the right moment before moving.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Value wisdom over brute force; hate killing and cherish life; hold profit lightly and people dearly; endure small losses to preserve the greater good; settle one's position before acting, and wait for the right moment before moving.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以修封疆，守要害，塹蹊隧，壘軍營，謹禁防，明斥候，務農以足食，練卒以蓄威，非萬全不謀，非百克不鬥。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus repair borders, hold strategic passes, trench paths and tunnels, fortify camps, strictly guard defenses, clearly post scouts, devote to agriculture to fill granaries, drill soldiers to store up might—do not plan without perfect readiness, do not fight without assurance of hundredfold victory.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus repair the borders, hold strategic passes, trench roads and tunnels, fortify camps, guard defenses strictly, post scouts clearly, devote to farming to fill the granaries, and drill soldiers to store up strength—do not plan without perfect readiness, and do not fight without assurance of overwhelming victory.

manualTranslations.zh: 寇小至則張聲勢以遏其入，寇大至則謀其人以邀其歸；
manualTranslations.literal: When raiders come in small numbers, display force to block their entry; when raiders come in large numbers, plot against their leaders to intercept their return;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When raiders come in small numbers, display force to block their entry; when they come in force, plot against their leaders to cut off their retreat;

manualTranslations.zh: 據險以乘之，多方以誤之。
manualTranslations.literal: Hold the terrain and exploit it against them, use many stratagems to mislead them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hold the terrain and turn it against them; use many stratagems to confuse them.

manualTranslations.zh: 使其勇無所加，眾無所用；
manualTranslations.literal: Cause their courage to have nothing to apply, their numbers to have no use;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Render their courage useless and their numbers impotent;

manualTranslations.zh: 掠則靡獲，攻則不能；
manualTranslations.literal: When they plunder they gain nothing, when they attack they cannot succeed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they plunder they gain nothing; when they attack they cannot prevail;

manualTranslations.zh: 進有腹背受敵之虞，退有首尾難救之患，所謂乘其弊，不戰而屈人之兵，此中國之所長也。
manualTranslations.literal: Advancing they face the peril of enemies front and rear; retreating they face the trouble of head and tail hard to rescue—what is called exploiting their weakness, subduing the enemy's army without battle—this is what China excels at.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: advancing they face enemies before and behind; retreating they find no rescue possible—what is called exploiting their weakness and subduing the enemy without battle. This is what China does best.

manualTranslations.zh: 我之所長，乃戎狄之所短；
manualTranslations.literal: What we excel at is precisely what the Rong and Di are deficient in;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What we do best is precisely what the Rong and Di do worst;

manualTranslations.zh: 我之所易，乃戎狄之所難。
manualTranslations.literal: What is easy for us is precisely what is difficult for the Rong and Di.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: what is easy for us is precisely what is hard for them.

manualTranslations.zh: 以長制短，則用力寡而見功多；
manualTranslations.literal: Using the long to control the short, then effort applied is slight yet achievements seen are many;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Use strength against weakness, and little effort yields great results;

manualTranslations.zh: 以易敵難，則財不匱而事速就。
manualTranslations.literal: Using the easy to match the difficult, then wealth is not exhausted and affairs are quickly accomplished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: use the easy against the hard, and resources are not exhausted while success comes quickly.

manualTranslations.zh: 舍此不務，而反為所乘，斯謂倒持戈矛，以钅尊授寇者也！
manualTranslations.literal: Abandoning this and not devoting oneself to it, yet instead being exploited by them—this is what is called holding one's spear and halberd reversed, handing the socket to the raider!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To abandon this and instead be exploited by the enemy is what is called holding one's weapons reversed and handing the hilt to the raider!

manualTranslations.zh: 今則皆務之矣，猶且守封未固，寇戎未懲者，其病在於謀無定用，眾無適從。
manualTranslations.literal: Now all devote themselves to it, yet still border defenses are not secure and raiders are not chastised—the flaw lies in plans having no fixed application and the multitude having no clear direction to follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet though all now profess to pursue this course, the borders remain unsecured and the raiders undeterred—the flaw lies in plans without fixed application and the multitude without clear direction.

manualTranslations.zh: 所任不必才，才者不必任；
manualTranslations.literal: Those appointed are not necessarily capable; the capable are not necessarily appointed;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those appointed are not necessarily capable; the capable are not necessarily appointed;

manualTranslations.zh: 所聞不必實，實者不必聞；
manualTranslations.literal: What is heard is not necessarily true; what is true is not necessarily heard;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: what is heard is not necessarily true; what is true is not necessarily heard;

manualTranslations.zh: 所信不必誠，誠者不必信；
manualTranslations.literal: What is trusted is not necessarily sincere; the sincere are not necessarily trusted;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: what is trusted is not necessarily sincere; the sincere are not necessarily trusted;

manualTranslations.zh: 所行不必當，當者未必行。
manualTranslations.literal: What is done is not necessarily fitting; what is fitting is not necessarily done.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: what is done is not necessarily right; what is right is not necessarily done.

manualTranslations.zh: 故令措置乖方，課責虧度；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus orders are arranged wrongly, assessment and responsibility fall short of measure;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus policy is misdirected and accountability falls short;

manualTranslations.zh: 財匱於兵眾，力分於將多，怨生於不均，機失於遙制。
manualTranslations.literal: Wealth is exhausted by numerous troops, strength divided among many generals, resentment born from inequality, opportunity lost through remote control.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Treasury depleted by excessive troops, strength divided among too many generals, resentment born of inequity, opportunity lost through remote control.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣請為陛下粗陳六者之失，惟明主慎聽而熟察之：臣聞工欲善其事，必先利其器；
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant requests to briefly set forth for Your Majesty the faults of these six points—may the enlightened ruler listen carefully and examine them closely:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your servant requests to outline for Your Majesty the faults in these six areas—may the enlightened ruler listen carefully and examine them closely:

manualTranslations.zh: 武欲勝其敵，必先練其兵。
manualTranslations.literal: If a warrior wishes to defeat his enemy, he must first drill his troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if a warrior wishes to defeat his enemy, he must first drill his troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 練兵之中，所用復異。
manualTranslations.literal: Among methods of drilling troops, what is employed also differs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet among methods of drilling troops, what is employed also differs.

manualTranslations.zh: 用之於救急，則權以紓難；
manualTranslations.literal: Employed for emergency relief, then use expedient measures to ease crisis;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Employed for emergency relief, troops are used flexibly to ease crisis;

manualTranslations.zh: 用之於暫敵，則緩以應機。
manualTranslations.literal: Employed for temporary enemy engagement, then use flexibility to respond to opportunity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: employed for temporary engagement with the enemy, they are deployed flexibly to seize opportunity.

manualTranslations.zh: 故事有便宜，而不拘常制；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus affairs have what is expedient, without being bound by regular regulations;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus affairs have their expedients, unconstrained by regular regulations;

manualTranslations.zh: 謀有奇詭，而不徇眾情。
manualTranslations.literal: Plans have strange stratagems, without following popular sentiment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and plans have their stratagems, unconstrained by popular sentiment.

manualTranslations.zh: 進退死生，唯將所命，此所謂攻討之兵也！
manualTranslations.literal: Advance, retreat, life and death—all at the general's command—this is what is called offensive campaigning troops!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Advance, retreat, life and death—all at the general's command. These are what are called offensive campaigning troops!

manualTranslations.zh: 用之於屯戍，則事資可久；
manualTranslations.literal: Employed for garrison duty, then affairs rely on what can endure;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Employed for garrison duty, affairs depend on what can endure;

manualTranslations.zh: 勢異從權，非物理所愜不寧，非人情所欲不固。
manualTranslations.literal: Circumstances differ so follow expedient authority—unless nature's principles are satisfied there is no peace, unless human sentiment desires it there is no stability.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: circumstances differ, so one follows expedient measures—unless natural conditions are satisfied there is no peace, unless human sentiment is accommodated there is no stability.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫人情者，利焉則勸，習焉則安，保親戚則樂生，顧家業則忘死，故可以理術馭，不可以法制驅，此所謂鎮守之兵也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now human sentiment: where there is profit one is encouraged, where there is habit one is at ease, protecting kin one loves life, looking to family estate one forgets death—thus they can be governed by reason and art, but cannot be driven by law and regulation—this is what is called garrison defensive troops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Human sentiment responds to profit with effort, to habit with ease; men who protect their kin love life, and men who look to their families forget death. Such troops can be governed by reason but cannot be driven by regulation alone. These are what are called garrison defensive troops.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫欲備封疆，禦戎狄，非一朝一夕之事，固當選鎮守之兵以置焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Now, to prepare border defenses and control the Rong and Di is not a matter of one morning or one evening—it is right to select garrison troops and station them there.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To prepare the borders and defend against the Rong and Di is not work of a single day—it is right to select garrison troops and station them accordingly.

manualTranslations.zh: 古之善選置者，必量其性習，辨其土宜，察其伎能，知其欲惡。
manualTranslations.literal: Those skilled in selection and stationing in antiquity necessarily gauged their natures and habits, distinguished regional suitability, observed their skills and abilities, and knew their desires and aversions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those skilled in selection and stationing in antiquity gauged men's natures and habits, distinguished regional suitability, observed their skills, and knew their desires and aversions.

manualTranslations.zh: 用其力而不違其性，齊其俗而不易其宜；
manualTranslations.literal: Employing their strength without violating their nature, aligning their customs without changing their suitability;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They employed men's strength without violating their nature, and aligned their customs without forcing them against their proper place.

manualTranslations.zh: 引其善而不責其所不能，禁其非而不處其所不欲。
manualTranslations.literal: Leading them by their strengths without holding them responsible for what they cannot do, restraining their faults without placing them in what they do not wish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They drew out men's strengths without demanding what they could not give, and checked their faults without posting them where they did not wish to be.

manualTranslations.zh: 而又類其紀伍，安其室家，然後能使之樂其居，定其誌，奮其氣勢，結其恩情。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover aligning their ranks and units, settling their households and families—only then could they make them content in their residence, fix their resolve, rouse their martial spirit, and bind their bonds of affection.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They organized their ranks, settled their families—and only then could men be made content where they lived, steady in purpose, bold in spirit, and bound to one another in loyalty.

manualTranslations.zh: 撫之以惠，則感而不驕；
manualTranslations.literal: Consoling them with kindness, then they are grateful and not arrogant;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Treat them with kindness and they respond with gratitude, not arrogance;

manualTranslations.zh: 臨之以威，則肅而不怨。
manualTranslations.literal: Confronting them with authority, then they are reverent and not resentful.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: confront them with authority and they stand in awe without resentment.

manualTranslations.zh: 靡督課而人自為用，弛禁防而眾自不攜。
manualTranslations.literal: Without supervision and assessment yet people of themselves apply their efforts; relaxed prohibitions and guards yet the masses of themselves do not rebel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without heavy supervision men applied themselves; with lighter restrictions the troops did not turn disloyal.

manualTranslations.zh: 故出則足兵，居則足食，守則固，戰則強。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus when deployed there were sufficient troops, when stationed sufficient provisions, in defense they were solid, in battle they were strong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deployed abroad they were sufficient in numbers; at rest they had enough food; in defense they stood firm; in battle they fought strong.

manualTranslations.zh: 其術無他，便於人情而已矣！
manualTranslations.literal: The method had nothing else—it was merely accommodating human sentiment, that is all!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The method was nothing more than this: accommodate human nature!

manualTranslations.zh: 今者散征士卒，分戍邊陲，更代往來，以為守備。
manualTranslations.literal: Now scattered conscription of soldiers, divided garrison at the border marches, rotation back and forth, taking this as border defense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today soldiers are conscripted from scattered sources, posted in rotation to the frontier marches, and sent back and forth in turn—all this passes for border defense.

manualTranslations.zh: 是則不量性習，不辨土宜，邀其所不能，強其所不欲。
manualTranslations.literal: This then does not gauge nature and habit, does not distinguish regional suitability, demands what they cannot do, forces what they do not wish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is to ignore men's natures and habits, disregard regional suitability, demand what they cannot give, and force what they do not wish.

manualTranslations.zh: 求廣其數而不考其用，將致其力而不察其情，斯可以為羽衛之儀，而無益於備禦之實也。
manualTranslations.literal: Seeking to broaden their numbers without examining their use, about to exert their strength without investigating their sentiments—this can serve as the form of guard escort, but is of no benefit to the substance of border defense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The state seeks to swell head counts without examining utility, and expects men's exertions without understanding their hearts. Such an army may look the part of a royal guard, but it does nothing for real border defense.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: Why is this so?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

manualTranslations.zh: 窮邊之地，千里蕭條，寒風裂膚，驚沙慘目；
manualTranslations.literal: The remote frontier—desolate for a thousand li, cold wind splitting skin, startling sand blinding the eyes;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The remote frontier is desolate for a thousand li; cold wind splits the skin and blinding sand stings the eyes;

manualTranslations.zh: 與豺狼為鄰伍，以戰鬥為嬉遊；
manualTranslations.literal: Neighboring wolves and jackals, taking battle as sport and play;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: men live among wolves and jackals and treat battle as sport;

manualTranslations.zh: 晝則荷戈而耕，夜則倚烽而覘；
manualTranslations.literal: By day carrying halberds while plowing, by night leaning on beacon towers to watch;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: by day they plow with weapons on their backs, by night they lean on beacon towers to keep watch;

manualTranslations.zh: 日有剽害之慮，永無休暇之娛，地惡人勤，於斯為甚！
manualTranslations.literal: Daily fear of plunder and harm, never a moment's leisure for pleasure—the land is harsh and the labor severe, nowhere more so than here!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: each day brings fear of raid and slaughter, never a moment's rest for pleasure—the land is harsh and the labor crushing, nowhere more so than here!

manualTranslations.zh: 自非生於其域，習於其風，幼而睹焉，長而安焉，不見樂土而遷焉，則罕能寧其居而狎其敵也。
manualTranslations.literal: Unless born in that region, accustomed to its winds, seeing it from youth and settling into it from age, never having known a pleasant land to move to—rarely can one settle contentedly in residence and grow familiar with the enemy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Unless a man is born there, raised in its ways, accustomed from childhood and settled in adulthood, never having known a gentler land to move to—rarely can he live content on the frontier or grow familiar with the enemy.

manualTranslations.zh: 關東之地，百物阜殷，從軍之徒，尤被優養。
manualTranslations.literal: The lands east of the pass abound in all goods; those who join the army are especially well cared for.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: East of the pass the land is rich in every commodity, and those who join the army are especially well cared for.

manualTranslations.zh: 慣於溫飽，狎於歡康，比諸邊隅，若異天地。
manualTranslations.literal: Accustomed to warmth and full bellies, familiar with ease and comfort—compared to the border corners, it is as if another heaven and earth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Accustomed to warmth and full bellies, to ease and comfort—they might as well live in another world from the borderlands.

manualTranslations.zh: 聞絕塞荒陬之苦，則辛酸動容；
manualTranslations.literal: Hearing of the bitter hardships of the far frontier wastes, their faces twist with anguish;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hear of the bitter hardships of the far frontier and their faces twist with anguish;

manualTranslations.zh: 聆強蕃勁虜之名，則懾駭奪氣。
manualTranslations.literal: Hearing the names of powerful fan tribes and fierce enemies, they are seized with terror and lose their spirit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: hear the names of powerful barbarian tribes and fierce enemies and terror steals their breath.

manualTranslations.zh: 而乃使之去親族，舍園廬，甘其所辛酸，抗其所懾駭，將冀為用，不亦疏乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet you would have them leave their kin, abandon their homes and gardens, accept those bitter hardships, and stand against what fills them with terror—and still expect them to be useful? How far-fetched!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet you would have them leave their kin, abandon their homes, accept those bitter hardships, and stand against what fills them with terror—and still expect them to be useful? How far-fetched!

manualTranslations.zh: 矧又有休代之期，無統帥之馭，資奉若驕子，姑息如倩人，進不邀之以成功，退不處之以嚴憲。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover there are periods of relief and rotation, no commanding general's control; provisions and pay as for spoiled children, indulgence as for hired hands; on advance not urged toward success, on retreat not held to strict discipline.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover they serve on fixed rotations under no commanding general's firm hand; rations and pay are lavished on them like spoiled children, indulgence extended like hired laborers; on advance they are not pressed toward victory, on retreat they are not held to strict discipline.

manualTranslations.zh: 其來也鹹負得色，其止也莫有固心，屈指計歸，張頤待飼。
manualTranslations.literal: When they arrive all wear the look of one who has gained something; when they halt none has a steadfast heart; they count on their fingers the days till return, mouths open awaiting rations.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When they arrive, all wear the look of men who have gained something; once posted, none has a steadfast heart. They count on their fingers the days till rotation, mouths open awaiting rations.

manualTranslations.zh: 僥倖者猶患還期之賒緩，常念戎醜之充斥；
manualTranslations.literal: Even the fortunate still worry that the rotation period will be delayed, constantly mindful that enemy raiders fill the land;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even the fortunate still worry that rotation will be delayed, constantly mindful that enemy raiders fill the land;

manualTranslations.zh: 王師挫傷，則將乘其亂離，布路東潰，情誌且爾，得之奚為？
manualTranslations.literal: If the imperial armies suffer defeat, they will seize the disorder to scatter eastward along every road—their hearts and wills being thus, what use is there in having them?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the imperial armies suffer defeat, they will seize the disorder to scatter eastward along every road—their hearts and wills being thus, what use is there in having them?

manualTranslations.zh: 平居則殫耗資儲以奉浮冗之眾，臨難則拔棄城鎮以搖遠近之心，其弊豈惟無益哉！
manualTranslations.literal: In ordinary times they exhaust stores and resources to support this idle redundant host; in crisis they abandon towns and forts and shake the hearts of near and far—the harm is not merely that they are useless!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In ordinary times they drain stores and resources to support this idle, redundant host; in crisis they abandon towns and forts and shake the hearts of near and far—the harm is not merely that they are useless!

manualTranslations.zh: 固亦將有所撓也。
manualTranslations.literal: They will also undermine our position.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They will also undermine our position.

manualTranslations.zh: 復有抵犯刑禁，謫徙軍城，意欲增戶實邊，兼令展效自贖。
manualTranslations.literal: There are also those who violate criminal prohibitions, exiled to garrison towns—the intent being to increase households and populate the border, and also to let them redeem themselves through service.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There are also criminals exiled to garrison towns—the intent being to increase households and populate the border, and also to let them redeem themselves through service.

manualTranslations.zh: 既是無良之類，且加懷土之情，思亂幸災，又甚戍卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Since they are already worthless types, and with the added attachment to home soil, longing for disorder and hoping for disaster—they are worse than regular garrison soldiers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They are already worthless men, and with their attachment to home they long for disorder and hope for disaster—they are worse than ordinary garrison soldiers.

manualTranslations.zh: 適足煩於防衛，諒無望於功庸，雖前代時或行之，固非良算之可遵者也。
manualTranslations.literal: They merely add to the burden of defense, surely with no hope of achievement; though former dynasties sometimes employed this policy, it is certainly not a sound plan to follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They merely add to the burden of defense, with no hope of achievement; though former dynasties sometimes employed this policy, it is certainly not a sound plan to follow.

manualTranslations.zh: 復有擁旄之帥，身不臨邊，但分偏師，俾守疆場。
manualTranslations.literal: There are also commanders bearing banners and staffs who do not personally go to the border, but only assign detached units to guard the frontier.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There are also commanders bearing banners and staffs who never go to the border themselves, but only assign detached units to guard the frontier.

manualTranslations.zh: 大抵軍中壯銳，元戎例選自隨，委其疲羸，乃配諸鎮。
manualTranslations.literal: Generally the strong and sharp troops in the army—the supreme commander as a rule selects for his own following, consigning the worn and weak to be assigned to the garrisons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a rule the supreme commander keeps the army's strongest and sharpest troops for himself and consigns the worn and weak to the garrisons.

manualTranslations.zh: 節將既居內地，精兵祗備紀綱，遂令守要禦沖，常在寡弱之輩。
manualTranslations.literal: Since the frontier commissioners remain in the interior, elite troops are kept only for discipline and order—and so those who hold key passes and guard approaches are constantly the weak and few.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since frontier commissioners remain in the interior and elite troops are kept only for discipline and order, those who hold key passes and guard approaches are constantly the weak and few.

manualTranslations.zh: 寇戎每至，乃勢不支，入壘者才足閉關，在野者悉遭劫執，恣其芟蹂，盡其搜驅。
manualTranslations.literal: Each time raiders arrive, the garrisons cannot hold; those who enter the ramparts barely manage to shut the gates; those in the open country are all seized in raids; the enemy ravages at will and drives off everything in search.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each time raiders arrive the garrisons cannot hold; those who reach the ramparts barely manage to shut the gates; those in the open country are all seized. The enemy ravages at will and drives off everything they can find.

manualTranslations.zh: 比及都府聞知，虜已克獲旋返。
manualTranslations.literal: By the time the regional headquarters learn of it, the enemy has already taken their plunder and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By the time the regional headquarters learn of it, the enemy has already taken their plunder and returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 且安邊之本，所切在兵，理兵若斯，可謂措置乖方矣！
manualTranslations.literal: The foundation of securing the border lies above all in the army—to manage troops in this fashion may be called misplaced arrangements!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The foundation of securing the border lies above all in the army—to manage troops in this fashion is what I call misplaced arrangements!

manualTranslations.zh: 夫賞以存勸，罰以示懲，勸以懋有庸，懲以威不恪。
manualTranslations.literal: Rewards exist to preserve encouragement; punishments to show chastisement; encouragement to promote achievement; chastisement to awe the undisciplined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rewards exist to preserve encouragement; punishments to show chastisement; encouragement to promote achievement; chastisement to awe the undisciplined.

manualTranslations.zh: 故賞罰之於馭眾也，猶繩墨之於曲直，權衡之揣重輕，輗軏之所以行車，銜勒之所以服馬也。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus rewards and punishments in governing the masses are like the carpenter's line for straight and crooked, the balance for weighing heavy and light, the yoke-bar for making the cart go, the bit and reins for making the horse obey.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus rewards and punishments in governing troops are like the carpenter's line for straight and crooked, the balance for weighing heavy and light, the yoke-bar that makes the cart go, the bit and reins that make the horse obey.

manualTranslations.zh: 馭眾而不用賞罰，則善惡相混而能否莫殊；
manualTranslations.literal: Governing the masses without using rewards and punishments, then good and evil mix together and the capable and incapable are not distinguished;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Governing troops without rewards and punishments mixes good and evil until the capable and incapable cannot be told apart;

manualTranslations.zh: 用之而不當功過，則奸妄寵榮而忠實擯抑。
manualTranslations.literal: Using them but not matching them to merit and fault, then the treacherous and arrogant are favored with glory while the loyal and honest are pushed aside.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: using them but not matching them to merit and fault favors the treacherous and arrogant while pushing aside the loyal and honest.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫如是，若聰明可衒，律度無章，則用與不用，其弊一也。
manualTranslations.literal: If matters stand thus—even if one has brilliance to display, if laws and standards are without rule, then using or not using rewards and punishments—the harm is the same.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If matters stand thus—even if one has brilliance to display, if laws and standards are without rule, then using or not using rewards and punishments, the harm is the same.

manualTranslations.zh: 自頃權移於下，柄失於朝，將之號令，既鮮克行之於軍，國之典章，又不能施之於將，務相遵養，茍度歲時。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently authority has shifted downward and control been lost at court; commanders' orders rarely prevail in the army, and the state's statutes cannot be enforced upon generals—they merely watch over one another indulgently, passing the years as they may.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently authority has shifted downward and control been lost at court; commanders' orders rarely prevail in the army, and the state's statutes cannot be enforced upon generals—they merely watch over one another indulgently, passing the years as they may.

manualTranslations.zh: 欲賞一有功，翻慮無功者反側；
manualTranslations.literal: Wishing to reward one who has merit, one instead worries that the meritless will grow restless;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wishing to reward one who has merit, one instead worries that the meritless will grow restless;

manualTranslations.zh: 欲罰一有罪，復慮同惡者憂虞。
manualTranslations.literal: Wishing to punish one who is guilty, one again worries that fellow evildoers will be anxious.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: wishing to punish one who is guilty, one again worries that fellow evildoers will be anxious.

manualTranslations.zh: 罪以隱忍而不彰，功以嫌疑而不賞，姑息之道，乃至於斯。
manualTranslations.literal: Crimes are hidden and tolerated rather than exposed; merit is left unrewarded through suspicion—the way of indulgence has reached this point.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Crimes are hidden and tolerated rather than exposed; merit is left unrewarded through suspicion—the way of indulgence has reached this point.

manualTranslations.zh: 故使忘身效節者，獲誚於等夷；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus those who forget themselves to serve loyalty are mocked by their peers;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus those who forget themselves in loyal service are mocked by their peers;

manualTranslations.zh: 率眾先登者，取怨於士卒；
manualTranslations.literal: Those who lead the ranks in the first assault earn the soldiers' resentment;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: those who lead the ranks in the first assault earn the soldiers' resentment;

manualTranslations.zh: 僨軍蹙國者，不懷於愧畏；
manualTranslations.literal: Those who fail the army and distress the state feel no shame or fear;
