manualTranslations.idiomatic: those who fail the army and distress the state feel no shame or fear;

manualTranslations.zh: 緩救失期者，自以為智能。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who delay relief and miss their deadlines consider themselves clever.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: those who delay relief and miss their deadlines consider themselves clever.

manualTranslations.zh: 褒貶既闕而不行，稱毀復紛然相亂，人雖欲善，誰為言之？
manualTranslations.literal: Praise and blame being absent and not enforced, slander and praise again swirl in confusion—though men wish to do good, who will speak for them?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With praise and blame absent and unenforced, slander and praise swirl in confusion—though men wish to do good, who will speak for them?

manualTranslations.zh: 況又公忠者，直己而不求於人，反罹困厄；
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the fair and loyal, upright in themselves and not seeking from others, instead suffer hardship;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover the fair and loyal, upright in themselves and not seeking from others, instead suffer hardship;

manualTranslations.zh: 敗撓者，行私而茍媚於眾，例獲優崇。
manualTranslations.literal: Failures and shirkers, pursuing private ends and fawning on the masses, routinely receive preferment and honor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: failures and shirkers, pursuing private ends and fawning on the masses, routinely receive preferment and honor.

manualTranslations.zh: 此義士所以痛心，勇夫所以解體也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is why men of principle are heartbroken and brave men lose their fighting spirit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is why men of principle are heartbroken and brave men lose their fighting spirit.

manualTranslations.zh: 又有遇敵而所守不固，陳謀而其效靡成；
manualTranslations.literal: There are also cases of encountering the enemy but failing to hold what was defended, of laying plans yet achieving no result;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There are also cases of encountering the enemy but failing to hold what was defended, of laying plans yet achieving no result;

manualTranslations.zh: 將帥則以資糧不足為詞，有司復以供給無闕為解。
manualTranslations.literal: The generals cite insufficient supplies as their excuse, while the responsible offices reply that provisions were delivered without shortage.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The generals cite insufficient supplies as their excuse, while the responsible offices reply that provisions were delivered without shortage.

manualTranslations.zh: 既相執證，理合辨明，朝廷每為含糊，未嘗窮究曲直。
manualTranslations.literal: Since each side holds to its proof, the truth ought to be sorted out—yet the court habitually responds with evasion and never thoroughly investigates right and wrong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since each side holds to its proof, the truth ought to be sorted out—yet the court habitually responds with evasion and never thoroughly investigates right and wrong.

manualTranslations.zh: 措理者吞聲而靡訴，誣善者罔上而不慚。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who have managed affairs swallow their words and cannot appeal; those who slander the good deceive their superiors without shame.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who have managed affairs swallow their words and cannot appeal; those who slander the good deceive their superiors without shame.

manualTranslations.zh: 馭眾若斯，可謂課責虧度矣！
manualTranslations.literal: To govern the masses in this fashion may be called deficient accountability!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To govern troops in this fashion is what I call deficient accountability!

manualTranslations.zh: 課責虧度，措置乖方，將不得竭其材，卒不得盡其力，屯集雖眾，戰陣莫前。
manualTranslations.literal: With deficient accountability and misplaced arrangements, generals cannot exhaust their talents, soldiers cannot give their full strength—though gathered in great numbers, none advance in battle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With deficient accountability and misplaced arrangements, generals cannot exhaust their talents and soldiers cannot give their full strength—though gathered in great numbers, none advance in battle.

manualTranslations.zh: 虜每越境橫行，若涉無人之地；
manualTranslations.literal: The enemy crosses the border and rampages at will, as if walking through unoccupied land;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The enemy crosses the border and rampages at will, as if walking through unoccupied land;

manualTranslations.zh: 遞相推倚，無敢誰何，虛張賊勢上聞，則曰兵少不敵。
manualTranslations.literal: Each shifts blame to the next, none dares act—and when they falsely inflate the enemy's strength in reports to the throne, they say their troops are too few to resist.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each shifts blame to the next, none dares act—and when they falsely inflate the enemy's strength in reports to the throne, they say their troops are too few to resist.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷莫之省察，惟務征發益師，無裨備禦之功，重增供億之弊。
manualTranslations.literal: The court does not examine this, but only presses conscription and reinforcements—adding nothing to border defense, only multiplying the burden of supply.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court does not examine this, but only presses conscription and reinforcements—adding nothing to border defense, only multiplying the burden of supply.

manualTranslations.zh: 閭井日耗，征求日繁，以編戶傾家破產之資，兼有司榷鹽稅酒之利，總其所入，半以事邊，制用若斯，可謂財匱於兵眾矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Registered households dwindle day by day, levies grow daily more oppressive—drawing on resources that ruin families and drain estates, together with monopoly profits on salt, wine, and taxes—of total revenue, half goes to the border. To manage resources thus may be called resources exhausted by the multitude of troops!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Registered households dwindle day by day and levies grow ever more oppressive—drawing on resources that ruin families and drain estates, together with monopoly profits on salt, wine, and taxes. Of total revenue, half goes to the border. To manage resources thus is what I call resources exhausted by the multitude of troops!

manualTranslations.zh: 今四夷之最強盛為中國甚患者，莫大於吐蕃，舉國勝兵之徒，才當中國十數大郡而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Among the four barbarians, the strongest and greatest threat to China is none greater than Tibet—their entire nation of able fighters amounts only to a dozen or so large commanderies of China.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among the four barbarians, the strongest and greatest threat to China is none greater than Tibet—their entire nation of able fighters amounts only to a dozen or so large commanderies of China.

manualTranslations.zh: 其於內虞外備，亦與中國不殊，所能寇邊，數則蓋寡。
manualTranslations.literal: In internal worries and external defenses they differ little from China; the forces they can send to raid the border are in number surely few.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In internal worries and external defenses they differ little from China; the forces they can send to raid the border are surely few in number.

manualTranslations.zh: 且又器非犀利，甲不堅完，識迷韜鈐，藝乏趫敏。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover their weapons are not sharp, their armor not solid and complete; their understanding of military arts is confused, their skills lack agility.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover their weapons are not sharp, their armor not solid and complete; their understanding of military arts is confused, their skills lack agility.

manualTranslations.zh: 動則中國畏其眾而不敢抗，靜則中國憚其強而不敢侵，厥理何哉？
manualTranslations.literal: When they move, China fears their numbers and dares not resist; when they rest, China dreads their strength and dares not attack—what is the reason for this?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When they move, China fears their numbers and dares not resist; when they rest, China dreads their strength and dares not attack—what is the reason for this?

manualTranslations.zh: 良以中國之節制多門，蕃醜之統帥專一故也。
manualTranslations.literal: Truly because China's command structure has many gates, while the barbarian chieftains' command is unified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Truly because China's command structure has many gates, while the barbarian chieftains' command is unified.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫統帥專則人心不分，人心不分則號令不貳，號令不貳則進退可齊，進退可齊則疾徐如意，疾徐如意則機會靡愆，機會靡愆則氣勢自壯！
manualTranslations.literal: When command is unified, hearts are not divided; when hearts are not divided, orders are not twofold; when orders are not twofold, advance and retreat can be aligned; when advance and retreat can be aligned, speed and pause obey the will; when speed and pause obey the will, opportunities are not missed; when opportunities are not missed, martial spirit naturally grows strong!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When command is unified, hearts are not divided; when hearts are not divided, orders are not twofold; when orders are not twofold, advance and retreat can be aligned; when advance and retreat can be aligned, speed and pause obey the will; when speed and pause obey the will, opportunities are not missed; when opportunities are not missed, martial spirit naturally grows strong!

manualTranslations.zh: 斯乃以少為眾，以弱為強，變化翕辟，在於反掌之內。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus with few they become many, with weak they become strong; transformation expanding and contracting lies within the turn of the palm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus with few they become many, with weak they become strong; transformation expanding and contracting lies within the turn of the palm.

manualTranslations.zh: 是猶臂之使指，心之制形，若所任得人，則何敵之有！
manualTranslations.literal: It is like the arm commanding the fingers, the heart governing the body—if the right men are appointed, what enemy could there be!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It is like the arm commanding the fingers, the heart governing the body—if the right men are appointed, what enemy could there be!

manualTranslations.zh: 夫節制多門則人心不一，人心不一則號令不行，號令不行則進退難必，進退難必則疾徐失宜，疾徐失宜則機會不及，機會不及則氣勢自衰！
manualTranslations.literal: When command has many gates, hearts are not united; when hearts are not united, orders are not carried out; when orders are not carried out, advance and retreat cannot be assured; when advance and retreat cannot be assured, speed and pause fall out of alignment; when speed and pause fall out of alignment, opportunities are not seized; when opportunities are not seized, martial spirit naturally wanes!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When command has many gates, hearts are not united; when hearts are not united, orders are not carried out; when orders are not carried out, advance and retreat cannot be assured; when advance and retreat cannot be assured, speed and pause fall out of alignment; when speed and pause fall out of alignment, opportunities are not seized; when opportunities are not seized, martial spirit naturally wanes!

manualTranslations.zh: 斯乃勇廢為尪，眾散為弱，逗撓離析，兆乎戰陣之前。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus courage collapses into weakness, the multitude scatters into feebleness—hesitation and dissolution show themselves before the battle line.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus courage collapses into weakness, the multitude scatters into feebleness—hesitation and dissolution show themselves before the battle line.

manualTranslations.zh: 是猶一國三公，十羊九牧，欲令齊肅，其可得乎？
manualTranslations.literal: It is like three dukes in one state, nine herdsmen for ten sheep—wishing to make them uniformly disciplined, how could it be achieved?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It is like three dukes in one state, nine herdsmen for ten sheep—wishing to make them uniformly disciplined, how could it be achieved?

manualTranslations.zh: 開元、天寶之間，控禦西北兩蕃，唯朔方、河西、隴右三節度而已，猶慮權分勢散，或使兼而領之。
manualTranslations.literal: Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, controlling the two fan peoples of the northwest required only the three frontier commissions of Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou—and even then there was concern that divided authority would scatter strength, so sometimes one man was made to command them jointly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, controlling the two northwestern barbarian peoples required only the three frontier commissions of Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou—and even then there was concern that divided authority would scatter strength, so sometimes one man was made to command them jointly.

manualTranslations.zh: 中興已來，未遑外討，僑隸四鎮於安定，權附隴右於扶風，所當西北兩蕃，亦朔方、涇原、隴右、河東節度而已，關東戍卒，至則屬焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Since the restoration, with no leisure for external campaigns, the Four Garrisons were provisionally attached at Anding and Longyou provisionally subordinated at Fufeng—against the two northwestern fan peoples there were again only the Shuofang, Jingyuan, Longyou, and Hedong commissions; garrison soldiers from east of the pass, when they arrived, fell under their authority.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since the restoration, with no leisure for external campaigns, the Four Garrisons were provisionally attached at Anding and Longyou provisionally subordinated at Fufeng. Against the two northwestern barbarian peoples there were again only the Shuofang, Jingyuan, Longyou, and Hedong commissions; garrison soldiers from east of the pass, when they arrived, fell under their authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖委任未盡得人，而措置尚存典制。
manualTranslations.literal: Though appointments did not always find the right men, the arrangements still preserved the proper institutions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though appointments did not always find the right men, the arrangements still preserved the proper institutions.

manualTranslations.zh: 自頃逆泚誘涇、隴之眾叛，懷光汙朔方之軍，割裂誅鋤，所余無幾。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently the rebel Zhu Ci induced the armies of Jing and Long to defect; Huai'guang corrupted the Shuofang army—after partition and purges, little remained.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently the rebel Zhu Ci induced the armies of Jing and Long to defect; Huai'guang corrupted the Shuofang army—after partition and purges, little remained.

manualTranslations.zh: 而又分朔方之地，建牙擁節者，凡三使焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Shuofang's territory was divided—those who established headquarters and bore commander's staffs numbered three in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover Shuofang's territory was divided—those who established headquarters and bore commander's staffs numbered three in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 其余鎮軍，數且四十，皆承特詔委寄，各降中貴監臨，人得抗衡，莫相稟屬。
manualTranslations.literal: The remaining garrison armies number nearly forty—all commissioned by special edict, each supervised by a palace eunuch envoy; men are equals to one another, none subordinate to another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The remaining garrison armies number nearly forty—all commissioned by special edict, each supervised by a palace eunuch envoy; men are equals to one another, none subordinate to another.

manualTranslations.zh: 每俟邊書告急，方令計會用兵，既無軍法下臨，唯以客禮相待。
manualTranslations.literal: Only when frontier dispatches report emergency are orders given to coordinate troops—and with no military law descending from above, they are treated only with the courtesy due guests.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only when frontier dispatches report emergency are orders given to coordinate troops—and with no military law descending from above, they are treated only with the courtesy due guests.

manualTranslations.zh: 是乃從容拯溺，揖讓救焚，冀無阽危，固亦難矣！
manualTranslations.literal: This is to save the drowning at leisure and fight the fire with bows and courtesies—to hope for no peril on the brink, how difficult that surely is!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is to save the drowning at leisure and fight the fire with bows and courtesies—to hope for no peril on the brink, how difficult that surely is!

manualTranslations.zh: 夫兵，以氣勢為用者也，氣聚則盛，散則消；
manualTranslations.literal: Warfare relies on martial spirit—when spirit gathers it flourishes, when it scatters it dissipates;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Warfare relies on martial spirit—when spirit gathers it flourishes, when it scatters it dissipates;

manualTranslations.zh: 勢合則威，析則弱。
manualTranslations.literal: When force combines it is formidable, when divided it is weak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When force combines it is formidable, when divided it is weak.

manualTranslations.zh: 今之邊備，勢弱氣消，建軍若斯，可謂力分於將多矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Today's border defenses—weak in force, dissipated in spirit—to establish armies thus may be called strength divided among too many generals!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today's border defenses are weak in force and dissipated in spirit—to establish armies thus is what I call strength divided among too many generals!

manualTranslations.zh: 理戎之要，最在均齊，故軍法無貴賤之差，軍實無多少之異，是將所以同其誌而盡其力也。
manualTranslations.literal: The crux of managing the frontier lies above all in equality and balance—thus military law makes no distinction of high and low rank, military provisions no difference of more and less—this is how generals unite men's resolve and exhaust their strength.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The crux of managing the frontier lies above all in equality and balance—thus military law makes no distinction of high and low rank, military provisions no difference of more and less. This is how generals unite men's resolve and exhaust their strength.

manualTranslations.zh: 如或誘其誌意，勉其藝能，則當閱其材，程其勇，校其勞逸，度其安危，明申練覆優劣之科，以為衣食等級之制。
manualTranslations.literal: If one would draw out their resolve and encourage their skills, one should assess their talent, measure their courage, compare their toil and rest, gauge their peril and safety—clearly establishing categories for training review and merit, to serve as the system of graded food and clothing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one would draw out their resolve and encourage their skills, one should assess their talent, measure their courage, compare their toil and rest, gauge their peril and safety—clearly establishing categories for training review and merit, to serve as the system of graded food and clothing.

manualTranslations.zh: 使能者企及，否者息心，雖有薄厚之殊，而無觖望之釁。
manualTranslations.literal: Let the capable strive to catch up, the incapable lay aside ambition—though there be differences of more and less, there will be no cause for discontent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let the capable strive to catch up, the incapable lay aside ambition—though there be differences of more and less, there will be no cause for discontent.

manualTranslations.zh: 蓋所謂日省月試，餼稟均事，如權量之無情於物，萬人莫不安其分而服其平也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is what is meant by daily review and monthly testing, rations distributed with equal fairness—like the balance scale indifferent to objects; ten thousand men none failing to rest content in their station and submit to its fairness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by daily review and monthly testing, rations distributed with equal fairness—like the balance scale indifferent to objects; ten thousand men none failing to rest content in their station and submit to its fairness.

manualTranslations.zh: 今者窮邊之地，長鎮之兵，皆百戰傷夷之余，終年勤苦之劇，角其所能則練習，度其所處則孤危，考其服役則勞，察其臨敵則勇。
manualTranslations.literal: Now on the remote frontier, the long-garrisoned troops—all are survivors of a hundred battles and wounds, enduring year-round the severest toil; matched against their abilities they are practiced, measured against their situation they stand alone and in peril, examined for their service they are worn with labor, observed facing the enemy they are brave.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now on the remote frontier, the long-garrisoned troops are all survivors of a hundred battles and wounds, enduring year-round the severest toil. Matched against their abilities they are practiced; measured against their situation they stand alone and in peril; examined for their service they are worn with labor; observed facing the enemy they are brave.

manualTranslations.zh: 然衣糧所給，唯止當身，例為妻子所分，常有凍餒之色。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet the clothing and grain provided reach only their own bodies, and as a rule are divided among wives and children—they constantly wear the look of cold and hunger.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet the clothing and grain provided reach only their own bodies, and as a rule are divided among wives and children—they constantly wear the look of cold and hunger.

manualTranslations.zh: 而關東戍卒，歲月踐更，不安危城，不習戎備，怯於應敵，懈於服勞。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet garrison soldiers from east of the pass, rotating through by month and year, untested in perilous fortresses, unpracticed in military readiness, timid in facing the enemy, slack in bearing labor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet garrison soldiers from east of the pass, rotating through by month and year, are untested in perilous fortresses, unpracticed in military readiness, timid in facing the enemy, and slack in bearing labor.

manualTranslations.zh: 然衣糧所頒，厚逾數等，繼以茶藥之饋，益以蔬醬之資。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet the clothing and grain they receive is generous by several grades, followed by gifts of tea and medicine, supplemented with vegetables and sauces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet the clothing and grain they receive is generous by several grades, followed by gifts of tea and medicine, supplemented with vegetables and sauces.

manualTranslations.zh: 豐約相形，懸絕斯甚。
manualTranslations.literal: Abundance and want set side by side—the gap is vast.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Abundance and want set side by side—the gap is vast.

manualTranslations.zh: 又有素非禁旅，本是邊軍，將校詭為媚詞，因請遙隸神策，不離舊所，唯改虛名，其於稟賜之饒，遂有三倍之益。
manualTranslations.literal: There are also men who were never of the imperial guard but were originally frontier troops—officers craftily using flattery petition to be nominally attached to the Shence Army from afar, never leaving their old posts, changing only an empty title—yet their rations and gifts become three times richer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There are also men who were never of the imperial guard but were originally frontier troops—officers craftily using flattery petition to be nominally attached to the Shence Army from afar, never leaving their old posts, changing only an empty title—yet their rations and gifts become three times richer.

manualTranslations.zh: 此儔類所以忿恨，忠良所以憂嗟，疲人所以流亡，經費所以褊匱。
manualTranslations.literal: This is why such comrades boil with resentment, loyal men sigh with worry, the worn-out flee into exile, and military funds run thin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is why such comrades boil with resentment, loyal men sigh with worry, the worn-out flee into exile, and military funds run thin.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫事業未異，而給養有殊，人情之所不能甘也，況乎矯佞行而稟賜厚，績藝劣而衣食優，茍未忘懷，能無慍怒！
manualTranslations.literal: When the service is no different yet sustenance is unequal—this human nature cannot accept; how much less when sycophancy wins rich rations while poor merit receives fine food and clothing—if one has not forgotten self, how could there be no anger!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the service is no different yet sustenance is unequal—this human nature cannot accept. How much less when sycophancy wins rich rations while poor merit receives fine food and clothing—if one has not forgotten self, how could there be no anger!

manualTranslations.zh: 不為戎首，則已可嘉，而欲使其協力同心，以攘寇難，雖有韓、白、孫、吳之將，臣知其必不能焉。
manualTranslations.literal: For them not to lead the barbarians' charge would already be praiseworthy—and to expect them to unite in heart and strength to repel the enemy, even with generals like Han Xin, Bai Qi, Sun Wu, and Wu Qi, I know it cannot be done.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For them not to lead the barbarians' charge would already be praiseworthy—and to expect them to unite in heart and strength to repel the enemy, even with generals like Han Xin, Bai Qi, Sun Wu, and Wu Qi, I know it cannot be done.

manualTranslations.zh: 養士若斯，可謂怨生於不均矣！
manualTranslations.literal: To sustain troops thus may be called resentment born of inequality!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To sustain troops thus is what I call resentment born of inequality!

manualTranslations.zh: 凡欲選任將帥，必先考察行能，然後指以所授之方，語以所委之事，令其自揣可否，自陳規模。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever one wishes to select and appoint generals, one must first examine conduct and ability, then point out the region to be entrusted and explain the duties assigned, letting them judge for themselves whether they can do it and state their own plans.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever one wishes to select and appoint generals, one must first examine conduct and ability, then point out the region to be entrusted and explain the duties assigned, letting them judge for themselves whether they can do it and state their own plans.

manualTranslations.zh: 須某色甲兵，藉某人參佐，要若干士馬，用若干資糧，某處置軍，某時成績，始終要領，悉俾經綸，於是觀其計謀，校其聲實。
manualTranslations.literal: One must specify what kind of armor and troops are needed, whom to rely on as aides, how many soldiers and horses are required, how much provisions and grain to use, where to deploy the army, when results are expected—the essentials from start to finish all entrusted to their planning—then observe their stratagems and weigh name against reality.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Specify the armor and troops required, the aides to be relied upon, the number of soldiers and horses needed, the provisions and grain to be supplied, where to deploy the army, and when results are expected. Entrust the essentials from start to finish to their planning, then observe their stratagems and weigh name against reality.

manualTranslations.zh: 若謂材無足取，言不可行，則當退之於初，不宜貽慮於其後也。
manualTranslations.literal: If one holds that his talent is not worth taking and his words cannot be carried out, then he should be dismissed at the outset—not left with concerns afterward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If his talent is deemed unworthy and his proposals unworkable, dismiss him at the outset; do not let doubts linger afterward.

manualTranslations.zh: 若謂志氣足任，方略可施，則當要之於終，不宜掣肘於其間也。
manualTranslations.literal: If one holds that his resolve is sufficient for the task and his strategy can be applied, then he should be held to the end—not hamstrung in the middle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If his resolve is judged sufficient and his strategy workable, hold him to the end; do not hamstring him midway.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫如是，則疑者不使，使者不疑；
manualTranslations.literal: If so, the doubtful are not employed, and those employed are not doubted;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the doubtful are not employed, and those employed are not doubted;

manualTranslations.zh: 勞神於選才，端拱於委任。
manualTranslations.literal: One strains the mind in selecting talent and sits upright in dignified repose to delegate authority.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Exert effort only in selecting talent, then sit back in dignified repose to delegate authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 既委其事，既足其求，然後可以核其否臧，行其賞罰。
manualTranslations.literal: Once the task is entrusted and their requests are fully met, then one may examine success or failure and apply rewards and punishments.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once the task is entrusted and their requests fully met, then one may judge success or failure and apply rewards and punishments.

manualTranslations.zh: 受賞者不以為濫，當罰者無得而辭，付授之柄既專，茍且之心自息。
manualTranslations.literal: Those rewarded will not call it excessive; those who deserve punishment have no excuse—the delegated authority being complete, the spirit of temporizing naturally subsides.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rewarded will not deem it excessive; the deserving of punishment will have no recourse. With authority fully delegated, the impulse to cut corners naturally dies away.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以古之遣將帥者，君親推轂而命之曰：「自閫以外，將軍裁之。」
manualTranslations.literal: Hence when ancient rulers dispatched generals, the ruler in person pushed the chariot wheel and commanded: "Beyond the frontier gate, the general decides."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hence when ancient rulers dispatched generals, the ruler in person would push the chariot wheel and say: "Beyond the frontier gate, the general decides.

manualTranslations.zh: 又賜鈇鉞，示令專斷。
manualTranslations.literal: He also bestowed the axe and halberd, signaling authority for independent judgment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also bestowed the axe and halberd, signaling authority for independent judgment.

manualTranslations.zh: 故軍容不入國，國容不入軍，將在軍，君命有所不受。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus military etiquette does not enter the state, and state etiquette does not enter the army; when the general is in the army, the ruler's orders may sometimes go unheeded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus military protocol does not enter the court, nor court protocol the army. When the general is in the field, he may sometimes refuse the ruler's orders.

manualTranslations.zh: 誠謂機宜不可以遠決，號令不可以兩從，未有委任不專，而望其克敵成功者也。
manualTranslations.literal: Truly, opportune action cannot be decided from afar, commands cannot have two masters; never has there been one whose delegation was not complete yet who was expected to defeat the enemy and succeed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Truly, opportune action cannot be decided from afar, nor commands obey two masters. No one whose authority was divided has ever been expected to defeat the enemy and succeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 自頃邊軍去就，裁斷多出宸衷，選置戎臣，先求易制，多其部以分其力，輕其任以弱其心，雖有所懲，亦有所失。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently the border armies' movements and deployments have mostly been decided from the imperial heart; in selecting military officials, easy control is sought first—giving them many subordinates to divide their strength, lightening their duties to weaken their resolve—though some gain is had, some is also lost.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently the border armies' movements have mostly been decided from the throne itself. In appointing military officials, easy control comes first: many subordinates to divide their strength, lighter duties to weaken their resolve. Though some good may come of this, much is also lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂令分閫責成之義廢，死綏任咎之誌衰，一則聽命，二亦聽命，爽於軍情亦聽命，乖於事宜亦聽命。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the principle of entrusting a sector with responsibility is abandoned, the resolve to die at one's post and bear blame fades—first one listens to orders, second also listens to orders; at odds with military conditions also listens to orders, contrary to what the situation requires also listens to orders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the principle of entrusting a sector with full responsibility is abandoned, and the resolve to die at one's post and bear blame fades. First one takes orders, then another takes orders; at odds with military conditions—take orders; contrary to the situation—take orders.

manualTranslations.zh: 若所置將帥，必取於承順無違，則如斯可矣；
manualTranslations.literal: If the generals appointed must be drawn from those who comply without dissent, then such a course would do;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the generals appointed must be those who comply without dissent, then such a course might suffice;

manualTranslations.zh: 若有意平兇靖難，則不可。
manualTranslations.literal: If one intends to pacify the violent and settle turmoil, it cannot be done.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But if one intends to pacify the violent and settle turmoil, it cannot be done.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫兩境相接，兩軍相持，事機之來，間不容息，蓄謀而俟，猶恐失之，臨時始謀，固已疏矣。
manualTranslations.literal: When two borders meet and two armies face each other, opportunity arrives allowing no pause for breath—even storing plans and waiting, one still fears missing it; to plan only when the moment comes is already too lax.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When two borders meet and two armies face each other, opportunity brooks no pause—even plans prepared in advance may still be missed; to plan only when crisis strikes is already far too late.

manualTranslations.zh: 況乎千里之遠，九重之深，陳述之難明，聽覽之不一，欲其事無遺策，雖聖者亦有所不能焉。
manualTranslations.literal: How much more when a thousand li lie between, and the ninefold palace is deep—the difficulty of making matters clear in reports, the inconsistency of imperial attention—to wish that nothing be overlooked, even a sage has what he cannot do.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How much worse when a thousand li lie between and the palace depths are impenetrable—reports hard to make clear, imperial attention inconsistent. To expect that nothing be overlooked is beyond even a sage.

manualTranslations.zh: 設使謀慮能周，其如權變無及！
manualTranslations.literal: Even if deliberation could be thorough, what of timely adaptation when there is no time!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even if deliberation could be thorough, what of timely adaptation when there is no time!

manualTranslations.zh: 戎虜馳突，迅如風飈，驛書上聞，旬月方報。
manualTranslations.literal: The barbarian foe charges swiftly, quick as a wind-gust; memorials by post reach the throne, and a reply comes only after ten days or a month.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The barbarian foe charges as swiftly as a wind-gust. Memorials by post reach the throne, and a reply may come only after ten days or a month.

manualTranslations.zh: 守土者以兵寡不敢抗敵，分鎮者以無詔不肯出師，逗留之間，寇已奔逼，托於救援未至，各且閉壘自全。
manualTranslations.literal: Territory defenders, finding their troops few, dare not resist the enemy; sector commanders, lacking an edict, refuse to march out; in the delay the bandits are already upon them—pleading that relief has not arrived, each closes his fortress to save himself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Local defenders, finding their troops too few, dare not resist. Sector commanders, lacking an edict, refuse to march out. While they delay, the raiders are already upon them. Pleading that relief has not arrived, each closes his fort and saves himself.

manualTranslations.zh: 牧馬屯牛，鞠為椎剽；
manualTranslations.literal: Pastured horses and penned cattle become fodder for raids;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Horses in pasture and cattle in pens become the spoil of raids;

manualTranslations.zh: 穡夫樵婦，罄作俘囚。
manualTranslations.literal: Farmers and wood-gathering women, all become captives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Farmers and wood-gathering women are taken wholesale as captives.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖詔諸鎮發兵，唯以虛聲應援，互相瞻顧，莫敢遮邀，賊既縱掠退歸，此乃陳功告捷。
manualTranslations.literal: Although edicts order the various sectors to send troops, they respond with only an empty sound of support, eyeing one another, none daring to intercept and engage; once the bandits have finished plundering and withdrawn, only then do they report merit and proclaim victory.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though edicts order the various sectors to mobilize, they respond with only a hollow show of support, watching one another, none daring to intercept the enemy. Once the raiders have finished plundering and withdrawn, they report merit and proclaim victory.

manualTranslations.zh: 其敗喪則減百而為一，其捃獲則張百而成千。
manualTranslations.literal: Their defeats and losses are reduced from a hundred to one; their gathered booty is inflated from a hundred to a thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Defeats and losses are reported at one-hundredth of their true scale; booty seized is inflated from hundreds into thousands.

manualTranslations.zh: 將帥既幸於總制在朝，不憂於罪累；
manualTranslations.literal: The generals, fortunate that overall control rests at court, need not worry about guilt and punishment;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The generals, fortunate that overall control rests at court, need not fear blame;

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下又以為大權由己，不究事情。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty also, believing that supreme authority rests with yourself, does not investigate the actual facts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, believing supreme authority rests with yourself, does not investigate the actual facts.

manualTranslations.zh: 用師若斯，可謂機失於遙制矣！
manualTranslations.literal: To use troops thus may be called losing opportunity through remote control!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To use troops thus is what I call losing opportunity through remote control!

manualTranslations.zh: 理兵而措置乖方，馭將而賞罰虧度，制用而財匱，建兵而力分，養士而怨生，用師而機失，此六者，疆場之蟊賊，軍旅之膏肓也。
manualTranslations.literal: Deploying troops with misplaced arrangements, governing generals with deficient rewards and punishments, controlling expenditures until funds run short, raising armies while strength is divided, sustaining soldiers until resentment arises, using troops while opportunity is lost—these six are the crop pests of the frontier and the deep ailment of the army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Deploying troops with misplaced arrangements, governing generals with deficient rewards and punishments, controlling expenditures until funds run short, raising armies while strength is divided, sustaining soldiers until resentment arises, using troops while opportunity is lost—these six are the crop pests of the frontier and the deep-rooted ailment of the army.

manualTranslations.zh: 蟊賊不除，而但滋之以糞溉，膏肓不療，而唯啖之以滑甘，適足以養其害，速其災，欲求稼穡豐登，膚革充美，固不可得也。
manualTranslations.literal: If crop pests are not removed but only nourished with manure and water, if the deep ailment is not treated but only fed sweet and slick things, this merely nurtures the harm and hastens disaster—to hope for rich harvests and full, healthy flesh is surely unattainable.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If crop pests are not removed but only fed with fertilizer, if the deep ailment is not treated but only pampered with sweet delicacies, this merely nurtures the harm and hastens disaster. To hope for rich harvests and a strong, healthy people is surely impossible.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣愚謂宜罷諸道將士番替防秋之制，率因舊數而三分之：其一分委本道節度使募少壯願住邊城者以徙焉；
manualTranslations.literal: Your humble servant holds that the system of rotating troops from all circuits for autumn border defense should be abolished, and the old quotas divided roughly into three parts: one part left to the circuit military commissioner to recruit young, strong men willing to dwell in border towns for resettlement there;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I hold that the system of rotating troops from all circuits for autumn border defense should be abolished, and the existing quotas divided into three. One part should be entrusted to each circuit's military commissioner to recruit able-bodied young men willing to settle in border towns.

manualTranslations.zh: 其一分則本道但供衣糧，委關內、河東諸軍州募蕃、漢子弟願傅邊軍者以給焉；
manualTranslations.literal: One part with the circuit supplying only clothing and grain, entrusting the districts and armies within the passes and in Hedong to recruit tribal and Han youth willing to serve with the border army;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For another part, the circuit would supply only clothing and grain, while districts and armies within the passes and in Hedong would recruit tribal and Han youth willing to join the border forces.

manualTranslations.zh: 又一分亦令本道但出衣糧，加給應募之人，以資新徙之業。
manualTranslations.literal: Another part likewise having the circuit provide only clothing and grain, with additional pay to those who enlist, to support the livelihood of the newly resettled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For a third part, the circuit would again supply only clothing and grain, with extra pay to recruits to support the livelihood of the newly resettled.

manualTranslations.zh: 又令度支散於諸道和市耕牛，兼雇召工人，就諸軍城繕造器具。
manualTranslations.literal: Further, order the Office of Revenue to disperse through the circuits to purchase plow oxen, and also hire workers to repair and make implements at the various military posts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Further, the Office of Revenue should purchase plow oxen throughout the circuits and hire workers to make and repair implements at the various military posts.

manualTranslations.zh: 募人至者，每家給耕牛一頭，又給田農水火之器，皆令充備。
manualTranslations.literal: When recruits arrive, each household should be given one plow ox, and also farming tools for field, fire, and water—all made fully sufficient.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When recruits arrive, each household should receive one plow ox and a full set of farming implements for field work and household use.

manualTranslations.zh: 初到之歲，與家口二人糧，並賜種子，勸之播植，待經一稔，俾自給家。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of arrival, provide grain for two family members, and also grant seed, encouraging them to sow and plant; after one harvest, let them support their own households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In their first year, provide grain for two family members and grant seed, encouraging them to plant. After one harvest, they should be able to support their own households.

manualTranslations.zh: 若有余糧，官為收糴，各酬倍價，務獎營田。
manualTranslations.literal: If there is surplus grain, the government should purchase it, paying double the price, vigorously encouraging border farming.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If there is surplus grain, the government should buy it at double the market price, vigorously encouraging border farming.

manualTranslations.zh: 既息踐更征發之煩，且無幸災茍免之弊。
manualTranslations.literal: This both ends the troubles of rotating service and levy, and removes the abuse of hoping for disaster to escape duty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This would end the troubles of rotating service and conscription, and remove the abuse of hoping for disaster as a way to escape duty.

manualTranslations.zh: 寇至則人自為戰，時至則家自力農。
manualTranslations.literal: When bandits come, each man fights on his own; when the season comes, each household farms on its own.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When raiders come, each man will fight on his own; when the season comes, each household will farm on its own.

manualTranslations.zh: 是乃兵不得不強，食不得不足，與夫倏來忽往，豈可同等而論哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Thus troops cannot but be strong, food cannot but be sufficient—compared with those who come suddenly and go suddenly, how can they be spoken of on equal terms!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the army must grow strong and provisions must suffice—how can this be compared with troops who come suddenly and depart just as quickly!

manualTranslations.zh: 臣又謂宜擇文武能臣一人為隴右元帥，應涇、隴、鳳翔、長武城、山南西道等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉；
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant further holds that one capable civil and military official should be chosen as Commander of the Right of Longyou, and all troops within the jurisdictions of the Jing, Long, Fengxiang, Changwucheng, and Shannan West circuit commands should be placed under him;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I further hold that one capable civil and military official should be chosen as Commander of the Right of Longyou, placing all troops under the Jing, Long, Fengxiang, Changwucheng, and Shannan West circuit commands under his authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 又擇一人為朔方元帥，應鄜坊、邠寧、靈夏等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉；
manualTranslations.literal: Choose another as Commander of Shuofang, and all troops within the Fufang, Binning, Lingxia, and related circuit commands should be placed under him;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Choose another as Commander of Shuofang, placing all troops under the Fufang, Binning, Lingxia, and related commands under his authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 又擇一人為河東元帥，河東、振武等節度管內兵馬，悉以屬焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Choose another as Commander of Hedong, and all troops within the Hedong and Zhenwu circuit commands should be placed under him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Choose another as Commander of Hedong, placing all troops under the Hedong and Zhenwu commands under his authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 三帥各選臨邊要會之州以為理所，見置節度，有非要者，隨所便近而並之。
manualTranslations.literal: Each of the three commanders should choose a strategic border prefecture as his headquarters; among existing military commissions, those not essential should be merged according to convenience and proximity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Each of the three commanders should establish headquarters at a strategic border prefecture. Among existing military commissions, nonessential ones should be merged according to convenience and proximity.

manualTranslations.zh: 唯元帥得置統軍，余並停罷。
manualTranslations.literal: Only the commanders-in-chief may appoint army overseers; all others should be abolished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only the commanders-in-chief may appoint army overseers; all other such posts should be abolished.

manualTranslations.zh: 其三帥部內太原、鳳翔等府及諸郡戶口稍多者，慎揀良吏以為尹守，外奉師律，內課農桑，俾為軍糧，以壯戎府。
manualTranslations.literal: Within the three commanders' territories, for Taiyuan, Fengxiang, and other prefectures and commanderies with relatively large populations, carefully select good officials as governors and prefects—outwardly observing military discipline, inwardly encouraging agriculture and sericulture, making them sources of army grain to strengthen the military posts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within the three commanders' territories, for Taiyuan, Fengxiang, and other prefectures with relatively large populations, carefully select good officials as governors. Outwardly they should observe military discipline; inwardly they should encourage agriculture and sericulture, supplying army grain to strengthen the military posts.

manualTranslations.zh: 理兵之宜既得，選帥之授既明，然後減奸濫虛浮之費以豐財，定衣糧等級之制以和眾，弘委任之道以宣其用，懸賞罰之典以考其成。
manualTranslations.literal: Once the right way to deploy troops is settled and the appointment of commanders is clear, then reduce corrupt, excessive, and empty expenditures to enrich the treasury, fix grades for clothing and grain to harmonize the ranks, broaden the way of delegation to display their usefulness, and publish standards of reward and punishment to assess their achievements.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once troop deployment is rightly ordered and commanders clearly appointed, reduce corrupt and wasteful expenditures to enrich the treasury, fix grades for clothing and grain to harmonize the ranks, broaden delegation to put talent to use, and publish standards of reward and punishment to assess achievement.

manualTranslations.zh: 而又慎守中國之所長，謹行當今之所易，則八利可致，六失可除。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, carefully hold to what China excels at, and diligently practice what is easy in the present day—then the eight benefits can be attained and the six failures removed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, carefully hold to China's strengths and diligently practice what is feasible today, and the eight benefits can be attained and the six failures removed.

manualTranslations.zh: 如是而戎狄不威懷，疆場不寧謐者，未之有也。
manualTranslations.literal: If this is done yet the barbarians are neither awed nor won over, and the frontier is not settled and quiet—never has such a thing been.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If this is done and yet the barbarians are neither awed nor reconciled, and the frontier is not settled—there has never been such a case.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸侯軌道，庶類服從。
manualTranslations.literal: The feudal lords would follow the correct path, and the common folk would submit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The regional lords would follow the correct path, and the people would submit.

manualTranslations.zh: 如是而教令不行，天下不理者，亦未之有也。
manualTranslations.literal: If this is done yet edicts and orders do not prevail and the realm is not well governed—never has such a thing been either.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If this is done and yet edicts do not prevail and the realm is not well governed—that too has never happened.

manualTranslations.zh: 以陛下之英鑒，民心之思安，四方之小休，兩寇之方靜，加以頻年豐稔，所在積糧，此皆天贊國家，可以立制垂統之時也。
manualTranslations.literal: With Your Majesty's keen insight, the people's wish for peace, a brief rest in the four quarters, the two enemy peoples just settling down, plus years of abundant harvests and grain stored everywhere—all this is Heaven aiding the state; it is a time to establish institutions and leave a lasting legacy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's keen insight, the people's longing for peace, a brief respite in the four quarters, the two enemy peoples just quieting down, and years of abundant harvest with grain stored everywhere—all this is Heaven aiding the state. It is a time to establish institutions and leave a lasting legacy.

manualTranslations.zh: 時不久居，事不常兼，已過而追，雖悔無及。
manualTranslations.literal: Time does not long remain, affairs do not usually coincide; once passed and pursued, though one regrets, it is too late.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Time does not long remain, and favorable conditions do not often coincide. Once the moment has passed, regret comes too late.

manualTranslations.zh: 明主者，不以言為罪，不以人廢言，罄陳狂愚，惟所省擇。
manualTranslations.literal: A wise ruler does not punish for words spoken, does not discard words because of the speaker—I lay out my foolishness fully and leave all to Your careful choice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A wise ruler does not punish for words spoken or discard counsel because of the speaker. I lay out my foolishness fully and leave all to Your careful judgment.

sourceRange.text: 贄不時奉詔，進狀論之曰：頃以理道乖錯，禍亂薦鐘，陛下思咎懼災，裕人罪己，屢降大號，誓將更新。天下之人，垂涕相賀，懲忿釋怨，煦仁戴明，畢力同心，共平多難。止土崩於絕岸，收版蕩於橫流，殄寇清都，不失舊物。實由陛下至誠動於天地，深悔感於神人，故得百靈降康，兆庶歸德。茍不如此，自古何嘗有捐棄宮闕，失守宗祧，繼逆於赴難之師，再遷於蒙塵之日，不逾半歲，而復興大業者乎！今渠魁始平，法駕將返，近自郊甸，遠周寰瀛，百役疲瘵之氓，重戰傷殘之卒，皆忍死扶病，傾耳聳肩，想聞德聲，翹望聖澤。陛下固當感上天悔禍之眷，荷列祖垂裕之休，念將士鋒刃之殃，湣黎元塗炭之酷。以致寇為戒，以居上為危，以務理為憂，以復宮為急。損之又損，尚懼汰侈之易滋；艱之惟艱，猶患戒慎之難久。謀始盡善，克終已稀；始而不謀，終則何有！夫以內人為號，蓋是中壺末流。天子之尊，富有宮掖，如此等輩，固繁有徒，但恐傷多，豈憂乏使！翦除元惡，曾未浹辰，奔賀往來，道途如織。何必自虧君德，首訪婦人，又令資裝速赴行在！萬目閱視，眾口流傳，恐非所以答慶賴之心，副惟新之望也。夫事有先後，義有重輕，重者宜先，輕者宜後。武王克殷，有未及下車而為之者，有下車而為之者，蓋美其不失先後之宜也。自翠華播越，萬姓靡依，清廟震驚，三時乏祀，當今所務，莫大於斯。誠宜速遣大臣，馳傳先往，迎復神主，修整郊壇，展禋享之儀，申告謝之意。然後吊恤死義，慰犒有功，綏輯黎蒸，優問耆耋。安定反側，寬宥脅從；宣暢郁堙，褒獎忠直；官失職之士，復廢業之人。是皆宜先，不可後也。至如崇飾服器，繕緝殿臺，備耳目之娛，選巾櫛之侍，是皆宜後，不可先也。散失內人，已經累月，既當離亂之際，必為將士所私。其人若稍有知，不求當自陳獻；其人若甚無識，求之適使憂虞。自因寇亂喪亡，頗有大於此者，一聞搜索，懷懼必多；余孽尚繁，群情未一，因而善撫，猶恐危疑，若又懼之，於何不有！昔人所以掩絕纓而飲盜馬者，豈必忘其情愛，蓋知為君之體然也。以小妨大，明者不為。天下固多褻人，何必獨在於此。所令撰賜渾瑊詔書，未敢順旨。

localRange.text: 贄不時奉詔，進狀論之曰：

manualTranslations.zh: 贄不時奉詔，進狀論之曰：頃以理道乖錯，禍亂薦鐘，陛下思咎懼災，裕人罪己，屢降大號，誓將更新。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi did not promptly obey the edict, submitted a memorial discussing it, saying:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi did not draft the edict immediately. Instead he submitted a memorial arguing:

manualTranslations.zh: 天下之人，垂涕相賀，懲忿釋怨，煦仁戴明，畢力同心，共平多難。
manualTranslations.literal: People under Heaven, tears hanging, congratulated one another; chastened anger released resentment, warmed by benevolence bearing brilliance, exhausted strength united in heart, together pacifying many difficulties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people wept with joy, set aside old grievances, and united in gratitude to restore peace together.

manualTranslations.zh: 止土崩於絕岸，收版蕩於橫流，殄寇清都，不失舊物。
manualTranslations.literal: Stopped earth collapse at sheer cliff, gathered floating boards in crosscurrent, exterminated bandits and cleared the capital, not losing old possessions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You halted collapse at the brink, gathered the fragments from the flood, destroyed the rebels, and recovered the capital without losing the dynasty's heritage.

manualTranslations.zh: 實由陛下至誠動於天地，深悔感於神人，故得百靈降康，兆庶歸德。
manualTranslations.literal: Truly because Your Majesty's utmost sincerity moved Heaven and Earth, deep repentance touched spirits and men, therefore obtained the hundred spirits descending with peace, the myriad masses returning to virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This was because Your Majesty's sincerity moved Heaven and Earth and your repentance touched gods and men, so that all spirits brought peace and the people returned to allegiance.

manualTranslations.zh: 茍不如此，自古何嘗有捐棄宮闕，失守宗祧，繼逆於赴難之師，再遷於蒙塵之日，不逾半歲，而復興大業者乎！
manualTranslations.literal: If not so, from antiquity when has there been abandoning palace halls, losing ancestral temple, rebel armies succeeding relief armies, twice moving on days of dust-covered robes—not exceeding half a year yet reviving the great enterprise!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without this, when in all history has an emperor who abandoned his palace, lost his ancestral shrine, faced successive rebellions while rallying relief armies, and fled twice in disgrace restored the empire in less than half a year?

manualTranslations.zh: 今渠魁始平，法駕將返，近自郊甸，遠周寰瀛，百役疲瘵之氓，重戰傷殘之卒，皆忍死扶病，傾耳聳肩，想聞德聲，翹望聖澤。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the ringleader just pacified, the imperial carriage about to return, near from suburban fields, far circling all within the seas—the hundred corvée-weary sick commoners, repeatedly battle-wounded maimed soldiers, all enduring death and supporting illness, inclining ears and raising shoulders, thinking to hear virtue's voice, craning to hope for sage grace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now that the rebel leader has just been crushed and the imperial carriage is about to return, from the capital outskirts to the farthest corners of the realm, exhausted laborers and battle-wounded soldiers alike endure their pain, straining to hear your benevolent words and hoping for your grace.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下固當感上天悔禍之眷，荷列祖垂裕之休，念將士鋒刃之殃，湣黎元塗炭之酷。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty should indeed feel Heaven's repentant calamity-favoring regard, bear the former emperors' overflowing surplus of blessing, recall the soldiers' blade calamity, pity the common people's charcoal-smeared cruelty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should respond to Heaven's mercy in turning aside disaster, honor the blessing left by your ancestors, remember the wounds of your soldiers, and pity the suffering of the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 以致寇為戒，以居上為危，以務理為憂，以復宮為急。
manualTranslations.literal: Take inviting bandits as warning, occupying the heights as peril, striving for order as worry, restoring the palace as urgency.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Take the rebels as a warning, regard your position as perilous, make good governance your concern, and return to the palace your urgent task.

manualTranslations.zh: 損之又損，尚懼汰侈之易滋；
manualTranslations.literal: Reduce again and again, still fearing extravagant excess easily spreading.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You must keep stripping away excess, for luxury spreads easily.

manualTranslations.zh: 艱之惟艱，猶患戒慎之難久。
manualTranslations.literal: Hard it is and only hard, still worrying vigilance and caution hard to last long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The road ahead is hard, and vigilance is hard to sustain.

manualTranslations.zh: 謀始盡善，克終已稀；
manualTranslations.literal: Planning the start with utmost goodness, completing the end is already rare.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Many begin well.

manualTranslations.zh: 始而不謀，終則何有！
manualTranslations.literal: Start without planning, end then what is there!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Few finish well. If you do not plan from the beginning, what can you hope for at the end?

manualTranslations.zh: 夫以內人為號，蓋是中壺末流。
manualTranslations.literal: As for using palace women as the call, this is the inner quarters' lowest stream.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To make palace women the priority belongs to the least worthy concerns of the inner court.

manualTranslations.zh: 天子之尊，富有宮掖，如此等輩，固繁有徒，但恐傷多，豈憂乏使！
manualTranslations.literal: The Son of Heaven's eminence richly possesses palace inner quarters; such as these indeed abound in multitudes—only fear hurting too many, how worry lacking servants!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has a full palace. Such women are hardly scarce. You should fear causing too much harm, not worry about finding attendants!

manualTranslations.zh: 翦除元惡，曾未浹辰，奔賀往來，道途如織。
manualTranslations.literal: Cutting away the origin villain, not yet ten days wet; rushing congratulations coming and going, roads like weaving.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The chief villain has been eliminated only days ago. Messengers of congratulation fill the roads like threads on a loom.

manualTranslations.zh: 何必自虧君德，首訪婦人，又令資裝速赴行在！
manualTranslations.literal: Why must you yourself diminish lordly virtue, first visiting women, again ordering supplies and dress swiftly sent to the traveling court!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why diminish your stature as ruler by seeking out women first and ordering them rushed to your camp with provisions?

manualTranslations.zh: 萬目閱視，眾口流傳，恐非所以答慶賴之心，副惟新之望也。
manualTranslations.literal: Ten thousand eyes watch and see, crowd mouths spread word—I fear this is not the means to answer celebratory reliance's hearts or fulfill renewal's hope.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ten thousand eyes are watching and ten thousand tongues are speaking. This will not meet the people's joy and hope for renewal.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫事有先後，義有重輕，重者宜先，輕者宜後。
manualTranslations.literal: Affairs have before and after, principle has heavy and light—heavy should be first, light should be after.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Affairs have their order of priority. Weighty matters come first; lesser ones afterward.

manualTranslations.zh: 武王克殷，有未及下車而為之者，有下車而為之者，蓋美其不失先後之宜也。
manualTranslations.literal: King Wu conquered Yin; some things not yet reached dismounting the chariot he did, some after dismounting—praising that he did not lose the fitting order of before and after.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When King Wu conquered the Shang, some things he did before he even left his chariot and others only after he dismounted—because he never lost the proper sense of priority.

manualTranslations.zh: 自翠華播越，萬姓靡依，清廟震驚，三時乏祀，當今所務，莫大於斯。
manualTranslations.literal: Since the azure carriage scattered and crossed, myriad people had none to rely on; the clear temple was shaken and alarmed, three seasons lacked sacrifice—today's affairs, nothing greater than this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since the imperial progress fled into exile, the people have been without refuge, the ancestral temple has been desecrated, and sacrifices have ceased for seasons. Nothing is more urgent than this.

manualTranslations.zh: 誠宜速遣大臣，馳傳先往，迎復神主，修整郊壇，展禋享之儀，申告謝之意。
manualTranslations.literal: Truly fitting to swiftly dispatch great ministers, post-horses speeding ahead, welcome and restore the spirit tablets, repair suburban altars, unfold sacrifice and offering rites, declare gratitude and apology's intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You should promptly send high ministers posthaste to recover the spirit tablets of the ancestors, restore the suburban altars, perform the sacrificial rites, and offer thanks to Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 然後吊恤死義，慰犒有功，綏輯黎蒸，優問耆耋。
manualTranslations.literal: Then condole and comfort those who died in righteousness, comfort and reward those with merit, pacify and gather the common masses, graciously inquire of the aged.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then mourn the dead, reward the meritorious, restore order among the people, and show kindness to the elderly.

manualTranslations.zh: 安定反側，寬宥脅從；
manualTranslations.literal: Stabilize the wavering, pardon the coerced followers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Reassure those who wavered and pardon those who were forced to follow the rebels.

manualTranslations.zh: 宣暢郁堙，褒獎忠直；
manualTranslations.literal: Proclaim and clear what was pent and blocked, praise and reward the loyal and upright.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Give voice to silenced grievances and honor the loyal and upright.

manualTranslations.zh: 官失職之士，復廢業之人。
manualTranslations.literal: Officials who lost their posts, people who resumed abandoned livelihoods.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Restore officials who lost their posts and help those whose livelihoods were destroyed.

manualTranslations.zh: 是皆宜先，不可後也。
manualTranslations.literal: These all should be first, cannot be after.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All of these should come first, not last.

manualTranslations.zh: 至如崇飾服器，繕緝殿臺，備耳目之娛，選巾櫛之侍，是皆宜後，不可先也。
manualTranslations.literal: As for honoring and adorning garments and vessels, repairing and joining halls and terraces, preparing eye-and-ear pleasure, selecting towel-and-comb attendants—these all should be after, cannot be first.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for fine dress and ornaments, palace repairs, diversions for amusement, and choosing personal attendants—these must wait and cannot come first.

manualTranslations.zh: 散失內人，已經累月，既當離亂之際，必為將士所私。
manualTranslations.literal: Scattered and lost palace women have already piled up months; having been at separation and disorder's moment, they must have been privately taken by soldiers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The displaced palace women have been gone for months. In the chaos they have surely been taken by soldiers.

manualTranslations.zh: 其人若稍有知，不求當自陳獻；
manualTranslations.literal: If the person slightly has understanding, without seeking she will naturally declare and present herself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If any are sensible, they will come forward on their own without being sought.

manualTranslations.zh: 其人若甚無識，求之適使憂虞。
manualTranslations.literal: If the person is very without understanding, seeking them only makes worry and anxiety.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If any are foolish, searching for them will only cause trouble.

manualTranslations.zh: 自因寇亂喪亡，頗有大於此者，一聞搜索，懷懼必多；
manualTranslations.literal: Since because of bandit disorder there are losses and deaths, quite many greater than this—once hearing search, harboring fear must be many.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Many have suffered losses far worse in the rebellion. Once a search is announced, fear will spread widely.

manualTranslations.zh: 余孽尚繁，群情未一，因而善撫，猶恐危疑，若又懼之，於何不有！
manualTranslations.literal: Remaining spawn still numerous, crowd sentiment not one—thereby well comforting, still fearing peril and doubt; if again feared, what would not exist!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Rebel remnants are still numerous and public feeling is not yet unified. Even with gentle handling they remain unsettled. If you frighten them further, what calamity might not follow?

manualTranslations.zh: 昔人所以掩絕纓而飲盜馬者，豈必忘其情愛，蓋知為君之體然也。
manualTranslations.literal: The ancients therefore covered the dropped cap cord and drank of the stolen horse—not that they must forget their affection, but knew the bearing of a lord is thus.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ancients who hid a dropped cap-string and watered a stolen horse did not forget personal attachment. They understood what conduct befits a ruler.

manualTranslations.zh: 以小妨大，明者不為。
manualTranslations.literal: Using small to obstruct great—clear-minded men do not do this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The wise do not let small matters obstruct great ones.

manualTranslations.zh: 天下固多褻人，何必獨在於此。
manualTranslations.literal: Under Heaven indeed has many immodest people—why must it be only among these?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The world has no shortage of humble women. Why must you focus on these alone?

manualTranslations.zh: 所令撰賜渾瑊詔書，未敢順旨。
manualTranslations.literal: The ordered draft edict granted to Hun Jian—your servant does not dare follow the intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your servant dare not draft the edict for Hun Jian as ordered.

sourceRange.text: 贄諫曰：「瓊林」、「大盈」，自古悉無其制，傳諸耆舊之說，皆云創自開元。貴臣貪權，飾巧求媚，乃言：「郡邑貢賦所用，盍各區分：賦稅當委於有司，以給經用；貢獻宜歸於天子，以奉私求。」玄宗悅之。新是二庫，蕩心侈欲，萌柢於茲，迨乎失邦，終以餌寇。《記》曰：「貨悖而入，必悖而出。」豈其效歟！陛下嗣位之初，務遵理道，敦行儉約，斥遠貪饕。雖內庫舊藏，未歸太府，而諸方曲獻，不入禁闈，清風肅然，海內丕變。近以寇逆亂常，鑾輿外幸，既屬憂危之運，宜增儆勵之誠。臣昨奉使軍營，出經行殿，忽睹右廓之下，榜列二庫之名，戄然若驚，不識所以。何者？天衢尚梗，師旅方殷，痛心呻吟之聲，噢咻未息；忠勤戰守之效，賞賚未行。諸道貢珍，遽私別庫，萬目所視，孰能忍情？竊揣軍情，或生觖望，或忿形謗讟，或醜肆謳謠，頗含思亂之情，亦有悔忠之意。是知氓俗昏鄙，識昧高卑，不可以尊極臨，而可以誠義感。頃者六師初降，百物無儲，外扞兇徒，內防危堞，晝夜不息，殆將五旬。凍餓交侵，死傷相枕，畢命同力，竟夷大艱。良以陛下不厚其身，不私其欲，絕甘以同卒伍，輟食以啖功勞。無猛制人而不攜，懷所感也；無厚賞士而不怨，悉所無也。今者攻圍已解，衣食已豐，而謗讟方興，軍情稍沮，豈不以勇夫常性，嗜貨矜功，其患難既與之同憂，而好樂不與之同利，茍異恬默，能無怨咨！此理之常，故不足怪。《記》曰：「財散則民聚。」豈其效歟！陛下天資英聖，見善必遷，是將化蓄怨為銜恩，反過差為至當，促殄遺寇，永垂鴻名，大聖應機，固當不俟終日。

manualTranslations.zh: 贄諫曰：「瓊林」、「大盈」，自古悉無其制，傳諸耆舊之說，皆云創自開元。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhi remonstrated, saying:
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhi remonstrated:

manualTranslations.zh: 貴臣貪權，飾巧求媚，乃言：「郡邑貢賦所用，盍各區分：賦稅當委於有司，以給經用；
manualTranslations.literal: Noble ministers greedy for power, adorning craft to seek favor, then said: "The uses of commandery and county tribute and levies—why not each be divided? Levies and taxes should be entrusted to the responsible offices to supply regular expenditure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Powerful ministers, greedy for influence and skilled in flattery, proposed: "Let us separate the uses of local tribute: taxes should go to the regular offices for state expenses,

manualTranslations.zh: 貢獻宜歸於天子，以奉私求。」
manualTranslations.literal: Tribute offerings should return to the Son of Heaven to serve private desires.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: while gifts of tribute should belong to the Son of Heaven for his private use.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄宗悅之。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuanzong was pleased with this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong approved.

manualTranslations.zh: 新是二庫，蕩心侈欲，萌柢於茲，迨乎失邦，終以餌寇。
manualTranslations.literal: Newly establishing these two storehouses, dissolving the heart in extravagant desire—the sprout and root began here; when it reached losing the realm, in the end it became bait for bandits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus were these two treasuries born, planting the seeds of dissolute desire. In the end the dynasty lost the realm and fed its enemies.

manualTranslations.zh: 《記》曰：「貨悖而入，必悖而出。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Record says: "Wealth that enters perversely must perversely go out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, "Wealth gained unjustly will be lost unjustly.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈其效歟！
manualTranslations.literal: Was this not its effect!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Is this not the lesson!

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下嗣位之初，務遵理道，敦行儉約，斥遠貪饕。
manualTranslations.literal: When Your Majesty first succeeded to the throne, you strove to follow the Way of principle, earnestly practiced frugality and restraint, and repelled the greedy and gluttonous from afar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, you devoted yourself to right governance, practiced frugality, and kept the greedy at a distance.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖內庫舊藏，未歸太府，而諸方曲獻，不入禁闈，清風肅然，海內丕變。
manualTranslations.literal: Although old stores of the inner treasury had not returned to the Grand Treasury, yet regional partial offerings did not enter the forbidden quarters; pure wind was solemn, within the seas greatly transformed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though the inner treasury's old hoards had not yet been returned to the Grand Treasury, regional gifts no longer entered the palace. A refreshing discipline prevailed, and the realm was transformed.

manualTranslations.zh: 近以寇逆亂常，鑾輿外幸，既屬憂危之運，宜增儆勵之誠。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently because bandit rebels disturbed the norm and the imperial carriage went abroad, this already belongs to a fortune of worry and peril—you should increase vigilant encouragement.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now rebellion has thrown the realm into disorder and the throne is in exile. In such a time of peril you should redouble vigilance and restraint.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣昨奉使軍營，出經行殿，忽睹右廓之下，榜列二庫之名，戄然若驚，不識所以。
manualTranslations.literal: Yesterday your servant, on mission to the army camps, going out passed the traveling palace and suddenly saw under the right corridor placards listing the two storehouse names—startled as if in shock, not knowing the reason.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yesterday, on mission to the army camps, I passed the traveling palace and suddenly saw under the right corridor placards bearing the names of those two treasuries. I was struck with alarm and could not understand why.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: Why is this so?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

manualTranslations.zh: 天衢尚梗，師旅方殷，痛心呻吟之聲，噢咻未息；
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven's thoroughfares are still blocked, armies and hosts are just now pressing; sounds of pained hearts and groaning, gasping and moaning have not ceased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The roads are still blocked, the armies still engaged. The wounded groan and cry without cease.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠勤戰守之效，賞賚未行。
manualTranslations.literal: The effects of loyal diligence in battle and defense—rewards and gifts have not been carried out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who fought loyally have yet to receive their rewards.

manualTranslations.zh: 諸道貢珍，遽私別庫，萬目所視，孰能忍情？
manualTranslations.literal: Tribute treasures from the various circuits are hastily set apart in private storehouses—ten thousand eyes behold this; who can bear the feeling?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tribute from the provinces is suddenly set aside in private treasuries before ten thousand watching eyes. Who can bear it?

manualTranslations.zh: 竊揣軍情，或生觖望，或忿形謗讟，或醜肆謳謠，頗含思亂之情，亦有悔忠之意。
manualTranslations.literal: Privately I gauge army sentiment: some may breed divided hopes, some show resentment in slander and abuse, some ugly and unrestrained in ballads and songs—quite containing thoughts of disorder, also having mind to regret loyalty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I fear the army may grow resentful, break into open slander, or spread ugly songs of discontent. Some already harbor thoughts of rebellion; others regret their loyalty.

manualTranslations.zh: 是知氓俗昏鄙，識昧高卑，不可以尊極臨，而可以誠義感。
manualTranslations.literal: From this one knows that common custom is benighted and base, knowledge dim to high and low—you cannot with utmost honor approach them, but can with sincere righteousness move them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The common people are dull and cannot judge high from low. They cannot be won by displays of majesty, but they can be moved by sincerity and justice.

manualTranslations.zh: 頃者六師初降，百物無儲，外扞兇徒，內防危堞，晝夜不息，殆將五旬。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently when the Six Armies first submitted, a hundred things had no stores; outwardly resisting fierce factions, inwardly defending perilous ramparts—day and night without rest, nearly fifty days.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the imperial armies first arrived, there were no stores of any kind. Outwardly they fought the rebels; inwardly they defended the walls. Day and night without rest—for nearly fifty days.

manualTranslations.zh: 凍餓交侵，死傷相枕，畢命同力，竟夷大艱。
manualTranslations.literal: Cold and hunger together assailed; dead and wounded pillowed one another; exhausting life with united strength, in the end they leveled the great hardship.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cold and hunger assailed them together; the dead and wounded lay piled upon one another. Yet they gave their all in common effort and at last overcame the great peril.

manualTranslations.zh: 良以陛下不厚其身，不私其欲，絕甘以同卒伍，輟食以啖功勞。
manualTranslations.literal: Truly because Your Majesty did not enrich his person, did not privatize his desires, cut off sweetness to share with the ranks, stopped food to feed merit and toil.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This was because Your Majesty did not pamper himself or indulge his desires—he gave up delicacies to share with the ranks and went without food to feed those who had earned it.

manualTranslations.zh: 無猛制人而不攜，懷所感也；
manualTranslations.literal: Without fierce control yet men not alienated—this was what they felt in their hearts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without harsh discipline the men did not desert you, because they felt your care.

manualTranslations.zh: 無厚賞士而不怨，悉所無也。
manualTranslations.literal: Without thick rewards yet soldiers not resentful—all because there was nothing to give.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without rich rewards they did not complain, because you had nothing to give.

manualTranslations.zh: 今者攻圍已解，衣食已豐，而謗讟方興，軍情稍沮，豈不以勇夫常性，嗜貨矜功，其患難既與之同憂，而好樂不與之同利，茍異恬默，能無怨咨！
manualTranslations.literal: Now the siege is already lifted, clothing and food already abundant, yet slander and abuse are just rising, army sentiment somewhat discouraged—is it not because brave men's constant nature loves goods and prizes achievement? Their hardship they already shared in worry with you, yet pleasure and profit they do not share with you in benefit; if this differs from calm silence, how can there be no resentment and complaint!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the siege is lifted and food and clothing are plentiful, yet slander rises and army morale falters. Brave men by nature love gain and prize merit. They shared your hardship but do not share your ease. How can they remain silent without complaint?

manualTranslations.zh: 此理之常，故不足怪。
manualTranslations.literal: This is the constant of principle—therefore not enough to marvel at.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is only human nature and is not to be wondered at.

manualTranslations.zh: 《記》曰：「財散則民聚。」
manualTranslations.literal: The Record says: "When wealth is scattered, the people gather.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, "When wealth is dispersed, the people gather.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈其效歟！
manualTranslations.literal: Was this not its effect!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Is this not the lesson!

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下天資英聖，見善必遷，是將化蓄怨為銜恩，反過差為至當，促殄遺寇，永垂鴻名，大聖應機，固當不俟終日。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty's Heaven-endowed talent is heroic and sage; seeing good you must turn—this will transform stored resentment into cherishing grace, reverse excess into utmost propriety, hasten the extermination of remaining bandits, forever trail great fame; the great sage responding to the moment—solidly should not wait for the day's end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is gifted and sage, and turns to good at once. You can turn stored resentment into gratitude, correct error into right conduct, destroy the remaining rebels, and win lasting fame. A great sage acts when the moment calls—surely he need not wait even a day.

sourceRange.text: 四月，詔曰：田承嗣出自行間，策名邊戍，早參戎秩，効用無聞，嘗輔兇渠，驅馳有素。洎再平河朔，歸命轅門。朝廷俯念遺黎，久罹兵革。自祿山召禍，瀛、博流離；思明繼釁，趙、魏堙厄；以至農桑井邑，靡獲安居，骨肉室家，不能相保。念其凋瘵，思用撫寧，以其先布款誠，寄之為理。所以委授旄鉞之任，假以方面之榮，期爾知恩，庶能自効。崇資茂賞，首冠朝倫，列異姓之苴茅，登上公之禮命。子弟童稚，皆聯臺閣之華；妻妾僕媵，並受國邑之號。人臣之寵，舉集其門；將相之權，兼領其職。夫宰相者，所以盡忠，而乃據國家之封壤，仗國家之兵戈，安國家之黎人，調國家之征賦。掩有資實，憑竊寵靈，內包兇邪，外示歸順。且相、衛之略，所管素殊，而逼脅軍人，使之翻潰。因其驚擾，便進軍師，事跡暴彰，姦邪可見。不然，豈志清之亂，曾未崇朝，子期、光朝，會于明日。足知先有成約，指期而來，是為蔑棄典刑，擅興戈甲。旣云相州騷擾，隣境救災，旋又更取磁州，重行威虐。此實自矛盾，不究始終。三州旣空，遠邇驚陷，更移兵馬，又赴洺州，實為暴惡不仁，窮極殘忍。薛雄乃衛州刺史，固非本藩，忿其不附，橫加凌虐，一門盡屠，非復噍類，酷烈無狀，人神所冤。又四州之地，皆列屯營，長史屬官，任情補署。精甲利刃，良馬勁兵，全實之資裝，農藏之積實，盡收魏府，罔有孑遺。其為蓋在無赦，欲行討問，正厥刑書。猶示含容，冀其遷善，抑於典憲，務在慰安。乃遣知古遠奉詔書，諭以深旨，乃命承昭副茲麾下，撫彼舊封。而承昭又遣親將劉渾先傳詔命。承嗣逡巡磁、相，仍劫知古偕行，先令姪悅權扇軍吏，至使引刀自割，抑令騰口相稽，當衆諠譁，請歸承嗣。論其姦狀，足以為憑，此而可容，何者為罪？承嗣宜貶永州刺史，仍許一幼男女從行，便路赴任。委河東節度使薛兼訓、成德軍節度使李寶臣、幽州節度留後朱滔、昭義節度李承昭、淄青節度李正己、淮西節度李忠臣、永平軍節度使李勉、汴宋節度田神玉等，掎角進軍。如承嗣不時就職，所在加討，按軍法處分。

sourceRange.text: 臯乃築壇於廷，血牲與將士等盟曰：「上天不吊，國家多難，逆臣乘間，盜據宮闈。而李楚琳亦扇兇徒，傾陷城邑，酷虐所加，爰及本使，既不事上，安能恤下。臯是用激心憤氣，不遑底寧，誓與群公，竭誠王室。凡我同盟，一心協力，仗順除兇，先祖之靈，必當幽贊。言誠則誌合，義感則心齊；粉骨糜軀，決無所顧。有渝此誌，明神殛之，迨於子孫，亦罔遺類。皇天後土，當兆斯言。」又遣使入吐蕃求援。十一月，加檢校禮部尚書。興元元年，德宗還京，征為左金吾衛將軍，尋遷大將軍。

manualTranslations.zh: 臯乃築壇於廷，血牲與將士等盟曰：「上天不吊，國家多難，逆臣乘間，盜據宮闈。
manualTranslations.literal: Gao then built an altar in the courtyard, sacrificed a bloody victim, and with the generals and soldiers swore an oath, saying, "Heaven does not pity us; the state faces many calamities; rebel ministers seize their chance and steal possession of the palace precincts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Gao built an altar in the courtyard, offered a blood sacrifice, and swore an oath with his officers and men: "Heaven has turned away; the realm is beset with troubles. Traitors have seized their moment and seized the palace.

manualTranslations.zh: 而李楚琳亦扇兇徒，傾陷城邑，酷虐所加，爰及本使，既不事上，安能恤下。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Chuolin too has incited violent men and overthrown cities; the cruelty he inflicts reaches even to this commissioner. Since he will not serve his sovereign, how can he care for his subordinates?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Chuolin too has stirred up ruffians and overrun cities. His cruelty has reached even to our commissioner. A man who will not serve his sovereign cannot care for his subordinates.

manualTranslations.zh: 臯是用激心憤氣，不遑底寧，誓與群公，竭誠王室。
manualTranslations.literal: For this reason Gao's heart is stirred and his anger aroused; he has no leisure for repose and swears with you all to devote his utmost loyalty to the royal house.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For this reason my heart burns and my anger will not rest. I swear with you all to give our full loyalty to the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡我同盟，一心協力，仗順除兇，先祖之靈，必當幽贊。
manualTranslations.literal: All who are allied with me—unite your hearts and join your strength; relying on righteousness, destroy the wicked; the spirits of our forefathers will surely aid us from the unseen realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Let all who stand with me unite in one purpose and, upholding the righteous cause, destroy these villains. The spirits of our ancestors will surely aid us.

manualTranslations.zh: 言誠則誌合，義感則心齊；
manualTranslations.literal: when words are sincere, wills align; when righteousness moves us, hearts unite;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When speech is sincere, purpose aligns; when righteousness moves us, hearts unite;

manualTranslations.zh: 粉骨糜軀，決無所顧。
manualTranslations.literal: to grind our bones to powder and waste our bodies—we will never hesitate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: though our bones be ground to dust and our bodies destroyed, we shall not flinch.

manualTranslations.zh: 有渝此誌，明神殛之，迨於子孫，亦罔遺類。
manualTranslations.literal: Whoever violates this oath, may the bright spirits strike him down, even unto his descendants, leaving none behind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whoever breaks this oath, may the spirits strike him down, even to his descendants, leaving not one survivor.

manualTranslations.zh: 皇天後土，當兆斯言。」
manualTranslations.literal: May Heaven above and Earth below bear witness to these words.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: May Heaven and Earth bear witness to these words.

manualTranslations.zh: 又遣使入吐蕃求援。
manualTranslations.literal: He also sent envoys into Tibet to seek aid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to Tibet to request assistance.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一月，加檢校禮部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: In the eleventh month he was additionally appointed acting minister of rites.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he received the additional title of acting minister of rites.

sourceRange.text: 詔曰：吳元濟逆絕人理，反易天常；不居父喪，擅領軍政。諭以詔旨，曾無謙恭，熒惑一方之人，迫脅三軍之眾。以少陽嘗經任使，為之軫悼，命申吊祭，臨遣使臣。陵虐封疆，遂致稽阻，絕朝廷之理，忘父子之恩。旋又掩寇舞陽，傷殘吏卒，焚燒葉縣，騷擾閭閻，恣行奪攘，無所畏忌。朕念賞延之義，重傷籓帥之門，尚欲納於忠順之途，處在顯榮之地。未能飭怒，猶為包荒，再降詔書，俾申招撫。而毒螫滋甚，奸心靡悛，壽春西南，又陷鎮柵，窮兇稔惡，縱暴延災。覆載之所不容，人神之所共棄，良非獲已，致此興戎。吳元濟在身官爵，並宜令削奪。令宣武、大寧、淮南、宣歙等道兵馬合勢，山南東道及魏博、荊南、江西、劍南東川兵馬與鄂嶽許會，東都防禦使與懷鄭汝節度及義成兵馬掎角相應，同期進討。

sourceRange.text: 及田悅反，詔惠元領禁兵三千與諸將討伐，戰御河，奪三橋，皆惠元之功也。尋加檢校工部尚書，攝貝州刺史，令以兵屬李懷光。建中四年冬，自河朔與懷光同赴國難，解奉天之圍。明年二月，懷光背國叛逆，惠元義不受汙，脫身奔竄奉天。會乘輿南幸，懷光怒惠元之逸，令其將冉宗以百余騎追及於好畤縣。惠元計窮，父子三人並投人家井中，冉宗並出而害之。興元元年，贈右僕射，仍賻絹百匹。惠元男尚食奉禦晟，贈殿中監，左衛兵曹參軍皓贈邠州刺史，褒死難也。

context.beforeSource: 上稱嘆久之，降璽書慰勞。
context.afterSource: 李元諒，本駱元光，姓安氏，其先安息人也。
context.beforeLocal: 上稱嘆久之，降璽書慰勞。
context.afterLocal: 李元諒，本駱元光，姓安氏，其先安息人也。

sourceRange.text: 時陜西、神策兩節度郭英乂、衛伯玉鎮陜州，以忠臣為兩軍節度兵馬使。魚朝恩亦在陜，俾忠臣與賊將李歸仁、李感義等戰於永寧、莎柵；前後數十陣，皆摧破之。會淮西節度王仲升為賊所擒，寶應元年七月，拜忠臣太常卿同正、兼御史中丞、淮西十一州節度。尋加安州刺史，仍鎮蔡州。其年，令忠臣會元帥諸軍收復東都。二年六月，就加御史大夫。時回紇可汗既歸其國，留判官安恪、石帝庭於河陽守禦財物，因此招聚亡命為寇，道路壅隔，詔忠臣討平之。永泰元年，吐蕃犯西陲，京師戒嚴。代宗命中使追兵，諸道多不時赴難。使至淮西，忠臣方會鞠，即令整師飾駕。監軍大將固請曰：「軍行須擇吉日。」忠臣奮臂於眾曰：「焉有父母遇寇難，待揀好日，方救患乎！」即日進發。自此方隅有警，忠臣必先期而至。由是代宗嘉其忠節，加本道觀察使，寵賜頗厚。及同華節度周智光舉兵反，詔忠臣與神策將李太清等討平之。大歷三年，加檢校工部尚書，實封通前三百戶。五年，加蔡州刺史。七年，檢校右僕射、知省事。李靈曜之叛，田承嗣使侄悅援之，忠臣與諸軍大破悅等，汴州平。十一年十二月，加檢校司空平章事、汴州刺史。

context.beforeSource: 召至京師，賜姓李氏，名忠臣，封隴西郡公，賜良馬、莊宅、銀器、彩物等。
context.afterSource: 忠臣性貪殘好色，將吏妻女多被誘脅以通之。
