manualTranslations.zh: 時陜西、神策兩節度郭英乂、衛伯玉鎮陜州，以忠臣為兩軍節度兵馬使。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the two circuits of Shaanxi and Shence—Guo Yingyi and Wei Boyu—garrisoned Shaan Prefecture; Zhongchen was made army commander for both armies of the military commissioners.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guo Yingyi and Wei Boyu of Shaanxi and Shence circuits held Shaan; Li Zhongchen was made joint army commander.

manualTranslations.zh: 魚朝恩亦在陜，俾忠臣與賊將李歸仁、李感義等戰於永寧、莎柵；
manualTranslations.literal: Yu Chaoen was also at Shaan; he had Zhongchen fight the rebel generals Li Guiren, Li Ganyi, and others at Yongning and Shazha;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yu Chaoen in Shaan sent Li Zhongchen against Li Guiren, Li Ganyi, and other rebels at Yongning and Shazha;

manualTranslations.zh: 前後數十陣，皆摧破之。
manualTranslations.literal: In front and behind, in some dozens of battles, all were crushed and broken.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: crushing them in dozens of battles.

manualTranslations.zh: 會淮西節度王仲升為賊所擒，寶應元年七月，拜忠臣太常卿同正、兼御史中丞、淮西十一州節度。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Huai-Xi military governor Wang Zhongsheng was captured by rebels; in the seventh month of the first year of Baoying, Zhongchen was appointed Minister of Ceremonies with honorary regular status, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of the eleven prefectures of Huai-Xi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Huai-Xi governor Wang Zhongsheng was captured, in seventh month, Baoying 1, Li Zhongchen became Minister of Ceremonies, Censor-in-Chief, and governor of eleven Huai-Xi prefectures.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋加安州刺史，仍鎮蔡州。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was additionally made prefect of An Prefecture, still garrisoning Cai Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He soon added An prefect and kept his seat at Cai.

manualTranslations.zh: 其年，令忠臣會元帥諸軍收復東都。
manualTranslations.literal: That year, he was ordered to join the field marshal's various armies in recovering the Eastern Capital.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year he joined the commander-in-chief's forces in retaking the Eastern Capital.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年六月，就加御史大夫。
manualTranslations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, he was immediately advanced to Censor Grandee.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In sixth month of year two he was promoted Censor Grandee.

manualTranslations.zh: 時回紇可汗既歸其國，留判官安恪、石帝庭於河陽守禦財物，因此招聚亡命為寇，道路壅隔，詔忠臣討平之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the Uyghur qaghan had already returned to his state, leaving judicial officers An Ke and Shi Diting at Heyang to guard stored goods; on this account they gathered fugitives to become bandits, and the roads were blocked and cut off; an edict ordered Zhongchen to suppress and pacify them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Uyghur qaghan had gone home but left An Ke and Shi Diting at Heyang to guard plunder; they recruited outlaws and cut the roads, so Li Zhongchen was ordered to pacify them.

manualTranslations.zh: 永泰元年，吐蕃犯西陲，京師戒嚴。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Tibet invaded the western frontier; the capital was placed under martial law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yongtai 1 Tibet struck the western border and the capital went on alert.

manualTranslations.zh: 代宗命中使追兵，諸道多不時赴難。
manualTranslations.literal: Daizong ordered palace emissaries to rush troops; the various circuits mostly did not come to the rescue in timely fashion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Daizong sent palace envoys to hurry reinforcements, but most circuits failed to come promptly.

manualTranslations.zh: 使至淮西，忠臣方會鞠，即令整師飾駕。
manualTranslations.literal: When the emissary reached Huai-Xi, Zhongchen was just holding a banquet; he immediately ordered the army assembled and harnesses prepared.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached Huai-Xi, Li Zhongchen was at a banquet but immediately ordered his army mounted and ready.

manualTranslations.zh: 監軍大將固請曰：「軍行須擇吉日。」
manualTranslations.literal: The army supervisor great general firmly requested, saying, "An army march must choose an auspicious day."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The supervising general insisted, "We must pick an auspicious day to march.

manualTranslations.zh: 忠臣奮臂於眾曰：「焉有父母遇寇難，待揀好日，方救患乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhongchen raised his arm before the assembly and said, "How can it be that when one's parents meet bandit calamity, one waits to pick a good day before rescuing them from disaster!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen threw up his arm before the troops: "When your parents are under attack, do you wait for a lucky day to save them?"

manualTranslations.zh: 即日進發。
manualTranslations.literal: That very day they advanced and set out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: They marched that same day.

manualTranslations.zh: 自此方隅有警，忠臣必先期而至。
manualTranslations.literal: From this time on, whenever the border regions had an alarm, Zhongchen always arrived ahead of the expected time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After that, whenever trouble broke out on the frontiers, Li Zhongchen arrived ahead of schedule.

manualTranslations.zh: 由是代宗嘉其忠節，加本道觀察使，寵賜頗厚。
manualTranslations.literal: Because of this Daizong praised his loyalty and integrity, added him as observation commissioner of his own circuit, and favored and bestowed upon him quite generously.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Daizong rewarded his loyalty with the circuit observation commission and rich gifts.

manualTranslations.zh: 及同華節度周智光舉兵反，詔忠臣與神策將李太清等討平之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Tong-Hua military governor Zhou Zhiguang raised troops in rebellion, an edict ordered Zhongchen and Shence general Li Taiqing and others to suppress and pacify him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhou Zhiguang of Tong-Hua rebelled, Li Zhongchen and Shence general Li Taiqing were sent to crush him.

manualTranslations.zh: 大歷三年，加檢校工部尚書，實封通前三百戶。
manualTranslations.literal: In the third year of Dali, he was additionally made acting Minister of Works, with a cumulative enfeoffment through the prior grants of three hundred households.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dali 3 brought acting Minister of Works and three hundred cumulative tax households.

manualTranslations.zh: 五年，加蔡州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifth year, he was additionally made prefect of Cai Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In year five he added Cai prefect.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年，檢校右僕射、知省事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the seventh year, acting Right Vice Director, in charge of Secretariat affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Year seven he became acting Right Vice Director in charge of Secretariat business.

manualTranslations.zh: 李靈曜之叛，田承嗣使侄悅援之，忠臣與諸軍大破悅等，汴州平。
manualTranslations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled, Tian Chengsi sent his nephew Yue to aid him; Zhongchen with the various armies greatly defeated Yue and the others, and Bian Prefecture was pacified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled and Tian Chengsi's nephew Yue came to aid him, Li Zhongchen and the allies routed Yue and pacified Bian.

manualTranslations.zh: 十一年十二月，加檢校司空平章事、汴州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year, he was additionally made acting Minister of Works, co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and prefect of Bian Prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, year eleven, he became acting Minister of Works, co-director, and Bian prefect.

sourceRange.text: 及晉卒，令長源知留後事。長源揚言曰：「將士多弛慢，不守憲章，當以法繩之。」由是人人恐懼。加以叔度苛刻，多縱聲色，數至樂營與諸婦人嬉戲，自稱孟郎，眾皆薄之。舊例，使長薨，放散布帛於三軍制服。至是，人請服，長源初固不允，軍人求之不已，長源等議給其布直。叔度高其鹽價而賤為布直，每人不過得鹽三二斤，軍情大變。或勸長源，故事有大變，皆賞三軍，三軍乃安。長源曰：「不可使我同河北賊，以錢買健兒取旌節。」兵士怨怒滋甚，乃執長源及叔度等臠而食之，斯須骨肉糜散。長源死之日，詔下以為節度使，及聞其死，中外惜之，贈尚書右僕射。

context.beforeSource: 長源每事守法，晉或茍且，長源輒執而正之。
context.afterSource: 劉全諒，懷州武涉人也。
context.beforeLocal: 長源每事守法，晉或茍且，長源輒執而正之。
context.afterLocal: 劉全諒，懷州武涉人也。

manualTranslations.literal: Changyuan declared openly, "The officers and soldiers are mostly slack and do not keep the statutes; they must be restrained by law.

manualTranslations.zh: 由是人人恐懼。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon everyone was afraid.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Everyone was terrified.

manualTranslations.zh: 加以叔度苛刻，多縱聲色，數至樂營與諸婦人嬉戲，自稱孟郎，眾皆薄之。
manualTranslations.literal: Added to this, Shudu was harsh; he indulged in music and women, often went to the music camp to sport with various women, called himself Master Meng, and all despised him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shudu was harsh, chased women in the music camp, called himself Master Meng, and was despised.

manualTranslations.zh: 舊例，使長薨，放散布帛於三軍制服。
manualTranslations.literal: By old custom, when a commissioner died, cloth and silk were distributed to the three armies for mourning dress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By custom, when a commissioner died, cloth was issued to the army for mourning.

manualTranslations.zh: 至是，人請服，長源初固不允，軍人求之不已，長源等議給其布直。
manualTranslations.literal: On this occasion the men asked for mourning dress; at first Changyuan firmly refused; the soldiers pressed unceasingly; Changyuan and the others discussed giving them cash in lieu of cloth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The troops asked for mourning cloth; Changyuan refused, then offered cash instead.

manualTranslations.zh: 叔度高其鹽價而賤為布直，每人不過得鹽三二斤，軍情大變。
manualTranslations.literal: Shudu raised the price of salt and cheapened the cash-for-cloth rate, so each man received no more than two or three jin of salt; army sentiment changed greatly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shudu inflated salt prices and cheated the cash payment—each man got only a few pounds of salt—and the army turned.

manualTranslations.zh: 或勸長源，故事有大變，皆賞三軍，三軍乃安。
manualTranslations.literal: Some urged Changyuan that by precedent, when there is great upheaval, the three armies are always rewarded and then pacified.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some urged that custom required rewarding the army after upheaval to calm them.

manualTranslations.zh: 長源曰：「不可使我同河北賊，以錢買健兒取旌節。」
manualTranslations.literal: Changyuan said, "I cannot let me be like the Hebei rebels, buying stalwart soldiers with money to seize the commander's banner and seal.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Changyuan said, "I will not buy troops with money like the Hebei rebels.

manualTranslations.zh: 兵士怨怒滋甚，乃執長源及叔度等臠而食之，斯須骨肉糜散。
manualTranslations.literal: The soldiers' resentment and rage grew ever worse; they seized Changyuan and Shudu and others, dismembered them, and ate them; in an instant flesh and bone were scattered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The enraged troops seized Changyuan and Shudu, dismembered them, and devoured them on the spot.

manualTranslations.zh: 長源死之日，詔下以為節度使，及聞其死，中外惜之，贈尚書右僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: On the day Changyuan died an edict had just come down appointing him military governor; when his death was heard, inside and outside the court regretted it, and he was posthumously made Right Vice Director.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The day he died his commission as governor arrived; the court mourned him and made him Right Vice Director.

sourceRange.text: 五月，全義與少誠將吳秀、吳少陽等戰於溵水南，官軍復敗。七月，全義頓軍於五樓行營，為賊所乘，大潰，全義與都監軍使賈秀英、賈國良等夜遁，遂城守溵水。汴宋、徐泗、淄青兵馬直趣陳州，列營四面。少誠兵逼溵水五、六里下營，韓全義諸軍又退保陳州。其汴州、河陽等兵各私歸本道，陳許將孟元陽與神策兵各率所部留軍溵水。全義斬昭義、滑州、河陽、河中都將凡四人，然竟未嘗整陣交鋒，而王師累挫潰。少誠尋引兵退歸蔡州。遂下詔洗雪，復其官爵，累加檢校僕射。順宗即位，加同中書門平章事。元和初，遷檢校司空，依前平章事。元和四年十一月卒，年六十，廢朝三日，贈司徒。

sourceRange.text: 式方，字考元。以廕授揚府參軍，轉常州晉陵尉。浙西觀察使王緯辟為從事，入為太子通事舍人，改太常寺主簿。明練鐘律，有所考定，深為高郢所賞。時父作鎮揚州，家財鉅萬，甲第在安仁裏，杜城有別墅，亭館林池，為城南之最。昆仲皆在朝廷，與時賢遊從，樂而有節。既而佑入中書，出為昭應令。丁父憂，服闋，遷司農少卿，賜金紫，加正議大夫、太仆卿。時少子悰選尚公主，式方以右戚移病不視事。久之，穆宗即位，轉兼御史中丞，充桂管觀察都防禦使。長慶二年三月，卒於位，贈禮部尚書。

sourceRange.text: 南仲上疏諫曰：伏聞貞懿皇后今於城東章敬寺北以起陵廟，臣不知有司之請乎，陛下之意乎，陰陽家流希旨乎？臣愚以為非所宜也。謹具疏陳論，伏願暫留天睠而省察焉。臣聞人臣宅於家，君上宅於國。長安城，是陛下皇居也，其可穿鑿興動，建陵墓於其側乎？此非宜一也。夫葬者藏也，欲人之不得見也。是以古帝前王葬后妃，莫不憑丘原，遠郊郭。今則西臨宮闕，南迫康莊，若使近而可見，死而復生，雖在西宮待之可也。如骨肉歸土，魂無不之，章敬之北，竟何所益？視之兆庶，則彰溺愛；垂之萬代，則累明德，此非所宜二也。夫帝王者，居高明，燭幽滯。先皇所以因龍首建望春，蓋為此也。今若起陵目前，動傷宸慮，天心一傷，數日不平。且匹夫向隅，滿堂為之不樂；萬乘不樂，人其可歡心乎？又暇日起歌，動鐘於內，此地皆聞，此非宜三也。伏以貞懿皇后，坤德合天，母慈逮下，陛下以切軫旒扆，久俟蓍龜。始謚之以貞懿，終待之以褻近，臣竊惑焉，非所以稱述後德，光被下泉也。今國人皆曰：「貞懿皇后之陵邇於城下者，主上將日省而時望焉。」斯有損於聖德，無益於貞懿。將欲寵之，而反辱之，此非宜四也。凡此數事，實玷大猷，天下鹹知，伏惟陛下熟計而取其長也。陛下方將偃武靖人，一誤於此，其傷實多。臣恐君子是非，史官褒貶，大明忽虧於掩蝕，至德翻後於堯、舜，不其惜哉！今指日尚遙，改卜何害？抑皇情之殊眷，成貞懿之美號。

sourceRange.text: 十九年夏旱，孟容上疏曰：臣伏聞陛下數月已來，齋居損膳，為兆庶心疲，又敕有司，走於群望，牲於百神，而密雲不雨，首種未入。豈觴醪有闕，祈祝非誠，為陰陽適然，豐歉前定，何聖意精至，甘澤未答也？臣歷觀自古天人交感事，未有不由百姓利病之急者、切者，邦家教令之大者、遠者。京師是萬國所會，強幹弱枝，自古通規。其一年稅錢及地租，出入一百萬貫。臣伏冀陛下即日下令，全放免之；其次，三分放二。且使旱涸之際，免更流亡。若播種無望，征斂如舊，則必愁怨遷徙，不顧墳墓矣。臣愚以為德音一發，膏澤立應，變災為福，期在斯須。戶部所收掌錢，非度支歲計，本防緩急別用。今此炎旱，直支一百余萬貫，代京兆百姓一年差科，實陛下巍巍睿謀，天下鼓舞歌揚者也。復更省察庶政之中，有流移征防，當還而未還者，徒役禁錮，當釋而未釋者，逋懸饋送，當免而未免者，沈滯郁抑，當伸而未伸者，有一於此，則特降明命，令有司條列，三日內聞奏。其當還、當釋、當免、當伸者，下詔之日，所在即時施行。臣愚以為如此而神不監，歲不稔，古未之有。

sourceRange.text: 文宗即位，韋處厚輔政，大去奸黨。既逐棲楚，又詔曰：「孔門高懸百行，由至順者，其身必榮；朝廷廣設眾官，踐正途者，其道必達。前鄉貢進士熊望，因緣薄伎，偷冀褻幸。營居中之密職，擾惑朝經；鼓逼下之囂聲，因依邪隙。及眾議波湧，累月不寧；司門驗繻，累月至四。考覆謬妄，乃非坦途。朕大啟康莊，以端群望，俾示投荒之典，用正向方之流。可漳州司戶。

context.beforeSource: 棲楚以望名薦送，事未行而昭湣崩。
context.afterSource: 」柏耆者，將軍良器之子。
context.beforeLocal: 棲楚以望名薦送，事未行而昭湣崩。
context.afterLocal: 柏耆者，將軍良器之子。

manualTranslations.zh: 文宗即位，韋處厚輔政，大去奸黨。
manualTranslations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne Wei Chuhou assisted in government and greatly removed treacherous factions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Wei Chuhou directed the government and purged the treacherous factions.

manualTranslations.zh: 既逐棲楚，又詔曰：「孔門高懸百行，由至順者，其身必榮；
manualTranslations.literal: Having expelled Qichu, there was also an edict: "At Confucius's gate a hundred conducts are hung high; those who follow utmost obedience, their persons will surely be honored;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After expelling Liu Qichu, the court issued an edict: "At Confucius's gate a hundred virtues are held in esteem; those who follow the path of utmost obedience will surely win honor;

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷廣設眾官，踐正途者，其道必達。
manualTranslations.literal: the court broadly establishes the multitude of offices; those who tread the upright path, their Way will surely reach fulfillment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the court establishes many offices so that those who tread the upright path may surely attain their goal.

manualTranslations.zh: 前鄉貢進士熊望，因緣薄伎，偷冀褻幸。
manualTranslations.literal: The former presented scholar Xiong Wang, relying on slight skill, stealthily hoped for familiar favor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The former presented scholar Xiong Wang, trading on slight talents, sought by stealth the emperor's intimate favor.

manualTranslations.zh: 營居中之密職，擾惑朝經；
manualTranslations.literal: He schemed for secret posts within the inner palace and disturbed and confused court regulations;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He schemed for secret posts within the inner palace and disturbed court governance;

manualTranslations.zh: 鼓逼下之囂聲，因依邪隙。
manualTranslations.literal: he drummed up and pressed clamor from below and relied on wicked openings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: he stirred up clamor among subordinates and relied on wicked patrons.

manualTranslations.zh: 及眾議波湧，累月不寧；
manualTranslations.literal: When public discussion surged like waves, for months there was no peace;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Public outrage surged for months without abating;

manualTranslations.zh: 司門驗繻，累月至四。
manualTranslations.literal: the Gate Office verified passes, accumulating to four months.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the Gate Office tallied his passes month after month until they reached four.

manualTranslations.zh: 考覆謬妄，乃非坦途。
manualTranslations.literal: Examination and review showed error and absurdity; this was not the level road.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Investigation proved his conduct absurd and improper—not the level path of public service.

manualTranslations.zh: 朕大啟康莊，以端群望，俾示投荒之典，用正向方之流。
manualTranslations.literal: We broadly open the great highway to set aright the multitude's expectations, causing to display the precedent of casting into the wilderness and using it to correct the current flowing toward wrong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: We open the broad highway of public service to set right the people's expectations, and now display the precedent of banishment to correct those who stray from the proper path.

manualTranslations.zh: 可漳州司戶。
manualTranslations.literal: He may be made Registrar of Zhangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He is demoted to registrar of Zhangzhou.

sourceRange.text: 敬宗即位，畋遊稍多，坐朝常晚。棲楚出班，以額叩龍墀出血，苦諫曰：「臣歷觀前王，嗣位之初，莫不躬勤庶政，坐以待旦。陛下即位已來，放情嗜寢，樂色忘憂，安臥宮闈，日晏方起。西宮密邇，未過山陵，鼓吹之聲，日喧於外。伏以憲宗皇帝、大行皇帝，皆是長君，恪勤庶政，四方猶有叛亂。陛下運當少主，即位未幾，惡德布聞，臣慮福祚之不長也。臣忝諫官，致陛下有此，請碎首以謝！」遂以額叩龍墀，久之不已。宰臣李逢吉出位宣曰：「劉棲楚休叩頭，候詔旨。」棲楚捧首而起，因更陳論，磕頭見血。上為之動容，以袖連揮令出。棲楚又云：「不可臣奏，臣即碎首死。」中書侍郎牛僧孺復宣示而出，敬宗為之動容。

context.beforeSource: 逢吉以為鷹犬之用，欲中傷裴度及殺李紳。
context.afterSource: 無何，遷起居郎，至諫議。
context.beforeLocal: 逢吉以為鷹犬之用，欲中傷裴度及殺李紳。
context.afterLocal: 無何，遷起居郎，至諫議。

manualTranslations.zh: 敬宗即位，畋遊稍多，坐朝常晚。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, hunting and pleasure-seeking gradually increased, and he often held court late.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he spent more time hunting and at play, and often held court late in the day.

manualTranslations.zh: 棲楚出班，以額叩龍墀出血，苦諫曰：「臣歷觀前王，嗣位之初，莫不躬勤庶政，坐以待旦。
manualTranslations.literal: Qichu stepped forth from the ranks, knocked his forehead on the imperial terrace steps until it bled, and remonstrated bitterly, saying: "Your servant has broadly observed former kings—at the beginning of their succession, none failed personally to attend diligently to common affairs, sitting until dawn.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu stepped forward from the ranks, pounding his forehead against the steps of the imperial dais until it bled, and remonstrated fiercely: "I have studied the reigns of past emperors. At the start of every new reign, the sovereign personally applied himself to governance, sitting up until dawn.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下即位已來，放情嗜寢，樂色忘憂，安臥宮闈，日晏方起。
manualTranslations.literal: Since Your Majesty's accession, you have indulged your feelings and loved sleep, delighted in beauty and forgotten cares, lying at ease within the inner palace, and only rise when the sun is high.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, you have indulged in sleep, given yourself over to pleasure, and lain at ease within the inner palace—not rising until the sun is well up.

manualTranslations.zh: 西宮密邇，未過山陵，鼓吹之聲，日喧於外。
manualTranslations.literal: The Western Palace is close at hand; the imperial tombs have not yet passed their mourning period, yet the sounds of drums and pipes daily clamor outside.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Western Palace lies close by, and the mourning period for the late emperor has not yet ended—yet the sound of music and revelry clamors outside every day.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏以憲宗皇帝、大行皇帝，皆是長君，恪勤庶政，四方猶有叛亂。
manualTranslations.literal: I submit that Emperor Xianzong and the late emperor were both mature rulers who diligently attended to common affairs, yet the four quarters still had rebellions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong and the late emperor were seasoned rulers who applied themselves tirelessly to governance—and even they faced rebellions across the empire.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下運當少主，即位未幾，惡德布聞，臣慮福祚之不長也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty's fate is that of a young ruler; you have reigned but a short time, and ill repute spreads abroad—I fear your fortune and reign will not be long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a young ruler, and you have not long been on the throne. Ill report of your conduct is already spreading. I fear your reign will not last.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣忝諫官，致陛下有此，請碎首以謝！」
manualTranslations.literal: Your servant disgraces the remonstrating office and has allowed Your Majesty to come to this—I beg to smash my head to atone!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As a remonstrating official, I am ashamed to have allowed Your Majesty to come to this. I beg leave to dash out my brains in atonement!

manualTranslations.zh: 遂以額叩龍墀，久之不已。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he knocked his forehead on the imperial terrace for a long time without stopping.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: With that he resumed pounding his forehead against the steps, and would not stop for a long while.

manualTranslations.zh: 宰臣李逢吉出位宣曰：「劉棲楚休叩頭，候詔旨。」
manualTranslations.literal: Chief minister Li Fengji stepped forward and announced: "Liu Qichu, cease knocking your head; await the imperial decree."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Fengji stepped forward and proclaimed: "Liu Qichu, stop your kowtow and await the emperor's command.

manualTranslations.zh: 棲楚捧首而起，因更陳論，磕頭見血。
manualTranslations.literal: Qichu held his head and rose, then again presented his arguments, knocking his head until blood showed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu lifted his bloodied head and rose, then continued his remonstrance—kowtowing until the blood ran again.

manualTranslations.zh: 上為之動容，以袖連揮令出。
manualTranslations.literal: The emperor was moved by this and repeatedly waved his sleeve ordering him out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The emperor was visibly shaken and waved him away again and again with his sleeve.

manualTranslations.zh: 棲楚又云：「不可臣奏，臣即碎首死。」
manualTranslations.literal: Qichu again said: "If Your Majesty will not hear my memorial, your servant will immediately dash out his brains and die."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Liu Qichu cried out: "If Your Majesty will not hear me out, I will dash out my brains on this spot!

manualTranslations.zh: 中書侍郎牛僧孺復宣示而出，敬宗為之動容。
manualTranslations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Niu Sengru again announced the order for him to withdraw, and Jingzong was moved by this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Niu Sengru again ordered him to withdraw—and even Jingzong was visibly moved.

sourceRange.text: 長慶元年，幽、鎮繼亂。遜請身先討賊，不許。但命以兵一萬，會於行營。遜奉詔，即日發兵，故先諸軍而至，由是進位檢校吏部尚書。尋改鳳翔節度使，行至京師，以疾陳乞，改刑部尚書。長慶三年正月卒，年六十三，廢朝一日，贈右僕射。

context.beforeSource: 及遜至，集大軍與之約束，嚴具示賞罰必信，號令數百言，士皆感悅。
context.afterSource: 遜幼孤，寓居江陵。

manualTranslations.zh: 長慶元年，幽、鎮繼亂。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, Youzhou and Zhenzhou rebelled in succession.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing, the circuits of Youzhou and Zhenzhou rebelled in turn.

manualTranslations.zh: 遜請身先討賊，不許。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun requested to take the lead in attacking the rebels; permission was denied.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun asked to lead the campaign personally, but the request was denied.

manualTranslations.zh: 但命以兵一萬，會於行營。
manualTranslations.literal: He was only ordered to send ten thousand troops to rendezvous at the field headquarters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was ordered instead to dispatch ten thousand troops to join the field headquarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 遜奉詔，即日發兵，故先諸軍而至，由是進位檢校吏部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Xun obeyed the edict and mobilized troops that same day; therefore he arrived before the other armies and was promoted to Acting Minister of the Ministry of Civil Office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xun obeyed at once and marched his troops out the same day, arriving ahead of the other armies. For this he was promoted to acting minister of civil appointments.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋改鳳翔節度使，行至京師，以疾陳乞，改刑部尚書。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Fengxiang; when he reached the capital he pleaded illness and was changed to Minister of Justice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to military commissioner of Fengxiang, but upon reaching the capital he pleaded illness and was reassigned as minister of justice.

manualTranslations.zh: 長慶三年正月卒，年六十三，廢朝一日，贈右僕射。
manualTranslations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Changqing he died, aged sixty-three; court mourning was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted the right vice grand councilor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the third year of Changqing, aged sixty-three. Court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted right vice grand councilor.

manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bin, Yan, and Tan all directed the imperial examinations and oversaw personnel appointments.

manualTranslations.zh: 冠族聞望，為時名德。
manualTranslations.literal: A foremost clan in reputation and prestige, they were celebrated men of virtue in their age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A leading clan in prestige and renown, they were celebrated as men of virtue in their time.

sourceRange.text: 懿宗即位，遷檢校戶部尚書，兼青州刺史、平戶節度觀察處置等使。入為戶部侍郎，轉吏部，絟綜平允，不受請托。為執政所惡，出為邠州刺史、邠寧節度使。宰相杜審權素不悅於澳，會吏部發澳時簿籍，吏緣為奸，坐罷鎮，以秘書監分司東都。嘗戲吟云：「若將韋鑒同殷鑒，錯認容身作保身。」此句聞於京師，權幸尤怒之。上表求致仕，宰相疑其怨望，拜河南尹。制出，累上章辭疾，以松槚在秦川，求歸樊川別業，許之。逾年，復授戶部侍郎。以疾不拜而卒。贈戶部尚書，謚曰貞。

sourceRange.text: 元和七年，惠昭太子薨，穆宗時為遂王，憲宗以澧王居長，又多內助，將建儲貳，命群與澧王作讓表。群上言曰：「大凡己合當之，則有陳讓之儀；己不合當，因何遽有讓表？今遂王嫡長，所宜正位青宮。」竟從其奏。時魏博節度使田季安進絹五千匹，充助修開業寺。群以為事實無名，體尤不可，請止其所進。群前後所論多愜旨，無不聽納。遷禮部侍郎，選拔才行，咸為公當。轉戶部侍郎。

sourceRange.text: 絪以文學進，恬淡，踐歷華顯，出入中外者逾四十年。所居雖無赫奕之稱，而守道敦篤，耽悅墳典，與當時博聞好古之士，為講論名理之遊，時人皆仰其耆德焉。及文宗即位，以年力衰耄，累表陳乞，遂以太子太傅致仕。三年十月卒，年七十八，贈司空，謚曰宣。子祗德。

sourceRange.text: 長慶初，遷鳳翔節度使，依前檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。歲末，復授許州節度使。朝廷以光顏昔鎮陳許，頗得士心，將討鎮、冀，故有此拜。赴鎮日，宰相百僚以故事送別於章敬寺，穆宗禦通化門臨送之，賜錦彩、銀器、良馬、玉帶等物。二年，討王廷湊，命光顏兼深州行營諸軍節度使。光顏既受命而行，懸軍討賊，艱於饋運。朝廷又以滄、景、德、棣等州俾之兼管，以其鄰賊之郡，可便飛挽。光顏以朝廷制置乖方，賊帥連結，未可朝夕平定，事若差跌，即前功悉棄，乃懇辭兼鎮。尋以疾作，表祈歸鎮。朝廷果討賊無功而赦廷湊。四年，敬宗即位，正拜司徒。

context.beforeSource: 已而帶平章復鎮，所以報勛臣也。
context.afterSource: 汴州李絺逐其帥叛，詔光顏率陳許之師討之。

manualTranslations.zh: 長慶初，遷鳳翔節度使，依前檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he was transferred to military commissioner of Fengxiang, retaining his former ranks as acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era he became military commissioner of Fengxiang, keeping his titles as acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor.

manualTranslations.zh: 歲末，復授許州節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: At year's end he was again appointed military commissioner of Xuzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before the year was out he was reassigned as military commissioner of Xuzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷以光顏昔鎮陳許，頗得士心，將討鎮、冀，故有此拜。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Guangyan had once governed Chen and Xu and had well won the troops' hearts, and because the court intended to campaign against Zhen and Ji, this appointment was made.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guangyan had once held Chen-Xu and won deep loyalty from the ranks. With a campaign against Zhen and Ji in view, the court gave him this post.

manualTranslations.zh: 赴鎮日，宰相百僚以故事送別於章敬寺，穆宗禦通化門臨送之，賜錦彩、銀器、良馬、玉帶等物。
manualTranslations.literal: On the day he departed for his post, chancellors and the hundred officials saw him off according to custom at Zhangjing Temple; Muzong proceeded to Tonghua Gate to send him off in person and bestowed brocade silks, silver vessels, fine horses, a jade belt, and other gifts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the day he left for his command, the full court saw him off at Zhangjing Temple by custom. Muzong went in person to Tonghua Gate to farewell him, gifting brocades, silverware, fine horses, and a jade belt.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，討王廷湊，命光顏兼深州行營諸軍節度使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year, campaigning against Wang Tingcou, Guangyan was ordered to serve concurrently as military commissioner of all armies in the Shenzhou forward camp.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year, for the campaign against Wang Tingcou, he was named overall commander of the Shenzhou expedition.

manualTranslations.zh: 光顏既受命而行，懸軍討賊，艱於饋運。
manualTranslations.literal: Once Guangyan accepted the commission and set out, his army advanced deep into hostile country to attack rebels, and supply transport proved arduous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guangyan accepted the command and marched out, but his army was deep in enemy territory and supply lines quickly became a struggle.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷又以滄、景、德、棣等州俾之兼管，以其鄰賊之郡，可便飛挽。
manualTranslations.literal: The court also put Cang, Jing, De, Di, and other prefectures under his concurrent administration, since those districts bordered the rebels and could speed emergency transport.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court added Cang, Jing, De, Di, and neighboring prefectures to his jurisdiction, hoping their proximity to the enemy would ease rapid resupply.

manualTranslations.zh: 光顏以朝廷制置乖方，賊帥連結，未可朝夕平定，事若差跌，即前功悉棄，乃懇辭兼鎮。
manualTranslations.literal: Guangyan held that the court's dispositions were ill judged—the rebel chieftains were linked together and could not be settled overnight; if affairs stumbled, all prior merit would be squandered—and he earnestly declined the additional commands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Guangyan argued the court's plan was unsound: the rebel leaders were allied and would not fall quickly, and one misstep would waste everything already won. He begged off the extra territories.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋以疾作，表祈歸鎮。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon illness set in and he memorialized asking to return to his original command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and petitioned to return to his own headquarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷果討賊無功而赦廷湊。
manualTranslations.literal: The court indeed failed to subdue the rebels and pardoned Tingcou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As he had foreseen, the campaign failed and the court pardoned Wang Tingcou.

manualTranslations.zh: 四年，敬宗即位，正拜司徒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fourth year Jingzong succeeded to the throne, and Guangyan was formally appointed Grand Preceptor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Jingzong took the throne and Guangyan was formally made Grand Preceptor.

sourceRange.text: 從諫自將作監主簿，起復雲麾將軍，守金吾衛大將軍同正、檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，充昭義節度副大使，知節度觀察等留後。二年，加金吾上將軍、檢校工部尚書，充昭義節度等使。文宗即位，進檢校司空。六年十二月入覲。七年春歸籓，加同中書門下平章事。九年，李訓事敗，宰相王涯等四人被禍。時涯兼掌邦計，雖不與李訓同謀，然不自異於其間，既死非其罪。從諫素德涯之私恩，心頗不平，四上章請涯等罪名，仇士良輩深憚之。是時中官頗橫，天子不能制。朝臣日憂陷族，賴從諫論列，而鄭覃、李石方能粗秉朝政。

context.beforeSource: 宰相李逢吉、中尉王守澄受其賂，曲為奏請。
context.afterSource: 先是，有蕭洪者，詐稱太后弟，因仇士良保任，許之厚賂。

manualTranslations.zh: 從諫自將作監主簿，起復雲麾將軍，守金吾衛大將軍同正、檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，充昭義節度副大使，知節度觀察等留後。
manualTranslations.literal: Congjian rose from Master Recorder in the Directorate for Palace Buildings; recalled from mourning as General of the Cloud-Banner Guard; appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant; concurrent Censor-in-Chief; deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi; and acting inspector of the circuit and related duties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Congjian was recalled from mourning from his post as Master Recorder in the Directorate for Palace Buildings, appointed General of the Cloud-Banner Guard, Acting Left Regular Attendant, and Censor-in-Chief, and made deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi with acting authority over the circuit and related duties.

manualTranslations.zh: 二年，加金吾上將軍、檢校工部尚書，充昭義節度等使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year he was given Senior General of the Golden Guard, Acting Minister of Works, and full military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Senior General of the Golden Guard, Acting Minister of Works, and full military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

manualTranslations.zh: 文宗即位，進檢校司空。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong acceded, he was advanced to Acting Sikong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Congjian was promoted to Acting Sikong.

manualTranslations.zh: 六年十二月入覲。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he came to audience.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he came to court.

manualTranslations.zh: 七年春歸籓，加同中書門下平章事。
manualTranslations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he returned to his post and was given Concurrent Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he returned to his command and was made Concurrent Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

manualTranslations.zh: 九年，李訓事敗，宰相王涯等四人被禍。
manualTranslations.literal: In the ninth year the Li Xun affair failed; Grand Councilor Wang Ya and three others met disaster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Li Xun plot failed, and Grand Councilor Wang Ya and three others were destroyed.

manualTranslations.zh: 時涯兼掌邦計，雖不與李訓同謀，然不自異於其間，既死非其罪。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time Wang Ya also oversaw state finance; though he had not conspired with Li Xun, he had not kept himself apart from the affair, and his death was not deserved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Ya was then also in charge of state finance. Though he had not plotted with Li Xun, he had not kept himself apart from the affair, and his execution was undeserved.

manualTranslations.zh: 從諫素德涯之私恩，心頗不平，四上章請涯等罪名，仇士良輩深憚之。
manualTranslations.literal: Congjian had long owed Wang Ya a personal debt of gratitude and was quite unsettled in mind; four times he submitted memorials asking what crimes Wang Ya and the others had committed; Qiu Shiliang and his faction deeply feared him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Congjian had long felt a personal debt to Wang Ya and was deeply troubled by the case. Four times he memorialized asking what crimes Wang Ya and the others had committed. Qiu Shiliang and his faction feared him greatly.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時中官頗橫，天子不能制。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time eunuch officials were quite overbearing and the emperor could not control them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuch officials were rampant, and the emperor could not restrain them.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝臣日憂陷族，賴從諫論列，而鄭覃、李石方能粗秉朝政。
manualTranslations.literal: Court officials daily feared the extermination of their clans; they relied on Congjian's forthright memorials, and only then could Zheng Tan and Li Shi roughly hold the reins of court governance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Court officials lived in daily fear that their entire clans would be wiped out. They depended on Congjian's outspoken memorials, and only then could Zheng Tan and Li Shi roughly hold the reins of government.

sourceRange.text: 稹自監察御史謫為江陵府士曹掾，翰林學士李絳、崔群上前面論稹無罪，居易累疏切諫曰：臣昨緣元稹左降，頻已奏聞。臣內察事情，外聽眾議，元稹左降有不可者三。何者？元稹守官正直，人所共知。自授御史已來，舉奏不避權勢，只如奏李佐公等事，多是朝廷親情。人誰無私，因以挾恨，或假公議，將報私嫌，遂使誣謗之聲，上聞天聽。臣恐元稹左降已後，凡在位者，每欲舉職，必先以稹為誡，無人肯為陛下當官守法，無人肯為陛下嫉惡繩愆。內外權貴親黨，縱有大過大罪者，必相容隱而已，陛下從此無由得知。此其不可者一也。昨元稹所追勘房式之事，心雖徇公，事稍過當。既從重罰，足以懲違，況經謝恩，旋又左降。雖引前事以為責辭，然外議喧喧，皆以為稹與中使劉士元爭廳，因此獲罪。至於爭廳事理，已具前狀奏陳。況聞士元蹋破驛門，奪將鞍馬，仍索弓箭，嚇辱朝官，承前已來，未有此事。今中官有罪，未聞處置；御史無過，卻先貶官。遠近聞知，實損聖德。臣恐從今已後，中官出使，縱暴益甚；朝官受辱，必不敢言。縱有被淩辱毆打者，亦以元稹為戒，但吞聲而已。陛下從此無由得聞。此其不可二也。臣又訪聞元稹自去年已來，舉奏嚴礪在東川日枉法，沒入平人資產八十餘家；又奏王沼違法給券，令監軍押柩及家口入驛；又奏裴玢違敕征百姓草；又奏韓臯使軍將封杖打殺縣令。如此之事，前後甚多，屬朝廷法行，悉有懲罰。計天下方鎮，皆怒元稹守官。今貶為江陵判司，即是送與方鎮，從此方便報怨，朝廷何由得知？臣伏聞德宗時有崔善貞者，告李锜必反，德宗不信，送與李锜，锜掘坑熾火，燒殺善貞。曾未數年，李锜果反，至今天下為之痛心。臣恐元稹貶官，方鎮有過，無人敢言，陛下無由得知不法之事。此其不可者三也。若無此三不可，假如朝廷誤左降一御史，蓋是小事，臣安敢煩瀆聖聽，至於再三！誠以所損者深，所關者大，以此思慮，敢不極言！

context.beforeSource: 居易與河南元稹相善，同年登制舉，交情隆厚。

manualTranslations.zh: 臣昨緣元稹左降，頻已奏聞。
manualTranslations.literal: Yesterday this subject, on account of Yuan Zhen's demotion to a lower post, repeatedly submitted memorials to report it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yesterday, on account of Yuan Zhen's demotion, I repeatedly submitted memorials on the matter.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣內察事情，外聽眾議，元稹左降有不可者三。
manualTranslations.literal: This subject inwardly examined the matter and outwardly listened to public discussion; Yuan Zhen's demotion has three points that must not be allowed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Having examined the matter inwardly and listened to public discussion outwardly, I find three reasons Yuan Zhen's demotion must not stand.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: What are they?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What are they?

manualTranslations.zh: 元稹守官正直，人所共知。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan Zhen in holding office is upright; all men know it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Everyone knows that Yuan Zhen is upright in office.

manualTranslations.zh: 自授御史已來，舉奏不避權勢，只如奏李佐公等事，多是朝廷親情。
manualTranslations.literal: Since receiving appointment as censor, in impeachments and memorials he has not avoided power and influence; matters such as memorializing against Li Zuogong and others mostly involved court intimates and kin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since his appointment as censor, he has not shied from power and influence in his impeachments; cases such as his memorial against Li Zuogong and others mostly involved court intimates and kin.

manualTranslations.zh: 人誰無私，因以挾恨，或假公議，將報私嫌，遂使誣謗之聲，上聞天聽。
manualTranslations.literal: Who among men is without private feeling? Accordingly they harbor resentment, or borrow public discussion to repay private grudges, so that slanderous voices reach the imperial ear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who is without private feeling? Resentment has been harbored; public discussion has been borrowed to settle private grudges, and slander has reached Your Majesty's ears.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣恐元稹左降已後，凡在位者，每欲舉職，必先以稹為誡，無人肯為陛下當官守法，無人肯為陛下嫉惡繩愆。
manualTranslations.literal: This subject fears that after Yuan Zhen's demotion, all who hold office, whenever they wish to perform their duties, will first take Zhen as a warning; no one will be willing to hold office and uphold the law for Your Majesty, no one willing to hate evil and restrain transgression for Your Majesty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I fear that after Zhen's demotion, every official who wishes to perform his duties will first take him as a warning; no one will be willing to hold office and uphold the law for you, or to hate evil and restrain wrongdoing on your behalf.

manualTranslations.zh: 內外權貴親黨，縱有大過大罪者，必相容隱而已，陛下從此無由得知。
manualTranslations.literal: Inside and outside, powerful nobles and their kin, even if they have great faults and great crimes, will only cover and conceal one another; Your Majesty from this will have no means of learning of it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Powerful nobles and their kin, inside and outside the court, will only cover for one another no matter how grave their faults; from this you will have no way to learn of them.

manualTranslations.zh: 此其不可者一也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is the first point that must not be allowed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is the first reason it must not stand.

manualTranslations.zh: 昨元稹所追勘房式之事，心雖徇公，事稍過當。
manualTranslations.literal: Yesterday, in the matter of Fang Shi that Yuan Zhen pursued and investigated, though his heart followed public duty, the affair was somewhat excessive.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In yesterday's matter of Fang Shi, which Zhen pursued and investigated, his heart followed public duty, but the affair was somewhat excessive.

manualTranslations.zh: 既從重罰，足以懲違，況經謝恩，旋又左降。
manualTranslations.literal: He has already received heavy punishment, sufficient to chastise transgression; moreover he had already thanked for imperial grace, yet was again demoted to a lower post.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He has already received heavy punishment, enough to chastise the offense; moreover, he had already thanked you for imperial grace, yet was again demoted.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖引前事以為責辭，然外議喧喧，皆以為稹與中使劉士元爭廳，因此獲罪。
manualTranslations.literal: Although earlier matters were cited as grounds for reproach, yet outside discussion is clamorous, all holding that Zhen quarreled with the palace envoy Liu Shiyuan over quarters and for this received punishment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Although earlier matters were cited as grounds for reproach, public talk is loud: all believe Zhen was punished because he quarreled with the palace envoy Liu Shiyuan over quarters.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於爭廳事理，已具前狀奏陳。
manualTranslations.literal: As for the rights and wrongs of the quarrel over quarters, they have already been fully set forth in the previous memorial.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rights and wrongs of the quarrel over quarters have already been fully set forth in my previous memorial.

manualTranslations.zh: 況聞士元蹋破驛門，奪將鞍馬，仍索弓箭，嚇辱朝官，承前已來，未有此事。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover one hears that Shiyuan kicked through the relay station gate, seized a general's saddle and horse, and still demanded bow and arrows, terrifying and insulting court officials; from former times until now there has never been such a thing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover I have heard that Shiyuan kicked through the relay station gate, seized a general's saddle and horse, and still demanded bow and arrows, terrifying and insulting court officials; nothing like this has ever occurred before.

manualTranslations.zh: 今中官有罪，未聞處置；
manualTranslations.literal: Now the palace official has guilt, yet no disposition has been heard of;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the palace official is guilty, yet no punishment has been heard of;

manualTranslations.zh: 御史無過，卻先貶官。
manualTranslations.literal: the censor is without fault, yet was first demoted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: yet the censor, though without fault, was demoted first.

manualTranslations.zh: 遠近聞知，實損聖德。
manualTranslations.literal: Near and far, on hearing of it, it truly damages sagely virtue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Near and far, all who hear of it know that it truly damages your sagely virtue.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣恐從今已後，中官出使，縱暴益甚；
manualTranslations.literal: This subject fears that from now on, when palace officials go on missions, unrestrained violence will grow still worse;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I fear that from now on, when palace officials go on missions, unrestrained violence will grow still worse;

manualTranslations.zh: 朝官受辱，必不敢言。
manualTranslations.literal: court officials who suffer insult will certainly not dare to speak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: court officials who suffer insult will certainly not dare to speak out.

manualTranslations.zh: 縱有被淩辱毆打者，亦以元稹為戒，但吞聲而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Even if there are those who are insulted and beaten, they too will take Yuan Zhen as a warning and only swallow their voices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Even those who are insulted and beaten will take Zhen as a warning and only swallow their voices.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下從此無由得聞。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty from this will have no means of hearing of it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this you will have no way to hear of it.

manualTranslations.zh: 此其不可二也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is the second point that must not be allowed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is the second reason it must not stand.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣又訪聞元稹自去年已來，舉奏嚴礪在東川日枉法，沒入平人資產八十餘家；
manualTranslations.literal: This subject has also inquired and heard that since last year Yuan Zhen has memorialized that Yan Li, during his days in eastern Shu, violated the law and confiscated the property of more than eighty households of common people;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have also learned that since last year Zhen has memorialized that Yan Li, during his days in eastern Shu, violated the law and confiscated the property of more than eighty common households;

manualTranslations.zh: 又奏王沼違法給券，令監軍押柩及家口入驛；
manualTranslations.literal: he also memorialized that Wang Zhao illegally issued passes, ordering the military supervisor to escort the coffin and household members into the relay station;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: he also memorialized that Wang Zhao illegally issued passes, ordering the military supervisor to escort the coffin and household members into the relay station;

manualTranslations.zh: 又奏裴玢違敕征百姓草；
manualTranslations.literal: he also memorialized that Pei Bin violated an imperial order in levying fodder from the common people;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: he also memorialized that Pei Bin violated an imperial order in levying fodder from the common people;

manualTranslations.zh: 又奏韓臯使軍將封杖打殺縣令。
manualTranslations.literal: he also memorialized that Han Gao had a military officer beat the county magistrate to death with a sealed staff.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: he also memorialized that Han Gao had a military officer beat the county magistrate to death with a sealed staff.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此之事，前後甚多，屬朝廷法行，悉有懲罰。
manualTranslations.literal: Matters such as these, before and after, are very numerous; when the court's law was applied, all received punishment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Such matters are very numerous; when the court applied the law, all received punishment.

manualTranslations.zh: 計天下方鎮，皆怒元稹守官。
manualTranslations.literal: Considering it, the military governors throughout the realm are all angry at Yuan Zhen for upholding office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I reckon that the military governors throughout the realm are all angry at Zhen for upholding his office.

manualTranslations.zh: 今貶為江陵判司，即是送與方鎮，從此方便報怨，朝廷何由得知？
manualTranslations.literal: Now demoted to judicial adjutant at Jiangling, this is in effect delivering him to the military governors; from this they will conveniently repay their grudges—how is the court to learn of it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now that he is demoted to judicial adjutant at Jiangling, he is in effect delivered to the military governors; from this they can conveniently settle their grudges—how is the court to learn of it?

manualTranslations.zh: 臣伏聞德宗時有崔善貞者，告李锜必反，德宗不信，送與李锜，锜掘坑熾火，燒殺善貞。
manualTranslations.literal: This subject humbly has heard that in the time of Emperor Dezong there was one Cui Shanzhen who reported that Li Qi would certainly rebel; Dezong did not believe him and sent him to Li Qi, and Qi dug a pit, kindled a fire, and burned Shanzhen to death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly recall that in Emperor Dezong's time Cui Shanzhen reported that Li Qi would certainly rebel; Dezong did not believe him and sent him to Li Qi, who dug a pit, kindled a fire, and burned Shanzhen to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 曾未數年，李锜果反，至今天下為之痛心。
manualTranslations.literal: Before several years had passed, Li Qi did in fact rebel; to this day all under Heaven grieves over it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within a few years Li Qi did rebel; to this day the realm grieves over it.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣恐元稹貶官，方鎮有過，無人敢言，陛下無由得知不法之事。
manualTranslations.literal: This subject fears that with Yuan Zhen demoted, when military governors have faults no one will dare to speak, and Your Majesty will have no means of learning of unlawful matters.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I fear that with Zhen demoted, when military governors commit faults no one will dare speak, and you will have no way to learn of unlawful conduct.

manualTranslations.zh: 此其不可者三也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is the third point that must not be allowed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is the third reason it must not stand.

manualTranslations.zh: 若無此三不可，假如朝廷誤左降一御史，蓋是小事，臣安敢煩瀆聖聽，至於再三！
manualTranslations.literal: If there were not these three points that must not be allowed, supposing the court mistakenly demoted one censor to a lower post, it would merely be a small matter—how would this subject dare to trouble and offend the imperial ear, even to the point of repeating it again and again!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Were it not for these three reasons, a mistaken demotion of one censor would be a small matter—how would I dare trouble your imperial ear again and again!

manualTranslations.zh: 誠以所損者深，所關者大，以此思慮，敢不極言！
manualTranslations.literal: Truly because what is harmed is deep and what is involved is great, with this in mind, how would I not dare speak to the utmost!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Truly, because the harm is deep and the stakes are great, with this in mind I cannot but speak to the utmost!

sourceRange.text: 稹長慶末因編刪其文稿，《自敘》曰：劉歆云：制不可削。予以為有可得而削之者，貢謀猷，持嗜欲，君有之則譽歸於上，臣專之則譽歸於下。茍而存之，其攘也，非道也。經制度，明利害，區邪正，辨嫌惑，存之則事分著，去之則是非冺。茍而削之，其過也，非道也。元和初，章武皇帝新即位，臣下未有以言刮視聽者。予時始以對詔在拾遺中供奉，由是獻《教本書》、《諫職》、《論事》等表十數通，仍為裴度、李正辭、韋熏訟所言當，而宰相曲道上語。上頗悟，召見問狀。宰相大惡之，不一月，出為河南尉。後累歲，補御史，使東川。謹以元和赦書，劾節度使嚴礪籍塗山甫等八十八家，過賦梓、遂之民數百萬。朝廷異之，奪七刺史料，悉以所籍歸於人。會潘孟陽代礪為節度使，貪過礪，且有所承迎，雖不敢盡廢詔，因命當得所籍者皆入資。資過其稱，榷薪盜賦無不為，仍為礪密狀不當得醜謚。予自東川還，朋礪者潛切齒矣。無何，分蒞東都臺。天子久不在都，都下多不法者。百司皆牢獄，有裁接吏械人逾歲而臺府不得而知之者，予因飛奏絕百司專禁錮。河南尉判官，予劾之，忤宰相旨。監徐使死於軍，徐帥郵傳其柩，柩至洛，其下歐詬主郵吏，予命吏徙柩於外，不得復乘傳。浙西觀察使封杖決安吉令至死；河南尹誣奏書生尹太階請死之；飛龍使誘趙寔家逃奴為養子；田季安盜娶洛陽衣冠女；汴州沒入死商錢且千萬；滑州賦於民以千，授於人以八百；朝廷饋東師，主計者誤命牛車四千三百乘飛芻越太行。類是數十事，或移或奏，皆主之。貞元已來，不慣用文法，內外寵臣皆喑嗚。會河南尹房式詐諼事發，奏攝之。前所喑嗚者叫噪。宰相素以劾叛官事相銜，乘是黜予江陵掾。後十年，始為膳部員外郎。穆宗初，宰相更相用事，丞相段公一日獨得對，因請亟用兵部郎中薛存慶、考功員外郎牛僧孺，予亦在請中，上然之。不十數日次用為給、舍，他忿恨者日夜構飛語，予懼罪，比上書自明。上憐之，三召與語。語及兵賦洎西北邊事，因命經紀之。是後書奏及進見，皆言天下事，外間不知，多臆度。陛下益憐其不漏禁中語，召入禁林，且欲亟用為宰相。是時裴度在太原，亦有宰相望，巧者謀欲俱廢之，乃以予所無構於裴。裴奏至，驗之皆失實。上以裴方握兵，不欲校曲直，出予為工部侍郎，而相裴之期亦衰矣。不累月，上盡得所構者，雖不能暴揚之，遂果初意，卒用予與裴俱為宰相。復有購狂民告予借客刺裴者，鞫之復無狀，而裴與予以故俱罷免。始元和十五年八月得見上，至是未二歲，僭忝恩寵，無是之速者；遭罹謗咎，亦無是之甚者。是以心腹腎腸，糜費於扶衛危亡之不暇，又惡暇經紀陛下之所付哉！然而造次顛沛之中，前後列上兵賦邊防之狀，可得而存者一百一十五。茍而削之，是傷先帝之器使也。至於陳暢辨謗之章，去之則無以自明於朋友矣。其餘郡縣之奏請，賀慶之禮，因亦附於件目。始《教本書》，至於為人雜奏，二十有七軸，凡二百二十有七奏。終歿吾世，貽之子孫式，所以明經制之難行，而銷毀之易至也。

manualTranslations.zh: 稹長慶末因編刪其文稿，《自敘》曰：劉歆云：制不可削。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of the Changqing era Zhen edited and abridged his collected writings; his "Self-Account" read: Liu Xin said: Institutions must not be cut away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end of the Changqing era he edited and abridged his collected writings; his "Self-Account" read: Liu Xin said: Institutions must not be cut away.

manualTranslations.zh: 予以為有可得而削之者，貢謀猷，持嗜欲，君有之則譽歸於上，臣專之則譽歸於下。
manualTranslations.literal: I believe there are some that may be cut away: presenting plans and counsel, restraining appetites and desires—if the ruler possesses them, praise returns to the sovereign; if ministers monopolize them, praise returns to those below.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I believe there are some that may be cut away: presenting plans and counsel, restraining appetites and desires—if the ruler possesses them, praise returns to the sovereign; if ministers monopolize them, praise returns to those below.

manualTranslations.zh: 茍而存之，其攘也，非道也。
manualTranslations.literal: If they are kept, their usurpation is not the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they are kept, their usurpation is not the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 經制度，明利害，區邪正，辨嫌惑，存之則事分著，去之則是非冺。
manualTranslations.literal: Passing through institutions, clarifying benefit and harm, distinguishing the wicked and upright, discerning suspicion and confusion—if kept, affairs are divided and clear; if removed, right and wrong are obscured.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Passing through institutions, clarifying benefit and harm, distinguishing the wicked and upright, discerning suspicion and confusion—if kept, affairs are divided and clear; if removed, right and wrong are obscured.

manualTranslations.zh: 茍而削之，其過也，非道也。
manualTranslations.literal: If they are cut away, the fault is not the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they are cut away, the fault is not the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 元和初，章武皇帝新即位，臣下未有以言刮視聽者。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, Emperor Muzong had newly ascended the throne, and among his subjects none yet spoke to cleanse his sight and hearing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe, Emperor Muzong had newly ascended the throne, and among his subjects none yet spoke to cleanse his sight and hearing.

manualTranslations.zh: 予時始以對詔在拾遺中供奉，由是獻《教本書》、《諫職》、《論事》等表十數通，仍為裴度、李正辭、韋熏訟所言當，而宰相曲道上語。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time I had just entered service among the remonstrance officials by imperial examination response, and thereby presented more than ten memorials including the Book on Foundations of Instruction, On the Duties of Remonstrance, and On Affairs; I also joined Pei Du, Li Zhengchen, and Wei Xun in litigation over what was said to be correct, while the chancellor twisted the way and reported upward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time I had just entered service among the remonstrance officials by imperial examination response, and thereby presented more than ten memorials including the Book on Foundations of Instruction, On the Duties of Remonstrance, and On Affairs; I also joined Pei Du, Li Zhengchen, and Wei Xun in litigation over what was said to be correct, while the chancellor twisted the matter and reported upward.

manualTranslations.zh: 上頗悟，召見問狀。
manualTranslations.literal: The sovereign was somewhat enlightened and summoned me to audience to inquire into the matter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sovereign was somewhat enlightened and summoned me to audience to inquire into the matter.

manualTranslations.zh: 宰相大惡之，不一月，出為河南尉。
manualTranslations.literal: The chancellor greatly hated this; within a month I was sent out as marshal of Henan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The chancellor greatly hated this; within a month I was sent out as marshal of Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 後累歲，補御史，使東川。
manualTranslations.literal: After several years I was appointed censor and dispatched to Dongchuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After several years I was appointed censor and dispatched to Dongchuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 謹以元和赦書，劾節度使嚴礪籍塗山甫等八十八家，過賦梓、遂之民數百萬。
manualTranslations.literal: In accordance with the Yuanhe amnesty edict, I impeached the military governor Yan Li for confiscating the property of Tu Shanfu and eighty-seven other households, over-taxing the people of Zi and Sui by several million.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In accordance with the Yuanhe amnesty edict, I impeached the military governor Yan Li for confiscating the property of Tu Shanfu and eighty-seven other households, over-taxing the people of Zi and Sui by several million.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷異之，奪七刺史料，悉以所籍歸於人。
manualTranslations.literal: The court was astonished, stripped him of seven grades of censorial authority, and returned all confiscated property to the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court was astonished, stripped him of seven grades of censorial authority, and returned all confiscated property to the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 會潘孟陽代礪為節度使，貪過礪，且有所承迎，雖不敢盡廢詔，因命當得所籍者皆入資。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that Pan Mengyang replaced Yan Li as military governor; he was greedier than Yan Li and moreover sought to curry favor. Though he did not dare wholly abolish the edict, he therefore ordered that all who should have received confiscated property must pay a fee to enter it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It happened that Pan Mengyang replaced Yan Li as military governor; he was greedier than Yan Li and moreover sought to curry favor. Though he did not dare wholly abolish the edict, he therefore ordered that all who should have received confiscated property must pay a fee to obtain it.

manualTranslations.zh: 資過其稱，榷薪盜賦無不為，仍為礪密狀不當得醜謚。
manualTranslations.literal: The fees exceeded their worth; monopolizing firewood and theft of taxes—nothing was left undone. He also submitted a secret memorial on Yan Li's behalf that he ought not receive an ugly posthumous title.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The fees exceeded their worth; he monopolized firewood and stole taxes—nothing was left undone. He also submitted a secret memorial on Yan Li's behalf that he ought not receive a disgraceful posthumous title.

manualTranslations.zh: 予自東川還，朋礪者潛切齒矣。
manualTranslations.literal: When I returned from Dongchuan, Yan Li's partisans secretly ground their teeth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When I returned from Dongchuan, Yan Li's partisans secretly ground their teeth in hatred.

manualTranslations.zh: 無何，分蒞東都臺。
manualTranslations.literal: Before long I was assigned to oversee the Eastern Capital Censorate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before long I was assigned to oversee the Eastern Capital Censorate.

manualTranslations.zh: 天子久不在都，都下多不法者。
manualTranslations.literal: The Son of Heaven had long been absent from the capital, and under the capital there were many lawless men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven had long been absent from the capital, and in the capital there were many lawless men.

manualTranslations.zh: 百司皆牢獄，有裁接吏械人逾歲而臺府不得而知之者，予因飛奏絕百司專禁錮。
manualTranslations.literal: Every office was a prison; there were receiving clerks who shackled men for more than a year while the censorate could not know of it. I therefore submitted an urgent memorial to forbid every office from exclusive imprisonment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Every office was a prison; there were receiving clerks who shackled men for more than a year while the censorate could not know of it. I therefore submitted an urgent memorial to forbid every office from exclusive imprisonment.

manualTranslations.zh: 河南尉判官，予劾之，忤宰相旨。
manualTranslations.literal: The Henan marshal's aide—I impeached him, offending the chancellor's intent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I impeached the Henan marshal's aide, offending the chancellor's intent.

manualTranslations.zh: 監徐使死於軍，徐帥郵傳其柩，柩至洛，其下歐詬主郵吏，予命吏徙柩於外，不得復乘傳。
manualTranslations.literal: The supervisory commissioner of Xu died in the army; the Xu commander sent his coffin by post relay. When the coffin reached Luoyang, his subordinates beat and reviled the chief postal clerk. I ordered the clerks to move the coffin outside and forbade further use of post relay.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The supervisory commissioner of Xu died in the army; the Xu commander sent his coffin by post relay. When the coffin reached Luoyang, his subordinates beat and reviled the chief postal clerk. I ordered the clerks to move the coffin outside and forbade further use of post relay.

manualTranslations.zh: 浙西觀察使封杖決安吉令至死；
manualTranslations.literal: The Zhexi observation commissioner sealed a staff and adjudged the magistrate of Anji to death;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Zhexi observation commissioner sealed a staff and adjudged the magistrate of Anji to death;

manualTranslations.zh: 河南尹誣奏書生尹太階請死之；
manualTranslations.literal: the Henan governor falsely memorialized that the scholar Yin Taijie requested death;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the Henan governor falsely memorialized that the scholar Yin Taijie requested death;

manualTranslations.zh: 飛龍使誘趙寔家逃奴為養子；
manualTranslations.literal: the Feilong commissioner enticed a runaway slave of Zhao Shi's household to become an adopted son;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the Feilong commissioner enticed a runaway slave of Zhao Shi's household to become an adopted son;

manualTranslations.zh: 田季安盜娶洛陽衣冠女；
manualTranslations.literal: Tian Ji'an secretly married a genteel woman of Luoyang;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tian Ji'an secretly married a genteel woman of Luoyang;

manualTranslations.zh: 汴州沒入死商錢且千萬；
manualTranslations.literal: Bian Prefecture confiscated the money of a dead merchant, nearly ten million;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Bian Prefecture confiscated the money of a dead merchant, nearly ten million;

manualTranslations.zh: 滑州賦於民以千，授於人以八百；
manualTranslations.literal: Hua Prefecture levied a thousand from the people and handed over eight hundred to others;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hua Prefecture levied a thousand from the people and handed over only eight hundred;

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷饋東師，主計者誤命牛車四千三百乘飛芻越太行。
manualTranslations.literal: the court supplied the eastern army; the chief accountant mistakenly ordered four thousand three hundred ox carts to fly fodder over the Taihang Mountains.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the court supplied the eastern army; the chief accountant mistakenly ordered four thousand three hundred ox carts to rush fodder over the Taihang Mountains.

manualTranslations.zh: 類是數十事，或移或奏，皆主之。
manualTranslations.literal: Matters like these numbered in the dozens; whether by dispatch or memorial, I took charge of them all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Matters like these numbered in the dozens; whether by dispatch or memorial, I took charge of them all.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞元已來，不慣用文法，內外寵臣皆喑嗚。
manualTranslations.literal: Since the Zhenyuan era, people were unaccustomed to using written law; favored ministers within and without all roared and clamored.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenyuan era, people were unaccustomed to using written law; favored ministers within and without all roared and clamored.

manualTranslations.zh: 會河南尹房式詐諼事發，奏攝之。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that the Henan governor Fang Shi's fraud and false accusation came to light; I memorialized to take him into custody.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It happened that the Henan governor Fang Shi's fraud and false accusation came to light; I memorialized to take him into custody.

manualTranslations.zh: 前所喑嗚者叫噪。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who had previously roared and clamored now shouted and made an uproar.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who had previously roared and clamored now shouted and made an uproar.

manualTranslations.zh: 宰相素以劾叛官事相銜，乘是黜予江陵掾。
manualTranslations.literal: The chancellor had long harbored resentment over my impeachment of a rebellious official; seizing this opportunity he dismissed me to aide in Jiangling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The chancellor had long harbored resentment over my impeachment of a rebellious official; seizing this opportunity he dismissed me to aide in Jiangling.

manualTranslations.zh: 後十年，始為膳部員外郎。
manualTranslations.literal: After ten years I was at last made vice director of the Board of Appointments.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After ten years I was at last made vice director of the Board of Appointments.

manualTranslations.zh: 穆宗初，宰相更相用事，丞相段公一日獨得對，因請亟用兵部郎中薛存慶、考功員外郎牛僧孺，予亦在請中，上然之。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Muzong's reign, chancellors alternated in wielding power. Chancellor Duan Wenchang one day alone obtained audience and thereupon requested the prompt use of Xue Cunqing, director of the Ministry of War, and Niu Sengru, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel examinations—I was also among those requested, and the sovereign approved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Muzong's reign, chancellors alternated in wielding power. Chancellor Duan Wenchang one day alone obtained audience and thereupon requested the prompt appointment of Xue Cunqing, director of the Ministry of War, and Niu Sengru, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel examinations—I was also among those requested, and the sovereign approved.

manualTranslations.zh: 不十數日次用為給、舍，他忿恨者日夜構飛語，予懼罪，比上書自明。
manualTranslations.literal: Within less than ten days I was next appointed drafting and palace aide; others who resented me day and night fabricated flying rumors. I feared punishment and repeatedly submitted memorials to clarify myself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within less than ten days I was next appointed drafting and palace aide; others who resented me day and night fabricated flying rumors. I feared punishment and repeatedly submitted memorials to clarify myself.

manualTranslations.zh: 上憐之，三召與語。
manualTranslations.literal: The sovereign pitied me and thrice summoned me to speak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sovereign pitied me and thrice summoned me to speak.

manualTranslations.zh: 語及兵賦洎西北邊事，因命經紀之。
manualTranslations.literal: Our conversation reached military levies and northwestern border affairs, and he thereupon ordered me to manage them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Our conversation reached military levies and northwestern border affairs, and he thereupon ordered me to manage them.

manualTranslations.zh: 是後書奏及進見，皆言天下事，外間不知，多臆度。
manualTranslations.literal: After this, in written memorials and audiences I spoke of affairs under Heaven; those outside did not know and mostly speculated.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After this, in written memorials and audiences I spoke of affairs under Heaven; those outside did not know and mostly speculated.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下益憐其不漏禁中語，召入禁林，且欲亟用為宰相。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty all the more pitied that I did not leak palace talk, summoned me into the forbidden grove, and wished to promptly use me as chancellor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty all the more valued that I did not leak palace talk, summoned me into the Hanlin Academy, and wished to promptly appoint me chancellor.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時裴度在太原，亦有宰相望，巧者謀欲俱廢之，乃以予所無構於裴。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Pei Du was in Taiyuan and also had prospects of chancellorship; the crafty plotted to abolish both together and therefore fabricated against Pei what I did not have.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Du was in Taiyuan and also had prospects of chancellorship; the crafty plotted to abolish both together and therefore fabricated against Pei charges that I had not made.

manualTranslations.zh: 裴奏至，驗之皆失實。
manualTranslations.literal: Pei's memorial arrived; upon verification all was untrue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pei's memorial arrived; upon verification all was untrue.

manualTranslations.zh: 上以裴方握兵，不欲校曲直，出予為工部侍郎，而相裴之期亦衰矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The sovereign, because Pei was then holding troops, did not wish to judge right and wrong, and sent me out as vice minister of works; the prospect of Pei becoming chancellor also faded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sovereign, because Pei was then holding troops, did not wish to judge right and wrong, and sent me out as vice minister of works; the prospect of Pei becoming chancellor also faded.

manualTranslations.zh: 不累月，上盡得所構者，雖不能暴揚之，遂果初意，卒用予與裴俱為宰相。
manualTranslations.literal: Within not many months the sovereign fully obtained those who had fabricated; though he could not publicly expose them, he then fulfilled his original intent and in the end used both me and Pei as chancellors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within not many months the sovereign fully obtained those who had fabricated; though he could not publicly expose them, he then fulfilled his original intent and in the end appointed both me and Pei as chancellors.

manualTranslations.zh: 復有購狂民告予借客刺裴者，鞫之復無狀，而裴與予以故俱罷免。
manualTranslations.literal: Again there was one who bribed a mad commoner to report that I had borrowed a guest to assassinate Pei; upon interrogation again there was no substance, yet Pei and I were both dismissed for the old matter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again someone bribed a mad commoner to report that I had borrowed a guest to assassinate Pei; upon interrogation again there was no substance, yet Pei and I were both dismissed for the old matter.

manualTranslations.zh: 始元和十五年八月得見上，至是未二歲，僭忝恩寵，無是之速者；
manualTranslations.literal: From first seeing the sovereign in the eighth month of Yuanhe 15 to this time was not yet two years; presumptuously receiving favor and grace, none was so swift;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From first seeing the sovereign in the eighth month of Yuanhe 15 to this time was not yet two years; presumptuously receiving favor and grace, none was so swift;

manualTranslations.zh: 遭罹謗咎，亦無是之甚者。
manualTranslations.literal: suffering slander and blame, none was so severe.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: suffering slander and blame, none was so severe.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以心腹腎腸，糜費於扶衛危亡之不暇，又惡暇經紀陛下之所付哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Thus heart, belly, kidneys, and bowels were wasted on supporting and defending in peril of destruction with no leisure—how could there be leisure to manage what Your Majesty entrusted!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus heart and soul were consumed supporting and defending in peril of destruction with no leisure—how could there be leisure to manage what Your Majesty entrusted!

manualTranslations.zh: 然而造次顛沛之中，前後列上兵賦邊防之狀，可得而存者一百一十五。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet amid haste and hardship, the military levy and border defense reports submitted before and after, of which copies can be preserved, number one hundred fifteen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet amid haste and hardship, the military levy and border defense reports submitted before and after, of which copies can be preserved, number one hundred fifteen.

manualTranslations.zh: 茍而削之，是傷先帝之器使也。
manualTranslations.literal: If they are cut away, this wounds the late emperor's employment of his vessel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they are cut away, this wounds the late emperor's employment of his servant.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於陳暢辨謗之章，去之則無以自明於朋友矣。
manualTranslations.literal: As for the chapters clarifying slander in full expression, if removed there would be no means to clarify myself before friends.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for the chapters clarifying slander in full expression, if removed there would be no means to clarify myself before friends.

manualTranslations.zh: 其餘郡縣之奏請，賀慶之禮，因亦附於件目。
manualTranslations.literal: The rest—county and prefecture memorials and requests, congratulatory rites—are also appended to the list of items.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rest—county and prefecture memorials and requests, congratulatory rites—are also appended to the list of items.

manualTranslations.zh: 始《教本書》，至於為人雜奏，二十有七軸，凡二百二十有七奏。
manualTranslations.literal: From the Book on Foundations of Instruction to miscellaneous memorials on behalf of others, there are twenty-seven scrolls, altogether two hundred twenty-seven memorials.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the Book on Foundations of Instruction to miscellaneous memorials on behalf of others, there are twenty-seven scrolls, altogether two hundred twenty-seven memorials.

manualTranslations.zh: 終歿吾世，貽之子孫式，所以明經制之難行，而銷毀之易至也。
manualTranslations.literal: To the end of my life and death I bequeath them to descendants as a model, thereby making clear how hard institutions are to carry out and how easily destruction arrives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To the end of my life I bequeath them to descendants as a model, thereby making clear how hard institutions are to carry out and how easily destruction arrives.

sourceRange.text: 乃獻《教本書》曰：臣伏見陛下降明詔，修廢學，增胄子，選司成。大哉，堯之為君，伯夷典禮，夔教胄子之深旨也！然而事有萬萬於此者，臣敢冒昧殊死而言之。臣聞諸賈生曰：「三代之君，仁且久者，教之然也。」誠哉是言！且夫周成王，人之中才也，近管、蔡則讒入，有周、召則義聞，豈可謂天聰明哉？然而克終於道者，得不謂教之然耶？俾伯禽、唐叔與之遊，《禮》、《樂》、《詩》、《書》為之習，目不得閱淫艷妖誘之色，耳不得聞優笑淩亂之音，口不得習操斷擊博之書，居不得近容順陰邪之黨，遊不得縱追禽逐獸之樂，玩不得有遐異僻絕之珍。凡此數者，非謂備之於前而不為也，亦將不得見之矣。及其長而為君也，血氣既定，遊習既成，雖有放心快己之事日陳於前，固不能奪已成之習、已定之心矣。則彼忠直道德之言，固吾之所習聞也，陳之者有以諭焉；彼庸佞違道之說，固吾之所積懼也，諂之者有以辨焉。人之情，莫不欲耀其所能而黨其所近；茍將得志，則必快其所蘊矣。物之性亦然。是以魚得水而遊，馬逸駕而走，鳥得風而翔，火得薪而熾。此皆物之快其所蘊也。今夫成王所蘊道德也，所近聖賢也。是以舉其近，則周公左而召公右，伯禽魯而太公齊。快其蘊，則興禮樂而朝諸侯，措刑罰而美教化。教之至也，可不謂信然哉！及夫秦則不然。滅先王之學，曰將以愚天下；黜師保之位，曰將以明君臣。胡亥之生也，《詩》、《書》不得聞，聖賢不得近。彼趙高者，詐宦之戮人也；而傅之以殘忍戕賊之術，且曰恣睢天下以為貴，莫見其面以為尊。是以天下之人人未盡愚，而胡亥固已不能分獸畜矣。趙高之威懾天下，而胡亥固已自幽於深宮矣。彼李斯，秦之寵丞相也。因讒冤死，無所自明，而況於疏遠之臣庶乎！若然，則秦之亡有以致之也。漢高承之以兵革，漢文守之以廉謹，卒不能蘇復大訓。是以景、武、昭、宣，天資甚美，才可以免禍亂；哀、平之間，則不能虞篡弒矣。然而惠帝廢易之際，猶賴羽翼以勝邪心。是後有國之君，議教化者，莫不以興廉舉孝、設學崇儒為意，曾不知教化之不行，自貴始。略其貴者，教其賤者，無乃鄰於倒置乎？洎我太宗文皇帝之在籓邸，以至於為太子也，選知道德者十八人與之遊習。即位之後，雖遊宴飲食之間，若十八人者，實在其中。上失無不言，下情無不達。不四三年而名高盛古，豈一日二日而致是乎？遊習之漸也！貞觀已還，師傅皆宰相兼領，其餘宮僚，亦甚重焉。馬周以位高恨不得為司議郎，此其驗也。文皇之後，漸疏賤之。用至母後臨朝，翦棄王室。當中、睿二聖勤勞之際，雖有骨鯁敢言之士，既不得在調護保安之職，終不能吐扶衛之一辭。而令醫匠安金藏剖腹以明之，豈不大哀也耶？兵興已來，茲弊尤甚。師資保傅之官，非疾廢眊聵不任事者為之，即休戎罷帥不知書者處之。至於友諭贊議之徒，疏冗散賤之甚者，縉紳恥由之。夫以匹士之愛其子者，猶求明哲慈惠之師以教之，直諒多聞之友以成之。豈天下之元良，而可以疾廢眊聵不知書者為之師乎？疏冗散賤不適用者為之友乎？此何不及上古之甚也！近制，宮僚之外，往往以沈滯僻老之儒，充侍直、侍讀之選，而又疏棄斥逐之，越月逾時，不得召見，彼又安能傅成道德而保養其身躬哉？臣以為積此弊者，豈不以皇天眷佑，祚我唐德，以舜繼堯，傳陛下十一聖矣，莫不生而神明，長而仁聖，以是為屑屑習儀者故不之省耳。臣獨以為於列聖之謀則可也，計傳後嗣則不可。脫或萬代之後，若有周成之中才，而又生於深宮優笑之間，無周、召保助之教，則將不能知喜怒哀樂之所自矣，況稼穡艱難乎？今陛下以上聖之資，肇臨海內，是天下之人傾耳註心之日。特願陛下思成王訓導之功，念文皇遊習之漸，選重師保，慎擇宮僚，皆用博厚弘深之儒，而又明達機務者為之。更相進見，日就月將。因令皇太子聚諸生，定齒胄講業之儀，行嚴師問道之禮。至德要道以成之，徹膳記過以警之。血氣未定，則去禽色之娛以就學；聖質已備，則資遊習之善以弘德。此所謂「一人元良，萬方以貞」之化也。豈直修廢學，選司成，而足倫匹其盛哉？而又俾則百王，莫不幼同師，長同術，識君道之素定，知天倫之自然，然後選用賢良，樹為籓屏。出則有晉、鄭、魯、衛之盛，入則有東牟、硃虛之強，蓋所謂宗子維城、犬牙盤石之勢也，又豈與夫魏、晉以降，囚賤其兄弟而自翦其本枝者，同年而語哉？

localRange.text: 乃獻《教本書》曰：

context.beforeSource: 是以訓導太子宮官，宜選正人。
context.afterSource: 憲宗覽之甚悅。
context.beforeLocal: 是以訓導太子宮官，宜選正人。
context.afterLocal: 憲宗覽之甚悅。
