manualTranslations.zh: 居易既以尹正罷歸，每獨酌賦詠於舟中，因為《池上篇》曰：東都風土水木之勝在東南偏，東南之勝在履道里，裏之勝在西北隅，西闬北垣第一第，即白氏叟樂天退老之地。
manualTranslations.literal: Juyi, having left office as capital intendant and returned home, would often drink alone and compose verses in his boat; he therefore wrote his "Essay on the Pool," which read: The excellence of the Eastern Capital's terrain, waters, and trees lies in the southeastern quarter; the excellence of the southeast lies in Lüdao Ward; the excellence within the ward lies in the northwest corner—the first residence at the western gate and northern wall, the place where the old gentleman of the Bai clan, Juyi, retired in old age.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After leaving office as capital intendant and returning home, he would often drink alone and compose verses in his boat; he therefore wrote his "Essay on the Pool," which read: In the Eastern Capital, the finest scenery of land and water lay in the southeast; the choicest part of the southeast was Lüdao Ward; and the choicest spot in the ward was the northwest corner—the first mansion on the western lane and northern wall, where the Bai clansman Juyi lived out his retirement.

manualTranslations.zh: 地方十七畝，屋室三之一，水五之一，竹九之一，而島樹橋道間之。
manualTranslations.literal: The grounds covered seventeen mu; buildings occupied one third, water one fifth, bamboo one ninth, and islands, trees, bridges, and paths were interspersed among them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The estate covered seventeen mu: a third in buildings, a fifth in water, a ninth in bamboo, with islands, trees, bridges, and paths distributed throughout.

manualTranslations.zh: 初樂天既為主，喜且曰：「雖有池臺，無粟不能守也」，乃作池東粟廩。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, once Juyi had become master of the place, he said with delight: "Though there are pools and terraces, without grain one cannot sustain them," and so built a grain storehouse east of the pool.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Juyi first took possession, he said happily, "Though one has pools and terraces, without grain one cannot keep them up," and built a granary east of the pool.

manualTranslations.zh: 又曰：「雖有子弟，無書不能訓也。」
manualTranslations.literal: He said again: "Though there are sons and younger kin, without books one cannot instruct them."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also said, "Though one has sons and kin, without books one cannot teach them."

manualTranslations.zh: 乃作池北書庫。
manualTranslations.literal: And so he built a book repository north of the pool.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and built a library north of the pool.

manualTranslations.zh: 又曰：「雖有賓朋，無琴酒不能娛也」，乃作池西琴亭，加石樽焉。
manualTranslations.literal: He said again: "Though there are guests and friends, without zither and wine one cannot enjoy oneself," and so built a zither pavilion west of the pool, adding stone wine jars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He added, "Though one has guests and friends, without zither and wine one cannot entertain," and built a zither pavilion west of the pool, with stone wine vessels added.

manualTranslations.zh: 樂天罷杭州刺史，得天竺石一、華亭鶴二以歸。
manualTranslations.literal: When Juyi left the post of prefect of Hangzhou, he obtained one stone from Tianzhu and two cranes from Huating and brought them home.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After leaving his post as prefect of Hangzhou, Juyi brought home one stone from Tianzhu and two cranes from Huating.

manualTranslations.zh: 始作西平橋，開環池路。
manualTranslations.literal: He then built the West Flat Bridge and opened the circuit road around the pool.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He then built West Flat Bridge and opened a circuit road around the pool.

manualTranslations.zh: 罷蘇州刺史時，得太湖石五、白蓮、折腰菱、青板舫以歸，又作中高橋，通三島逕。
manualTranslations.literal: When he left the post of prefect of Suzhou, he obtained five Lake Tai stones, white lotuses, waist-bent water chestnuts, and a blue-planked boat and brought them home; he also built the Middle High Bridge, linking a path to the three islands.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he left the prefecture of Suzhou, he returned with five Taihu stones, white lotuses, bent-neck water chestnuts, and a blue-planked boat, and built Middle High Bridge to connect a path to the three islands.

manualTranslations.zh: 罷刑部侍郎時，有粟千斛，書一車，洎臧獲之習管磬弦歌者指百以歸。
manualTranslations.literal: When he left the post of vice minister of justice, he had a thousand hu of grain, a cartload of books, and roughly a hundred servants trained in pipes, chimes, zithers, and song who returned with him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he stepped down as vice minister of justice, he had a thousand hu of grain, a cartload of books, and about a hundred household servants skilled in pipes, chimes, strings, and song.

manualTranslations.zh: 先是潁川陳孝仙與釀酒法，味甚佳；
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, Chen Xiaoxian of Yingchuan had given him a brewing method; the flavor was excellent;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Earlier Chen Xiaoxian of Yingchuan had taught him a brewing method of excellent flavor;

manualTranslations.zh: 博陵崔晦叔與琴，韻甚清；
manualTranslations.literal: Cui Huishu of Boling had given him a zither; its tone was very clear;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cui Huishu of Boling had given him a zither of very clear tone;

manualTranslations.zh: 蜀客姜發授《秋思》，聲甚淡；
manualTranslations.literal: the Shu guest Jiang Fa had taught him "Autumn Thoughts"; the sound was very subdued;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the Shu visitor Jiang Fa had taught him "Autumn Thoughts," its sound very subdued;

manualTranslations.zh: 弘農楊貞一與青石三，方長平滑，可以坐臥。
manualTranslations.literal: Yang Zhenyi of Hongnong had given him three blue stones, square, long, and smooth, on which one could sit or lie.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and Yang Zhenyi of Hongnong had given him three blue stones, square, long, and smooth enough to sit or lie upon.

manualTranslations.zh: 太和三年夏，樂天始得請為太子賓客，分秩於洛下，息躬於池上。
manualTranslations.literal: In summer of the third year of Taihe, Juyi first obtained permission to serve as guest of the heir apparent, took up his stipend at Luoyang, and rested his person at the pool.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of Taihe 3, Juyi was at last permitted to serve as guest of the heir apparent, drew his stipend at Luoyang, and rested at his poolside estate.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡三任所得，四人所與，洎吾不才身，今率為池中物。
manualTranslations.literal: Everything gained from three offices, given by four men, and extending to my unworthy person—all are now entirely possessions of the pool.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Everything accumulated across three offices, bestowed by four friends, together with my own unworthy self—all are now part of the pool estate.

manualTranslations.zh: 每至池風春，池月秋，水香蓮開之旦，露清鶴唳之夕，拂楊石，舉陳酒，援崔琴，彈《秋思》，頹然自適，不知其他。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever it was spring breezes over the pool, autumn moon on the pool, the morning of fragrant water and opening lotuses, or the evening of clear dew and crane cries, he would brush the Yang stones, raise Chen's wine, take up Cui's zither, play "Autumn Thoughts," and lapse contentedly into self-sufficiency, unaware of anything else.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever spring breezes stirred over the pool or autumn moonlight bathed it—on mornings when the water smelled sweet and lotuses opened, or evenings when dew lay clear and cranes called—he would brush the Yang stones, pour Chen's wine, take up Cui's zither, and play "Autumn Thoughts," sinking into contentment and forgetting everything else.

manualTranslations.zh: 酒酣琴罷，又命樂童登中島亭，含奏《霓裳散序》，聲隨風飄，或凝或散，悠揚於竹煙波月之際者久之。
manualTranslations.literal: When the wine was deep and the zither done, he would also command music youths to ascend Middle Island Pavilion and perform in ensemble the "Prelude to Rainbow Skirts"; the sound drifted with the wind, now gathering, now dispersing, lingering long amid bamboo, mist, waves, and moon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When wine ran deep and the zither fell silent, he would have young musicians climb Middle Island Pavilion to perform the "Prelude to Rainbow Skirts"; the sound drifted on the wind, now lingering, now scattering, rising and falling long among bamboo, mist, waves, and moonlight.

manualTranslations.zh: 曲未竟，而樂天陶然石上矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Before the piece was finished, Juyi was already blissfully drowsing on the stones.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before the piece ended, Juyi had already drifted contentedly asleep on the stones.

manualTranslations.zh: 睡起偶詠，非詩非賦，阿龜握筆，因題石間。
manualTranslations.literal: Waking from sleep he chanted casually; it was neither poem nor fu; A'gui took the brush and inscribed it among the stones.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On waking he improvised a piece—neither quite poem nor prose—and A'gui took up the brush and inscribed it on the stones.

manualTranslations.zh: 視其粗成韻章，命為《池上篇》云：十畝之宅，五畝之園，有水一池，有竹千竿。
manualTranslations.literal: Seeing that the rhymed piece had roughly taken shape, he named it "On the Pool" and wrote: A dwelling of ten mu, a garden of five mu, one pool of water, a thousand bamboo stalks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seeing the rough rhymed piece complete, he titled it "On the Pool": A ten-mu dwelling, a five-mu garden, one pool of water, and a thousand bamboo shoots.

manualTranslations.zh: 勿謂土狹，勿謂地偏，足以容膝，足以息肩。
manualTranslations.literal: Do not say the land is narrow; do not say the place is remote—it is enough to hold the knees, enough to rest the shoulders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Call not the ground too narrow or the spot too remote—it is room enough for one's knees and rest enough for one's shoulders.

manualTranslations.zh: 有堂有亭，有橋有船，有書有酒，有歌有弦。
manualTranslations.literal: There is a hall, there is a pavilion, bridges and boats, books and wine, song and strings.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hall and pavilion, bridge and boat, books and wine, song and strings.

manualTranslations.zh: 有叟在中，白須颯然，識分知足，外無求焉。
manualTranslations.literal: An old man is in their midst, white beard rustling; knowing his lot and content, he seeks nothing beyond.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An old man dwells at the center, white beard stirring in the breeze; knowing his place and content, he desires nothing more.

manualTranslations.zh: 如鳥擇木，姑務巢安；
manualTranslations.literal: Like a bird choosing its tree, he simply strives to nest in peace;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Like a bird choosing a tree, he seeks only a secure nest;

manualTranslations.zh: 如蛙作坎，不知海寬。
manualTranslations.literal: like a frog digging its pit, he does not know the sea's breadth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: like a frog digging its hollow, he knows nothing of the sea's vastness.

manualTranslations.zh: 靈鵲怪石，紫菱白蓮，皆吾所好，盡在我前。
manualTranslations.literal: Spirit magpies, strange rocks, purple water chestnuts, white lotuses—all are what I love, all lie before me.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Spirit magpies, curious rocks, purple water chestnuts, white lotuses—all that I love lies spread before me.

manualTranslations.zh: 時引一杯，或吟一篇。
manualTranslations.literal: At times I raise a cup; at times I chant a piece.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sometimes I lift a cup; sometimes I chant a verse.

manualTranslations.zh: 妻孥熙熙，雞犬閑閑。
manualTranslations.literal: Wife and children are cheerful; chickens and dogs are at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wife and children are happy; chickens and dogs are tranquil.

manualTranslations.zh: 優哉遊哉，吾將老乎其間。
manualTranslations.literal: Easy and free, easy and free—I shall grow old amid it all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At ease, at leisure—I shall grow old within this place.

sourceRange.text: 拜命之日，獻疏言事曰：蒙恩授臣左拾遺，依前翰林學士，已與崔群同狀陳謝。但言忝冒，未吐衷誠。今再瀆宸嚴，伏惟重賜詳覽。臣謹按《六典》，左右拾遺，掌供奉諷諫，凡發令舉事，有不便於時、不合於道者，小則上封，大則廷諍。其選甚重，其秩甚卑，所以然者，抑有由也。大凡人之情，位高則惜其位，身貴則愛其身；惜位則偷合而不言，愛身則茍容而不諫，此必然之理也。故拾遺之置，所以卑其秩者，使位未足惜，身未足愛也。所以重其選者，使下不忍負心，上不忍負恩也。夫位不足惜，恩不忍負，然後能有闕必規，有違必諫。朝廷得失無不察，天下利病無不言。此國朝置拾遺之本意也。由是而言，豈小臣愚劣暗懦所宜居之哉？況臣本鄉校豎儒，府縣走吏，委心泥滓，絕望煙霄。豈意聖慈，擢居近職，每宴飲無不先預，每慶賜無不先沾，中廄之馬代其勞，內廚之膳給其食。朝慚夕惕，已逾半年，塵曠漸深，憂愧彌劇。未申微效，又擢清班。臣所以授官已來僅經十日，食不知味，寢不遑安。唯思粉身以答殊寵，但未獲粉身之所耳。今陛下肇臨皇極，初受鴻名，夙夜憂勤，以求致理。每施一政、舉一事，無不合於道、便於時者。萬一事有不便於時者，陛下豈不欲聞之乎？萬一政有不合於道者，陛下豈不欲知之乎？倘陛下言動之際，詔令之間，小有闕遺，稍關損益，臣必密陳所見，潛獻所聞，但在聖心裁斷而已。臣又職在禁中，不同外司，欲竭愚誠，合先陳露。伏希天鑒，深察赤誠。

localRange.text: 拜命之日，獻疏言事曰：

context.beforeSource: 居易自以逢好文之主，非次拔擢，欲以生平所貯，仰酬恩造。
context.afterSource: 居易與河南元稹相善，同年登制舉，交情隆厚。

manualTranslations.zh: 拜命之日，獻疏言事曰：蒙恩授臣左拾遺，依前翰林學士，已與崔群同狀陳謝。
manualTranslations.literal: On the day he received his appointment, he submitted a memorial on affairs of state, which read: Receiving grace, Your Majesty appointed this subject Left Reminder, continuing as before as Hanlin academician; I have already submitted a joint memorial of thanks with Cui Qun.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On the day he received his appointment, he submitted a memorial on affairs of state, which read: Receiving your grace, you appointed me Left Reminder while continuing me as Hanlin academician; I have already submitted a joint memorial of thanks with Cui Qun.

manualTranslations.zh: 但言忝冒，未吐衷誠。
manualTranslations.literal: I spoke only of unworthy acceptance and did not express my inner sincerity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I spoke only of unworthy acceptance and did not express my inner sincerity.

manualTranslations.zh: 今再瀆宸嚴，伏惟重賜詳覽。
manualTranslations.literal: Now again offending the imperial presence, I humbly beg that you again bestow careful reading.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now again intruding upon your imperial presence, I humbly beg your careful reading once more.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹按《六典》，左右拾遺，掌供奉諷諫，凡發令舉事，有不便於時、不合於道者，小則上封，大則廷諍。
manualTranslations.literal: This subject respectfully consults the Administrative Compendium: the Left and Right Reminders oversee attendance and admonition; whenever orders are issued or affairs undertaken that are inconvenient to the times or not in accord with the Way, for small matters they submit sealed memorials, for great matters they remonstrate at court.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully consult the Administrative Compendium: the Left and Right Reminders oversee attendance and admonition; whenever orders or undertakings are inconvenient to the times or not in accord with the Way, for small matters they submit sealed memorials, for great matters they remonstrate at court.

manualTranslations.zh: 其選甚重，其秩甚卑，所以然者，抑有由也。
manualTranslations.literal: Their selection is very weighty, their rank very low; the reason it is so indeed has a cause.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Their selection is weighty, their rank low; there is indeed a reason for this.

manualTranslations.zh: 大凡人之情，位高則惜其位，身貴則愛其身；
manualTranslations.literal: Generally speaking, in human feeling, when position is high one cherishes one's position, when the person is noble one loves one's person;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Generally speaking, when position is high one cherishes one's position, when status is exalted one loves one's person;

manualTranslations.zh: 惜位則偷合而不言，愛身則茍容而不諫，此必然之理也。
manualTranslations.literal: cherishing position then one steals agreement and does not speak; loving one's person then one is compliant and does not remonstrate—this is the inevitable principle.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: cherish position and one steals agreement without speaking; love one's person and one is compliant without remonstrating—this is inevitable.

manualTranslations.zh: 故拾遺之置，所以卑其秩者，使位未足惜，身未足愛也。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore in establishing the Reminders, the reason their rank is made low is to make position not yet worth cherishing and person not yet worth loving.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore the Reminders are given low rank so that position is not yet worth cherishing and person not yet worth loving.

manualTranslations.zh: 所以重其選者，使下不忍負心，上不忍負恩也。
manualTranslations.literal: The reason their selection is made weighty is to make subordinates unable to bear betraying their hearts and superiors unable to bear betraying grace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Their selection is made weighty so that subordinates cannot bear to betray their hearts and superiors cannot bear to betray grace.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫位不足惜，恩不忍負，然後能有闕必規，有違必諫。
manualTranslations.literal: When position is not worth cherishing and grace cannot be betrayed, only then can one where there are faults certainly admonish and where there are violations certainly remonstrate.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When position is not worth cherishing and grace cannot be betrayed, only then can one admonish wherever there are faults and remonstrate wherever there are violations.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝廷得失無不察，天下利病無不言。
manualTranslations.literal: The court's gains and losses are all examined; the realm's benefits and harms are all spoken of.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court's gains and losses are all examined; the realm's benefits and harms are all spoken of.

manualTranslations.zh: 此國朝置拾遺之本意也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is the original intent of our dynasty in establishing the Reminders.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is our dynasty's original intent in establishing the Reminders.

manualTranslations.zh: 由是而言，豈小臣愚劣暗懦所宜居之哉？
manualTranslations.literal: Speaking from this, how could it be a post fit for a petty minister stupid, inferior, and timid?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this perspective, how could it be a post fit for a petty minister as stupid, inferior, and timid as I?

manualTranslations.zh: 況臣本鄉校豎儒，府縣走吏，委心泥滓，絕望煙霄。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover this subject was originally a village-school pedant and a runner-clerk in prefecture and county; my heart was cast into the mire, my hopes cut off from the clouds.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover I was originally a village-school pedant and a runner-clerk in prefecture and county; my heart was cast into the mire, my hopes cut off from the clouds.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈意聖慈，擢居近職，每宴飲無不先預，每慶賜無不先沾，中廄之馬代其勞，內廚之膳給其食。
manualTranslations.literal: Who would have thought of sagely kindness raising me to a nearby post: at every feast and drink I was invariably first to attend, at every celebratory bestowal invariably first to receive benefit; the imperial stable's horses bore my labor, the inner kitchen's meals supplied my food.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who would have thought your sagely kindness would raise me to a nearby post: at every feast I was first to attend, at every celebratory bestowal first to benefit; the imperial stable's horses bore my labor, the inner kitchen's meals supplied my food.

manualTranslations.zh: 朝慚夕惕，已逾半年，塵曠漸深，憂愧彌劇。
manualTranslations.literal: Morning ashamed, evening wary, already more than half a year; the dust of neglect grows deeper, worry and shame grow keener.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ashamed morning and wary evening for more than half a year, the dust of neglect grows deeper and my worry and shame grow keener.

manualTranslations.zh: 未申微效，又擢清班。
manualTranslations.literal: Before I had rendered the slightest service, I was again promoted to the pure ranks.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before I had rendered the slightest service, I was again promoted to the pure ranks.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣所以授官已來僅經十日，食不知味，寢不遑安。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore since receiving office it has been only ten days; in eating I do not know flavor, in sleeping I have no leisure for rest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore, in the ten days since receiving office, I have eaten without tasting and slept without rest.

manualTranslations.zh: 唯思粉身以答殊寵，但未獲粉身之所耳。
manualTranslations.literal: I think only of grinding my body to repay extraordinary favor, yet have not yet obtained the place to grind my body.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I think only of giving my body to repay extraordinary favor, yet have not yet found the occasion to do so.

manualTranslations.zh: 今陛下肇臨皇極，初受鴻名，夙夜憂勤，以求致理。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Your Majesty has newly ascended the imperial pinnacle and first received the great name; day and night anxious and diligent, seeking to bring order.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now you have newly ascended the throne and first received the great name; day and night anxious and diligent, seeking to bring order.

manualTranslations.zh: 每施一政、舉一事，無不合於道、便於時者。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever you enact a policy or undertake an affair, none fails to accord with the Way and suit the times.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever you enact a policy or undertake an affair, none fails to accord with the Way and suit the times.

manualTranslations.zh: 萬一事有不便於時者，陛下豈不欲聞之乎？
manualTranslations.literal: If by chance there is an affair inconvenient to the times, would Your Majesty not wish to hear of it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If by chance there is an affair inconvenient to the times, would you not wish to hear of it?

manualTranslations.zh: 萬一政有不合於道者，陛下豈不欲知之乎？
manualTranslations.literal: If by chance there is a policy not in accord with the Way, would Your Majesty not wish to know of it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If by chance there is a policy not in accord with the Way, would you not wish to know of it?

manualTranslations.zh: 倘陛下言動之際，詔令之間，小有闕遺，稍關損益，臣必密陳所見，潛獻所聞，但在聖心裁斷而已。
manualTranslations.literal: If in Your Majesty's words and actions, among edicts and orders, there are small omissions or slight matters bearing on benefit and harm, this subject will certainly secretly set forth what I have seen and quietly present what I have heard—only awaiting the sagely heart's judgment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If in your words and actions, among edicts and orders, there are small omissions or slight matters bearing on benefit and harm, I will secretly set forth what I have seen and quietly present what I have heard—only awaiting your judgment.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣又職在禁中，不同外司，欲竭愚誠，合先陳露。
manualTranslations.literal: This subject's duties are moreover within the forbidden precincts, unlike outer offices; wishing to exhaust my foolish sincerity, I ought first to disclose it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: My duties are moreover within the forbidden precincts, unlike outer offices; wishing to exhaust my sincerity, I ought first to disclose it.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏希天鑒，深察赤誠。
manualTranslations.literal: I humbly hope for Heaven's discernment and deep perception of my red sincerity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly hope for Heaven's discernment and deep perception of my sincerity.

sourceRange.text: 嘗與稹書，因論作文之大旨曰：夫文，尚矣，三才各有文。天之文三光首之；地之文五材首之；人之文《六經》道之。就《六經》言，《詩》又首之。何者？聖人感人心而天下和平。感人心者，莫先乎情，莫始乎言，莫切乎聲，莫深乎義。詩者，根情，苗言，華聲，實義。上自賢聖，下至愚騃，微及豚魚，幽及鬼神。群分而氣同，形異而情一。未有聲入而不應、情交而不感者。聖人知其然，因其言，經之以六義；緣其聲，緯之以五音。音有韻，義有類。韻協則言順，言順則聲易入；類舉則情見，情見則感易交。於是乎孕大含深，貫微洞密，上下通而二氣泰，憂樂合而百志熙。二帝三王所以直道而行、垂拱而理者，揭此以為大柄，決此以為大竇也。故聞「元首明，股肱良」之歌，則知虞道昌矣。聞五子洛汭之歌，則知夏政荒矣。言者無罪，聞者作誡，言者聞者莫不兩盡其心焉。洎周衰秦興，采詩官廢，上不以詩補察時政，下不以歌泄導人情。用至於諂成之風動，救失之道缺。於時六義始剚矣。《國風》變為《騷辭》，五言始於蘇、李。《詩》、《騷》皆不遇者，各系其志，發而為文。故河梁之句，止於傷別；澤畔之吟，歸於怨思。仿徨抑郁，不暇及他耳。然去《詩》未遠，梗概尚存。故興離別則引雙鳧一雁為喻，諷君子小人則引香草惡鳥為比。雖義類不具，猶得風人之什二三焉。於時六義始缺矣。晉、宋已還，得者蓋寡。以康樂之奧博，多溺於山水；以淵明之高古，偏放於田園。江、鮑之流，又狹於此。如梁鴻《五噫》之例者，百無一二。於時六義浸微矣！陵夷至於梁、陳間，率不過嘲風雪、弄花草而已。噫！風雪花草之物，三百篇中豈舍之乎？顧所用何如耳。設如「北風其涼」，假風以刺威虐；「雨雪霏霏」，因雪以湣征役；「棠棣之華」，感華以諷兄弟；「采采芣苡」，美草以樂有子也。皆興發於此而義歸於彼。反是者，可乎哉！然則「餘霞散成綺，澄江凈如練」，「歸花先委露，別葉乍辭風」之什，麗則麗矣，吾不知其所諷焉。故僕所謂嘲風雪、弄花草而已。於時六義盡去矣。唐興二百年，其間詩人不可勝數。所可舉者，陳子昂有《感遇詩》二十首，鮑防《感興詩》十五篇。又詩之豪者，世稱李、杜。李之作，才矣！奇矣！人不迨矣！索其風雅比興，十無一焉。杜詩最多，可傳者千餘首。至於貫穿古今，覙縷格律，盡工盡善，又過於李焉。然撮其《新安》、《石壕》、《潼關吏》、《蘆子關》、《花門》之章，「硃門酒肉臭，路有凍死骨」之句，亦不過十三四。杜尚如此，況不迨杜者乎？僕常痛詩道崩壞，忽忽憤發，或廢食輟寢，不量才力，欲扶起之。嗟乎！事有大謬者，又不可一二而言，然亦不能不粗陳於左右。僕始生六七月時，乳母抱弄於書屏下，有指「之」字、「無」字示僕者，僕口未能言，心已默識。後有問此二字者，雖百十其試，而指之不差。則知僕宿習之緣，已在文字中矣。及五六歲，便學為詩。九歲諳識聲韻。十五六，始知有進士，苦節讀書。二十已來，書課賦，夜課書，間又課詩，不遑寢息矣。以至於口舌成瘡，手肘成胝。既壯而膚革不豐盈，未老而齒發早衰白；瞀然如飛蠅垂珠在眸子中者，動以萬數，蓋以苦學力文之所致！又自悲家貧多故，年二十七，方從鄉賦。既第之後，雖專於科試，亦不廢詩。及授校書郎時，已盈三四百首。或出示交友如足下輩，見皆謂之工，其實未窺作者之域耳。自登朝來，年齒漸長，閱事漸多。每與人言，多詢時務；每讀書史，多求理道。始知文章合為時而著，歌詩合為事而作。是時皇帝初即位，宰府有正人，屢降璽書，訪人急病。僕當此日，擢在翰林，身是諫官，月請諫紙。啟奏之間，有可以救濟人病，裨補時闕，而難於指言者，輒詠歌之，欲稍稍進聞於上。上以廣宸聽，副憂勤；次以酬恩獎，塞言責；下以復吾平生之志。豈圖志未就而悔已生，言未聞而謗已成矣！又請為左右終言之。凡聞僕《賀雨詩》，眾口籍籍，以為非宜矣；聞僕《哭孔戡詩》，眾面脈脈，盡不悅矣；聞《秦中吟》，則權豪貴近者，相目而變色矣；聞《登樂遊園》寄足下詩，則執政柄者扼腕矣；聞《宿紫閣村》詩，則握軍要者切齒矣！大率如此，不可遍舉。不相與者，號為沽譽，號為詆訐，號為訕謗。茍相與者，則如牛僧孺之誡焉。乃至骨肉妻孥，皆以我為非也。其不我非者，舉世不過三兩人。有鄧魴者，見僕詩而喜，無何魴死。有唐衢者，見僕詩而泣，未幾而衢死。其餘即足下。足下又十年來困躓若此。嗚呼！豈六義四始之風，天將破壞，不可支持耶？抑又不知天意不欲使下人病苦聞於上耶？不然，何有志於詩者，不利若此之甚也！然僕又自思關東一男子耳，除讀書屬文外，其他懵然無知，乃至書畫棋博，可以接群居之歡者，一無通曉，即其愚拙可知矣！初應進士時，中朝無緦麻之親，達官無半面之舊；策蹇步於利足之途，張空拳於戰文之場。十年之間，三登科第，名落眾耳，跡升清貫，出交賢俊，入侍冕旒。始得名於文章，終得罪於文章，亦其宜也。日者聞親友間說，禮、吏部舉選人，多以僕私試賦判為準的。其餘詩句，亦往往在人口中。僕恧然自愧，不之信也。及再來長安，又聞有軍使高霞寓者，欲聘倡妓，妓大誇曰：「我誦得白學士《長恨歌》，豈同他哉？」由是增價。又足下書云：到通州日，見江館柱間有題僕詩者。何人哉？又昨過漢南日，適遇主人集眾娛樂，他賓諸妓見僕來，指而相顧曰：此是《秦中吟》、《長恨歌》主耳。自長安抵江西三四千里，凡鄉校、佛寺、逆旅、行舟之中，往往有題僕詩者；士庶、僧徒、孀婦、處女之口，每有詠僕詩者。此誠雕篆之戲，不足為多，然今時俗所重，正在此耳。雖前賢如淵、雲者，前輩如李、杜者，亦未能忘情於其間。古人云：「名者公器，不可多取。」僕是何者，竊時之名已多。既竊時名，又欲竊時之富貴，使己為造物者，肯兼與之乎？今之屯窮，理固然也。況詩人多蹇，如陳子昂、杜甫，各授一拾遺，而屯剝至死。孟浩然輩不及一命，窮悴終身。近日孟郊六十，終試協律；張籍五十，未離一太祝。彼何人哉！況僕之才又不迨彼。今雖謫佐遠郡，而官品至第五，月俸四五萬，寒有衣，饑有食，給身之外，施及家人。亦可謂不負白氏子矣。微之，微之！勿念我哉！僕數月來，檢討囊帙中，得新舊詩，各以類分，分為卷目。自拾遺來，凡所遇所感，關於美刺興比者；又自武德至元和，因事立題，題為《新樂府》者，共一百五十首，謂之諷諭詩。又或退公，或臥病閑居，知足保和，吟玩性情者一百首，謂之閑適詩。又有事物牽於外，情理動於內，隨感遇而形於嘆詠者一百首，謂之感傷詩。又有五言、七言、長句、絕句，自百韻至兩韻者，四百餘首，謂之雜律詩。凡為十五卷，約八百首。異時相見，當盡致於執事。微之，古人云：「窮則獨善其身，達則兼濟天下。」僕雖不肖，常師此語。大丈夫所守者道，所待者時。時之來也，為雲龍，為風鵬，勃然突然，陳力以出；時之不來也，為霧豹，為冥鴻，寂兮寥兮，奉身而退。進退出處，何往而不自得哉！故僕志在兼濟，行在獨善，奉而始終之則為道，言而發明之則為詩。謂之諷諭詩，兼濟之志也；謂之閑適詩，獨善之義也。故覽僕詩者，知僕之道焉。其餘雜律詩，或誘於一時一物，發於一笑一吟，率然成章，非平生所尚者，但以親朋合散之際，取其釋恨佐歡，今銓次之間，未能刪去。他時有為我編集斯文者，略之可也。微之，夫貴耳賤目，榮古陋今，人之大情也。僕不能遠征古舊，如近歲韋蘇州歌行，才麗之外，頗近興諷；其五言詩，又高雅閑淡，自成一家之體，今之秉筆者誰能及之？然當蘇州在時，人亦未甚愛重，必待身後，人始貴之。今僕之詩，人所愛者，悉不過雜律詩與《長恨歌》已下耳。時之所重，僕之所輕。至於諷諭者，意激而言質；閑適者，思淡而辭迂。以質合迂，宜人之不愛也。今所愛者，並世而生，獨足下耳。然百千年後，安知復無如足下者出，而知愛我詩哉？故自八九年來，與足下小通則以詩相戒，小窮則以詩相勉，索居則以詩相慰，同處則以詩相娛。知吾罪吾，率以詩也。如今年春遊城南時，與足下馬上相戲，因各誦新艷小律，不雜他篇，自皇子陂歸昭國裏，叠吟遞唱，不絕聲者二十里餘。攀、李在傍，無所措口。知我者以為詩仙，不知我者以為詩魔。何則？勞心靈，役聲氣，連朝接夕，不自知其苦，非魔而何？偶同人當美景，或花時宴罷，或月夜酒酣，一詠一吟，不覺老之將至。雖驂鸞鶴、遊蓬瀛者之適，無以加於此焉，又非仙而何？微之，微之！此吾所以與足下外形骸、脫蹤跡、傲軒鼎、輕人寰者，又以此也。當此之時，足下興有餘力，且欲與僕悉索還往中詩，取其尤長者，如張十八古樂府，李二十新歌行，盧、楊二秘書律詩，竇七、元八絕句，博搜精掇，編而次之，號為《元白往還集》。眾君子得擬議於此者，莫不踴躍欣喜，以為盛事。嗟乎！言未終而足下左轉，不數月而僕又繼行，心期索然，何日成就？又可為之太息矣！僕常語足下，凡人為文，私於自是，不忍於割截，或失於繁多。其間妍媸，益又自惑。必待交友有公鑒無姑息者，討論而削奪之，然後繁簡當否，得其中矣。況僕與足下，為文尤患其多。己尚病，況他人乎？今且各纂詩筆，粗為卷第，待與足下相見日，各出所有，終前志焉。又不知相遇是何年，相見是何地，溘然而至，則如之何？微之知我心哉！潯陽臘月，江風苦寒，歲暮鮮歡，夜長少睡。引筆鋪紙，悄然燈前，有念則書，言無銓次。勿以繁雜為倦，且以代一夕之話言也。
