manualTranslations.zh: 嘗與稹書，因論作文之大旨曰：夫文，尚矣，三才各有文。
manualTranslations.literal: He once wrote to Zhen, discussing the great principles of composition, saying: Writing is exalted indeed; the three powers each have their writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He once wrote to Zhen discussing the great principles of composition, saying: Writing is exalted indeed; heaven, earth, and humanity each have their own literature.

manualTranslations.zh: 天之文三光首之；
manualTranslations.literal: Heaven's writing takes the three luminaries as foremost;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Heaven's literature is headed by the sun, moon, and stars;

manualTranslations.zh: 地之文五材首之；
manualTranslations.literal: earth's writing takes the five materials as foremost;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: earth's literature is headed by the five elements;

manualTranslations.zh: 人之文《六經》道之。
manualTranslations.literal: humanity's writing is guided by the Six Classics.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: human literature is guided by the Six Classics.

manualTranslations.zh: 就《六經》言，《詩》又首之。
manualTranslations.literal: Speaking of the Six Classics, the Odes again come first.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among the Six Classics, the Odes come first.

manualTranslations.zh: 何者？
manualTranslations.literal: Why?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why is this?

manualTranslations.zh: 聖人感人心而天下和平。
manualTranslations.literal: The sage moves people's hearts and the realm is at peace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The sage moves people's hearts, and the realm is at peace.

manualTranslations.zh: 感人心者，莫先乎情，莫始乎言，莫切乎聲，莫深乎義。
manualTranslations.literal: What moves people's hearts: nothing comes before feeling, nothing begins before words, nothing cuts closer than sound, nothing runs deeper than meaning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What moves the heart begins with feeling, starts with words, is sharpened by sound, and is grounded in meaning.

manualTranslations.zh: 詩者，根情，苗言，華聲，實義。
manualTranslations.literal: Poetry takes feeling as root, words as shoot, sound as blossom, and meaning as fruit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Poetry has feeling for its root, words for its shoot, sound for its blossom, and meaning for its fruit.

manualTranslations.zh: 上自賢聖，下至愚騃，微及豚魚，幽及鬼神。
manualTranslations.literal: From sages and worthies above to fools and dullards below, it reaches subtly to pigs and fish and darkly to ghosts and spirits.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It ranges from sages and worthies down to fools and dullards, reaching subtly even to pigs and fish and darkly even to ghosts and spirits.

manualTranslations.zh: 群分而氣同，形異而情一。
manualTranslations.literal: Classes are many but the breath is one; forms differ but feelings are the same.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though classes are many, the vital breath is one; though forms differ, feelings are the same.

manualTranslations.zh: 未有聲入而不應、情交而不感者。
manualTranslations.literal: There has never been sound entering the ear without response, or feelings exchanged without mutual stirring.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Never does sound enter the ear without response, nor feelings meet without mutual stirring.

manualTranslations.zh: 聖人知其然，因其言，經之以六義；
manualTranslations.literal: The sage knew this to be so; taking their words, he threaded them with the six principles;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Knowing this, the sage took people's words and threaded them with the six principles;

manualTranslations.zh: 緣其聲，緯之以五音。
manualTranslations.literal: following their sounds, he wove them with the five tones.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and following their sounds, wove them with the five tones.

manualTranslations.zh: 音有韻，義有類。
manualTranslations.literal: Sounds have rhyme; meanings have categories.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sound has rhyme; meaning has category.

manualTranslations.zh: 韻協則言順，言順則聲易入；
manualTranslations.literal: When rhyme harmonizes, words flow; when words flow, sound enters easily;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When rhyme harmonizes, words flow smoothly; when words flow, sound enters easily;

manualTranslations.zh: 類舉則情見，情見則感易交。
manualTranslations.literal: when categories are set forth, feeling appears; when feeling appears, mutual stirring comes easily.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when categories are set forth, feeling shows; when feeling shows, mutual stirring comes easily.

manualTranslations.zh: 於是乎孕大含深，貫微洞密，上下通而二氣泰，憂樂合而百志熙。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus it bears the great and holds the deep, penetrates the subtle and threads the dense; above and below communicate and the two breaths are at peace, sorrow and joy unite and the hundred aims flourish.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus it bears the great and holds the deep, penetrates the subtle and threads the dense; above and below communicate and the two breaths are at peace, sorrow and joy unite and the hundred aims flourish.

manualTranslations.zh: 二帝三王所以直道而行、垂拱而理者，揭此以為大柄，決此以為大竇也。
manualTranslations.literal: The reason the Two Emperors and Three Kings could walk the straight path and govern with folded arms was that they raised this as the great handle and opened this as the great gateway.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Two Emperors and Three Kings could walk the straight path and govern with folded arms because they raised this as the great handle and opened this as the great gateway.

manualTranslations.zh: 故聞「元首明，股肱良」之歌，則知虞道昌矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus upon hearing the song "The head is bright, the arms are good," one knows the way of Yu flourished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus hearing the song "The head is bright, the arms are good," one knows the way of Yu flourished.

manualTranslations.zh: 聞五子洛汭之歌，則知夏政荒矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Upon hearing the song of the Five Sons at Luorui, one knows the government of Xia was in disorder.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearing the song of the Five Sons at Luorui, one knows the government of Xia was in disorder.

manualTranslations.zh: 言者無罪，聞者作誡，言者聞者莫不兩盡其心焉。
manualTranslations.literal: The speaker is without guilt; the hearer takes warning—speaker and hearer alike fully give their hearts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The speaker bears no guilt; the hearer takes warning—speaker and hearer alike give their full hearts.

manualTranslations.zh: 洎周衰秦興，采詩官廢，上不以詩補察時政，下不以歌泄導人情。
manualTranslations.literal: By the time Zhou declined and Qin rose, the poetry-gathering office was abolished; above, poetry was not used to supplement and examine current government; below, songs were not used to vent and guide human feeling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined and Qin rose, the poetry-gathering office was abolished; above, poetry no longer supplemented and examined government; below, songs no longer vented and guided human feeling.

manualTranslations.zh: 用至於諂成之風動，救失之道缺。
manualTranslations.literal: Use came to the point where the wind of flattery and complacency stirred, and the way of remedying loss was lacking.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Flattery and complacency took hold, and the way of remedying loss was lost.

manualTranslations.zh: 於時六義始剚矣。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the six principles were first cut away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then the six principles were first cut away.

manualTranslations.zh: 《國風》變為《騷辭》，五言始於蘇、李。
manualTranslations.literal: The Airs of the States turned into Sao verse; five-character poetry began with Su and Li.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Airs of the States became Sao verse; five-character poetry began with Su Wu and Li Ling.

manualTranslations.zh: 《詩》、《騷》皆不遇者，各系其志，發而為文。
manualTranslations.literal: Those of the Odes and Sao were all men who did not meet with favor; each attached to his own aim and, giving vent, produced writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The authors of the Odes and Sao were all men who met with no favor; each clung to his own aim and, giving vent, produced writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 故河梁之句，止於傷別；
manualTranslations.literal: Thus the lines at River Bridge stop at grieving parting;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus the lines at River Bridge stop at grieving parting;

manualTranslations.zh: 澤畔之吟，歸於怨思。
manualTranslations.literal: the chant beside the marsh returns to resentful brooding.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: the chant beside the marsh returns to resentful brooding.

manualTranslations.zh: 仿徨抑郁，不暇及他耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Wandering, depressed, they had no leisure for anything else.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wandering and depressed, they had no leisure for anything else.

manualTranslations.zh: 然去《詩》未遠，梗概尚存。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet they were not far from the Odes; the rough outline still remained.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet they were not far from the Odes; the rough outline still remained.

manualTranslations.zh: 故興離別則引雙鳧一雁為喻，諷君子小人則引香草惡鳥為比。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus in treating parting they cited paired ducks and a single goose as metaphor; in satirizing gentleman and petty man they cited fragrant herbs and evil birds as comparison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus in treating parting they cited paired ducks and a single goose as metaphor; in satirizing gentleman and petty man they cited fragrant herbs and evil birds as comparison.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖義類不具，猶得風人之什二三焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Though the categories of meaning were not complete, they still preserved two or three out of ten of the Airs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though the categories of meaning were not complete, they still preserved two or three out of ten of the Airs.

manualTranslations.zh: 於時六義始缺矣。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the six principles were first lacking.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then the six principles were first lacking.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉、宋已還，得者蓋寡。
manualTranslations.literal: From Jin and Song onward, those who attained it were few indeed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Jin and Song onward, those who attained it were few indeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 以康樂之奧博，多溺於山水；
manualTranslations.literal: In Xie Lingyun's profundity and breadth, many drowned in landscape;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Xie Lingyun's profundity and breadth, many drowned in landscape;

manualTranslations.zh: 以淵明之高古，偏放於田園。
manualTranslations.literal: in Tao Yuanming's lofty antiquity, many were set loose in fields and gardens.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: in Tao Yuanming's lofty antiquity, many were set loose in fields and gardens.

manualTranslations.zh: 江、鮑之流，又狹於此。
manualTranslations.literal: The stream of Jiang and Bao was narrower still.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The stream of Jiang Yan and Bao Zhao was narrower still.

manualTranslations.zh: 如梁鴻《五噫》之例者，百無一二。
manualTranslations.literal: Cases like Liang Hong's "Five Sighs" were not one or two in a hundred.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cases like Liang Hong's "Five Sighs" were not one or two in a hundred.

manualTranslations.zh: 於時六義浸微矣！
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the six principles gradually faded!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By then the six principles were gradually fading!

manualTranslations.zh: 陵夷至於梁、陳間，率不過嘲風雪、弄花草而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Decline reached Liang and Chen, when as a rule it was no more than mocking wind and snow and toying with flowers and grasses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Decline reached Liang and Chen, when as a rule poetry was no more than mocking wind and snow and toying with flowers and grasses.

manualTranslations.zh: 噫！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 風雪花草之物，三百篇中豈舍之乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Are wind, flowers, snow, and grass absent from the three hundred pieces?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Are wind, flowers, snow, and grass absent from the three hundred pieces?

manualTranslations.zh: 顧所用何如耳。
manualTranslations.literal: It depends on how they are used.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It depends on how they are used.

manualTranslations.zh: 設如「北風其涼」，假風以刺威虐；
manualTranslations.literal: Suppose "The north wind is cold"—borrowing wind to satirize cruel oppression;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Take "The north wind is cold"—wind is borrowed to satirize cruel oppression;

manualTranslations.zh: 「雨雪霏霏」，因雪以湣征役；
manualTranslations.literal: "The snow falls thickly"—through snow to pity conscript labor;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "The snow falls thickly"—through snow to pity conscript labor;

manualTranslations.zh: 「棠棣之華」，感華以諷兄弟；
manualTranslations.literal: "The cherry-apple in flower"—moved by blossom to satirize brothers;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "The cherry-apple in flower"—moved by blossom to satirize brothers;

manualTranslations.zh: 「采采芣苡」，美草以樂有子也。
manualTranslations.literal: "Gathering plantain"—praising the herb to rejoice in having sons.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Gathering plantain"—praising the herb to rejoice in having sons.

manualTranslations.zh: 皆興發於此而義歸於彼。
manualTranslations.literal: All rise from this and meaning returns to that.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: All rise from this and meaning returns to that.

manualTranslations.zh: 反是者，可乎哉！
manualTranslations.literal: To do the opposite—can that be allowed!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To do the opposite—can that be allowed!

manualTranslations.zh: 然則「餘霞散成綺，澄江凈如練」，「歸花先委露，別葉乍辭風」之什，麗則麗矣，吾不知其所諷焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Then the pieces "Leftover glow scatters into brocade; the clear river is smooth as silk" and "Returning flowers first shed dew; parting leaves suddenly leave the wind"—lovely they are indeed, but I do not know what they satirize.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then pieces like "Leftover glow scatters into brocade; the clear river is smooth as silk" and "Returning flowers first shed dew; parting leaves suddenly leave the wind" are lovely indeed, but I do not know what they satirize.

manualTranslations.zh: 故僕所謂嘲風雪、弄花草而已。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus what I call mocking wind and snow and toying with flowers and grasses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is what I mean by mocking wind and snow and toying with flowers and grasses.

manualTranslations.zh: 於時六義盡去矣。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the six principles were entirely gone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By then the six principles were entirely gone.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐興二百年，其間詩人不可勝數。
manualTranslations.literal: Tang has risen two hundred years; poets in that time are beyond counting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Tang has risen for two hundred years; poets in that time are beyond counting.

manualTranslations.zh: 所可舉者，陳子昂有《感遇詩》二十首，鮑防《感興詩》十五篇。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who may be cited: Chen Zi'ang had twenty pieces of "Poems on Encountering Feeling"; Bao Fang had fifteen pieces of "Poems Stirred by Feeling."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who may be cited: Chen Zi'ang had twenty "Poems on Encountering Feeling"; Bao Fang had fifteen "Poems Stirred by Feeling."

manualTranslations.zh: 又詩之豪者，世稱李、杜。
manualTranslations.literal: Again, the mighty in poetry—the age calls them Li and Du.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again, the mighty in poetry—the age calls them Li and Du.

manualTranslations.zh: 李之作，才矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Li's works—talented indeed!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Bai's works—talented indeed!

manualTranslations.zh: 奇矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Strange indeed!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Strange indeed!

manualTranslations.zh: 人不迨矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Men cannot reach him!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men cannot reach him!

manualTranslations.zh: 索其風雅比興，十無一焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Search for elegance, Airs, comparison, and stirring— not one in ten.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Search for elegance, Airs, comparison, and stirring—not one in ten.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜詩最多，可傳者千餘首。
manualTranslations.literal: Du's poems are most numerous; those that can be transmitted number more than a thousand.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Fu's poems are most numerous; those that can be transmitted number more than a thousand.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於貫穿古今，覙縷格律，盡工盡善，又過於李焉。
manualTranslations.literal: As for penetrating past and present, threading through rules and forms, achieving utmost craft and utmost goodness—he surpasses Li.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In penetrating past and present, threading through rules and forms, and achieving utmost craft and goodness, he surpasses Li Bai.

manualTranslations.zh: 然撮其《新安》、《石壕》、《潼關吏》、《蘆子關》、《花門》之章，「硃門酒肉臭，路有凍死骨」之句，亦不過十三四。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet gather his chapters "Xin'an," "Shihao," "Tong Pass Officer," "Luzi Pass," and "Flower Gate," and the line "Vermilion gates reek of wine and meat; on the road lie bones of the frozen dead"—these too are no more than thirteen or fourteen out of a hundred.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet gather his chapters "Xin'an," "Shihao," "Tong Pass Officer," "Luzi Pass," and "Flower Gate," and the line "Vermilion gates reek of wine and meat; on the road lie bones of the frozen dead"—these too are no more than thirteen or fourteen out of a hundred.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜尚如此，況不迨杜者乎？
manualTranslations.literal: If Du is still like this, how much more those who do not reach Du?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Du Fu is still like this, how much more those who do not reach Du Fu?

manualTranslations.zh: 僕常痛詩道崩壞，忽忽憤發，或廢食輟寢，不量才力，欲扶起之。
manualTranslations.literal: I have often grieved that the way of poetry was collapsing; suddenly, in angry agitation, I would abandon eating or stop sleeping, not measuring talent and strength, wishing to raise it up again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have often grieved that the way of poetry was collapsing; suddenly, in angry agitation, I would abandon eating or stop sleeping, not measuring my talent and strength, wishing to raise it up again.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗟乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 事有大謬者，又不可一二而言，然亦不能不粗陳於左右。
manualTranslations.literal: There are great errors in affairs that cannot be told one by one, yet I also cannot fail to set them out roughly before you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There are great errors in affairs that cannot be told one by one, yet I also cannot fail to set them out roughly before you.

manualTranslations.zh: 僕始生六七月時，乳母抱弄於書屏下，有指「之」字、「無」字示僕者，僕口未能言，心已默識。
manualTranslations.literal: When I was six or seven months old, my wet nurse held me playing beneath a book screen; someone pointed out the characters "zhi" and "wu" to me; though my mouth could not yet speak, my heart had already silently recognized them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When I was six or seven months old, my wet nurse held me playing beneath a book screen; someone pointed out the characters "zhi" and "wu" to me; though my mouth could not yet speak, my heart had already silently recognized them.

manualTranslations.zh: 後有問此二字者，雖百十其試，而指之不差。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, when asked about these two characters, though tested a hundred or ten times, I pointed without error.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, when asked about these two characters, though tested a hundred or ten times, I pointed without error.

manualTranslations.zh: 則知僕宿習之緣，已在文字中矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Then I knew that the bond of my former learning was already within writing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then I knew that the bond of my former learning was already within writing.

manualTranslations.zh: 及五六歲，便學為詩。
manualTranslations.literal: By five or six I was already learning to write poetry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By five or six I was already learning to write poetry.

manualTranslations.zh: 九歲諳識聲韻。
manualTranslations.literal: At nine I was thoroughly versed in rhyme.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At nine I was thoroughly versed in rhyme.

manualTranslations.zh: 十五六，始知有進士，苦節讀書。
manualTranslations.literal: At fifteen or sixteen I first learned of the jinshi degree and studied books with bitter discipline.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At fifteen or sixteen I first learned of the jinshi degree and studied books with bitter discipline.

manualTranslations.zh: 二十已來，書課賦，夜課書，間又課詩，不遑寢息矣。
manualTranslations.literal: From twenty onward, by day I studied fu, by night books; in between I also studied poetry, with no leisure for sleep and rest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From twenty onward, by day I studied fu, by night books; in between I also studied poetry, with no leisure for sleep and rest.

manualTranslations.zh: 以至於口舌成瘡，手肘成胝。
manualTranslations.literal: It reached the point where my mouth and tongue formed sores and my hands and elbows formed calluses.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It reached the point where my mouth and tongue formed sores and my hands and elbows formed calluses.

manualTranslations.zh: 既壯而膚革不豐盈，未老而齒發早衰白；
manualTranslations.literal: Though grown, my skin and flesh were not full; though not yet old, my teeth and hair prematurely whitened early;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though grown, my skin and flesh were not full; though not yet old, my teeth and hair whitened early;

manualTranslations.zh: 瞀然如飛蠅垂珠在眸子中者，動以萬數，蓋以苦學力文之所致！
manualTranslations.literal: dazed as though flies hanging beads in the pupils, numbering in the tens of thousands—this was caused by bitter study and forcing writing!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: dazed as though flies hanging beads in the pupils, numbering in the tens of thousands—this was caused by bitter study and forcing writing!

manualTranslations.zh: 又自悲家貧多故，年二十七，方從鄉賦。
manualTranslations.literal: Again I grieved for myself that my family was poor and full of troubles; only at twenty-seven did I set out for the provincial examination.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again I grieved that my family was poor and full of troubles; only at twenty-seven did I set out for the provincial examination.

manualTranslations.zh: 既第之後，雖專於科試，亦不廢詩。
manualTranslations.literal: After passing, though I specialized in the civil examinations, I did not abandon poetry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After passing, though I specialized in the civil examinations, I did not abandon poetry.

manualTranslations.zh: 及授校書郎時，已盈三四百首。
manualTranslations.literal: By the time I was appointed collator, I already had three or four hundred pieces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By the time I was appointed collator, I already had three or four hundred pieces.

manualTranslations.zh: 或出示交友如足下輩，見皆謂之工，其實未窺作者之域耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Sometimes I showed them to friends like you; all who saw them called them skilled, but in truth I had not yet glimpsed the domain of the true author.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Sometimes I showed them to friends like you; all who saw them called them skilled, but in truth I had not yet glimpsed the domain of the true author.

manualTranslations.zh: 自登朝來，年齒漸長，閱事漸多。
manualTranslations.literal: Since entering court, my years gradually lengthened and affairs I witnessed gradually grew.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since entering court, my years gradually lengthened and affairs I witnessed gradually grew.

manualTranslations.zh: 每與人言，多詢時務；
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever I spoke with others, I often inquired about current affairs;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever I spoke with others, I often inquired about current affairs;

manualTranslations.zh: 每讀書史，多求理道。
manualTranslations.literal: whenever I read books and histories, I often sought the way and its principles.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: whenever I read books and histories, I often sought the way and its principles.

manualTranslations.zh: 始知文章合為時而著，歌詩合為事而作。
manualTranslations.literal: I then knew that writing should be composed for the age, and songs and poems should be made for affairs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I then knew that writing should be composed for the age, and songs and poems should be made for affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時皇帝初即位，宰府有正人，屢降璽書，訪人急病。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the emperor had just taken the throne; the chief ministers had upright men; repeatedly imperial edicts were sent down, inquiring into people's urgent ills.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had just taken the throne; the chief ministers had upright men; repeatedly imperial edicts were sent down, inquiring into people's urgent ills.

manualTranslations.zh: 僕當此日，擢在翰林，身是諫官，月請諫紙。
manualTranslations.literal: On that day I was promoted to the Hanlin; my person was remonstrance official; monthly I requested remonstrance paper.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On that day I was promoted to the Hanlin; my person was remonstrance official; monthly I requested remonstrance paper.

manualTranslations.zh: 啟奏之間，有可以救濟人病，裨補時闕，而難於指言者，輒詠歌之，欲稍稍進聞於上。
manualTranslations.literal: Between memorials and reports, when there was something that could relieve people's ills, supplement and repair current lacks, yet was hard to speak of directly, I would chant and sing it, wishing gradually to advance it to the emperor's hearing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Between memorials and reports, when there was something that could relieve people's ills, supplement and repair current lacks, yet was hard to speak of directly, I would chant and sing it, wishing gradually to advance it to the emperor's hearing.

manualTranslations.zh: 上以廣宸聽，副憂勤；
manualTranslations.literal: Above, to broaden the imperial ear and assist anxious diligence;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Above, to broaden the imperial ear and assist anxious diligence;

manualTranslations.zh: 次以酬恩獎，塞言責；
manualTranslations.literal: next, to repay favor and reward and fulfill the duty of speech;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: next, to repay favor and reward and fulfill the duty of speech;

manualTranslations.zh: 下以復吾平生之志。
manualTranslations.literal: below, to fulfill my lifelong aim.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: below, to fulfill my lifelong aim.

manualTranslations.zh: 豈圖志未就而悔已生，言未聞而謗已成矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Who would have thought that before the aim was achieved regret was already born, before the words were heard slander was already formed!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that before the aim was achieved regret was already born, before the words were heard slander was already formed!

manualTranslations.zh: 又請為左右終言之。
manualTranslations.literal: Again I ask to speak to the end before you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again I ask to speak to the end before you.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡聞僕《賀雨詩》，眾口籍籍，以為非宜矣；
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever people heard my "Poem on Congratulating the Rain," mouths were all abuzz, thinking it improper;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever people heard my "Poem on Congratulating the Rain," mouths were all abuzz, thinking it improper;

manualTranslations.zh: 聞僕《哭孔戡詩》，眾面脈脈，盡不悅矣；
manualTranslations.literal: when they heard my "Poem on Mourning Kong Kan," faces were all stern, entirely displeased;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they heard my "Poem on Mourning Kong Kan," faces were all stern, entirely displeased;

manualTranslations.zh: 聞《秦中吟》，則權豪貴近者，相目而變色矣；
manualTranslations.literal: when they heard "Chants of Qin," then powerful families and the noble and near exchanged glances and changed color;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they heard "Chants of Qin," then powerful families and the noble and near exchanged glances and changed color;

manualTranslations.zh: 聞《登樂遊園》寄足下詩，則執政柄者扼腕矣；
manualTranslations.literal: when they heard the poem "Ascending Leyou Garden" sent to you, then those who held the reins of government clenched their wrists;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they heard the poem "Ascending Leyou Garden" sent to you, then those who held the reins of government clenched their wrists;

manualTranslations.zh: 聞《宿紫閣村》詩，則握軍要者切齒矣！
manualTranslations.literal: when they heard the poem "Lodging at Zige Village," then those who grasped military power gnashed their teeth!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they heard the poem "Lodging at Zige Village," then those who grasped military power gnashed their teeth!

manualTranslations.zh: 大率如此，不可遍舉。
manualTranslations.literal: Mostly it was like this; it cannot all be cited.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Mostly it was like this; it cannot all be cited.

manualTranslations.zh: 不相與者，號為沽譽，號為詆訐，號為訕謗。
manualTranslations.literal: Those not on good terms with me called it seeking reputation, called it slander, called it ridicule.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those not on good terms with me called it seeking reputation, called it slander, called it ridicule.

manualTranslations.zh: 茍相與者，則如牛僧孺之誡焉。
manualTranslations.literal: If on good terms, then like Niu Sengru's admonition.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If on good terms, then like Niu Sengru's admonition.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃至骨肉妻孥，皆以我為非也。
manualTranslations.literal: It reached the point that flesh and bone, wife and children—all regarded me as wrong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It reached the point that flesh and bone, wife and children—all regarded me as wrong.

manualTranslations.zh: 其不我非者，舉世不過三兩人。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who did not regard me as wrong—in the whole realm were no more than two or three.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who did not regard me as wrong—in the whole realm were no more than two or three.

manualTranslations.zh: 有鄧魴者，見僕詩而喜，無何魴死。
manualTranslations.literal: There was Deng Fang, who saw my poems and rejoiced; before long Fang died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There was Deng Fang, who saw my poems and rejoiced; before long Fang died.

manualTranslations.zh: 有唐衢者，見僕詩而泣，未幾而衢死。
manualTranslations.literal: There was Tang Qu, who saw my poems and wept; before long Qu died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: There was Tang Qu, who saw my poems and wept; before long Qu died.

manualTranslations.zh: 其餘即足下。
manualTranslations.literal: The rest is you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rest is you.

manualTranslations.zh: 足下又十年來困躓若此。
manualTranslations.literal: You too have been thwarted like this for ten years.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You too have been thwarted like this for ten years.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗚呼！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 豈六義四始之風，天將破壞，不可支持耶？
manualTranslations.literal: Is the wind of the six principles and four beginnings of heaven about to be destroyed, beyond support?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Is the wind of the six principles and four beginnings of heaven about to be destroyed, beyond support?

manualTranslations.zh: 抑又不知天意不欲使下人病苦聞於上耶？
manualTranslations.literal: Or again, does one not know whether heaven's intent is unwilling to let the suffering of those below be heard above?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Or again, does one not know whether heaven's intent is unwilling to let the suffering of those below be heard above?

manualTranslations.zh: 不然，何有志於詩者，不利若此之甚也！
manualTranslations.literal: If not, why are those who aspire to poetry so greatly disadvantaged!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If not, why are those who aspire to poetry so greatly disadvantaged!

manualTranslations.zh: 然僕又自思關東一男子耳，除讀書屬文外，其他懵然無知，乃至書畫棋博，可以接群居之歡者，一無通曉，即其愚拙可知矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Yet I again reflect that I am but a man of east of the Pass; apart from reading books and composing writing, in other things I am blankly ignorant—even calligraphy, painting, chess, and gambling, which can join the pleasure of group living, I have not one that I understand; from this my foolish awkwardness can be known!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet I again reflect that I am but a man of east of the Pass; apart from reading books and composing writing, in other things I am blankly ignorant—even calligraphy, painting, chess, and gambling, which can join the pleasure of group living, I have not one that I understand; from this my foolish awkwardness can be known!

manualTranslations.zh: 初應進士時，中朝無緦麻之親，達官無半面之舊；
manualTranslations.literal: When I first answered the jinshi examination, in the central court I had no relative within the mourning-garment bond; among high officials I had no acquaintance of half a face;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When I first answered the jinshi examination, in the central court I had no relative within the mourning-garment bond; among high officials I had no acquaintance of half a face;

manualTranslations.zh: 策蹇步於利足之途，張空拳於戰文之場。
manualTranslations.literal: I urged lame steps on the path of swift feet and brandished empty fists on the battlefield of literary combat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I urged lame steps on the path of swift feet and brandished empty fists on the battlefield of literary combat.

manualTranslations.zh: 十年之間，三登科第，名落眾耳，跡升清貫，出交賢俊，入侍冕旒。
manualTranslations.literal: Within ten years I thrice passed the examinations; my name fell on many ears, my track rose to the clear roster; going out I associated with worthy and eminent men, entering I attended the imperial crown.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Within ten years I thrice passed the examinations; my name fell on many ears, my track rose to the clear roster; going out I associated with worthy and eminent men, entering I attended the imperial crown.

manualTranslations.zh: 始得名於文章，終得罪於文章，亦其宜也。
manualTranslations.literal: At first I gained name through writing; in the end I offended through writing—it is fitting.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At first I gained name through writing; in the end I offended through writing—it is fitting.

manualTranslations.zh: 日者聞親友間說，禮、吏部舉選人，多以僕私試賦判為準的。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently I heard from among kin and friends that the Ministries of Rites and Personnel, in selecting candidates, often took my private examination fu and judgments as the standard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently I heard from among kin and friends that the Ministries of Rites and Personnel, in selecting candidates, often took my private examination fu and judgments as the standard.

manualTranslations.zh: 其餘詩句，亦往往在人口中。
manualTranslations.literal: The rest of the poetic lines too are often on people's lips.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rest of the poetic lines too are often on people's lips.

manualTranslations.zh: 僕恧然自愧，不之信也。
manualTranslations.literal: I was ashamed and doubted it myself, not believing it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I was ashamed and doubted it myself, not believing it.

manualTranslations.zh: 及再來長安，又聞有軍使高霞寓者，欲聘倡妓，妓大誇曰：「我誦得白學士《長恨歌》，豈同他哉？」
manualTranslations.literal: When I came again to Chang'an, I also heard that Military Commissioner Gao Xiayu wished to hire a singing girl; the girl greatly boasted, saying: "I can recite Academician Bai's 'Song of Everlasting Sorrow'—how can I be like the others?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When I came again to Chang'an, I also heard that Military Commissioner Gao Xiayu wished to hire a singing girl; the girl greatly boasted, saying: "I can recite Academician Bai's 'Song of Everlasting Sorrow'—how can I be like the others?"

manualTranslations.zh: 由是增價。
manualTranslations.literal: and thereby raised her price.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: and thereby raised her price.

manualTranslations.zh: 又足下書云：到通州日，見江館柱間有題僕詩者。
manualTranslations.literal: Again your letter says: On reaching Tongzhou, I saw on a pillar of the river lodge someone had inscribed my poem.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again your letter says: On reaching Tongzhou, I saw on a pillar of the river lodge someone had inscribed my poem.

manualTranslations.zh: 何人哉？
manualTranslations.literal: Who was it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Who was it?

manualTranslations.zh: 又昨過漢南日，適遇主人集眾娛樂，他賓諸妓見僕來，指而相顧曰：此是《秦中吟》、《長恨歌》主耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Again yesterday, passing Hannan, I happened to meet the host gathering the crowd for entertainment; other guests and singing girls, seeing me come, pointed and looked at one another, saying: This is the master of "Chants of Qin" and "Song of Everlasting Sorrow."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again yesterday, passing Hannan, I happened to meet the host gathering the crowd for entertainment; other guests and singing girls, seeing me come, pointed and looked at one another, saying: This is the master of "Chants of Qin" and "Song of Everlasting Sorrow."

manualTranslations.zh: 自長安抵江西三四千里，凡鄉校、佛寺、逆旅、行舟之中，往往有題僕詩者；
manualTranslations.literal: From Chang'an to Jiangxi, three or four thousand li—everywhere in village schools, Buddhist temples, inns, and boats on the road, there are often inscriptions of my poems;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Chang'an to Jiangxi, three or four thousand li—everywhere in village schools, Buddhist temples, inns, and boats on the road, there are often inscriptions of my poems;

manualTranslations.zh: 士庶、僧徒、孀婦、處女之口，每有詠僕詩者。
manualTranslations.literal: from the mouths of commoners and gentry, monks, widows, and maidens, there are often those who chant my poems.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: from the mouths of commoners and gentry, monks, widows, and maidens, there are often those who chant my poems.

manualTranslations.zh: 此誠雕篆之戲，不足為多，然今時俗所重，正在此耳。
manualTranslations.literal: This is truly the sport of carving and inlay—not enough to count for much; yet what the present age values lies just in this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is truly the sport of carving and inlay—not enough to count for much; yet what the present age values lies just in this.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖前賢如淵、雲者，前輩如李、杜者，亦未能忘情於其間。
manualTranslations.literal: Though former worthies like Tao and Xie, and elders like Li and Du, also could not forget feeling in this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though former worthies like Tao Yuanming and Xie Lingyun, and elders like Li Bai and Du Fu, also could not forget feeling in this.

manualTranslations.zh: 古人云：「名者公器，不可多取。」
manualTranslations.literal: The ancients said: "Fame is a public vessel; one must not take too much of it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Fame is a public vessel; one must not take too much of it."

manualTranslations.zh: 僕是何者，竊時之名已多。
manualTranslations.literal: What sort of man am I, that I have already stolen more than my share of fame of the age?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What sort of man am I, that I have already stolen more than my share of fame of the age?

manualTranslations.zh: 既竊時名，又欲竊時之富貴，使己為造物者，肯兼與之乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Having already stolen the age's name, I also wish to steal the age's wealth and honor—if I were the Creator, would He grant both together?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Having already stolen the age's name, I also wish to steal the age's wealth and honor—if I were the Creator, would He grant both together?

manualTranslations.zh: 今之屯窮，理固然也。
manualTranslations.literal: Today's hardship and obstruction—by principle it is surely so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today's hardship and obstruction—by principle it is surely so.

manualTranslations.zh: 況詩人多蹇，如陳子昂、杜甫，各授一拾遺，而屯剝至死。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover poets mostly meet with obstruction; like Chen Zi'ang and Du Fu, each was granted a remonstrance post and yet met hardship and stripping unto death.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover poets mostly meet with obstruction; like Chen Zi'ang and Du Fu, each was granted a remonstrance post and yet met hardship and stripping unto death.

manualTranslations.zh: 孟浩然輩不及一命，窮悴終身。
manualTranslations.literal: Men like Meng Haoran did not reach even one appointment and ended their lives in poverty and emaciation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Men like Meng Haoran did not reach even one appointment and ended their lives in poverty and emaciation.

manualTranslations.zh: 近日孟郊六十，終試協律；
manualTranslations.literal: Recently Meng Jiao at sixty finally passed the Harmonizing Office examination;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently Meng Jiao at sixty finally passed the Harmonizing Office examination;

manualTranslations.zh: 張籍五十，未離一太祝。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Ji at fifty had still not left the post of grand libationer.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji at fifty had still not left the post of grand libationer.

manualTranslations.zh: 彼何人哉！
manualTranslations.literal: What sort of men were they!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What sort of men were they!

manualTranslations.zh: 況僕之才又不迨彼。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover my talent again does not reach them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover my talent again does not reach them.

manualTranslations.zh: 今雖謫佐遠郡，而官品至第五，月俸四五萬，寒有衣，饑有食，給身之外，施及家人。
manualTranslations.literal: Though now demoted as assistant in a distant commandery, my official rank reaches the fifth grade, monthly salary four or five myriad; in cold I have clothes, in hunger food; beyond supplying my person, it extends to my family.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though now demoted as assistant in a distant commandery, my official rank reaches the fifth grade, monthly salary four or five myriad; in cold I have clothes, in hunger food; beyond supplying my person, it extends to my family.

manualTranslations.zh: 亦可謂不負白氏子矣。
manualTranslations.literal: One may also say I have not failed the son of the Bai clan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One may also say I have not failed the son of the Bai clan.

manualTranslations.zh: 微之，微之！
manualTranslations.literal: Zhen, Zhen!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhen, Zhen!

manualTranslations.zh: 勿念我哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Do not think of me!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Do not think of me!

manualTranslations.zh: 僕數月來，檢討囊帙中，得新舊詩，各以類分，分為卷目。
manualTranslations.literal: For several months I have examined satchels and folders, obtaining old and new poems, each sorted by category into fascicle titles.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For several months I have examined satchels and folders, obtaining old and new poems, each sorted by category into fascicle titles.

manualTranslations.zh: 自拾遺來，凡所遇所感，關於美刺興比者；
manualTranslations.literal: From remonstrance officer onward, all that I encountered and felt, relating to praise, satire, stirring, and comparison;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From remonstrance officer onward, all that I encountered and felt, relating to praise, satire, stirring, and comparison;

manualTranslations.zh: 又自武德至元和，因事立題，題為《新樂府》者，共一百五十首，謂之諷諭詩。
manualTranslations.literal: again from Wude to Yuanhe, setting titles according to affairs, titled "New Ballads"—altogether one hundred fifty pieces, called satirical-remonstrance poems.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: again from Wude to Yuanhe, setting titles according to affairs, titled "New Ballads"—altogether one hundred fifty pieces, called satirical-remonstrance poems.

manualTranslations.zh: 又或退公，或臥病閑居，知足保和，吟玩性情者一百首，謂之閑適詩。
manualTranslations.literal: Again, whether leaving office or lying ill in leisure residence, content and preserving harmony, chanting and savoring one's nature—one hundred pieces, called leisurely-contentment poems.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again, whether leaving office or lying ill in leisure residence, content and preserving harmony, chanting and savoring one's nature—one hundred pieces, called leisurely-contentment poems.

manualTranslations.zh: 又有事物牽於外，情理動於內，隨感遇而形於嘆詠者一百首，謂之感傷詩。
manualTranslations.literal: Again, when external things pull and inner principle stirs, following encounter and feeling and taking form in sighing chant—one hundred pieces, called poems of stirred feeling.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again, when external things pull and inner principle stirs, following encounter and feeling and taking form in sighing chant—one hundred pieces, called poems of stirred feeling.

manualTranslations.zh: 又有五言、七言、長句、絕句，自百韻至兩韻者，四百餘首，謂之雜律詩。
manualTranslations.literal: Again, five-character, seven-character, long lines, and quatrains, from one hundred rhymes down to two rhymes—more than four hundred pieces, called miscellaneous regulated poems.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again, five-character, seven-character, long lines, and quatrains, from one hundred rhymes down to two rhymes—more than four hundred pieces, called miscellaneous regulated poems.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡為十五卷，約八百首。
manualTranslations.literal: Altogether fifteen fascicles, about eight hundred pieces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Altogether fifteen fascicles, about eight hundred pieces.

manualTranslations.zh: 異時相見，當盡致於執事。
manualTranslations.literal: When we meet another time, I shall present them all to you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When we meet another time, I shall present them all to you.

manualTranslations.zh: 微之，古人云：「窮則獨善其身，達則兼濟天下。」
manualTranslations.literal: Zhen, the ancients said: "In obstruction, cultivate the self alone; in attainment, benefit all under heaven together."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhen, the ancients said: "In obstruction, cultivate the self alone; in attainment, benefit all under heaven together."

manualTranslations.zh: 僕雖不肖，常師此語。
manualTranslations.literal: Though I am unworthy, I constantly take this saying as teacher.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I constantly take this saying as teacher.

manualTranslations.zh: 大丈夫所守者道，所待者時。
manualTranslations.literal: What a great man keeps is the Way; what he awaits is the time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What a great man keeps is the Way; what he awaits is the time.

manualTranslations.zh: 時之來也，為雲龍，為風鵬，勃然突然，陳力以出；
manualTranslations.literal: When the time comes, he becomes cloud and dragon, wind and peng, suddenly bursting forth and offering his strength;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the time comes, he becomes cloud and dragon, wind and peng, suddenly bursting forth and offering his strength;

manualTranslations.zh: 時之不來也，為霧豹，為冥鴻，寂兮寥兮，奉身而退。
manualTranslations.literal: when the time does not come, he becomes mist leopard, dark swan, silent and sparse, withdrawing his person.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when the time does not come, he becomes mist leopard, dark swan, silent and sparse, withdrawing his person.

manualTranslations.zh: 進退出處，何往而不自得哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Advancing, retreating, going out, staying—wherever he goes he is not without self-sufficiency!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Advancing, retreating, going out, staying—wherever he goes he is not without self-sufficiency!

manualTranslations.zh: 故僕志在兼濟，行在獨善，奉而始終之則為道，言而發明之則為詩。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus my aim lies in benefiting all together; my conduct lies in cultivating the self alone; keeping it from beginning to end is the Way; speaking and making it clear is poetry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus my aim lies in benefiting all together; my conduct lies in cultivating the self alone; keeping it from beginning to end is the Way; speaking and making it clear is poetry.

manualTranslations.zh: 謂之諷諭詩，兼濟之志也；
manualTranslations.literal: Calling them satirical-remonstrance poems is the aim of benefiting all together;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Calling them satirical-remonstrance poems is the aim of benefiting all together;

manualTranslations.zh: 謂之閑適詩，獨善之義也。
manualTranslations.literal: calling them leisurely-contentment poems is the meaning of cultivating the self alone.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: calling them leisurely-contentment poems is the meaning of cultivating the self alone.

manualTranslations.zh: 故覽僕詩者，知僕之道焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus those who read my poems know my Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus those who read my poems know my Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 其餘雜律詩，或誘於一時一物，發於一笑一吟，率然成章，非平生所尚者，但以親朋合散之際，取其釋恨佐歡，今銓次之間，未能刪去。
manualTranslations.literal: The rest of the miscellaneous regulated poems—sometimes tempted by one time or one thing, arising from one laugh or one chant, composed on the spur of the moment, not what I esteem in life—are only for the moment when kin and friends gather or part, taking them to release resentment and assist pleasure; in present selection and ordering I have not been able to delete them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The rest of the miscellaneous regulated poems—sometimes tempted by one time or one thing, arising from one laugh or one chant, composed on the spur of the moment, not what I esteem in life—are only for the moment when kin and friends gather or part, taking them to release resentment and assist pleasure; in present selection and ordering I have not been able to delete them.

manualTranslations.zh: 他時有為我編集斯文者，略之可也。
manualTranslations.literal: If another time someone compiles this writing for me, he may omit them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If another time someone compiles this writing for me, he may omit them.

manualTranslations.zh: 微之，夫貴耳賤目，榮古陋今，人之大情也。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhen, to honor the ear and despise the eye, to glorify the old and despise the present—this is the great feeling of men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhen, to honor the ear and despise the eye, to glorify the old and despise the present—this is the great feeling of men.

manualTranslations.zh: 僕不能遠征古舊，如近歲韋蘇州歌行，才麗之外，頗近興諷；
manualTranslations.literal: I cannot go far to cite antiquity; take in recent years Wei Suzhou's song-lines—beyond talent and beauty, they are quite near stirring satire;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I cannot go far to cite antiquity; take in recent years Wei Yingwu's song-lines—beyond talent and beauty, they are quite near stirring satire;

manualTranslations.zh: 其五言詩，又高雅閑淡，自成一家之體，今之秉筆者誰能及之？
manualTranslations.literal: his five-character poems again are lofty, elegant, leisurely, and plain, forming a style of their own—among those who wield the brush today, who can reach him?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: his five-character poems again are lofty, elegant, leisurely, and plain, forming a style of their own—among those who wield the brush today, who can reach him?

manualTranslations.zh: 然當蘇州在時，人亦未甚愛重，必待身後，人始貴之。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet when Suzhou was alive, people also did not greatly love and esteem him; it had to wait until after his death before people began to value him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet when Suzhou was alive, people also did not greatly love and esteem him; it had to wait until after his death before people began to value him.

manualTranslations.zh: 今僕之詩，人所愛者，悉不過雜律詩與《長恨歌》已下耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Today what people love in my poems is entirely no more than miscellaneous regulated poems and "Song of Everlasting Sorrow" and below.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today what people love in my poems is entirely no more than miscellaneous regulated poems and "Song of Everlasting Sorrow" and below.

manualTranslations.zh: 時之所重，僕之所輕。
manualTranslations.literal: What the age values is what I lightly esteem.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What the age values is what I lightly esteem.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於諷諭者，意激而言質；
manualTranslations.literal: As for satirical-remonstrance poems, the intent is sharp and the words plain;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for satirical-remonstrance poems, the intent is sharp and the words plain;

manualTranslations.zh: 閑適者，思淡而辭迂。
manualTranslations.literal: as for leisurely-contentment poems, the thought is bland and the diction circuitous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: as for leisurely-contentment poems, the thought is bland and the diction circuitous.

manualTranslations.zh: 以質合迂，宜人之不愛也。
manualTranslations.literal: Plain joined with circuitous—it is fitting that people do not love them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Plain joined with circuitous—it is fitting that people do not love them.

manualTranslations.zh: 今所愛者，並世而生，獨足下耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who love them now, born in the same age—only you.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who love them now, born in the same age—only you.

manualTranslations.zh: 然百千年後，安知復無如足下者出，而知愛我詩哉？
manualTranslations.literal: Yet a hundred or a thousand years hence, who knows whether again someone like you will appear and know to love my poems?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet a hundred or a thousand years hence, who knows whether again someone like you will appear and know to love my poems?

manualTranslations.zh: 故自八九年來，與足下小通則以詩相戒，小窮則以詩相勉，索居則以詩相慰，同處則以詩相娛。
manualTranslations.literal: Thus from eight or nine years ago, with you when slightly in accord I admonish through poetry, when slightly in hardship I encourage through poetry, when living apart I console through poetry, when together I delight through poetry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thus from eight or nine years ago, with you when slightly in accord I admonish through poetry, when slightly in hardship I encourage through poetry, when living apart I console through poetry, when together I delight through poetry.

manualTranslations.zh: 知吾罪吾，率以詩也。
manualTranslations.literal: Knowing me or blaming me—in all cases it is through poetry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Knowing me or blaming me—in all cases it is through poetry.

manualTranslations.zh: 如今年春遊城南時，與足下馬上相戲，因各誦新艷小律，不雜他篇，自皇子陂歸昭國裏，叠吟遞唱，不絕聲者二十里餘。
manualTranslations.literal: Like this spring when touring south of the city, with you jesting on horseback, we each recited new and gorgeous short regulated pieces, not mixing other pieces; from Prince's Mound returning to Zhaoguo Ward, chanting and singing in turn, the sound unbroken for more than twenty li.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Like this spring when touring south of the city, with you jesting on horseback, we each recited new and gorgeous short regulated pieces, not mixing other pieces; from Prince's Mound returning to Zhaoguo Ward, chanting and singing in turn, the sound unbroken for more than twenty li.

manualTranslations.zh: 攀、李在傍，無所措口。
manualTranslations.literal: Pan and Li were at the side, with no place to put their mouths.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Pan and Li were at the side, with no place to put their mouths.

manualTranslations.zh: 知我者以為詩仙，不知我者以為詩魔。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who knew me called me poetry immortal; those who did not know me called me poetry demon.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who knew me called me poetry immortal; those who did not know me called me poetry demon.

manualTranslations.zh: 何則？
manualTranslations.literal: Why?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why?

manualTranslations.zh: 勞心靈，役聲氣，連朝接夕，不自知其苦，非魔而何？
manualTranslations.literal: Toiling the mind and spirit, enslaving breath and sound, connecting morning to evening, not knowing one's own suffering—is that not demon?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Toiling the mind and spirit, enslaving breath and sound, connecting morning to evening, not knowing one's own suffering—is that not demon?

manualTranslations.zh: 偶同人當美景，或花時宴罷，或月夜酒酣，一詠一吟，不覺老之將至。
manualTranslations.literal: By chance with companions amid fine scenery, or when the flower-season banquet ends, or when on a moonlit night the wine is deep, one chant and one recitation—before one knows it old age is near.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: By chance with companions amid fine scenery, or when the flower-season banquet ends, or when on a moonlit night the wine is deep, one chant and one recitation—before one knows it old age is near.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖驂鸞鶴、遊蓬瀛者之適，無以加於此焉，又非仙而何？
manualTranslations.literal: Though the ease of riding paired cranes or roaming Penglai cannot be added to beyond this—again, is that not immortal?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though the ease of riding paired cranes or roaming Penglai cannot be added to beyond this—again, is that not immortal?

manualTranslations.zh: 微之，微之！
manualTranslations.literal: Zhen, Zhen!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhen, Zhen!

manualTranslations.zh: 此吾所以與足下外形骸、脫蹤跡、傲軒鼎、輕人寰者，又以此也。
manualTranslations.literal: This is why I with you shed bodily form, cast off tracks, disdain regalia and tripods, and lightly esteem the human realm—again for this reason.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This is why I with you shed bodily form, cast off tracks, disdain regalia and tripods, and lightly esteem the human realm—again for this reason.

manualTranslations.zh: 當此之時，足下興有餘力，且欲與僕悉索還往中詩，取其尤長者，如張十八古樂府，李二十新歌行，盧、楊二秘書律詩，竇七、元八絕句，博搜精掇，編而次之，號為《元白往還集》。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time you still had surplus energy and also wished with me to search thoroughly all the poems exchanged back and forth, take the especially fine among them—like Zhang Eighteen's old ballads, Li Twenty's new song-lines, Secretaries Lu and Yang's regulated poems, Dou Seven and Yuan Eight's quatrains—search broadly, select finely, compile and arrange them, and title them "Collection of Yuan and Bai's Exchanges."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time you still had surplus energy and also wished with me to search thoroughly all the poems exchanged back and forth, take the especially fine among them—like Zhang Eighteen's old ballads, Li Twenty's new song-lines, Secretaries Lu and Yang's regulated poems, Dou Seven and Yuan Eight's quatrains—search broadly, select finely, compile and arrange them, and title them "Collection of Yuan and Bai's Exchanges."

manualTranslations.zh: 眾君子得擬議於此者，莫不踴躍欣喜，以為盛事。
manualTranslations.literal: The gentlemen who obtained a place to discuss this were all leaping with joy, taking it as a great event.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The gentlemen who obtained a place to discuss this were all leaping with joy, taking it as a great event.

manualTranslations.zh: 嗟乎！
manualTranslations.literal: Alas!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas!

manualTranslations.zh: 言未終而足下左轉，不數月而僕又繼行，心期索然，何日成就？
manualTranslations.literal: Before the words were finished you were transferred left; within a few months I followed in going; the heart's expectation was desolate—what day would it be achieved?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before the words were finished you were transferred left; within a few months I followed in going; the heart's expectation was desolate—what day would it be achieved?

manualTranslations.zh: 又可為之太息矣！
manualTranslations.literal: Again one may sigh deeply over this!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again one may sigh deeply over this!

manualTranslations.zh: 僕常語足下，凡人為文，私於自是，不忍於割截，或失於繁多。
manualTranslations.literal: I have often told you: for any person composing writing, he is partial to his own work, unwilling to cut and trim, or errs in being too numerous.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have often told you: for any person composing writing, he is partial to his own work, unwilling to cut and trim, or errs in being too numerous.

manualTranslations.zh: 其間妍媸，益又自惑。
manualTranslations.literal: Among them the beautiful and ugly—further he himself is confused.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among them the beautiful and ugly—further he himself is confused.

manualTranslations.zh: 必待交友有公鑒無姑息者，討論而削奪之，然後繁簡當否，得其中矣。
manualTranslations.literal: One must wait for a friend who has fair judgment without indulgence, discuss and pare away, and only then whether prolix or concise is appropriate can reach the mean.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One must wait for a friend who has fair judgment without indulgence, discuss and pare away, and only then whether prolix or concise is appropriate can reach the mean.

manualTranslations.zh: 況僕與足下，為文尤患其多。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover I with you, in writing especially fear its being too much.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover I with you, in writing especially fear its being too much.

manualTranslations.zh: 己尚病，況他人乎？
manualTranslations.literal: I myself still find it sickening—how much more others?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I myself still find it sickening—how much more others?

manualTranslations.zh: 今且各纂詩筆，粗為卷第，待與足下相見日，各出所有，終前志焉。
manualTranslations.literal: For now let each compile poetic drafts, roughly into fascicles; wait until the day we meet face to face, each bring out what he has, and fulfill the former aim.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: For now let each compile poetic drafts, roughly into fascicles; wait until the day we meet face to face, each bring out what he has, and fulfill the former aim.

manualTranslations.zh: 又不知相遇是何年，相見是何地，溘然而至，則如之何？
manualTranslations.literal: Again I do not know in what year we will meet, in what place we will see each other; if suddenly it comes, then what is to be done?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Again I do not know in what year we will meet, in what place we will see each other; if suddenly it comes, then what is to be done?

manualTranslations.zh: 微之知我心哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Zhen knows my heart!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Zhen knows my heart!

manualTranslations.zh: 潯陽臘月，江風苦寒，歲暮鮮歡，夜長少睡。
manualTranslations.literal: Xunyang, twelfth month; river wind bitter cold; year's end with little joy; night long and little sleep.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xunyang, twelfth month; river wind bitter cold; year's end with little joy; night long and little sleep.

manualTranslations.zh: 引筆鋪紙，悄然燈前，有念則書，言無銓次。
manualTranslations.literal: I draw the brush and spread paper, quietly before the lamp; when there is a thought I write; the words are without order of selection.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I draw the brush and spread paper, quietly before the lamp; when there is a thought I write; the words are without order of selection.

manualTranslations.zh: 勿以繁雜為倦，且以代一夕之話言也。
manualTranslations.literal: Do not weary at prolixity; let it stand in place of one evening's conversation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Do not weary at prolixity; let it stand in place of one evening's conversation.

sourceRange.text: 翰林學士韋處厚上言曰：臣聞汲黯在朝，淮南不敢謀叛；幹木處魏，諸侯不敢加兵。王霸之理，皆以一士而止百萬之師，以一賢而制千里之難。臣伏以裴度勛高中夏，聲播外夷，廷湊、克融皆憚其用，吐蕃、回鶻悉服其名。今若置之巖廊，委其參決，西夷北虜，未測中華；河北山東，必稟廟算。況幽、鎮未靜，尤資重臣。管仲曰：「人離而聽之則愚，合而聽之則聖。」理亂之本，非有他術，順人則理，違人則亂。伏承陛下當食嘆息，恨無蕭、曹。今有一裴度尚不留驅使，此馮生所以感悟漢文，雲雖有廉頗、李牧不能用也。夫禦宰相，當委之信之，親之禮之。如於事不效，於國無勞，則置之散僚，黜之遠郡。如此，則在位者不敢不勵，將進者不敢茍求。陛下存終始之分，但不永棄，則君臣之厚也。今進皆負四海責望，退不失六部尚書，不肖者無因而勸。臣與李逢吉素無讎嫌，臣嘗被裴度因事貶黜。今之所陳，上答聖明，下達君議，披肝感激，伏地涕流。伏望鑒臣愛君，矜臣體國，則天下幸甚。

sourceRange.text: 翌日，詔曰：輔弼之臣，軍國是賴。興化致理，秉鈞以居。取威定功，則分閫而出。所以同君臣之體，一中外之任焉。屬者問罪汝南，致誅淮右，蓋欲刷其汙俗，吊彼頑人。雖挈地求生者實繁有徒，而嬰城執迷者未翦其類，何獸困而猶鬥，豈鳥窮之無歸歟？由是遙聽鼓鼙，更張琴瑟，煩我臺席，董茲戎旃。朝議大夫、守中書侍郎、同平章事、飛騎尉、賜紫金魚袋裴度，為時降生，協朕夢卜，精辨宣力，堅明納忠。當軸而才謀老成，運籌而智略有定。司其樞務，備知四方之事；付以兵要，必得萬人之心。是用禱於上玄，揀此吉日，帶丞相之印綬，所以尊其名；賜諸侯之斧鉞，所以重其命。爾宜宣布清問，恢壯皇猷，感勵連營，蕩平多壘，招懷孤疾，字撫夷傷。況淮西一軍，素效忠節，過海赴難，史冊書勛。建中初，攻破襄陽，擒滅崇義。比者脅於兇逆，歸命無由。每念前勞，常思安撫。所以內輟輔臣，俾為師率，實欲保全慰諭，各使得宜。汝往欽哉！無越我丕訓。可門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事、蔡州刺史，充彰義軍節度、申光蔡觀察等使，仍充淮西宣慰招討處置使。

sourceRange.text: 四年六月，詔曰：昔漢以孔光降置幾之詔，晉以鄭沖申奉冊之命。雖優隆耆德，顯重元臣，而議政不及於咨詢，用禮止在於安逸。朕勤求至理，所寶唯賢，顧諟舊勞，敢不加敬。由是委宰制於大政，釋參決於繁務。時因聽斷，誠望弼諧，遷秩上公，式是殊寵。特進、守司徒、兼門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事，充集賢殿大學士、上柱國、晉國公、食邑三千戶、食實封三百戶裴度，稟河嶽之英靈，受乾坤之間氣；珪璋特達，城府洞開。外茂九功，內苞一德。器為社稷之鎮，才實邦國之楨。故能祗事累朝，宣融景化。在憲宗時，掃滌區宇，爾則有出車殄寇之勛；在穆宗時，混同文軌，爾則有參戎入輔之績；在敬宗時，阜康兆庶，爾則有活國庇人之勤。迨弼朕躬，總齊方夏，爾則有吊伐底寧之力。皆不遺廟算，布在簡編，功利及人，不可悉數。而朝論益重，我心實知。方用臯陶之謨，適值留侯之疾，瀝懇牢讓，備列奏章，塞詔上言，動形顏色。果聞勿藥之喜，更俟調鼎之功，而體力未和，音容尚阻。不有優崇之命，孰彰寵待之恩？宜其協贊機衡，弘敷教典；論道而儀刑卿士，宣德而鎮撫華夷。嗇養精神，保綏福履，為國元老，毗予一人。可司徒、平章軍國重事，待疾損日，每三日、五日一度入中書。散官勛封實封如故。仍備禮冊命。

sourceRange.text: 天下皆言稹恃寵熒惑上聽，度在軍上疏論之曰：臣聞主聖臣直。今既遇聖主，輒為直臣，上答殊私，下塞群謗，誓除國蠹，無以家為。茍獻替之可行，何性命之足惜？伏惟皇帝陛下恭承丕業，光啟雄圖，方殄頑人之風，以立太平之事。而逆豎構亂，震驚山東；奸臣作朋，撓敗國政。陛下欲掃蕩幽、鎮，宜肅清朝廷。何者？為患有大小，議事有先後。河朔逆賊，只亂山東；禁闈奸臣，必亂天下。是則河朔患小，禁闈患大。小者，臣等與諸戎臣必能翦滅；大者，非陛下制斷，非陛下覺悟，無計驅除。今文武百僚，中外萬品，有心者無不憤忿，有口者無不咨嗟。直以威權方重，獎用方深，無所畏避，不敢抵觸，恐事未行禍已及，不為國計，且為身謀。臣比者猶思隱忍，不願發明。一則以罪惡如山，怨謗如雷，伏料聖明，必自誅殛；一則以四方無事，萬樞且過，雖紀綱潛壞，賄賂公行，俟其貫盈，必自顛覆。今屬兇徒擾攘，宸衷憂軫，凡有制命，計於安危。痛此奸邪，恣行欺罔，幹亂聖略，非止一途。又翰苑舊臣，結為朋黨，陛下聽其所說，更訪於近臣，私相計會，更唱叠和，蔽惑聰明。所以臣自兵興已來，所陳章疏，事皆要切，所奉書詔，多有參差。惜陛下委付之意不輕，被奸臣抑損之事不少。臣素知佞幸，亦無讎嫌，只是昨者，臣請乘傳詣闕，面陳戎事，奸臣之徒，最所畏懼。知臣若到御坐之前，必能悉數其過，以此百計止臣此行。臣又請領兵齊進，逐便攻討，奸臣之黨，曲加阻礙。恐臣統率諸道，或有成功，進退皆受羈牽，意見悉遭蔽塞。復共一二憸狡，同辭合力。或兩道招撫，逗留旬時；或遣蔚州行營，拖曳日月。但欲令臣失所，使臣無成，則天下理亂，山東勝負，悉不顧矣。為臣事君，一至於此。且陛下左右前後，忠良至多，亦有熟會典章，亦有飽諳師旅，足得任使，何獨斯人？以臣愚見，若朝中奸臣盡去，則河朔逆賊，不討而自平；若朝中奸臣尚在，則逆賊縱平無益。臣讀國史，知代宗朝蕃戎侵軼，直犯都城。代宗不知，蓋被程元振蒙蔽，幾危社稷。當時柳伉，乃太常一博士耳，猶能抗表歸罪，為國除害。今臣年處，兼總將相，豈肯坐觀兇邪，有曀日月。不勝感憤嫉惡之至！謹附中使趙奉國以聞。倘陛下未信忠言，猶惑奸黨，伏乞出臣此表，令三事大夫與百僚集議。彼不受責，臣合伏辜，天鑒孔明，照臣肝血。但得天下之人，知臣不負陛下，則雖死之日，猶生之年。

sourceRange.text: 潾上疏諫曰：臣聞除天下之害者，受天下之利；共天下之樂者，饗天下之福。故上自黃帝、顓頊、堯、舜、禹、湯，下及周文王、武王，鹹以功濟生靈，德配天地，故天皆報之以上壽，垂祚於無疆。伏見陛下以大孝安宗廟，以至仁牧黎元。自踐祚已來，刬積代之妖兇，開削平之洪業。而禮敬宰輔，待以終始；內能大斷，外寬小故。夫此神功聖化，皆自古聖主明君所不及，陛下躬親行之，實光映千古矣。是則天地神祇，必報陛下以山嶽之壽；宗廟聖靈，必福陛下以億萬之齡；四海蒼生，鹹祈陛下以覆載之永。自然萬靈保祐，聖壽無疆。伏見自去年已來，諸處頻薦藥術之士，有韋山甫、柳泌等，或更相稱引，迄今狂謬，薦送漸多。臣伏以真仙有道之士，皆匿其名姓，無求於代，潛遁山林，滅影雲壑，唯恐人見，唯懼人聞。豈肯幹謁公卿，自鬻其術？今者所有誇炫藥術者，必非知道之士。鹹為求利而來，自言飛煉為神，以誘權貴賄賂。大言怪論，驚聽惑時，及其假偽敗露，曾不恥於逃遁。如此情狀，豈可保信其術，親餌其藥哉？《禮》曰：「夫人，食味別聲，被色而生者也。」《春秋左氏傳》曰：「味以行氣，氣以實誌。」又曰：「水火醯醢鹽梅，以烹魚肉。宰夫和之，齊之以味；君子食之，以平其心。」夫三牲五谷，稟自五行，發為五味，蓋天地生之所以奉人也，是以聖人節而食之，以致康強逢吉之福。若夫藥石者，前聖以之療疾，蓋非常食之物。況金石皆含酷烈熱毒之性，加以燒治，動經歲月，既兼烈火之氣，必恐難為防制。若乃遠征前史，則秦、漢之君，皆信方士，如盧生、徐福、欒大、李少君，其後皆奸偽事發，其藥竟無所成。事著《史記》、《漢書》，皆可驗視。《禮》曰：「君之藥，臣先嘗之；親之藥，子先嘗之。」臣子一也，臣願所有金石，煉藥人及所薦之人，皆先服一年，以考其真偽，則自然明驗矣。伏惟元和聖文神武法天應道皇帝陛下，合日月照臨之明，稟乾元利貞之德，崇正若指南，受諫如轉規，是必發精金之刃，斷可疑之網。所有藥術虛誕之徒，伏乞特賜罷遣，禁其幻惑。使浮雲盡徹，朗日增輝；道化侔羲、農，悠久配天地，實在此矣。伏以貞觀已來，左右起居有褚遂良、杜正倫、呂向、韋述等，鹹能竭其忠誠，悉心規諫。小臣謬參侍從，職奉起居，侍從之中，最近左右。傳曰：「近臣盡規。」則近侍之臣，上達忠款，實其本職也。
