manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, reverent and frugal in seeking good order, in the second year of Taihe the examination for worthy and good men said, "I have heard that the governance of ancient sage-kings was darkly silent and non-active; seated upright they pondered the Way, molded the people's hearts to dwell in simplicity, concentrated daily use without interfering, enriched those below to establish the root, and extended sincerity to build the center."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, reverent and frugal in seeking good order, in 828 the examination for worthy and good men said, "I have heard that the governance of ancient sage-kings was darkly silent and non-active; seated upright they pondered the Way, molded the people's hearts to dwell in simplicity, concentrated daily use without interfering, enriched those below to establish the root, and extended sincerity to build the center.

manualTranslations.zh: 是天人通，隂陽和，俗躋仁壽，物無疵癘。
manualTranslations.literal: Then Heaven and man were in communication, yin and yang were harmonious, custom reached benevolence and longevity, and things had no blemish or pestilence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then Heaven and man were in communication, yin and yang were harmonious, custom reached benevolence and longevity, and things had no blemish or pestilence.

manualTranslations.zh: 噫，盛徳之所臻，夐乎莫可及也。
manualTranslations.literal: Alas, what supreme virtue reaches is far beyond compare.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Alas, what supreme virtue reaches is far beyond compare.

manualTranslations.zh: 三代令王，質文迭䆒，百偽滋熾，風流寖微，自漢而降，定徴蓋寡。
manualTranslations.literal: The worthy kings of the Three Dynasties alternated substance and ornament; a hundred falsities grew fierce, refined custom gradually declined; from Han downward, fixed signs were few indeed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The worthy kings of the Three Dynasties alternated substance and ornament; a hundred falsities grew fierce, refined custom gradually declined; from Han downward, fixed signs were few indeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 朕顧惟昧道，祗荷丕構，奉若謨訓，不敢怠荒。
manualTranslations.literal: I reflect that my understanding of the Way is dim; I reverently bear the great edifice, follow the instructions, and dare not be idle or negligent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I reflect that my understanding of the Way is dim; I reverently bear the great edifice, follow the instructions, and dare not be idle or negligent.

manualTranslations.zh: 任賢惕厲，宵衣旰食，詎追三五之遐軌，庻紹祖宗之鴻緒。
manualTranslations.literal: Employing the worthy with vigilance, dressing at dawn and eating at dusk, how can I not pursue the distant tracks of the Three and Five, that I may continue the grand line of the ancestors?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Employing the worthy with vigilance, dressing at dawn and eating at dusk, how can I not pursue the distant tracks of the Three and Five, that I may continue the grand line of the ancestors?

manualTranslations.zh: 而心有所未逹，行有所未孚，由中及外，闕政斯廣。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet in my heart there are things not attained, in my conduct things not trusted; from center to outer reaches, neglected governance is wide.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet in my heart there are things not attained, in my conduct things not trusted; from center to outer reaches, neglected governance is wide.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以人不率化，氣或堙厄，災旱竟歲，播植愆時。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore people do not follow transformation; qi sometimes is blocked in distress; drought and disaster last the whole year; planting misses its season.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore people do not follow transformation; qi sometimes is blocked in distress; drought and disaster last the whole year; planting misses its season.

manualTranslations.zh: 國廪罕蓄，乏九年之儲；
manualTranslations.literal: The state granaries rarely store; there is a lack of nine years' reserves;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The state granaries rarely store; there is a lack of nine years' reserves;

manualTranslations.zh: 吏道多端，微三載之績。
manualTranslations.literal: The way of officials is many-branched; the achievement of three years' service is slight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The way of officials is many-branched; the achievement of three years' service is slight.

manualTranslations.zh: 京師，諸夏之本也，将以觀理，而豪猾時踰檢；
manualTranslations.literal: The capital is the root of all the Xia; I intend to observe governance there, yet the powerful and cunning sometimes overstep bounds;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The capital is the root of all the Xia; I intend to observe governance there, yet the powerful and cunning sometimes overstep bounds;

manualTranslations.zh: 太學，明教之源也，期於變風，而生徒多惰業。
manualTranslations.literal: The Imperial Academy is the source of enlightened teaching; I expect to change custom there, yet students are mostly idle in their studies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy is the source of enlightened teaching; I expect to change custom there, yet students are mostly idle in their studies.

manualTranslations.zh: 列郡在乎頒條，而干禁或未絕；
manualTranslations.literal: Prefectures depend on promulgating regulations, yet violations of prohibitions are not yet ended;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prefectures depend on promulgating regulations, yet violations of prohibitions are not yet ended;

manualTranslations.zh: 百工在乎按度，而滛巧或未衰。
manualTranslations.literal: The hundred crafts depend on measuring standards, yet licentious craft has not yet declined.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The hundred crafts depend on measuring standards, yet licentious craft has not yet declined.

manualTranslations.zh: 俗墮風靡，積訛成蠧。
manualTranslations.literal: Custom falls and the wind scatters; accumulated error becomes pest.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Custom falls and the wind scatters; accumulated error becomes pest.

manualTranslations.zh: 其擇官濟理也，聽人以言，則枝葉難辨；
manualTranslations.literal: In selecting officials to aid governance, if one listens to people's words, branches and leaves are hard to distinguish;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In selecting officials to aid governance, if one listens to people's words, branches and leaves are hard to distinguish;

manualTranslations.zh: 御下以法，則耻格不形。
manualTranslations.literal: In governing subordinates by law, shame and correction do not appear.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In governing subordinates by law, shame and correction do not appear.

manualTranslations.zh: 其阜財發號也，生之寡而食之衆，煩於令而鮮於理。
manualTranslations.literal: In enriching wealth and issuing orders, those born are few and those who eat are many; orders are troublesome while governance is scarce.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In enriching wealth and issuing orders, those born are few and those who eat are many; orders are troublesome while governance is scarce.

manualTranslations.zh: 思所以䆒此繆盭，致之治平，兹心浩然，若渉泉水。
manualTranslations.literal: I think how to untie these knots and errors and bring about ordered peace; this heart is vast, as if wading a spring stream.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I think how to untie these knots and errors and bring about ordered peace; this heart is vast, as if wading a spring stream.

manualTranslations.zh: 故前詔有司，博延群彦，佇啓宿懵，冀臻時雍。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore I previously ordered the offices to broadly extend eminent men, await the opening of long-held confusion, and hope to reach timely harmony.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore I previously ordered the offices to broadly extend eminent men, await the opening of long-held confusion, and hope to reach timely harmony.

manualTranslations.zh: 子大夫識逹古今，明於康濟，造廷待問，副朕虛懷。
manualTranslations.literal: You, grand masters, know past and present and are clear on bringing relief; come to court and await questioning to match my open mind.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You, grand masters, know past and present and are clear on bringing relief; come to court and await questioning to match my open mind.

manualTranslations.zh: 必當箴主之闕，辨政之疵，明綱條之致紊，稽富庶之所急。
manualTranslations.literal: You must admonish the ruler's faults, distinguish flaws in governance, clarify what causes laws and regulations to fall into disorder, and examine what the prosperous and numerous urgently need.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You must admonish the ruler's faults, distinguish flaws in governance, clarify what causes laws and regulations to fall into disorder, and examine what the prosperous and numerous urgently need.

manualTranslations.zh: 何施斯革於前弊，何澤斯惠乎下土，何脩而理古可近，何道而和氣克充，推之本源，著於條對。
manualTranslations.literal: What measure will reform former abuses? What grace will benefit the people below? What cultivation will bring near the governance of antiquity? What Way will fully fill harmonious qi? Trace to the root source and set forth in numbered replies.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What measure will reform former abuses? What grace will benefit the people below? What cultivation will bring near the governance of antiquity? What Way will fully fill harmonious qi? Trace to the root source and set forth in numbered replies.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於夷吾輕重之權，孰輔於理；
manualTranslations.literal: As for Guan Zhong's weighty and light authority, what aids governance?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for Guan Zhong's weighty and light authority, what aids governance?

manualTranslations.zh: 嚴尤底定之䇿，孰叶於時；
manualTranslations.literal: As for Yan You's plan to settle the frontier, what fits the times?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for Yan You's plan to settle the frontier, what fits the times?

manualTranslations.zh: 元凱之考課何先；
manualTranslations.literal: In Yuankai's examination of achievement, what comes first?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Yuankai's examination of achievement, what comes first?

manualTranslations.zh: 叔子之克平何務。
manualTranslations.literal: In Shujizi's task of pacification, what is the business?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In Shujizi's task of pacification, what is the business?

manualTranslations.zh: 推此龜鏡，擇乎中庸，期在洽聞，朕將親覽。
manualTranslations.literal: Push this mirror of tortoise shell; choose the mean; expect comprehensive knowledge—I shall personally review.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Push this mirror of tortoise shell; choose the mean; expect comprehensive knowledge—I shall personally review.

manualTranslations.zh: 時對策者百餘人，所對止循常務，唯蕡切論黄門太横，将危宗社，對曰：臣誠不佞，有匡國致君之術，無位而不得行；
manualTranslations.literal: At the time more than a hundred men answered the examination; their replies merely followed routine affairs. Only Fen sharply discussed the Yellow Gate's excessive power, which would endanger the altars of state. He replied, "Your subject is truly unworthy, yet has the art of stabilizing the state and serving the ruler, but no position from which to carry it out;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time more than a hundred men answered the examination; their replies merely followed routine affairs. Only Fen sharply discussed the Yellow Gate's excessive power, which would endanger the altars of state. He replied, "Your subject is truly unworthy, yet has the art of stabilizing the state and serving the ruler, but no position from which to carry it out;

manualTranslations.zh: 有犯顏敢諫之心，無路而不得進。
manualTranslations.literal: he has the heart to offend the countenance and dare remonstrate, but no road by which to advance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: he has the heart to offend the countenance and dare remonstrate, but no road by which to advance.

manualTranslations.zh: 但懷憤鬱抑，思有時而一發耳。
manualTranslations.literal: He only harbors indignant depression, thinking to release it at some moment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He only harbors indignant depression, thinking to release it at some moment.

manualTranslations.zh: 常欲與庶人議於道，商旅謗於市，得通上聽，一悟主心，雖被妖言之罪，無所悔焉。
manualTranslations.literal: He has often wished to discuss with common people on the road and have travelers complain in the market, that it might reach the ruler's hearing and awaken the ruler's heart in one stroke—even if punished for perverse speech, he would not regret it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He has often wished to discuss with common people on the road and have travelers complain in the market, that it might reach the ruler's hearing and awaken the ruler's heart in one stroke—even if punished for perverse speech, he would not regret it.

manualTranslations.zh: 況逢陛下以至德嗣興，以大明垂照，詢求過闕，咨訪謨猷，制詔中外，舉直言極諫者。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, encountering Your Majesty succeeding with supreme virtue and shining with great brilliance, seeking faults and oversights and consulting on plans, issuing edicts throughout the realm calling for forthright speech and extreme remonstrance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover, encountering Your Majesty succeeding with supreme virtue and shining with great brilliance, seeking faults and oversights and consulting on plans, issuing edicts throughout the realm calling for forthright speech and extreme remonstrance.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣旣辱斯舉，專承大問，敢不悉意以言。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject has been honored with this summons and specially receives this great questioning—how dare he not speak with full intent?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your subject has been honored with this summons and specially receives this great questioning—how dare he not speak with full intent?

manualTranslations.zh: 至於上之所忌，時之所禁，權倖之所諱惡，有司之所與奪，臣愚不識。
manualTranslations.literal: As for what the ruler fears, what the times forbid, what favorites hate, and what offices grant or withhold, your subject in his foolishness does not know.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for what the ruler fears, what the times forbid, what favorites hate, and what offices grant or withhold, your subject in his foolishness does not know.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟陛下少加優容，不使聖朝有讜直而受戮者，乃天下之幸也。
manualTranslations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will grant a little indulgence and not let the sagely court have forthright men who are punished—this would be the fortune of the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will grant a little indulgence and not let the sagely court have forthright men who are punished—this would be the fortune of the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 謹昧死以對。
manualTranslations.literal: I respectfully risk death in reply.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully risk death in reply.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟聖策，有思先古之理，念玄默之化，將欲通天人以齊俗，和陰陽以煦物，見陛下慕道之深也。
manualTranslations.literal: I humbly consider the sagely question: there is thought of the governance of ancient sages and remembrance of darkly silent transformation, intending to join Heaven and man to equalize custom and harmonize yin and yang to warm things—this shows how deeply Your Majesty cherishes the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly consider the sagely question: there is thought of the governance of ancient sages and remembrance of darkly silent transformation, intending to join Heaven and man to equalize custom and harmonize yin and yang to warm things—this shows how deeply Your Majesty cherishes the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣以為哲王之理，其則不遠，惟陛下致之之道何如爾。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject thinks the governance of a wise king—the rule is not far off; it depends only on how Your Majesty brings it about.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your subject thinks the governance of a wise king—the rule is not far off; it depends only on how Your Majesty brings it about.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟聖策，有祗荷丕構而不敢荒寧，奉若謨訓而罔有怠忽，見陛下憂勞之志也。
manualTranslations.literal: I humbly consider the sagely question: there is reverently bearing the great edifice without daring idle ease, following instructions without negligence—this shows Your Majesty's resolve of anxious labor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly consider the sagely question: there is reverently bearing the great edifice without daring idle ease, following instructions without negligence—this shows Your Majesty's resolve of anxious labor.

manualTranslations.zh: 若夫任賢惕厲，宵衣旰食，宜黜左右之纖佞，進股肱之大臣；
manualTranslations.literal: As for employing the worthy with vigilance and dressing at dawn and eating at dusk, one should dismiss the slender sycophants at the ruler's side and advance the great ministers who are the ruler's limbs;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for employing the worthy with vigilance and dressing at dawn and eating at dusk, one should dismiss the slender sycophants at the ruler's side and advance the great ministers who are the ruler's limbs;

manualTranslations.zh: 若夫追蹤三五，紹復祖宗，宜鑒前古之興亡，明當時之成敗。
manualTranslations.literal: As for pursuing the Three and Five and restoring the ancestors, one should mirror the rise and fall of former antiquity and clarify the success and failure of the present time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for pursuing the Three and Five and restoring the ancestors, one should mirror the rise and fall of former antiquity and clarify the success and failure of the present time.

manualTranslations.zh: 心有所未達，以下情塞而不得上通；
manualTranslations.literal: Where the heart has not attained, it is because feelings below are blocked and cannot reach above;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Where the heart has not attained, it is because feelings below are blocked and cannot reach above;

manualTranslations.zh: 行有所未孚，以上澤壅而不得下浹。
manualTranslations.literal: Your conduct has points it has not won trust; above, favor is dammed and cannot flow downward to soak all."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your conduct has not won full trust; above, your grace is dammed and cannot reach the people below."

manualTranslations.zh: 欲人之化也，在脩己以先之；
manualTranslations.literal: If one wishes people to be transformed, one must cultivate oneself first;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one wishes people to be transformed, one must cultivate oneself first;

manualTranslations.zh: 欲氣之和也，在遂性以導之。
manualTranslations.literal: if one wishes qi to be harmonious, one must follow nature and guide it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: if one wishes qi to be harmonious, one must follow nature and guide it.

manualTranslations.zh: 救災患在致乎精誠，廣播植在視乎食力。
manualTranslations.literal: Relieving disaster and drought lies in utmost sincerity; broad planting lies in seeing to the people's labor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Relieving disaster and drought lies in utmost sincerity; broad planting lies in seeing to the people's labor.

manualTranslations.zh: 國廩罕蓄，本乎冗食尚繁；
manualTranslations.literal: That the state granaries rarely store lies in redundant eaters still being numerous;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That the state granaries rarely store lies in redundant eaters still being numerous;

manualTranslations.zh: 吏道多端，本乎選用失當。
manualTranslations.literal: The official way has many divisions; fundamentally it lies in inappropriate appointment and employment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The bureaucratic disorder has many branches, but at root it comes from appointing the wrong men.

manualTranslations.zh: 豪猾踰制，由中外之法殊；
manualTranslations.literal: Overbearing ruffians overstep regulations, because the laws of the inner and outer courts differ;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Overbearing wrongdoers exceed all bounds because the rules of court and provinces no longer align;

manualTranslations.zh: 生徒墮業，由學校之官廢。
manualTranslations.literal: Students fall from their studies, because the officials of the schools have been abandoned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Students neglect their studies because the schools have been left without proper officers.

manualTranslations.zh: 列郡干禁，由授任非人；
manualTranslations.literal: Commandery after commandery violate prohibitions, because appointments are given to unfit men;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Prefecture after prefecture breaks the law because unworthy men hold office;

manualTranslations.zh: 百工淫巧，由制度不立。
manualTranslations.literal: The hundred crafts pursue extravagant cleverness, because institutions are not established.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Artisans chase wasteful luxury because proper standards have never been fixed.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏以聖策，有擇官濟理之心，阜財發號之歎，見陛下教化之本也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject observes that in the sage edict there is the intent to select officials to aid governance and the sigh over enriching wealth and issuing commands — this shows Your Majesty's foundation of instruction and transformation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your decree shows Your Majesty's intent to appoint the right officials and your concern to strengthen public finance — the very roots of good governance.

manualTranslations.zh: 且進人以行，則枝葉安有難別乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, if one advances men by conduct, then how could branches and leaves be hard to distinguish?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If promotions were based on character, how could the worthy and unworthy be hard to tell apart?

manualTranslations.zh: 防下以禮，則耻格安有不形乎？
manualTranslations.literal: If one restrains subordinates by ritual, then how could the shame of correction fail to appear?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If subordinates were governed by ritual, would shame not restrain wrongdoing plainly enough?

manualTranslations.zh: 念生寡而食衆，可罷斥惰游；
manualTranslations.literal: Reflecting that producers are few while consumers are many, one may dismiss the idle and the wandering;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seeing that producers are few and dependents many, dismiss the idle and the dissolute;

manualTranslations.zh: 念令煩而理鮮，要察其行否。
manualTranslations.literal: Reflecting that commands are numerous while good order is scarce, the essential thing is to examine whether conduct is sound or not.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Seeing how laws multiply while effective rule grows scarce, examine officials' conduct strictly.

manualTranslations.zh: 博延群彥，願陛下必納其言；
manualTranslations.literal: Broadly extending to gather worthy talents — I hope Your Majesty will surely accept their words;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: You have summoned worthy men widely; I pray Your Majesty will heed what they say.

manualTranslations.zh: 造廷待問，則小臣安敢愛死。
manualTranslations.literal: Summoned to court to await questioning — how would this humble subject dare spare his life?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Called to court to answer — how could your humble servant hold back, even at the cost of his life?

manualTranslations.zh: 伏以聖策，有求賢箴闕之言，審政辨疵之念，見陛下咨訪之勤也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject observes that in the sage edict there are words of seeking the worthy and admonishing shortcomings, and thoughts of examining government and distinguishing flaws — this shows Your Majesty's diligence in consultation and inquiry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your decree shows Your Majesty's desire to seek worthy men, admonish your own faults, and examine policy for defects — proof of your earnest consultation.

manualTranslations.zh: 遂小臣屏姦豪之志，則弊革於前；
manualTranslations.literal: Then this humble subject's resolve to shut out wicked magnates would reform abuses beforehand;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then your servant's resolve to drive out wicked magnates would reform abuses before they spread;

manualTranslations.zh: 守陛下念康濟之心，則惠敷於下。
manualTranslations.literal: Upholding Your Majesty's mind intent on peace and relief, then favor would spread below.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Uphold Your Majesty's concern for the people's welfare, and blessings would reach every level of society.

manualTranslations.zh: 邪正之道分，則理古可近；
manualTranslations.literal: If the ways of the wicked and the upright are separated, then governing as in antiquity may be approached;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Separate the wicked from the upright, and the governance of antiquity may be approached again;

manualTranslations.zh: 禮樂之方著，而和氣克充。
manualTranslations.literal: If the methods of ritual and music are made manifest, then harmonious qi can fully fill the realm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Establish ritual and music in their proper place, and harmonious order will prevail throughout the land.

manualTranslations.zh: 至若夷吾之法，非皇王之權；
manualTranslations.literal: As for the methods of Guan Zhong, they are not the authority of an august king;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for Guan Zhong's methods, they are not the prerogative of a true sovereign;

manualTranslations.zh: 嚴尤所陳，無最上之策。
manualTranslations.literal: What Yan You presented offers no supreme policy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What Yan You proposed was no policy of the highest order.

manualTranslations.zh: 元凱之所先，不若唐、虞之考績；
manualTranslations.literal: What Yi Yin and Yu Ya put first is not equal to the performance evaluation of Yao and Shun;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The priorities of Yi Yin and Yu Ya cannot match Yao and Shun's system of evaluating merit;

manualTranslations.zh: 叔子之所務，不若重華之舞干。
manualTranslations.literal: What Lu Meng made his task is not equal to Shun's dancing with shields and axes.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Meng's preoccupations cannot compare with Emperor Shun's triumph over the Miao through ritual rather than arms;

manualTranslations.zh: 且俱非大德之中庸，未為上聖之龜鑑，何足以為陛下道之哉！
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, all alike fall short of the golden mean of great virtue and are not the tortoise mirror of the highest sage — how could they suffice as models for Your Majesty!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: None of these measures embodies the golden mean of supreme virtue or offers the sure mirror of the sage — how could they serve as Your Majesty's guide!

manualTranslations.zh: 或有以繫安危之機，兆存亡之變者，臣請披瀝肝膽，為陛下別白而重言之。
manualTranslations.literal: If there are matters that bear on the pivot of safety and danger and foreshadow the turn of survival and ruin, your subject asks leave to lay bare his liver and gall and speak them out separately and emphatically for Your Majesty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On matters that touch the pivot of safety and danger and foreshadow survival or ruin, I beg leave to lay bare my heart and speak plainly once more.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「哲王之理，其則不遠」者，在陛下慎思之，力行之，終始不懈而已。
臣謹按春秋：「元者，氣之始也；
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Yuan is the beginning of qi;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Yuan is the beginning of vital force;

manualTranslations.zh: 春者，歲之始也。
manualTranslations.literal: Spring is the beginning of the year."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Spring is the beginning of the year."

manualTranslations.zh: 」春秋以元加於歲，以春加於王，明王者當奉若天道，以謹其始也。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals adds yuan to the year and spring to the king — making clear that the king ought to revere and follow Heaven's Way in being careful at the beginning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Annals places yuan before the year and spring before the king's name, showing that a ruler must honor Heaven's Way and be scrupulous at the outset.

manualTranslations.zh: 又舉時以終歲，舉月以終時，春秋雖無事，必書首月以存時，明王者當奉若天道，以謹其終也。
manualTranslations.literal: It also takes the season to end the year and the month to end the season; though the Annals records no event, it always writes the first month to preserve the season — making clear that the king ought to revere and follow Heaven's Way in being careful at the end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: It marks the season to close the year and the month to close the season; even when nothing happens, it always records the first month to preserve the calendar — showing that a ruler must honor Heaven's Way and be scrupulous to the end.

manualTranslations.zh: 王者動作終始必法於天者，以其運行不息也。
manualTranslations.literal: The reason a king's actions from beginning to end must take Heaven as model is that Heaven's movement never ceases.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A king's conduct from beginning to end must follow Heaven's model, for Heaven never ceases its course.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下旣能謹其始，又能謹其終，懋而脩之，勤而行之，則可以執契而居簡，無為而不宰，廣立本之大業，崇建中之盛德矣。
manualTranslations.literal: If Your Majesty can be careful at the beginning and careful at the end, exert yourself in cultivating this and diligently carry it out, then you may hold the tally and dwell in simplicity, act without acting yet govern all, broadly establish the great enterprise of laying the foundation, and exalt the splendid virtue of the Jianzhong era.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty can be scrupulous at the beginning and at the end, cultivate this earnestly and act on it diligently, you may hold the tally of rule in tranquil simplicity, govern without force, broadly establish the foundation of the state, and restore the splendid virtue of the Jianzhong reign.

manualTranslations.zh: 又安有三代循環之弊，而為百偽滋熾之漸乎？
manualTranslations.literal: How then could there still be the cyclical abuses of the Three Dynasties and the gradual growth of a hundred falsities!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How then could the cyclical decay of the Three Dynasties return, or a hundred corruptions take root again!

manualTranslations.zh: 臣故曰「惟陛下致之之道何如耳」。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore your subject says, "It depends only on what path Your Majesty takes to achieve it."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That is why I said, "It depends only on the path Your Majesty chooses to achieve it."

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「若夫任賢惕厲，宵衣旰食，宜罷黜左右之纖佞，進股肱之大臣」者，實以陛下憂勞之至也。
臣聞不宜憂而憂者，國必衰；
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject has heard that when one worries over what ought not to be worried over, the state must decline;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a ruler worries over the wrong things, the state must decline;

manualTranslations.zh: 宜憂而不憂者，國必危。
manualTranslations.literal: When one fails to worry over what ought to be worried over, the state must be endangered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When a ruler fails to worry over what he ought to worry over, the state must be in peril.

manualTranslations.zh: 今陛下不以國家存亡之事、社稷安危之策，而降於清問。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Your Majesty does not bring down clear inquiry upon matters of the state's survival or ruin and policies for the altars' safety or danger.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty has not addressed the questions of the state's survival and the altars' safety in your clear inquiry.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣未知陛下以布衣之臣不足以定大計耶？
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject does not know whether Your Majesty thinks that a subject in plain cloth is insufficient to settle the great plan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I do not know whether Your Majesty thinks a common subject unfit to settle great affairs.

manualTranslations.zh: 或萬機之勤，而聖慮有所未至耶？
manualTranslations.literal: Or whether amid the diligence of the myriad affairs, the sage consideration has not yet reached certain points?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Or whether amid the press of ten thousand affairs your sage consideration has not yet reached the heart of the matter?

manualTranslations.zh: 不然，何宜憂而不憂者乎？
manualTranslations.literal: If not, then why is this a case of failing to worry over what ought to be worried over?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If not, why do you fail to worry over what you ought to worry over?

manualTranslations.zh: 臣以為陛下宜先憂者，宮闈將變，社稷將危，天下將傾，海內將亂。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject believes that what Your Majesty ought to worry about first is this: the inner palace is about to change, the altars of state are about to be endangered, the realm is about to topple, and within the seas disorder is about to break out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty's first concerns ought to be these: the inner palace is on the verge of upheaval, the altars of state are in danger, the realm is tottering, and turmoil is about to engulf the empire.

manualTranslations.zh: 此四者，國家已然之兆，故臣謂聖慮宜先及之。
manualTranslations.literal: These four are already manifest signs of the state; therefore your subject says the sage consideration ought to reach them first.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: These four are already manifest signs of national crisis; therefore I say Your Majesty's concern ought to reach them first.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫帝業旣艱難而成之，故不可容易而守之。
manualTranslations.literal: Since the imperial enterprise was achieved only through hardship, it cannot be guarded lightly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since the imperial enterprise was won only through hardship, it cannot be held lightly.

manualTranslations.zh: 昔太祖肇其基，高祖勤其績，太宗定其業，玄宗繼其明，至于陛下，二百有餘載矣。
manualTranslations.literal: In the past Taizu laid its foundation, Gaozu toiled at its achievements, Taizong fixed its enterprise, and Xuanzong continued its brilliance; down to Your Majesty, more than two hundred years have passed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Taizu laid the foundation, Gaozu built on his work, Taizong secured the enterprise, and Xuanzong carried forward its brilliance; down to Your Majesty, more than two hundred years have passed.

manualTranslations.zh: 其間明聖相因，憂亂繼作，未有不委用賢士，親近正人，而能紹興其徽烈者也。
manualTranslations.literal: In that interval sage rulers followed one another and worry and disorder arose in succession; never was there a case that did not entrust employment to worthy scholars, keep upright men near, and thereby continue and revive their splendid achievements.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Through that span sage rulers succeeded one another and crises arose in turn; never once did a dynasty survive without entrusting power to worthy men, keeping upright counselors near, and thereby renewing its glory.

manualTranslations.zh: 或一日不念，則顛覆大器，宗廟之耻，萬古為恨。
manualTranslations.literal: If for a single day one fails to reflect, then the great vessel is overturned — the shame of the ancestral temple becomes a regret for ten thousand ages.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Neglect it for a single day and the great vessel is overturned — the shame of the ancestral temple becomes an eternal regret.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹按春秋，人君之道在體元以居正，昔董仲舒為漢武帝言之略矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: the way of a ruler lies in embodying the origin and occupying the correct position; long ago Dong Zhongshu spoke of this to Emperor Wu of Han in outline.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: the ruler's way lies in embodying the origin and holding the correct position — Dong Zhongshu explained this to Emperor Wu of Han long ago.

manualTranslations.zh: 其所未盡者，臣得為陛下備而論之。
manualTranslations.literal: What he did not fully set forth, your subject may set out completely for Your Majesty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What he left unsaid, I may now set forth fully for Your Majesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫繼故必書即位，所以正其始也；
manualTranslations.literal: When one succeeds the former ruler, the accession must be recorded — this is to rectify the beginning;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When a ruler succeeds his predecessor, the accession must be recorded — to set the beginning right;

manualTranslations.zh: 終必書所終之地，所以正其終也。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end one must record the place where he ended — this is to rectify the end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the end one must record where he died — to set the ending right.

manualTranslations.zh: 故為君者，所發必正言，所履必正道，所居必正位，所近必正人。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore for one who is ruler: what he issues must be upright words, what he treads must be the upright Way, where he dwells must be the upright position, and whom he keeps near must be upright men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore a ruler must speak upright words, walk the upright path, occupy the rightful place, and keep upright men near.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣又按春秋「閽弒吳子餘祭」，不書其君。
春秋譏其疏遠賢士，昵近刑人，有不君之道矣。
manualTranslations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals rebukes him for keeping worthy scholars at a distance and drawing near to men of punishment — he had the way of one who is not a ruler.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Annals rebukes him for keeping worthy men at a distance and drawing near to executioners — he had ceased to be a true ruler.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟陛下思祖宗開國之勤，念春秋繼故之誡。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will reflect on the toil of the founding ancestors and keep in mind the admonition of the Spring and Autumn Annals on succeeding the former ruler.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to reflect on the founding ancestors' toil and heed the Annals' warning on succession.

manualTranslations.zh: 將明法度之端，則發正言而履正道；
manualTranslations.literal: If you wish to clarify the beginning of law and institutions, then issue upright words and tread the upright Way;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To clarify the foundations of law and order, speak upright words and walk the upright path;

manualTranslations.zh: 將杜篡弒之漸，則居正位而近正人。
manualTranslations.literal: If you wish to cut off the gradual growth of usurpation and regicide, then occupy the correct position and keep upright men near.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: To choke off the drift toward regicide, hold the throne in dignity and keep honest men close.

manualTranslations.zh: 遠刀鋸之賤，親骨鯁之直，輔相得以專其任，庶職得以守其官。
manualTranslations.literal: Keep far from the base of the knife and saw; be close to blunt, loyal remonstrators; let the chief ministers fully carry out their duties, and let the hundred offices keep to their posts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Banish the butcher's minions; cherish the blunt counselors who speak truth; let your chief ministers govern, and let every office do its work.

manualTranslations.zh: 奈何以褻近五六人，總天下大政，外專陛下之命，內竊陛下之權，威懾朝廷，勢傾海內，群臣莫敢指其狀，天子不得制其心。
manualTranslations.literal: How can you let five or six lewd intimates hold all great government of the realm — outwardly monopolizing Your Majesty's commands, inwardly stealing Your Majesty's authority, awing the court with their power and tilting their influence across the seas, so that no minister dares point out their condition and the Son of Heaven cannot control their hearts?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How can five or six favored intimates run the empire — issuing Your Majesty's orders in name while seizing your power in fact, awing the court and dominating the realm, so that no minister dares speak and the Son of Heaven cannot control them?

manualTranslations.zh: 禍稔蕭牆，姦生帷幄，臣恐曹節、侯覽，復生於今日，此宮闈之所以將變也。
manualTranslations.literal: Disaster ripens within the palace walls; treachery is born inside the curtain. Your subject fears Cao Jie and Hou Lan are being reborn in our own day — this is why the inner palace is about to change.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Disaster is ripening behind the palace walls; treachery is breeding within the curtained hall. I fear that Cao Jie and Hou Lan live again in our time — this is why the inner palace is on the verge of upheaval.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹按春秋，魯定公元年春王不言正月者，春秋以其先君不得正其終，則後君不得正其始，故曰定無正也。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: in the first year of Duke Ding of Lu, in spring the king is recorded but the first month is not spoken — the Annals holds that because the former ruler could not end his reign properly, the later ruler could not begin his properly; therefore it says Duke Ding had no proper beginning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: in Duke Ding of Lu's first year, spring is recorded but the first month is not — because the former ruler could not end his reign properly, the successor could not begin his properly; hence the Annals says Duke Ding had no legitimate beginning.

manualTranslations.zh: 今忠賢無腹心之奇，閽寺持廢立之權，陷先君不得正其終，致陛下不得正其始。
manualTranslations.literal: Now loyal worthies have no place to lodge their hearts; eunuch gate commanders hold the power to depose and establish; they trapped the late emperor so that he could not end his reign properly, and they have caused Your Majesty not to begin yours properly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today loyal ministers have nowhere to place their trust; eunuch commanders hold the power to make and unmake emperors. They prevented your predecessor from ending his reign in peace and have kept you from beginning yours in legitimacy.

manualTranslations.zh: 況皇儲未建，郊祀未脩，將相之職不歸，名分之宜不定，此社稷之所以將危也。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the crown heir is not established, the suburban sacrifices are not performed, the duties of generals and ministers are not returned to their proper holders, and the proprieties of rank and title are not fixed — this is why the altars of state are about to be endangered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover no crown heir has been appointed, the suburban sacrifices have not been performed, the roles of generals and ministers remain unsettled, and rank and title are in confusion — this is why the altars of state are in danger.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹按春秋「王札子殺召伯、毛伯」。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Wang Zhaozi killed the Earl of Shao and the Earl of Mao"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Wang Zhaozi killed the Earl of Shao and the Earl of Mao"

manualTranslations.zh: 春秋之義，兩下相殺不書。
manualTranslations.literal: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that when two parties kill each other it is not recorded.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Annals' principle is that mutual killings between equals are not recorded.

manualTranslations.zh: 而此書者，重其專王命也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet this is recorded — to emphasize his usurpation of the king's command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet this case is recorded — to emphasize his usurpation of the royal command.

manualTranslations.zh: 且天之所授者在君，君之所授者在命。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover, what Heaven confers rests with the ruler; what the ruler confers rests with his command.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What Heaven bestows rests with the ruler; what the ruler bestows rests with his command.

manualTranslations.zh: 操其命而失之者，是不君也；
manualTranslations.literal: One who holds the command yet loses it — such a one is not a ruler;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One who holds the command yet loses it is no ruler;

manualTranslations.zh: 侵其命而專之者，是不臣也。
manualTranslations.literal: One who encroaches on the command and monopolizes it — such a one is not a minister.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: One who encroaches on the command and monopolizes it is no minister.

manualTranslations.zh: 君不君，臣不臣，此天下所以將傾也。
manualTranslations.literal: Ruler not acting as ruler, minister not acting as minister — this is why the realm is about to topple.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When ruler and minister no longer act as they should, the realm is about to topple — this is why.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹按春秋，晉趙鞅以晉陽之兵叛入于晉。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: Zhao Yang of Jin led the troops of Jinyang in rebellion and entered Jin.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: Zhao Yang of Jin led the troops of Jinyang in rebellion against the state.

manualTranslations.zh: 今威柄凌夷，藩臣跋扈。
manualTranslations.literal: Now imperial authority declines day by day, and the frontier lords are arrogant and domineering.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today sovereign power erodes daily, while the military commissioners grow insolent on their borders.

manualTranslations.zh: 或有不達人臣之節，首亂者以安君為名；
manualTranslations.literal: Some who do not understand a subject's propriety take the lead in disorder in the name of securing the ruler;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Some who know nothing of a subject's duty take the lead in rebellion in the name of saving the throne;

manualTranslations.zh: 不究春秋之微，稱兵者以逐惡為義。
manualTranslations.literal: Without investigating the subtle meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, those who raise armies call it righteous to drive out the wicked.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Without heeding the Annals' subtle warnings, those who raise armies claim righteousness in driving out evil.

manualTranslations.zh: 則政刑不由乎天子，攻伐必自於諸侯，此海內之所以將亂也。
manualTranslations.literal: Then government and punishments no longer proceed from the Son of Heaven, and attacks and campaigns necessarily begin with the feudal lords — this is why within the seas disorder is about to break out.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then government and punishment no longer come from the throne, and war begins with the regional lords — this is why turmoil is about to engulf the empire.

manualTranslations.zh: 又樊噲排闥而雪涕，爰盎當車以抗詞，京房發憤以殞身，竇武不顧而畢命，此皆陛下明知之矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover Fan Kuai pushed open the door in tears, Yuan Ang blocked the carriage with bold words, Jing Fang gave vent to indignation and lost his life, and Dou Wu paid no heed to danger and ended his life — all this Your Majesty clearly knows.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai burst through the door in tears; Yuan Ang blocked the carriage with bold remonstrance; Jing Fang spoke in righteous anger and lost his life; Dou Wu ignored all danger and died for his cause — Your Majesty knows all this well.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹按春秋，晉狐射姑殺陽處父。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: Hu Shegu of Jin killed Yang Chufu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: Hu Shegu of Jin killed Yang Chufu.

manualTranslations.zh: 襄公不能固陰重之機，處父所以及戕賊之禍，故春秋非之。
manualTranslations.literal: Duke Xiang could not secure the hidden, weighty pivot; therefore Chufu met the disaster of slaughter — for this the Spring and Autumn Annals rebukes him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang failed to secure the hidden levers of power, and Chufu met a violent death — for this the Annals rebukes him.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫上漏其情，則下不敢盡意；
manualTranslations.literal: When the ruler leaks his feelings, then those below dare not fully express their intent;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the ruler reveals his mind, those below dare not speak their full mind;

manualTranslations.zh: 上泄其事，則下不敢盡言。
manualTranslations.literal: When the ruler divulges their affairs, then those below dare not fully speak.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the ruler leaks what is said to him, those below dare not speak freely.

manualTranslations.zh: 傳有「造膝」「詭辭」之文，易有「殺身」「害成」之戒。
今公卿大臣，非不能為陛下言之，慮陛下必不能用之。
manualTranslations.literal: Now the chief ministers and great officials are not unable to speak to Your Majesty — they fear Your Majesty will surely not employ what they say.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today's chief ministers are not unable to speak — they fear Your Majesty will not act on what they say.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下旣忽之而不用，必洩其言；
manualTranslations.literal: If Your Majesty neglects their words and does not employ them, you will surely leak what they say;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty ignores their counsel, you will inevitably leak what they say;

manualTranslations.zh: 臣下旣言之而不行，必嬰其禍。
manualTranslations.literal: If subjects have spoken yet their words are not carried out, they will surely meet disaster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If ministers speak and nothing is done, they will surely suffer for it.

manualTranslations.zh: 適足以鉗直臣之口，重奸臣之威。
manualTranslations.literal: This is exactly enough to clamp shut the mouths of upright ministers and increase the authority of wicked ministers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: This only silences upright ministers and strengthens wicked ones.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以欲盡其言，則起失身之懼；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore if they wish to speak fully, the fear of losing their lives arises;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore if they wish to speak fully, they fear for their lives;

manualTranslations.zh: 欲盡其意，則有害成之憂。
manualTranslations.literal: If they wish to express their intent fully, then the worry of ruining the achievement arises.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If they wish to speak their full mind, they fear ruining what good might yet be done.

manualTranslations.zh: 故徘徊鬱塞，以俟陛下感悟，然後盡其啟沃耳。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore they hesitate and are blocked and depressed, waiting for Your Majesty's awakening — only then will they fully offer their nourishing counsel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: So they hesitate and hold back, waiting for Your Majesty to understand — only then will they offer their full counsel.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下何不以聽朝之餘，時御便殿，召當時賢相與舊德老臣，訪持變扶危之謀，求定傾救亂之術。
manualTranslations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not, in the intervals after hearing court affairs, from time to time enter the informal hall, summon the worthy chancellors of the day and old ministers of established virtue, and inquire after plans to hold off change and support what is endangered, and seek methods to set right what is toppling and rescue what is in disorder?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Why not, between sessions of court, from time to time enter the informal hall, summon the worthy chancellors and venerable ministers of the day, and ask their plans for holding off disaster and restoring order?

manualTranslations.zh: 塞陰邪之路，屏褻狎之臣，制侵凌迫脅之心，復門戶掃除之役，戒其所宜戒，憂其所宜憂。
manualTranslations.literal: Block the paths of hidden wickedness; remove lewd and familiar ministers; restrain the mind that encroaches, oppresses, and coerces; restore the work of clearing the gate and courtyard; warn against what ought to be warned against; worry over what ought to be worried over.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Block the paths of hidden evil; remove favored intimates; restrain those who encroach and coerce; restore the work of purging faction; warn against what must be warned against; worry over what must be worried over.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣不能治於前，當治於後；
manualTranslations.literal: If you could not govern properly before, you ought to govern properly afterward;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you could not set things right before, set them right now;

manualTranslations.zh: 旣不能正其始，當正其終。
manualTranslations.literal: If you could not rectify the beginning, you ought to rectify the end.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you could not set the beginning right, set the ending right.

manualTranslations.zh: 則可以虔奉典謨，克承丕構，終任賢之効，無旰食之憂矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Then you may reverently uphold the canonical plans, fully inherit the great enterprise, ultimately achieve the effect of employing the worthy, and be free of the worry of eating after dusk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then you may reverently uphold the canonical models, fully inherit the great enterprise, achieve the fruits of employing worthy men, and be free of the worry of toiling past dusk.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「若夫追蹤三五，紹復祖宗，宜鑒前古之興亡，明當時之成敗」者。
臣聞堯、舜之為君而天下之人理者，以其能任九官四嶽十二牧，不失其舉，不貳其業，不侵其職。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject has heard that Yao and Shun as rulers brought order to all under Heaven because they could appoint the nine ministers, the four mountain lords, and the twelve pasture lords — not missing the right appointment, not duplicating their tasks, not encroaching on their duties.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard that Yao and Shun brought order to the realm because they could appoint the nine ministers, the four mountain lords, and the twelve pasture lords — making the right appointments, assigning clear duties, and never encroaching on their offices.

manualTranslations.zh: 居官惟其能，左右惟其賢。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who held office were chosen for their ability; those at the ruler's side were chosen for their worth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Offices went to the capable; the ruler's circle to the worthy.

manualTranslations.zh: 元凱在下，雖微必舉；
manualTranslations.literal: Yi Yin and Yu Ya were below, yet though humble they were surely raised up;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yi Yin and Yu Ya stood below, yet though humble they were surely elevated;

manualTranslations.zh: 四凶在朝，雖強必誅。
manualTranslations.literal: The Four Evils were at court, yet though powerful they were surely executed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The Four Evils sat at court, yet though powerful they were surely punished.

manualTranslations.zh: 考其安危，明其取捨。
manualTranslations.literal: Examine safety and danger; clarify what to take and what to discard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Weigh safety against danger; know what to embrace and what to reject.

manualTranslations.zh: 至秦之二代，漢之元、成，咸欲措國如唐、虞，致身如堯、舜，而終敗亡者，以其不見安危之機，不知取捨之道，不任大臣，不辨姦人，不親忠良，不遠讒佞。
manualTranslations.literal: Down to the two generations of Qin and the Yuan and Cheng reigns of Han — all wished to set the state in order as in the age of Yao and Shun and to make themselves like Yao and Shun, yet in the end perished — because they did not see the pivot of safety and danger, did not know the way of choosing and discarding, did not entrust great ministers, did not distinguish wicked men, did not keep loyal worthies near, and did not keep slanderers and flatterers far.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Down to the two generations of Qin and the Yuan and Cheng reigns of Han — all wished to govern like Yao and Shun, yet in the end perished because they failed to see the pivot of safety and danger, did not know what to embrace and reject, did not entrust great ministers, did not distinguish the wicked, did not keep loyal men near, and did not banish slanderers.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟陛下察唐、虞之所以興，而景行於前；
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will examine why Tang and Yu rose, and take that as a bright model ahead;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to examine why Yao and Shun rose, and take that as your bright model;

manualTranslations.zh: 鑒秦、漢之所以亡，而戒懼於後。
manualTranslations.literal: Take as mirror why Qin and Han perished, and be warned and fearful afterward.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Take as mirror why Qin and Han fell, and be warned and vigilant hereafter.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下無謂廟堂無賢相，庶官無賢士。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty must not say that in the temple hall there are no worthy chancellors and among the hundred offices there are no worthy scholars.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Do not say that the court lacks worthy chancellors or that the offices lack worthy men.

manualTranslations.zh: 今紀綱未絕，典刑猶在，人誰不欲致身為王臣，致時為太平，陛下何忽而不用之耶？
manualTranslations.literal: Now the statutes are not yet severed and the canonical punishments still remain — who would not wish to devote himself as a king's minister and bring his age to peace? Why does Your Majesty neglect them and not employ them?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The statutes are not yet broken and the laws still stand — who would not wish to serve as your minister and bring peace to the age? Why does Your Majesty neglect them?

manualTranslations.zh: 又有居官非其能，左右非其賢，其惡如四凶，其詐如趙高，其姦如恭、顯，陛下又何憚而不去之耶？
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover there are those who hold office beyond their ability and stand at the side though they are not worthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong Yu and Shi Xian — why should Your Majesty hesitate to remove them?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: And there are men in office beyond their ability and at your side though unworthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong Yu and Shi Xian — why should Your Majesty hesitate to remove them?

manualTranslations.zh: 神器固有歸，天命固有分，祖廟固有靈，忠臣固有心，陛下其念之哉！
manualTranslations.literal: The sacred vessel has its proper destination; Heaven's mandate has its proper allotment; the ancestral temple has its numinous power; loyal ministers have their steadfast hearts — Your Majesty, reflect on this!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The throne has its rightful holder; Heaven's mandate its proper allotment; the ancestral temple its numinous power; loyal ministers their steadfast hearts — Your Majesty, remember this!

manualTranslations.zh: 昔秦之亡也，失於強暴；
manualTranslations.literal: In the past Qin's perishing lay in excessive harshness;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Qin perished through excessive harshness;

manualTranslations.zh: 漢之亡也，失於微弱。
manualTranslations.literal: Han's perishing lay in excessive weakness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han perished through excessive weakness.

manualTranslations.zh: 強暴則賊臣畏死而害上，微弱則姦臣竊權而震主。
manualTranslations.literal: When harsh, wicked ministers fear death and harm their ruler; when weak, treacherous ministers steal authority and shake their master.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Harshness drives wicked ministers to kill their ruler from fear of death; weakness lets treacherous ministers steal power and intimidate the throne.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏見敬宗皇帝不虞亡秦之禍，不翦其萌；
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject observes that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against the disaster of Qin's fall and did not cut off its first shoots;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I observe that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against Qin's disaster and did not cut off its first shoots;

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟陛下深軫亡漢之憂，以杜其漸。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will deeply feel the worry of Han's fall and stop its gradual growth.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to deeply heed the lesson of Han's fall and stop the drift while it can still be stopped.

manualTranslations.zh: 則祖宗之鴻業可紹，三五之遐軌可追矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Then the great enterprise of the ancestors may be continued and the distant tracks of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors may be pursued.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then the ancestors' great enterprise may be renewed and the distant example of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors may be pursued.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「陛下心有所未達，以下情塞而不能上通；
manualTranslations.literal: What your subject said earlier — "Your Majesty's mind has points it has not reached; below, feelings are blocked and cannot pass upward;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "Your Majesty's mind has not reached every truth; below, the people's feelings are blocked and cannot reach you;

manualTranslations.zh: 行有所未孚，以上澤壅而不得下浹」者。
且百姓塗炭之苦，陛下無由而知；
manualTranslations.literal: Moreover the people's suffering in fire and smearing — Your Majesty has no means to know it;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover the people's suffering in misery — Your Majesty has no way to know it;

manualTranslations.zh: 則陛下有子育之心，百姓無由而信。
manualTranslations.literal: Then though Your Majesty has the heart of nourishing children, the people have no means to believe it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then though Your Majesty has a parent's heart for the people, they have no way to believe it.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣謹按春秋書「梁亡」，不書取者，梁自亡也，以其思慮昏而耳目塞，上出惡政，人為寇盜，皆不知其所以然，以自取其滅亡也。
臣聞國君之所以尊者，重其社稷也；
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject has heard that the reason a state's ruler is honored is that he gives weight to his altars of soil and grain;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard that a ruler is honored because he gives weight to the altars of state;

manualTranslations.zh: 社稷之所以重者，存其百姓也。
manualTranslations.literal: The reason the altars of soil and grain are given weight is that the people are preserved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The altars are weighty because the people are preserved.

manualTranslations.zh: 苟百姓之不存，則社稷不得固其重；
manualTranslations.literal: If the people are not preserved, then the altars cannot secure their weight;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the people are not preserved, the altars cannot hold their weight;

manualTranslations.zh: 苟社稷之不重，則國君不得保其尊。
manualTranslations.literal: If the altars are not weighty, then the state's ruler cannot preserve his honor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the altars lose their weight, the ruler cannot preserve his honor.

manualTranslations.zh: 故治天下不可不知百姓之情。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore in governing all under Heaven one cannot fail to know the people's condition.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore to govern the realm one must know the people's condition.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫百姓者，陛下之赤子也。
manualTranslations.literal: The people are Your Majesty's red infants.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The people are Your Majesty's own children.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下宜令仁慈者親育之，如保傅焉，如乳哺焉，如師之教導焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty ought to have the benevolent personally nurture them — as protector and tutor, as nursing and feeding, as a teacher's instruction and guidance.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to have the benevolent nurture them personally — as protector and tutor, as nurse and feeder, as teacher and guide.

manualTranslations.zh: 故人信於上也，敬之如神明，愛之如父母。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore when people trust their ruler above, they revere him as a spirit and love him as parents.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When people trust their ruler, they revere him as a spirit and love him as a parent.

manualTranslations.zh: 今或不然。
manualTranslations.literal: Now it is perhaps not so.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today it is not so.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下親近貴倖，分曹補署，建除卒吏，召致賔客，因其貨賄，假其氣勢。
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty keeps near the noble favorites; they are assigned by department and post; clerks of the Jian and Chu cycles are summoned and guests are brought in; relying on their bribes, you lend them your authority and momentum.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty keeps favored intimates near; they are assigned to offices by department; clerks and clients are summoned and installed; relying on their bribes, you lend them your authority.

manualTranslations.zh: 大者統藩方，小者為牧守。
manualTranslations.literal: The greater ones command frontier regions; the lesser ones serve as prefects and governors.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The greater ones command military regions; the lesser ones serve as prefects and governors.

manualTranslations.zh: 居上無清惠之政。
manualTranslations.literal: In high office they have no pure and generous government.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In high office they offer no pure and generous government.

manualTranslations.zh: 而有饕餮之害；
manualTranslations.literal: Yet they have the harm of gluttonous devouring;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Only the harm of gluttonous greed;

manualTranslations.zh: 居下無忠誠之節，而有姦欺之罪。
manualTranslations.literal: In low office they have no loyal and steadfast integrity, but have the crime of treachery and deceit.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In low office they show no loyal integrity, only treachery and fraud.

manualTranslations.zh: 故人之於上也，畏之如豺狼，惡之如讎敵。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore in their relation to their ruler above, people fear him as wolves and jackals and hate him as a sworn enemy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore the people fear their rulers like wolves and jackals and hate them like sworn enemies.

manualTranslations.zh: 今海內困窮，處處流散，饑者不得食，寒者不得衣，鰥寡孤獨者不得存，老幼疾病者不得養。
manualTranslations.literal: Now within the seas there is destitution and poverty; people are scattered everywhere; the hungry cannot obtain food, the cold cannot obtain clothing, widowers and orphans cannot survive, and the old, the young, and the sick cannot be cared for.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now the empire is destitute; people scatter everywhere; the hungry cannot eat, the cold cannot be clothed, widows and orphans cannot survive, and the old, young, and sick cannot be cared for.

manualTranslations.zh: 加以國之權柄，專在左右，貪臣聚斂以固寵，姦吏因緣而弄法。
manualTranslations.literal: Added to this, the state's authority rests solely with those at the side; greedy ministers gather wealth to secure favor, and treacherous clerks exploit connections to manipulate the law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Moreover the state's power rests solely with those at your side; greedy ministers extort wealth to secure favor, and corrupt clerks manipulate the law for their own ends.

manualTranslations.zh: 冤痛之聲，上達于九天，下流於九泉，鬼神怨怒，陰陽為之愆錯。
manualTranslations.literal: The sounds of wrongful suffering reach up to the nine heavens and flow down to the nine springs; ghosts and spirits resent in anger, and yin and yang are thrown into disorder for it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cries of injustice reach up to heaven and down to the underworld; ghosts and spirits seethe with anger, and yin and yang fall out of balance.

manualTranslations.zh: 君門萬里而不得告訴，士人無所歸化，百姓無所歸命。
manualTranslations.literal: The ruler's gate is ten thousand li away and grievances cannot be told; scholars have nowhere to turn for guidance, and the people have nowhere to place their trust.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The ruler's gate is ten thousand li away and grievances cannot be heard; scholars have nowhere to turn, and the people have nowhere to place their trust.

manualTranslations.zh: 官亂人貧，盜賊並起，土崩之勢，憂在旦夕。
manualTranslations.literal: Officials are in disorder and the people are poor; bandits and robbers rise together; the momentum of earth collapsing — the worry lies within the day or the morrow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Officials are corrupt and the people impoverished; bandits rise on every side; the state is crumbling — disaster may come at any moment.

manualTranslations.zh: 即不幸因之以疾癘，繼之以凶荒，臣恐陳勝、吳廣不獨起於秦，赤眉、黃巾不獨起於漢，故臣所以為陛下發憤扼腕，痛心泣血爾。
manualTranslations.literal: If misfortune adds plague upon this and famine and disaster follow, your subject fears that Chen Sheng and Wu Guang will not rise only in Qin, and the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans will not rise only in Han — therefore your subject beats his breast and wrings his wrists for Your Majesty, his heart pained to the point of weeping blood.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If plague and famine follow, I fear Chen Sheng and Wu Guang will rise again — not only in Qin — and the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans — not only in Han. That is why I beat my breast in anguish and weep blood for Your Majesty.

manualTranslations.zh: 如此則百姓有塗炭之苦，陛下何由而知之；
manualTranslations.literal: If it is thus, then the people have suffering in fire and smearing — by what means can Your Majesty know it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If this is so, the people suffer in misery — how can Your Majesty know it?

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下有子育之心，百姓安得而信之乎？
manualTranslations.literal: Your Majesty has the heart of nourishing children — how can the people believe it?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has a parent's heart for the people — how can they believe it?

manualTranslations.zh: 致使陛下「行有所未孚，必有所未達」者，固其然也。
臣聞昔漢元帝即位之初，更制七十餘事，其心甚誠，其稱甚美。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject has heard that at the beginning of Emperor Yuan of Han's accession, he changed more than seventy institutions; his heart was very sincere and his reputation very fine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Emperor Yuan of Han first took the throne, he reformed more than seventy institutions; his heart was sincere and his reputation splendid.

manualTranslations.zh: 然而紀綱日紊，國祚日衰，姦宄日強，黎元日困者，以其不能擇賢明而任之，失其操柄也。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet the statutes grew daily disordered, the dynastic fortune daily declined, wickedness daily strengthened, and the common people daily distressed — because he could not select the worthy and bright and employ them, and lost hold of the helm.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet the statutes grew daily disordered, the dynasty daily declined, wickedness daily strengthened, and the people daily distressed — because he could not select worthy men and employ them, and lost hold of the helm.

manualTranslations.zh: 即陛下御宇，憂勤兆庶，屢降德音，四海之內，莫不抗首而長思，自喜復生於死亡之中也。
manualTranslations.literal: Since Your Majesty holds the realm, you have toiled in worry and diligence for the myriad masses, repeatedly issuing virtuous pronouncements; within the four seas none failed to raise their heads and sigh long, rejoicing that they were reborn from among the dead.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty has held the realm, you have toiled in worry and diligence for the myriad masses, repeatedly issuing virtuous pronouncements; throughout the four seas none failed to raise their heads and sigh with relief, rejoicing that they were reborn from among the dead.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏惟陛下慎終如始，以塞萬方之望。
manualTranslations.literal: I prostrate myself and beg Your Majesty to be careful at the end as at the beginning, to satisfy the hopes of the ten thousand directions.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to be careful at the end as at the beginning, to satisfy the hopes of all under Heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 誠能揭國權以歸其相，持兵柄以歸其將，去貪臣聚斂之政，除姦吏因緣之害，惟忠賢是近，惟正直是用，內寵便僻，無所聽焉。
manualTranslations.literal: If you can truly raise state authority and return it to the chancellor, hold the military handle and return it to the generals, remove the government of greedy ministers gathering levies, eliminate the harm of treacherous officials seizing opportunities, draw near only the loyal and worthy, employ only the upright — hear none of the words of inner favorites and convenient flatterers.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you can truly return state authority to the chancellor and military authority to the generals, remove the government of greedy ministers gathering levies, eliminate the harm of treacherous officials seizing opportunities, draw near only the loyal and worthy and employ only the upright — hear none of the words of inner favorites and convenient flatterers.

manualTranslations.zh: 選清慎之官，擇仁惠之長，敏之以利，煦之以仁，教之以孝慈，導之以德義，去耳目之塞，通上下之情，俾萬國歡康，兆民蘇息，則心無不達，行無不孚矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Select officials who are clear and cautious, choose leaders who are benevolent and gracious, quicken them with benefit, warm them with benevolence, teach them with filial piety and kindness, guide them with virtue and righteousness, remove the blockage of ears and eyes, connect the feelings of above and below — then make the ten thousand states joyful and at peace, the myriad masses revive and rest; then what the heart intends will not fail to reach, what is enacted will not fail to win trust.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Select officials who are clear and cautious, choose leaders who are benevolent and gracious, quicken them with benefit, warm them with benevolence, teach them filial piety and kindness, guide them with virtue and righteousness, remove the blockage of ears and eyes, connect the feelings of above and below — then make the ten thousand states joyful and at peace and the myriad masses revive and rest; then what you intend will reach everywhere and what you enact will win trust everywhere.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「欲兆人之化也，在脩己以先之」者。
臣聞德以脩己，教以導人，脩之也則人不勸而自至，導之也則人敦行而率從。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject has heard: virtue is for cultivating the self, teaching is for guiding others; cultivate it, then men without exhortation come of themselves; guide it, then men earnestly act and broadly follow.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have heard: virtue is for cultivating the self, teaching is for guiding others; cultivate it, then men without exhortation come of themselves; guide it, then men earnestly act and broadly follow.

manualTranslations.zh: 是以君子欲政之必行也，故以身先之；
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore the noble man wishes government necessarily to be carried out, and so he takes the lead with his person;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore the noble man wishes government to be carried out, and so he takes the lead with his own person;

manualTranslations.zh: 欲人之從化也，故以道御之。
manualTranslations.literal: wishes men to follow transformation, and so he governs them with the Way.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: wishes men to follow transformation, and so he governs them with the Way.

manualTranslations.zh: 今陛下先之以身而政未必行，御之以道而人未從化，豈不以立教之旨未盡其方也。
manualTranslations.literal: Now Your Majesty takes the lead with your person yet government is not necessarily carried out, governs with the Way yet men have not followed transformation — is it that the aim of establishing teaching has not exhausted its methods?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Now you take the lead with your person yet government is not necessarily carried out, govern with the Way yet men have not followed transformation — is it that the aim of establishing teaching has not exhausted its methods?

manualTranslations.zh: 夫立教之方，在乎君以明制之，臣以忠行之，君以知人為明，臣以匡時為忠，知人則任賢而去邪，匡時則固本而守法。
manualTranslations.literal: The method of establishing teaching lies in the ruler clearly regulating it and the minister loyally carrying it out; the ruler takes knowing men as clarity, the minister takes correcting the times as loyalty; knowing men lies in employing the worthy and removing the perverse, correcting the times lies in securing the foundation and keeping to the law.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The method of establishing teaching lies in the ruler clearly regulating it and the minister loyally carrying it out; the ruler takes knowing men as clarity, the minister takes correcting the times as loyalty; knowing men lies in employing the worthy and removing the perverse, correcting the times lies in securing the foundation and keeping to the law.

manualTranslations.zh: 賢不任則重賞不足以勸善，邪不去則嚴刑不足以禁非，本不固則民流，法不守則政散，而欲教之使必至，化之使必行，不可得也。
manualTranslations.literal: If the worthy are not employed, heavy rewards are insufficient to encourage good; if the perverse are not removed, severe punishments are insufficient to prohibit wrong; if the foundation is not secure, people scatter; if the law is not kept, government disperses — yet wishing teaching necessarily to arrive and transformation necessarily to be carried out cannot be obtained.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If the worthy are not employed, heavy rewards are insufficient to encourage good; if the perverse are not removed, severe punishments are insufficient to prohibit wrong; if the foundation is not secure, people scatter; if the law is not kept, government disperses — yet wishing teaching to arrive and transformation to be carried out cannot be obtained.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下能斥姦邪不私其左右，舉賢正不遺其疏遠，則化浹於朝廷矣；
manualTranslations.literal: If Your Majesty can repel treacherous perversity without favoring those at left and right, raise the worthy and upright without neglecting the distant — then transformation will soak the court;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If you can repel treacherous perversity without favoring those at your side, raise the worthy and upright without neglecting the distant — then transformation will soak the court;

manualTranslations.zh: 愛人以敦本，分職而奉法，脩其身以及其人，始於中而成於外，則化行於天下矣。
manualTranslations.literal: love others and enrich the foundation, divide duties and keep to the law, cultivate the self and extend to others, begin within and accomplish without — then transformation will travel all under Heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: love others and enrich the foundation, divide duties and keep to the law, cultivate yourself and extend to others, begin within and accomplish without — then transformation will travel the realm.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「欲氣之和也，在於遂性以導之」者，當納人於仁壽也。
夫欲人之仁壽也，在乎立制度，脩教化。
manualTranslations.literal: If one wishes men benevolent and long-lived, it lies in establishing institutions and cultivating transformation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one wishes the people benevolent and long-lived, it lies in establishing institutions and cultivating transformation.

manualTranslations.zh: 夫制度立則財用省，財用省則賦斂輕，賦斂輕則人富矣；
manualTranslations.literal: When institutions are established, expenditures are economized; when expenditures are economized, levies are light; when levies are light, men are wealthy;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When institutions are established, expenditures are economized; when expenditures are economized, levies are light; when levies are light, the people grow wealthy;

manualTranslations.zh: 教化脩則爭競息，爭競息則刑罰清，刑罰清則人安矣。
manualTranslations.literal: when transformation is cultivated, contention ceases; when contention ceases, punishments are clear; when punishments are clear, men are at peace.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when transformation is cultivated, contention ceases; when contention ceases, punishments are clear; when punishments are clear, the people are at peace.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣富矣，則仁義興焉；
manualTranslations.literal: once wealthy, then benevolence and righteousness arise;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: once wealthy, then benevolence and righteousness arise;

manualTranslations.zh: 旣安矣，則壽考至焉。
manualTranslations.literal: once at peace, then longevity arrives.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: once at peace, then longevity arrives.

manualTranslations.zh: 仁壽之心感於下，和平之氣應於上，故災害不作，休祥荐臻，四方底寧，萬物咸遂矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Hearts of benevolence and longevity are moved below, qi of peace and harmony respond above — therefore disasters do not arise, auspicious omens arrive in succession, the four directions reach tranquility, and the ten thousand things all succeed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Hearts of benevolence and longevity are moved below, qi of peace and harmony respond above — therefore disasters do not arise, auspicious omens arrive in succession, the four directions reach tranquility, and the ten thousand things all succeed.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「救災旱在致乎精誠」者。
臣謹按春秋，魯僖公七月之中，三書不雨者，以其君有恤人之志也；
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: within the seventh month of Duke Xi of Lu, thrice recording "no rain" — because that ruler had the purpose of caring for the people;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: within the seventh month of Duke Xi of Lu, "no rain" is recorded three times — because that ruler had a mind to care for the people;

manualTranslations.zh: 魯文公三年之中，一書不雨者，以其君無憫人之心也。
manualTranslations.literal: within three years of Duke Wen, recording "no rain" once — because that ruler had no heart of compassion for the people.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: across three years of Duke Wen, it is recorded only once — because that ruler had no heart of compassion for the people.

manualTranslations.zh: 故僖公致精誠而旱不害物，文公無卹憫而旱則成災。
manualTranslations.literal: Therefore when Xi attained sincerity, drought did not harm things; when Wen lacked care and compassion, drought became disaster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Therefore when Xi attained sincerity, drought did not harm the crops; when Wen lacked care and compassion, drought became true disaster.

manualTranslations.zh: 陛下誠能有卹人之心，則無成災之變矣。
manualTranslations.literal: If Your Majesty truly has a heart to care for the people, there will be no change that becomes disaster.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly has a heart to care for the people, there will be no change that becomes disaster.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「廣播植在視乎食力」者。
臣謹按春秋：「君人者，必時視人之所勤。
manualTranslations.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: "One who rules the people must constantly observe what the people labor at.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: "A ruler must constantly observe what the people labor at.

manualTranslations.zh: 人勤於力，則功築罕；
manualTranslations.literal: When the people labor at strength, achievements and construction are rare;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the people labor at physical strength, public works grow scarce;

manualTranslations.zh: 人勤於財，則貢賦少；
manualTranslations.literal: when they labor at wealth, tribute and levies are few;
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they labor at wealth, tribute and levies shrink;

manualTranslations.zh: 人勤於食，則百事廢。
manualTranslations.literal: when they labor at food, the hundred affairs are abandoned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: when they labor at securing food, the hundred affairs are abandoned.

manualTranslations.zh: 」今財食與人力皆勤矣，願陛下廢百事之勞，廣三時之務，則播植不愆矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Now wealth, food, and strength are all labored — your subject wishes Your Majesty to abandon the toil of the hundred affairs and broaden the duties of the three seasons, then sowing and planting will not fail.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Today wealth, food, and strength are all overstrained. I beg Your Majesty to set aside the toil of the hundred affairs and broaden the work of the three farming seasons — then sowing and planting will not fail.

manualTranslations.zh: 臣前所謂「國廩罕蓄，本乎冗食尚繁」者。
臣謹按春秋「臧孫辰告糴于齊」，春秋譏其國無九年之蓄，一年不登而百姓饑。
