manualTranslations.zh: 蕭穎士者，字茂挺，與華同年登進士第。
manualTranslations.literal: Xiao Yingshi, style name Maoting, passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Hua.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingshi, whose courtesy name was Maoting, passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Li Hua.

manualTranslations.zh: 當開元中，天下承平，人物駢集如賈。
manualTranslations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era, the realm was at peace, and men of talent gathered thickly like merchants at a market.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, the empire was at peace and talented men flocked together like traders at a fair.

manualTranslations.zh: 曽席豫、張垍、韋述軰皆有盛名，而穎士皆與之遊。
manualTranslations.literal: Zeng Xiyu, Zhang Yong, Wei Shu, and their peers all had great renown, and Yingshi associated with all of them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Jia Zeng, Xi Yu, Zhang Yong, Wei Shu, and their circle all enjoyed great fame, and Yingshi moved in all their company.

manualTranslations.zh: 由是縉紳多譽之。
manualTranslations.literal: From this, many gentry and officials praised him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Because of this, many court officials spoke well of him.

manualTranslations.zh: 李林甫採其名，欲拔用之，乃召見。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Linfu took note of his name, wished to promote and employ him, and therefore summoned him for an audience.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Linfu heard of his reputation, wanted to advance and employ him, and summoned him to an audience.

manualTranslations.zh: 時穎士寓居廣陵，毋䘮，即縗麻而詣京師，徑謁林甫於政事省。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Yingshi was lodging in Guangling; his mother had died, so he went at once to the capital in hemp mourning garments and went straight to visit Li Linfu at the Secretariat for Administration.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the time Yingshi was living in Guangling. His mother had just died, so he set out for the capital in hemp mourning dress and went directly to call on Li Linfu at the administrative secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 林甫素不識，遽見縗麻大惡之，即令斥去。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Linfu did not know him at all; seeing the hemp mourning clothes he was greatly displeased and immediately ordered him driven away.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had never met him before. Seeing him in hemp mourning garb, he took an instant dislike to him and had him sent away at once.

manualTranslations.zh: 穎士大忿，乃為伐《櫻桃賦》以刺林甫云：「擢無用之剿質，蒙本枝而自庇；
manualTranslations.literal: Yingshi was deeply angry; he therefore wrote a satirical "Rhapsody on Cutting Cherry Trees" to criticize Li Linfu, saying: "Promoting useless pruned stock, taking shelter under the root branch;"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yingshi was furious and wrote a satirical "Rhapsody on Felling Cherry Trees" to attack Li Linfu, saying: "Raising up useless pruned wood, sheltering yourself under the parent branch;"

manualTranslations.zh: 汨群林而非據，專廟庭之右地。
manualTranslations.literal: "Drowning the whole grove without rightful standing, monopolizing the privileged ground of the temple court."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Flooding the grove without rightful claim, seizing the honored place in the temple courtyard."

manualTranslations.zh: 雖先寢而式薦，豈和羹之正味？
manualTranslations.literal: "Though placed first in the bed and carried in procession for offering, is it the proper flavor for harmonizing the soup?"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: "Though laid out first and borne forward for presentation, is it the true flavor for the harmonizing broth?"

manualTranslations.zh: 其狂率不遜，皆此類也，然而聰警絶倫。
manualTranslations.literal: His wildness, bluntness, and lack of deference were all of this sort; yet his intelligence was unrivaled.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His reckless bluntness and lack of deference were all of this kind, yet his brilliance was unmatched.

manualTranslations.zh: 甞與李華、陸據同遊洛南龍門，三人共讀路側古碑，穎士一閲即能誦之，華再閲，據三閲方能記之。
manualTranslations.literal: He once traveled with Li Hua and Lu Ju to Longmen south of Luoyang; the three together read an ancient stele by the roadside. Yingshi could recite it after one reading, Hua after two readings, and Ju only after three readings could he commit it to memory.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He once visited Longmen south of Luoyang with Li Hua and Lu Ju. The three of them read an old stele by the roadside together: Yingshi could recite it after a single reading, Hua after two, and Ju only after three.

manualTranslations.zh: 議者以三人才格髙下亦如此。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who discussed the matter held that the ranking of the three men's talent and character was likewise.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Commentators took the relative standing of the three men's talent and character to match this exactly.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時，外夷亦知穎士之名，新羅使入朝，言國人願得蕭夫子為師，其名動華夷，若此終以誕傲褊忿困躓而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time, foreign peoples also knew Yingshi's name; when a Silla envoy came to court he said his countrymen wished to have Master Xiao as their teacher. His fame moved both Chinese and foreigners; yet in the end, through arrogance, insolence, narrow resentment, and setbacks, he died in frustration.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time even foreign peoples knew Yingshi's name. When a Silla envoy came to court, he said his countrymen wished to have Master Xiao as their teacher. His fame stirred both China and the borderlands, yet in the end he died thwarted by his own arrogance, insolence, and narrow-spirited resentment.

manualTranslations.zh: 華宗人翰，亦以進士知名。
manualTranslations.literal: Han, a clansman of Hua's, also became known through the jinshi degree.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Han, a kinsman of Li Hua's, also won renown as a jinshi graduate.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寳中，寓居陽翟。
manualTranslations.literal: During the Tianbao era, he lived as a guest in Yangdi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he made his home as a guest in Yangdi.

manualTranslations.zh: 為文精密，用思苦澁。
manualTranslations.literal: His writing was meticulous; composing taxed his mind to bitterness and difficulty.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His prose was meticulous, and the labor of composition was bitter and arduous.

manualTranslations.zh: 常從陽翟令皇甫曽求音樂，每思涸則奏樂，神逸則著文。
manualTranslations.literal: He often sought music from Huangfu Zeng, magistrate of Yangdi; whenever his thoughts ran dry he would have music played, and when his spirit was at ease he would write.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He often asked Huangfu Zeng, magistrate of Yangdi, for music. Whenever his thoughts dried up he would have music played; when his mind was at ease he would write.

manualTranslations.zh: 禄山之亂，從友人張巡客宋州，巡率州人守城，賊攻圍經年，食盡矢窮方䧟。
manualTranslations.literal: During the An Lushan rebellion, he followed his friend Zhang Xun as a guest in Song prefecture. Xun led the people of the prefecture in defending the city; the rebels besieged it for a full year, and only when food was exhausted and arrows depleted did it fall.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion he followed his friend Zhang Xun as a guest in Song prefecture. Xun led the people of the prefecture in defending the city; the rebels besieged it for a year, and it fell only when food and arrows were exhausted.

manualTranslations.zh: 當時薄巡者，言其降賊，翰乃序巡守城事迹，撰張巡、姚誾等傳兩卷，上之肅宗。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who at the time slighted Xun said he had surrendered to the rebels; Han thereupon set forth Xun's deeds in defending the city, composed biographies of Zhang Xun, Yao Yin, and others in two scrolls, and submitted them to Emperor Suzong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Those who at the time looked down on Xun claimed he had surrendered to the rebels. Han thereupon recounted Xun's deeds in defending the city, wrote biographies of Zhang Xun, Yao Yin, and others in two scrolls, and submitted them to Emperor Suzong.

manualTranslations.zh: 方明巡之忠義士，友稱之。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereby Xun's loyalty and righteousness as a true man were made clear, and his friends praised him for it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In this way Xun's loyal and righteous character was made clear, and his friends praised Han for it.

manualTranslations.zh: 上元中，為衛縣尉，入朝為侍御史。
manualTranslations.literal: During the Shangyuan era he served as sheriff of Wei county; he entered court and became an attendant censor.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan reign he served as sheriff of Wei county, then entered court as an attendant censor.

manualTranslations.zh: 陸據者，周上庸公騰六代孫。
manualTranslations.literal: Lu Ju was the sixth-generation descendant of Teng, Duke of Shangyong of Zhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Lu Ju was a sixth-generation descendant of Teng, Duke of Shangyong of Zhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 少孤，文章俊逸，言論縱横。
manualTranslations.literal: He lost his parents while young; his writing was brilliant and unfettered, and his speech was bold and far-ranging.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he wrote with brilliance and ease and spoke with bold, sweeping eloquence.

manualTranslations.zh: 年三十餘，始遊京師，舉進士。
manualTranslations.literal: When he was a little over thirty he first traveled to the capital and took the jinshi examination.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Not until he was in his thirties did he first go to the capital and sit for the jinshi examination.

manualTranslations.zh: 公卿覽其文，稱重之。
manualTranslations.literal: High ministers and nobles who read his writing praised and valued him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When leading officials read his work, they spoke highly of him.

manualTranslations.zh: 辟為從事，累官至司勲員外郎。
manualTranslations.literal: He was recruited as an aide and rose in office to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel's merit office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was recruited as a staff officer and rose through successive posts to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寳十三載，卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in 754.

manualTranslations.zh: 開元、天寳間，文士知名者，汴州崔顥，京兆王昌齡、高適，㐮陽孟浩然，皆名位不振，唯高適官逹，自有傳。
manualTranslations.literal: Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, among literary men of renown were Cui Hao of Bian prefecture, Wang Changling and Gao Shi of Jingzhao, and Meng Haoran of Xiangyang. All failed to achieve matching rank and fame; only Gao Shi attained high office and has his own biography.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns, well-known men of letters included Cui Hao of Bianzhou, Wang Changling and Gao Shi of Jingzhao, and Meng Haoran of Xiangyang. None of them rose to commensurate rank and standing except Gao Shi, who attained high office and has his own biography.

manualTranslations.zh: 崔顥者，登進士第。
manualTranslations.literal: Cui Hao passed the jinshi examination.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Cui Hao passed the jinshi civil examination.

manualTranslations.zh: 有俊才無士行，好蒱博飲酒。
manualTranslations.literal: He had brilliant talent but no conduct befitting a gentleman; he loved gambling and drinking.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had outstanding talent but little of a gentleman's conduct, and was fond of gambling and drink.

manualTranslations.zh: 及遊京師，娶妻擇有貎者，稍不惬意即去之，前後數四。
manualTranslations.literal: When he traveled to the capital he took wives, choosing those with good looks; if he was slightly displeased he would leave them, doing so four or five times in all.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he went to the capital he married for beauty, choosing attractive women, and if he was the least dissatisfied he would cast them off—he did this four or five times in all.

manualTranslations.zh: 累官司勲員外郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Through successive offices he reached vice director in the Ministry of Personnel's merit office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寳十三年，卒。
manualTranslations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao he died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in 754.

manualTranslations.zh: 王昌齡者，進士登第，補秘書省，校書郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Changling passed the jinshi examination, was appointed to the Secretariat, and served as collator.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Changling passed the jinshi examination and was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

manualTranslations.zh: 又以博學宏詞登科，再遷汜水縣尉，不護細行，屢見貶斥，卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He also passed the examination in erudition and grand composition, was transferred again to sheriff of Sishui county, failed to guard his minor conduct, was repeatedly demoted and censured, and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He also passed the erudite-literary examination, was later transferred to sheriff of Sishui county, failed to watch his lesser conduct, was demoted and censured repeatedly, and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 昌齡為文緒微而思清，有集五卷。
manualTranslations.literal: Changling's writing was fine in texture and clear in thought; he had a collected works in five scrolls.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Changling wrote in a finely wrought style with lucid thought, and left a collected works in five scrolls.

manualTranslations.zh: 孟浩然，隠鹿門山，以詩自適。
manualTranslations.literal: Meng Haoran lived in seclusion on Mount Lumen and found contentment in poetry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Meng Haoran lived in seclusion on Mount Lumen and found his fulfillment in poetry.

manualTranslations.zh: 年四十來遊京師，應進士不第，還。
manualTranslations.literal: At the age of forty he came to the capital, took the jinshi examination without success, and returned home.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At forty he traveled to the capital, failed the jinshi examination, and went home.

manualTranslations.zh: 襄陽張九齡鎮荆州，署為從事，與之唱和，不逹而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Zhang Jiuling of Xiangyang governed Jing prefecture, appointed him as an aide, exchanged poems with him, and he died without attaining high office.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jiuling of Xiangyang governed Jingzhou, he appointed Meng Haoran as a staff officer and exchanged poems with him. Meng died without attaining high office.

manualTranslations.zh: 元德秀者，河南人，字紫芝。
manualTranslations.literal: Yuan Dexiu was a man of Henan; his style name was Zizhi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yuan Dexiu came from Henan; his courtesy name was Zizhi.

manualTranslations.zh: 開元二十一年登進士第。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 733 he passed the jinshi civil examination.

manualTranslations.zh: 性純朴，無緣餙，動師古道。
manualTranslations.literal: His nature was plain and unadorned; he made no pretense of ornament and always took the ancient way as his model.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was plain and unpretentious by nature, shunned artificial adornment, and always modeled himself on the ancient way.

manualTranslations.zh: 父為延州刺史。
manualTranslations.literal: His father served as prefect of Yan prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father served as prefect of Yanzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 德秀少孤貧，事母以孝聞。
manualTranslations.literal: Dexiu was orphaned and poor in youth; he served his mother and became known for filial piety.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dexiu was orphaned and poor as a youth; he cared for his mother and became known for filial devotion.

manualTranslations.zh: 開元中，從鄉賦，歳遊京師，不忍離親，毎行則自負板輿，與母詣長安。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, when he went up from the local district levy each year to the capital, unable to bear leaving his parent, whenever he traveled he himself carried a palanquin on his back and, with his mother, proceeded to Chang'an.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, when he went up each year for the provincial examinations, he could not bear to leave his mother behind. Each time he made the journey he carried her in a palanquin on his own back all the way to Chang'an.

manualTranslations.zh: 登第後，母亡，廬於墓所，食無鹽酪，藉無茵席，刺血畫像寫佛經。
manualTranslations.literal: After passing the examination, his mother died; he dwelt in a hut at the tomb site, ate without salt or dairy, slept on straw without mat or cushion, pricked his blood to paint her portrait, and copied Buddhist sutras.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After he passed the examination, his mother died. He lived in a hut beside her grave, ate no salt or dairy, slept on straw without even a mat, pricked his blood to paint her portrait, and copied Buddhist sutras.

manualTranslations.zh: 乆之，以孤㓜牽於禄仕，調授邢州南和尉。
manualTranslations.literal: After a long time, because orphaned youth constrained him to accept salary and office, he was assigned by transfer as assistant magistrate of Nanhe in Xing prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Eventually, the need to earn a living as an orphan drew him into official service, and he was posted as assistant magistrate of Nanhe in Xingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 佐治有惠政，黜陟使上聞，召補龍武録事參軍。
manualTranslations.literal: In assisting administration he had benevolent policies; the promotion-and-demotion inspector reported him to the throne, and he was summoned and appointed recorder-adjutant of the Longwu Army.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His assistance in governance brought benevolent rule; the touring inspector reported this to the court, and he was summoned to serve as recorder-adjutant of the Longwu Army.

manualTranslations.zh: 德秀早失恃怙，縗麻相繼，不及親在而娶。
manualTranslations.literal: Dexiu had early lost both parents; mourning garments followed one after another, and he had not married while his parents were alive.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Dexiu had lost both parents early; periods of mourning followed one after another, and he had never married while they were alive.

manualTranslations.zh: 既孤之後，遂不娶婚。
manualTranslations.literal: After becoming orphaned, he then did not marry.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once orphaned, he never married at all.

manualTranslations.zh: 族人以絶嗣規之，德秀曰：“吾兄有子，繼先人之祀。
manualTranslations.literal: Clansmen admonished him because the line would end; Dexiu said: "My elder brother has a son who will continue the ancestral sacrifices.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Kinsmen warned that he would leave no heir, but Dexiu said, "My elder brother has a son to carry on the ancestral rites.

manualTranslations.zh: ”以兄子婚娶，家貧無以為禮，求為魯山令。
manualTranslations.literal: " When his brother's son was to marry and the family was too poor to provide the rites, he sought appointment as magistrate of Lushan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " When his brother's son was to marry and the family could not afford the ceremony, he sought appointment as magistrate of Lushan.

manualTranslations.zh: 先是，墮車傷足，不任趨拜，汝郡守以客禮待之。
manualTranslations.literal: Earlier, he had fallen from a cart and injured his foot, could not perform the hurried bow, and the prefect of Ru commandery treated him with guest ceremony.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had earlier fallen from a cart and injured his foot, so he could not perform the quick ceremonial bow; the prefect of Ru treated him with the courtesy due a guest.

manualTranslations.zh: 部人為盗，吏捕之，繋獄。
manualTranslations.literal: A man of the district became a thief; officers arrested him and bound him in prison.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A local man turned to theft; officers arrested him and held him in prison.

manualTranslations.zh: 會縣界有猛獸為暴，盗自陳曰：“願格殺猛獸以自贖。
manualTranslations.literal: It happened that within the county border a fierce beast was ravaging; the thief volunteered, saying: "I wish to slay the fierce beast to redeem myself.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Just then a fierce beast was terrorizing the county border. The thief stepped forward and said, "I am willing to kill the beast to earn my pardon.

manualTranslations.zh: ”徳秀許之。
manualTranslations.literal: " Dexiu granted it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Dexiu agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 胥吏曰：“盗詭計茍免，擅放官囚，無乃累乎？
manualTranslations.literal: A clerk said: "The thief's trick is to escape for the moment; to release an official prisoner on your own authority—will this not bring trouble upon us?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: A clerk said, "This is only a ruse to escape punishment. If you release a prisoner on your own authority, will we not all be blamed?

manualTranslations.zh: ”徳秀曰：“吾不欲負約，累則吾坐，必請不及諸君。
manualTranslations.literal: " Dexiu said: "I do not wish to break my word; if there is trouble I alone shall bear it—rest assured it shall not reach you gentlemen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " Dexiu replied, "I will not break my word. If blame falls, I alone shall answer for it—I promise it will not reach any of you.

manualTranslations.zh: ”即破械出之。
manualTranslations.literal: " Immediately he broke the shackles and released him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: " He immediately removed the man's restraints and set him free.

manualTranslations.zh: 翌日，格猛獸而還。
manualTranslations.literal: The next day, he slew the fierce beast and returned.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next day the man killed the beast and returned.

manualTranslations.zh: 誠信化人，大率此類。
manualTranslations.literal: His sincerity and trustworthiness transformed people; most cases were like this.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He transformed people through sincerity and good faith; most of his conduct was of this sort.

manualTranslations.zh: 秩滿，南遊陸渾，見佳山水，杳然有長往之志，乃結廬山阿。
manualTranslations.literal: When his term expired, he traveled south to Luhun, saw fine mountains and waters, and with distant serenity conceived the resolve to leave the world for good; he then built a hut in a mountain dell.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he traveled south to Luhun. Struck by the beautiful landscape, he felt a deep longing to withdraw from the world for good and built a hut in a mountain hollow.

manualTranslations.zh: 歳屬饑歉，庖厨不㸑，而彈琴讀書，怡然自得。
manualTranslations.literal: A year fell into famine and dearth; the kitchen did not cook, yet he played the zither and read books, content and at ease.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In a year of famine his kitchen went cold, yet he played the zither and read books, entirely content.

manualTranslations.zh: 好事者載酒餚過之，不擇賢不肖，與之對酌，陶陶然遺身物外。
manualTranslations.literal: Men who delighted in such things brought wine and delicacies to visit him; he did not choose the worthy from the unworthy, drank facing them, and in easy joy forgot himself beyond worldly things.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Enthusiasts came bearing wine and food. He made no distinction between the worthy and the unworthy, drank with them freely, and in easy joy left the world behind.

manualTranslations.zh: 琴觴之餘，間以文詠，率情而書，語無雕刻。
manualTranslations.literal: Beyond zither and wine-cup, he would occasionally compose literary verse; he wrote as feeling moved him, with language unchiseled by artifice.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Between zither and wine cup he sometimes turned to verse, writing straight from feeling without ornamental carving of language.

manualTranslations.zh: 所著《季子聽樂論》、《蹇士賦》，為高人所稱。
manualTranslations.literal: His compositions "Jizi Hears Music" and "Rhapsody on the Lame Scholar" were praised by eminent men.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His works "On Prince Ji Listening to Music" and "Rhapsody on the Limping Scholar" won praise from leading men of letters.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寳十三年卒，時年五十九，門人相諡為文行先生。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Tianbao, at age fifty-nine; his disciples together posthumously styled him Master Wenxing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in Tianbao 13, aged fifty-nine; his disciples posthumously honored him as Master Wenxing.

manualTranslations.zh: 士大夫高其行，不名，謂之元魯山。
manualTranslations.literal: Scholar-officials admired his conduct and did not use his personal name, calling him Yuan of Lushan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials revered his character and, rather than use his personal name, called him Yuan of Lushan.

manualTranslations.zh: 王維，字摩詰，太原祁人。
manualTranslations.literal: Wang Wei, styled Mojie, was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, whose courtesy name was Mojie, came from Qi in Taiyuan.

manualTranslations.zh: 父處㢘，終汾州司馬，徙家于蒲，遂為河東人。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Chulian ended as vice administrator of Fen prefecture; the family moved to Pu and thus became men of Hedong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Chulian ended his career as vice administrator of Fenzhou; the family then moved to Pu and became natives of Hedong.

manualTranslations.zh: 維開元九年進士擢第。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Kaiyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei passed the jinshi examination in Kaiyuan 9.

manualTranslations.zh: 事母崔氏以孝聞。
manualTranslations.literal: He served his mother, Lady Cui, and was famed for filial devotion.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served his mother, Lady Cui, and was known for his filial devotion.

manualTranslations.zh: 與弟縉俱有俊才，博學多藝亦齊名，閨門友悌，多士推之。
manualTranslations.literal: With his younger brother Jin he alike had outstanding talent; their broad learning and many arts were equally famed, and within the household they were friendly and deferential as brothers, so many scholars praised them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Jin were both gifted; their broad learning and many talents won equal renown, and within the household they were devoted brothers, so scholars widely praised them.

manualTranslations.zh: 歴右拾遺、監察御史、左補闕、庫部郎中。
manualTranslations.literal: He served successively as Right Reminder, investigating censor, Left Supplementation-er, and director in the Ministry of Revenue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He served successively as Right Reminder, investigating censor, Left Supplementation-er, and director in the Ministry of Revenue.

manualTranslations.zh: 居母䘮，柴毁骨立，殆不勝䘮。
manualTranslations.literal: During mourning for his mother, he was wasted to the bone like firewood, almost unable to bear the mourning.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he wasted away to skin and bone, nearly unable to endure the grief.

manualTranslations.zh: 服闋，拜吏部郎中。
manualTranslations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寳末，為給事中。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he served as Supervising Secretariat Drafter.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Near the end of Tianbao he served as Supervising Secretariat Drafter.

manualTranslations.zh: 禄山䧟兩都，玄宗出幸，維扈從不及，為賊所得。
manualTranslations.literal: When Lushan seized the two capitals, Emperor Xuanzong fled on tour; Wei could not keep up with the entourage and was captured by the rebels.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When An Lushan seized the two capitals, Emperor Xuanzong fled the court. Wei failed to join the imperial entourage and was captured by the rebels.

manualTranslations.zh: 維服藥取痢，偽稱瘖病。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei took medicine to induce dysentery and falsely claimed he was mute from illness.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei took medicine to induce dysentery and pretended to be mute from illness.

manualTranslations.zh: 禄山素憐之，遣人迎置洛陽，拘於普施寺，迫以偽署。
manualTranslations.literal: Lushan had always favored him, sent men to welcome him and install him in Luoyang, kept him confined at Puji Monastery, and compelled him to accept a false appointment.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An Lushan had always favored him, sent men to bring him to Luoyang, confined him at Puji Monastery, and forced him to accept a false appointment.

manualTranslations.zh: 禄山宴其徒於凝碧宫，其樂工皆梨園弟子、教坊工人。
manualTranslations.literal: Lushan feasted his followers at Ningbi Palace; the musicians were all Liyuan disciples and Directorate of Music craftsmen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: An Lushan feasted his followers at Ningbi Palace; the musicians were all Liyuan disciples and craftsmen of the Directorate of Music.

manualTranslations.zh: 維聞之悲惻，潛為詩曰：「萬户傷心生野煙，百官何日再朝天？
manualTranslations.literal: Wei heard this and grieved; secretly he composed a poem saying: "In ten thousand homes sorrow rises with wild smoke—when shall the hundred officials again bow to Heaven's court?
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei heard this and was stricken with grief. Secretly he composed a poem: "In ten thousand homes sorrow rises with wild smoke—when will the hundred officials again bow to the Son of Heaven?

manualTranslations.zh: 秋槐花落空宫裏，凝碧池頭奏筦絃。
manualTranslations.literal: Autumn locust blossoms fall in the empty palace; at the head of Ningbi Pool pipe and string are played.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Autumn locust blossoms fall in the empty palace; at the head of Ningbi Pool, pipes and strings are played.

manualTranslations.zh: 賊平，陷賊官三等定罪。
manualTranslations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, officials who had served under the rebels were sentenced under the three grades of guilt.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, officials who had served under the rebels were judged under the three grades of culpability.

manualTranslations.zh: 維以凝碧詩聞于行在，肅宗嘉之，會縉請削己刑部侍郎以贖兄罪，特宥之，責授太子中允，乾元中，遷太子中庶子、中書舍人，復拜給事中，轉尚書右丞。
manualTranslations.literal: Because Wei's Ningbi poem reached the traveling court, Emperor Suzong praised it; at the same time Jin asked to give up his own post as Vice Minister of Justice to redeem his brother's guilt, and Wei was specially pardoned, demoted and appointed as Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent; in the Qianyuan era he was transferred to Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Secretariat Drafter, again appointed Supervising Secretariat Drafter, and then moved to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei's Ningbi poem reached the emperor at the traveling court, and Emperor Suzong praised it. At the same time Jin asked to surrender his own post as Vice Minister of Justice to redeem his brother's offense, and Wei was specially pardoned and demoted to Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent. In the Qianyuan era he rose to Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Secretariat Drafter, was again appointed Supervising Secretariat Drafter, and then became Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue.

manualTranslations.zh: 維以詩名盛於開元、天寶間，昆仲宦遊兩都，凡諸王駙馬豪右貴勢之門，無不拂席迎之，寧王、薛王待之如師友。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei's poetic fame flourished between Kaiyuan and Tianbao; the brothers served in office in the two capitals, and at the gates of princes, imperial sons-in-law, powerful magnates, and noble families none failed to sweep the mat and welcome them; the Princes of Ning and Xue treated them like teachers and friends.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei's poetic fame flourished during Kaiyuan and Tianbao. The brothers held office in both capitals, and at the gates of princes, imperial sons-in-law, and powerful nobles none failed to sweep the mat and welcome them; the Princes of Ning and Xue treated them as teachers and friends.

manualTranslations.zh: 維尤長五言詩。
manualTranslations.literal: Wei was especially skilled in five-character verse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wei was especially accomplished in five-character poetry.

manualTranslations.zh: 人有得奏樂圖，不知其名，維視之曰：「霓裳第三疊第一拍也。
manualTranslations.literal: Someone obtained a painting of musicians performing; not knowing its title, Wei looked at it and said: "This is the first beat of the third movement of Rainbow Skirts.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Someone acquired a painting of a musical performance but did not know its title. Wei looked at it and said, "This is the first beat of the third movement of 'Rainbow Skirts.'

manualTranslations.zh: 好事者集樂工按之，一無差，咸服其精思。
manualTranslations.literal: Those who delight in such things gathered musicians to perform according to it; not one note was off, and all admired his refined insight.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Enthusiasts assembled musicians to perform the piece accordingly, and not a single note was wrong. All marveled at his keen musical insight.

manualTranslations.zh: 維弟兄俱奉佛，居常蔬食，不茹葷血，晚年長齋，不衣文綵。
manualTranslations.literal: Both Wei and his brother practiced Buddhism; in daily life they ate vegetables, abstained from meat and blood, in later years kept long fasts, and wore no patterned silk.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Wei and his brother both devoted themselves to Buddhism. They ordinarily ate vegetarian food and abstained from meat; in later years Wang Wei kept long fasts and wore no fine patterned silks.

manualTranslations.zh: 得宋之問藍田别墅，在輞口，輞水周於舍下，别漲竹洲花塢，與道友裴廸浮舟往來，彈琴賦詩，嘯詠終日。
manualTranslations.literal: He obtained Song Zhiwen's Lantian villa at Wangkou; Wang River circled below the house, and separately he created bamboo islets and flower embankments; with his Daoist friend Pei Di he went back and forth in boats, playing the zither, composing poetry, and singing all day.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He acquired Song Zhiwen's villa at Lantian, at the mouth of Wang River, where the river wound around his dwelling below. There he laid out separate bamboo islets and flower embankments, and with his spiritual companion Pei Di he drifted back and forth in boats, playing the zither, composing poetry, and singing through the day.

manualTranslations.zh: 甞聚其田園所為詩，號輞川集。
manualTranslations.literal: Once he gathered the poems he had written in his garden estate and called the collection Wangchuan ji.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He once collected the poems he had written at his country estate and titled the collection Wangchuan ji.

manualTranslations.zh: 在京師日飯十數名僧，以玄談為樂。
manualTranslations.literal: In the capital he daily dined with a dozen or so monks and took refined discourse as his pleasure.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: While in the capital he daily shared meals with a dozen or so monks and took pleasure in abstruse Buddhist discussion.

manualTranslations.zh: 齋中無所有，唯茶鐺、藥臼、經案、繩牀而已。
manualTranslations.literal: In his study there was nothing at all except a tea kettle, a medicine mortar, a sutra desk, and a rope bed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His study held almost nothing—only a tea kettle, a medicine mortar, a sutra desk, and a rope bed.

manualTranslations.zh: 退朝之後，焚香獨坐，以禪誦為事。
manualTranslations.literal: After leaving court he burned incense and sat alone, making Chan recitation his occupation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After leaving court he would burn incense and sit alone, devoting himself to meditation and chanting.

manualTranslations.zh: 妻亡不再娶，三十年孤居一室，屏絶塵累。
manualTranslations.literal: When his wife died he did not marry again; for thirty years he lived alone in one room, shutting out worldly entanglements.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After his wife died he never remarried. For thirty years he lived alone in a single room, shutting out worldly cares.

manualTranslations.zh: 乾元二年七月卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He died in the seventh month of the second year of Qianyuan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of 759.

manualTranslations.zh: 臨終之際，以縉在鳳翔，忽索筆作别縉書，又與平生親故作别書數幅，多敦厲朋友奉佛脩心之旨，捨筆而絶。
manualTranslations.literal: At the moment of death, because Jin was at Fengxiang, he suddenly asked for a brush and wrote a farewell letter to Jin; he also wrote several farewell letters to close friends of his lifetime, mostly urging friends to practice Buddhism and cultivate the mind, then laid down the brush and died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: On his deathbed, learning that Wang Jin was at Fengxiang, he suddenly asked for a brush and wrote a farewell letter to him. He also wrote several parting letters to lifelong friends, mostly urging them to devote themselves to Buddhism and spiritual cultivation, then set down the brush and died.

manualTranslations.zh: 代宗時，縉為宰相，代宗好文，常謂縉曰：「卿之伯氏，天寳中詩名冠代，朕嘗於諸王座聞其樂章。
manualTranslations.literal: In the time of Daizong, Jin was chief minister; Daizong loved literature and often said to Jin: "Your elder brother, in the Tianbao era his poetic fame topped the age; I once heard his musical compositions at the princes' seats.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Daizong, Wang Jin served as chief minister. Daizong loved literature and often said to him, "Your elder brother's poetry was the finest of his age during the Tianbao reign. I once heard his compositions performed before the princes.

manualTranslations.zh: 今有多少文集，卿可進來。
manualTranslations.literal: How many collected writings are there now? You may present them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: How much of his collected writings survives? You may submit it to me.

manualTranslations.zh: 縉曰：「臣兄開元中詩百千餘篇，天寳事後，十不存一。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin said: "My brother in the Kaiyuan era had more than a hundred poems; after the Tianbao events, not one in ten remained.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jin replied, "My brother wrote more than a hundred poems during the Kaiyuan reign, but after the Tianbao upheavals fewer than one in ten survived.

manualTranslations.zh: 比於中外親故間相與編綴，都得四百餘篇。
manualTranslations.literal: Recently, compiling them together with relatives and friends inside and outside court, we obtained in all more than four hundred pieces.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Recently, by gathering what we could from relatives and friends inside and outside court, we recovered more than four hundred pieces.

manualTranslations.zh: 翌日上之，帝優詔襃賞。
manualTranslations.literal: The next day he presented them; the emperor issued a gracious edict praising and rewarding him.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The next day he submitted the collection, and the emperor responded with a gracious edict of praise and reward.

manualTranslations.zh: 縉自有傳。
manualTranslations.literal: Jin has his own biography.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Wang Jin has his own biography elsewhere.

manualTranslations.zh: 李白字太白，山東人。
manualTranslations.literal: Li Bai, style name Taibai, was a man of Shandong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Bai, whose courtesy name was Taibai, came from Shandong.

manualTranslations.zh: 少有逸才，志氣宏放，飄然有超世之心，父爲任城尉，因家焉。
manualTranslations.literal: In youth he had exceptional talent; his spirit was broad and unrestrained, and he seemed to have a mind set on transcending the world. His father served as district magistrate of Rencheng, and the family settled there.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From youth he possessed exceptional talent, a bold and expansive spirit, and an air of one who meant to rise above the world. His father served as district magistrate of Rencheng, and the family made its home there.

manualTranslations.zh: 少與魯中諸生孔巢父、韓沔、裴政、張叔明、陶沔等隠於徂徠山，酣歌縱酒，時號「竹溪六逸」
manualTranslations.literal: In youth, together with the scholars of Lu—Kong Chaofu, Han Mian, Pei Zheng, Zhang Shuming, Tao Mian, and others—he retired to Mount Culaishan, singing freely and drinking without restraint; at the time they were called "the Six Recluses of Zhuxi"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In his youth, together with the scholars of Lu—Kong Chaofu, Han Mian, Pei Zheng, Zhang Shuming, Tao Mian, and others—he withdrew to Mount Culaishan, singing freely and drinking without restraint. At the time they were known as "the Six Recluses of Bamboo Creek"

manualTranslations.zh: 天寳初，客遊會稽，與道士吳筠隱於剡中。
manualTranslations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he traveled as a guest to Kuaiji and, with the Daoist Wu Yun, retired in Shan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao reign he traveled as a guest to Kuaiji and lived in seclusion in Shan with the Daoist Wu Yun.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣而玄宗詔筠赴京師，筠薦之於朝，遣使召之，與筠俱待詔翰林。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon afterward Xuanzong summoned Yun to the capital; Yun recommended him to court, and the emperor sent envoys to summon him; together with Yun he awaited edicts in the Hanlin Academy.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Xuanzong summoned Wu Yun to the capital. Yun recommended Li Bai at court, and the emperor sent envoys to summon him. Li Bai and Wu Yun both served as Hanlin academicians awaiting imperial edicts.

manualTranslations.zh: 白旣嗜酒，日與飲徒醉於酒肆。
manualTranslations.literal: Bai, being fond of wine, daily got drunk with drinking companions in wine shops.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Bai was devoted to wine and spent his days drinking himself drunk with companions in taverns.

manualTranslations.zh: 玄宗度曲，欲造樂府新詞，亟召白，白已臥於酒肆矣。
manualTranslations.literal: Xuanzong composed a tune and wished to create new lyrics for the Music Bureau; he urgently summoned Bai, but Bai was already asleep in a wine shop.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong composed a tune and wanted new Music Bureau lyrics written for it, he urgently summoned Li Bai—but Li Bai was already asleep in a tavern.

manualTranslations.zh: 召入，以水灑面，即令秉筆，頃之成十餘章，帝頗嘉之。
manualTranslations.literal: He was summoned in; water was sprinkled on his face, and he was immediately ordered to take up the brush; in no time he completed more than ten pieces, and the emperor was quite pleased.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he was brought in, attendants splashed water on his face and immediately told him to write. In a short time he produced more than ten pieces, and the emperor was greatly pleased.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘗沉醉殿上，引足令高力士脫靴，由是斥去。
manualTranslations.literal: Once, drunk on the palace hall, he extended his foot and ordered Gao Lishi to remove his boots; for this he was dismissed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once, while drunk in the palace hall, he stretched out his foot and ordered Gao Lishi to pull off his boots. For this he was sent away from court.

manualTranslations.zh: 乃浪迹江湖，終日沉飲。
manualTranslations.literal: Thereupon he wandered the rivers and lakes, sinking into drink all day long.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereafter he wandered the country, drinking without restraint day after day.

manualTranslations.zh: 時侍御史崔宗之謫官金陵，與白詩酒唱和。
manualTranslations.literal: At the time the attendant censor Cui Zongzhi had been demoted to an office at Jinling and exchanged poems and wine with Bai.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time the attendant censor Cui Zongzhi had been demoted to a post at Jinling, and he exchanged poems and wine with Li Bai.

manualTranslations.zh: 嘗月夜乘舟，自采石達金陵，白衣宮錦袍，於舟中顧瞻笑傲，傍若無人。
manualTranslations.literal: Once on a moonlit night he took a boat from Caishi to Jinling, dressed in white palace brocade robes; in the boat he looked about laughing proudly, as if no one else were nearby.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Once, on a moonlit night, he took a boat from Caishi to Jinling dressed in white palace brocade robes, looking about the boat with a proud, laughing air as though no one else were present.

manualTranslations.zh: 初賀知章見白，賞之曰：「此天上謫仙人也。
manualTranslations.literal: When He Zhizhang first saw Bai, he admired him and said: "This is an immortal banished from heaven.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When He Zhizhang first met Li Bai, he praised him and said, "This is an immortal banished from heaven.

manualTranslations.zh: 祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀，在途以永王璘為江淮兵馬都督、揚州節度大使。
manualTranslations.literal: In the rebellion of Lushan, Xuanzong fled to Shu; on the way he appointed Prince Yong Li Lin commander-in-chief of the Jiang-Huai armies and military commissioner of Yangzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion, Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu. En route he appointed Prince Yong (Li Lin) commander of the Jiang-Huai armies and military commissioner of Yangzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 白在宣州謁見，遂辟爲從事。
manualTranslations.literal: Bai went to Xuanzhou to pay his respects and was then recruited as an aide.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Li Bai went to Xuanzhou to pay his respects and was recruited as an aide on Prince Yong's staff.

manualTranslations.zh: 永王謀亂，兵敗，白坐長流夜郎。
manualTranslations.literal: Prince Yong plotted rebellion; his army was defeated, and Bai was punished with exile to Ye Lang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Prince Yong plotted rebellion and his forces were defeated, Li Bai was sentenced to long-term exile in Ye Lang.

manualTranslations.zh: 後遇赦得還，竟以飲酒過度，醉死於宣城。
manualTranslations.literal: Later he met an amnesty and was able to return, but in the end, through excessive drinking, he died drunk at Xuancheng.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He later received an amnesty and was able to return, but in the end he drank himself to death at Xuancheng.

manualTranslations.zh: 有文集二十卷，行於時。
manualTranslations.literal: He had a collected writings in twenty scrolls, which circulated in his time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His collected writings in twenty scrolls circulated widely in his day.

manualTranslations.zh: 杜甫，字子美，本襄陽人，後徙河南鞏縣。
manualTranslations.literal: Du Fu, style name Zimei, was originally a man of Xiangyang and later moved to Gong county in Henan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Fu, whose courtesy name was Zimei, was originally from Xiangyang and later moved to Gong county in Henan.

manualTranslations.zh: 曽祖依藝，位終鞏令。
manualTranslations.literal: His great-grandfather Yiyi ended his office as magistrate of Gong.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Du Yiyi served to the end of his career as magistrate of Gong.

manualTranslations.zh: 祖審言，位終膳部員外郎，自有。
manualTranslations.literal: His grandfather Shenyan ended his office as assistant director in the Ministry of Rites; he has his own [biography].
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His grandfather Du Shenyan served to the end of his career as assistant director in the Ministry of Rites; he has his own biography elsewhere.

manualTranslations.zh: 父閑，終奉天令。
manualTranslations.literal: His father Xian ended as magistrate of Fengtian.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His father Du Xian ended his career as magistrate of Fengtian.

manualTranslations.zh: 甫天寳初應進士不第。
manualTranslations.literal: Fu at the beginning of Tianbao took the jinshi examination but did not pass.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao reign Du Fu took the jinshi examination but failed.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寳末，獻《三大禮賦》，宗奇之，召試文章，授京兆府兵曹叅軍。
manualTranslations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he presented the Three Great Rites Fu; the emperor found it remarkable, summoned him to test his writing, and appointed him military staff officer of the capital prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianbao reign he submitted the Three Great Rites Fu. Emperor Xuanzong was impressed, summoned him for a literary examination, and appointed him military staff officer of the capital prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 十五載，禄山䧟京師，肅宗徴兵靈武，甫自京師宵遁赴河西謁肅宗，於彭原郡拜右拾遺。
manualTranslations.literal: In the fifteenth year, An Lushan captured the capital. Suzong raised troops at Lingwu. Fu fled the capital by night, went west of the river to seek an audience with Suzong, and at Pengyuan commandery was appointed Remonstrance Officer of the Right.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 755 An Lushan took the capital. Emperor Suzong mustered troops at Lingwu. Du Fu slipped away from the capital by night, made his way west of the river to see Suzong, and at Pengyuan was appointed remonstrance officer of the right.

manualTranslations.zh: 房琯布衣時與甫善，時琯為宰相，請自帥師討賊，帝許之。
manualTranslations.literal: When Fang Guan was still in common dress he was on good terms with Fu. At that time Fang was chief minister and requested to lead troops himself to suppress the rebels; the emperor granted it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Fang Guan had been friendly with Du Fu when they were commoners. Now Fang was chief minister and asked to lead an army himself against the rebels; the emperor agreed.

manualTranslations.zh: 其年十月，琯兵敗於陳濤斜。
manualTranslations.literal: That year, in the tenth month, Fang's army was defeated at Chentao Slope.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That October Fang Guan's army was defeated at Chentao Slope.

manualTranslations.zh: 明年春，琯罷相，甫上疏言琯有才，不宜罷免。
manualTranslations.literal: The next spring Fang was removed as chief minister. Fu submitted a memorial saying Fang had talent and should not be dismissed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The following spring Fang Guan was dismissed as chief minister. Du Fu memorialized the throne that Fang had talent and ought not be removed.

manualTranslations.zh: 肅宗怒，貶琯為刺史，出甫為華州司功叅軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Suzong grew angry, demoted Fang to provincial governor, and sent Fu out as secretary in Huazhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Suzong was angered, demoted Fang Guan to provincial governor, and sent Du Fu out as secretary in Huazhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 時關畿亂離，糓食踊貴，甫寓居成州同谷縣，自負薪採稆，兒女餓殍者數人。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time the capital region was in chaos and dislocation, and grain grew extremely dear. Fu lodged in Tonggu county, Chengzhou, carrying firewood and gathering wild grains on his back; several of his children died of starvation.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The capital region was then in turmoil and grain prices soared. Du Fu lived in Tonggu county, Chengzhou, carrying firewood and gathering wild grains on his back; several of his children starved to death.

manualTranslations.zh: 乆之，召補京兆府功曹。
manualTranslations.literal: After a long while he was summoned and reappointed as secretary of the capital prefecture.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled and appointed secretary of the capital prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 上元二年冬，黄門侍郎、鄭國公嚴武鎮成都，奏為節度叅謀檢校尚書工部員外郎，賜緋魚袋。
manualTranslations.literal: In winter of the second year of Shangyuan, Vice Censor of the Yellow Gate and Duke of Zheng Yan Wu was stationed at Chengdu. He memorialized that Fu should serve as staff planning officer and acting vice minister of works, and he was granted the purple robe and fish insignia.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the winter of 762 Yan Wu, vice censor of the yellow gate and duke of Zheng, held Chengdu. He memorialized that Du Fu be made staff planning officer and acting vice minister of works, and Du Fu was granted the purple robe and fish insignia.

manualTranslations.zh: 武與甫世舊，待遇甚隆，甫性褊躁無器度，恃恩放恣，甞慿醉登武之牀瞪視武曰：「嚴挺之乃有此兒！
manualTranslations.literal: Yan Wu and Fu were old family friends, and Yan Wu treated him with great favor. Fu was by nature narrow-minded, quick-tempered, and without breadth of character; relying on favor he behaved recklessly. Once, drunk, he climbed onto Yan Wu's couch, stared at Yan Wu, and said: "Yan Tingzhi had a son like this!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yan Wu and Du Fu were old family friends, and Yan Wu treated him with great generosity. Du Fu was narrow-minded, quick-tempered, and lacking in forbearance; trusting in favor he grew reckless. Once, drunk, he climbed onto Yan Wu's couch, stared at him, and said: "So Yan Tingzhi had a son like this!

manualTranslations.zh: 武雖急暴，不以為忤。
manualTranslations.literal: Though Yan Wu was quick-tempered and violent, he took no offense.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though Yan Wu was hot-tempered and rough, he did not take it amiss.

manualTranslations.zh: 甫於成都浣花里種竹植樹，結廬枕江，縱酒嘯詠，與田夫野老相狎，蕩無拘檢，嚴武過之，有時不冠，其傲誕如此。
manualTranslations.literal: At Huanhua Lane in Chengdu Fu planted bamboo and trees, built a hut beside the river, drank freely, chanted and sang, and mingled familiarly with farmers and rustics, utterly unrestrained. When Yan Wu visited, he sometimes went bareheaded—so arrogant and unrestrained was he.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At Huanhua Lane in Chengdu Du Fu planted bamboo and trees and built a hut beside the river, drinking freely and chanting poetry, mingling freely with farmers and rustics without restraint. When Yan Wu visited, he sometimes received him bareheaded—so insolently unrestrained was he.

manualTranslations.zh: 永泰元年夏，武卒，甫無所依。
manualTranslations.literal: In summer of the first year of Yongtai, Yan Wu died, and Fu had nothing to depend on.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the summer of 765 Yan Wu died, and Du Fu was left without support.

manualTranslations.zh: 及郭英乂代武鎮成都，英乂武人粗暴，無能刺謁，乃遊東蜀依高適。
manualTranslations.literal: When Guo Yingyi replaced Yan Wu as military commander at Chengdu, Yingyi was a rough soldier and violent; Fu could not manage the formal calls of respect and therefore traveled east in Shu to seek refuge with Gao Shi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Guo Yingyi replaced Yan Wu at Chengdu, Yingyi was a rough soldier and brutal; Du Fu could not manage the formal courtesies and so traveled east in Shu to rely on Gao Shi.

manualTranslations.zh: 旣至而適卒。
manualTranslations.literal: He had barely arrived when Gao Shi died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He had scarcely arrived when Gao Shi died.

manualTranslations.zh: 是歲，崔寧殺英乂，楊子琳攻西川，蜀中大亂。
manualTranslations.literal: That year Cui Ning killed Yingyi, Yang Zilin attacked western Sichuan, and great chaos erupted in Shu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: That year Cui Ning killed Guo Yingyi, Yang Zilin attacked western Sichuan, and Shu fell into great disorder.

manualTranslations.zh: 甫以其家避亂荊、楚，扁舟下峽，未維舟而江陵亂，乃泝沿湘流，遊衡山，寓居耒陽。
manualTranslations.literal: Fu took his family to flee the disorder to Jing and Chu, boarded a small boat to go down through the gorges, and before he could moor the boat Jiangling fell into disorder. He therefore went upstream along the Xiang River, traveled to Mount Heng, and lodged at Leiyang.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Fu took his family to flee the turmoil into Jing and Chu, boarded a small boat to descend the gorges, and before he could moor, Jiangling erupted in disorder. He then went upstream along the Xiang, visited Mount Heng, and settled at Leiyang.

manualTranslations.zh: 甫嘗遊嶽廟，為暴水所阻，旬日不得食。
manualTranslations.literal: Fu once visited the temple on Mount Heng and was blocked by floodwaters; for ten days he had nothing to eat.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Fu once visited the temple on Mount Heng and was cut off by sudden floodwaters; for ten days he had nothing to eat.

manualTranslations.zh: 耒陽聶令知之，自棹舟迎甫而還。
manualTranslations.literal: The magistrate of Leiyang, surnamed Nie, learned of this and himself rowed a boat to welcome Fu back.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Leiyang, surnamed Nie, learned of this and himself rowed out to bring Du Fu back.

manualTranslations.zh: 永泰二年，啗牛肉白酒，一夕而卒於耒陽，時年五十九。
manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, after eating beef and drinking white liquor, he died one evening at Leiyang, aged fifty-nine.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 766, after eating beef and drinking white liquor, he died one night at Leiyang, aged fifty-nine.

manualTranslations.zh: 子宗武，流落湖、湘而卒。
manualTranslations.literal: His son Zongwu, drifting in Hunan and the Xiang region, also died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: His son Zongwu, adrift in Hunan and the Xiang region, also died.

manualTranslations.zh: 元和中，宗武子嗣業，自耒陽遷甫之柩，歸葬於偃師縣西北首陽山之前。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Zongwu's son Siye moved Fu's coffin from Leiyang and returned it for burial before Mount Shouyang, northwest of Yanshi county.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era Zongwu's son Siye moved Du Fu's coffin from Leiyang and had it reburied at the foot of Mount Shouyang, northwest of Yanshi county.

manualTranslations.zh: 天寶末詩人，甫與李白齊名，而白自負文格放達，譏甫齷齪，而有飯顆山之嘲誚。
manualTranslations.literal: Among poets at the end of Tianbao, Fu was as famous as Li Bai. But Bai, confident in his free and unrestrained literary manner, mocked Fu as cramped and narrow-minded, and there was the ridicule about Fanke Mountain.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Among poets at the end of Tianbao, Du Fu was as renowned as Li Bai. But Li Bai, confident in his free and unrestrained literary style, mocked Du Fu as cramped and petty, giving rise to the jibe about Fanke Mountain.

manualTranslations.zh: 元和中，詞人元稹論李、杜之優劣曰：予讀詩至杜子美而知小大之有所總萃焉。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Yuanhe era the writer Yuan Zhen discussed the relative merits of Li and Du, saying: "When I read poetry and reach Du Zimei, I know that great and small have their gathering point."
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era the writer Yuan Zhen discussed the relative merits of Li Bai and Du Fu, saying: "When I read poetry and reach Du Zimei, I understand that great and small each have their summation."

manualTranslations.zh: 始堯、舜之時，君臣以賡歌相和。
manualTranslations.literal: From the time of Yao and Shun, ruler and ministers responded to one another with successive songs.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From the age of Yao and Shun, rulers and ministers answered one another in successive songs.

manualTranslations.zh: 是後詩人繼作，歷夏、殷、周千餘年，仲尼緝拾選揀，取其干預教化之尤者三百，餘無所聞。
manualTranslations.literal: After this poets continued to compose. Through Xia, Yin, and Zhou for more than a thousand years, Confucius collected and selected, taking three hundred of those that most intervened in moral instruction; of the rest nothing is heard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereafter poets continued to write. Over more than a thousand years from Xia, Yin, and Zhou, Confucius gathered and sifted them, keeping three hundred that most served moral instruction; of the rest nothing survives.

manualTranslations.zh: 騷人作而怨憤之態繁，然猶去風、雅日近，尚相比擬。
manualTranslations.literal: When writers of the Sao style arose, resentful and indignant tones proliferated, yet they still were not far removed from the Feng and Ya in date and could still be compared with them.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Sao-style writers appeared, resentful and indignant tones multiplied, yet they were still not far from the Feng and Ya in time and could still be measured against them.

manualTranslations.zh: 秦、漢已還，採詩之官旣廢，天下妖謠民謳、歌頌諷賦、曲度嬉戲之辭，亦隨時間作。
manualTranslations.literal: From Qin and Han onward, the office for collecting poems was abolished, and throughout the realm demon songs, folk tunes, praise hymns, satirical rhapsodies, and lyrics for tunes and playful compositions also arose from time to time.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han onward the office for collecting poems was abolished, and throughout the realm demon songs, folk airs, hymns of praise, satirical rhapsodies, and lyrics for tunes and playful verses also appeared from time to time.

manualTranslations.zh: 至漢武賦柏梁而七言之體具。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Han rhapsodized on the Cypress Beam, the seven-character form was fully established.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Han composed the Cypress Beam rhapsody, the seven-character form was fully established.

manualTranslations.zh: 蘇子卿、李少卿之徒，尤工為五言。
manualTranslations.literal: Su Ziqing, Li Shaoqing, and their sort were especially skilled at five-character verse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Su Ziqing, Li Shaoqing, and men like them were especially adept at five-character verse.

manualTranslations.zh: 雖句讀文律各異，雅鄭之音亦雜，而辭意簡遠，指事言情，自非有為而為，則文不妄作。
manualTranslations.literal: Although sentence divisions and literary rules differed, and refined and popular tones were mixed, their wording was simple and far-reaching, naming affairs and expressing feelings; unless there was purposeful intent, they did not write recklessly.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Though their phrasing and metrical rules differed and refined and popular tones were mingled, their language was plain and far-reaching, naming events and expressing feeling; unless writing with purpose, they did not compose at random.

manualTranslations.zh: 建安之後，天下之士遭罹兵戰，曹氏父子鞍馬間為文，往往橫槊賦詩，故其遒壯抑揚、冤哀悲離之作，尤極於古。
manualTranslations.literal: After the Jian'an period, scholars throughout the realm suffered warfare. The Cao father and son composed literature between saddle and horse, often brandishing spears while writing poetry. Therefore their vigorous, forceful, repressed and rising works of grievance, sorrow, and parting were among the greatest of antiquity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After the Jian'an period scholars throughout the realm suffered warfare. The Cao father and son wrote between saddle and horse, often brandishing spears while composing poetry; hence their forceful, surging works of grievance, sorrow, and parting rank among the greatest of antiquity.

manualTranslations.zh: 晉世風概稍存。
manualTranslations.literal: In the Jin dynasty something of that spirit was still preserved.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the Jin dynasty something of that spirit still remained.

manualTranslations.zh: 宋、齊之間，教失根本，士以簡慢翕習舒徐相尚，文章以風容色澤、放曠精清為高，蓋吟寫性靈、留連光景之文也，意義格力無取焉。
manualTranslations.literal: Between Song and Qi, instruction lost its root and foundation; scholars took to simplicity, negligence, and ease and languor as their model. Literature prized graceful bearing, sensuous polish, freedom, and refined clarity. Such writing merely sang of one's innate disposition and lingered over passing scenery; in meaning, force, and stature it had nothing to recommend.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Between Song and Qi instruction lost its foundation; scholars came to esteem simplicity, negligence, and leisurely ease. Literature prized graceful bearing, sensuous polish, freedom, and refined clarity—writing that merely voiced one's inner nature and lingered over passing scenery, with nothing to commend in meaning, force, or stature.

manualTranslations.zh: 陵遲至於梁、陳，淫豔刻飾、佻巧小碎之詞劇，又宋、齊之所不取也。
manualTranslations.literal: Decline continued until Liang and Chen, where voluptuous, ornamental, and frivolously clever, finely fragmented lyrics greatly multiplied—what even Song and Qi had not accepted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Decline continued into Liang and Chen, where voluptuous ornament and frivolously clever, finely fragmented lyrics greatly multiplied—what even Song and Qi had rejected.

manualTranslations.zh: 唐興，官學大振，歷世之文，能者互出。
manualTranslations.literal: When Tang rose, official learning flourished greatly, and in successive ages writers of ability emerged one after another.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When the Tang rose, official learning flourished greatly, and in successive reigns capable writers appeared in turn.

manualTranslations.zh: 而又沈、宋之流，研練精切，穩順聲勢，謂之為律詩。
manualTranslations.literal: Then the likes of Shen Quanqi and Song Zhiwen refined and polished with precision, smoothing and ordering sound and rhythmic force—what came to be called regulated verse.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Then the likes of Shen Quanqi and Song Zhiwen refined their craft with precision, smoothing and ordering sound and rhythm—what came to be called regulated verse.

manualTranslations.zh: 由是之後，文體之變極焉。
manualTranslations.literal: From this point onward, literary forms changed to their fullest extent.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: From this point onward literary forms changed to their fullest extent.

manualTranslations.zh: 然而莫不好古者遺近，務華者去實，効齊、梁則不迨於魏、晉，工樂府則力屈於五言，律切則骨格不存，閑暇則纖穠莫備。
manualTranslations.literal: Yet those who favored antiquity neglected the recent; those who pursued ornament abandoned substance. In imitating Qi and Liang they did not reach Wei and Jin; skilled in yuefu they found their strength exhausted in five-character verse; with metrical precision the skeletal structure was lost; with leisurely ease the dense richness was incomplete.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Yet those who favored antiquity neglected the recent; those who pursued ornament abandoned substance. In imitating Qi and Liang they fell short of Wei and Jin; skilled in yuefu they exhausted their strength in five-character verse; with metrical precision skeletal structure was lost; with leisurely ease dense richness was incomplete.

manualTranslations.zh: 至於子美，蓋所謂上薄風、騷，下該沈、宋，言奪蘇、李，氣吞曹、劉，掩顏、謝之孤高，雜徐、庾之流麗，盡得古今之體勢，而兼人人之所獨專矣。
manualTranslations.literal: As for Zimei, he may be said to reach upward to the Feng and Sao, encompass downward Shen and Song, in wording surpass Su and Li, in spirit swallow Cao and Liu, cover over the solitary loftiness of Yan and Xie, blend in the flowing elegance of Xu and Yu, fully attain the formal resources of ancient and modern, and combine what each man had exclusively mastered.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: As for Zimei, he may be said to reach up to the Feng and Sao, encompass Shen and Song below, in wording surpass Su and Li, in spirit swallow Cao and Liu, overshadow the solitary loftiness of Yan and Xie, blend the flowing elegance of Xu and Yu, fully command the formal resources of ancient and modern, and combine what each poet had exclusively mastered.

manualTranslations.zh: 使仲尼考鍛其旨要，尚不知貴其多乎哉！
manualTranslations.literal: If Confucius were to examine and refine his essential points, would he not still value how much he contains!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If Confucius were to examine and refine his essential meaning, would he not still value how much he encompasses!

manualTranslations.zh: 苟以為能所不能，無可無不可，則詩人已來未有如子美者。
manualTranslations.literal: If one holds that he could do what others could not, and was bound by nothing yet could do everything, then since poets began there has never been anyone like Zimei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: If one holds that he could do what others could not and was bound by nothing yet could do everything, then since poets began there has never been anyone like Zimei.

manualTranslations.zh: 是時山東人李白，亦以文奇取稱，時人謂之李、杜。
manualTranslations.literal: At that time Li Bai of Shandong was also famed for his literary strangeness, and people of the time spoke of Li and Du.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At that time Li Bai of Shandong was also celebrated for his literary strangeness, and people of the time spoke of Li and Du.

manualTranslations.zh: 予觀其壯浪縱恣，擺去拘束，模寫物象，及樂府歌詩，誠亦差肩於子美俟。
manualTranslations.literal: I observe that in his bold, unrestrained freedom, casting off constraint, depicting objects and scenes, and in his yuefu songs and ballads, he indeed stands nearly shoulder to shoulder with Zimei.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I observe that in his bold, unrestrained freedom, casting off constraint, depicting objects and scenes, and in his yuefu songs and ballads, he indeed stands nearly shoulder to shoulder with Zimei.

manualTranslations.zh: 至若鋪陳終始，排比聲韻，大或千言，次猶數百，詞氣豪邁，而風調清深，屬對律切，而脫棄凡近，則李尚不能歷其藩翰，況堂奧乎！
manualTranslations.literal: But when it comes to laying out beginning and end, arranging parallel sound and rhyme—at greatest a thousand words, at minimum still several hundred—with diction and breath heroic and expansive yet tonal atmosphere clear and deep, with parallel structure and metrical precision while casting off the commonplace and near at hand—Li cannot yet even pass through his outer gate, how much less enter the inner hall!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: But when it comes to laying out beginning and end, arranging parallel sound and rhyme—at greatest a thousand words, at minimum still several hundred—with diction heroic and expansive yet tonal atmosphere clear and deep, with parallel structure and metrical precision while casting off the commonplace—Li Bai cannot yet even pass through his outer gate, how much less enter the inner hall!

manualTranslations.zh: 予嘗欲條析其文，體別相附，與來者為之準，特病懶未就爾。
manualTranslations.literal: I once wished to itemize and analyze his writings, sort them by form and attach them accordingly, and set a standard for those who come after, but in the end my laziness left the task unfinished.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I once wished to itemize and analyze his writings, classify them by form and attach them accordingly, and set a standard for those who come after, but in the end laziness kept me from completing it.

manualTranslations.zh: 自後屬文者，以稹論為是。
manualTranslations.literal: Afterward, those who wrote literature took Yuan Zhen's discussion as authoritative.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Thereafter writers took Yuan Zhen's judgment as authoritative.

manualTranslations.zh: 甫有文集六十卷。
manualTranslations.literal: Fu had a collected writings in sixty juan.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Du Fu's collected writings ran to sixty juan.

sourceRange.text: 上元元年，辭疾請歸，特賜良馬，及鄱陽公主邑司以居焉。當時知名之士宋令文、孟詵、盧照鄰等，執師資之禮以事焉。思邈嘗從幸九成宮，照鄰留在其宅。時庭前有病梨樹，照鄰為之賦，其序曰：「癸酉之歲，余臥疾長安光德坊之官舍。父老云：'是鄱陽公主邑司。昔公主未嫁而卒，故其邑廢。'時有孫思邈處士居之。邈道合古今，學殫數術。高談正一，則古之蒙莊子；深入不二，則今之維摩詰。其推步甲乙，度量乾坤，則洛下閎、安期先生之儔也。」照鄰有惡疾，醫所不能愈，乃問思邈：「名醫愈疾，其道何如？」思邈曰：吾聞善言天者，必質之於人，善言人者，亦本之於天。

localRange.text: 吾聞善言天者，必質之於人，善言人者，亦本之於天。

sourceRange.text: 原武尉盧甫妻李氏，隴西成紀人也。父瀾，永泰元年春任蘄縣令。界內先有草賊二千餘人。瀾挺身入賊，結以誠信，賊並降附，百姓復業者二百餘家。時曹升任徐州刺史，知賊降，領兵掩襲。賊得脫後，入縣殺瀾。瀾將被殺，從父弟渤，詣賊救瀾，請代兄死。瀾又請留弟，弟兄爭死。瀾女盧甫妻，又泣請代父死。並為賊所害，宣慰使、吏部侍郎李季卿以節義聞。

sourceRange.text: 楚王靈龜妃上官氏，秦州上邽人。父懷仁，右金吾將軍。上官年十八，歸於靈龜，繼楚哀王後。本生具存，朝夕侍奉，恭謹彌甚。凡有新味，非舅姑啖訖，未曾先嘗。經數載，靈龜薨。及將葬，其前妃閻氏，嫁不逾年而卒，又無近族，眾議欲不舉之。上官氏曰：「必神而靈，寧可使孤魂無托！」於是備禮同葬，聞者莫不嘉嘆。服終，諸兄姊謂曰：「妃年尚少，又無所生，改醮異門，禮儀常範，妃可思之。」妃掩泣對曰：「丈夫以義烈標名，婦人以守節為行。未能即先犬馬，以殉溝壑，寧可復飾妝服，有他志乎！」遽將刀截鼻割耳以自誓，諸兄姊知其志不可奪，嘆息而止。尋卒。

context.afterSource: 楊紹宗妻王氏，華州華陰人也。

manualTranslations.zh: 楚王靈龜妃上官氏，秦州上邽人。
manualTranslations.literal: Shangguan Shi, consort of Prince Lingui of Chu—Shangguan Shi was a native of Shanggui in Qinzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shangguan Shi, consort of Prince Lingui of Chu, was a native of Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.

manualTranslations.zh: 父懷仁，右金吾將軍。
manualTranslations.literal: Her father Huairen was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her father Huairen was a general of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

manualTranslations.zh: 上官年十八，歸於靈龜，繼楚哀王後。
manualTranslations.literal: When Shangguan was eighteen she married Lingui, succeeding after the lamented King of Chu.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, succeeding as consort after the lamented King of Chu.

manualTranslations.zh: 本生具存，朝夕侍奉，恭謹彌甚。
manualTranslations.literal: Her birth parents were still alive; morning and evening she attended them, her respect and care ever increasing.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Her birth parents were still alive; morning and evening she attended them with ever-increasing respect and care.

manualTranslations.zh: 凡有新味，非舅姑啖訖，未曾先嘗。
manualTranslations.literal: Whenever there was some new delicacy, unless her parents-in-law had finished tasting it, she never tasted it first.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Whenever there was a new delicacy, she never tasted it until her parents-in-law had finished.

manualTranslations.zh: 經數載，靈龜薨。
manualTranslations.literal: After several years Lingui died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After several years Prince Lingui died.

manualTranslations.zh: 及將葬，其前妃閻氏，嫁不逾年而卒，又無近族，眾議欲不舉之。
manualTranslations.literal: When he was about to be buried, his former consort Lady Yan, who had married less than a year before dying and had no close kin, the assembly debated not conducting her funeral.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When he was about to be buried, his former consort Lady Yan had married less than a year before dying and had no close kin; the assembly debated whether to bury her at all.

manualTranslations.zh: 上官氏曰：「必神而靈，寧可使孤魂無托！」
manualTranslations.literal: Shangguan said: "If spirits are divine and numinous, how could one let a solitary soul have no resting place!"
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Shangguan said, "If the dead retain consciousness, how could we leave a solitary soul without a resting place!"

manualTranslations.zh: 於是備禮同葬，聞者莫不嘉嘆。
manualTranslations.literal: She then prepared full rites and buried her together; all who heard of it sighed in admiration.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She prepared full rites and buried her with him; all who heard sighed in admiration.

manualTranslations.zh: 服終，諸兄姊謂曰：「妃年尚少，又無所生，改醮異門，禮儀常範，妃可思之。」
manualTranslations.literal: When her mourning ended, her elder brothers and sisters said: "The consort is still young and bore no children; to remarry into another house is ordinary ritual propriety—the consort should consider it.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When her mourning ended, her siblings said, "You are still young and bore no children; remarriage is ordinary custom—you should consider it.

manualTranslations.zh: 妃掩泣對曰：「丈夫以義烈標名，婦人以守節為行。
manualTranslations.literal: The consort covered her face and wept, replying: "A husband makes his name through righteous heroism; a wife makes her conduct through keeping integrity.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Covering her face, she wept and replied, "A husband wins renown through righteous courage; a wife wins it through steadfast integrity.

manualTranslations.zh: 未能即先犬馬，以殉溝壑，寧可復飾妝服，有他志乎！」
manualTranslations.literal: I have not yet been able to go before the hounds and horses and follow them into the ditch—how could I again adorn myself in dress and have another intent!
manualTranslations.idiomatic: I have not yet been able to follow my husband into the grave—how could I adorn myself again and turn to another man!

manualTranslations.zh: 遽將刀截鼻割耳以自誓，諸兄姊知其志不可奪，嘆息而止。
manualTranslations.literal: She at once took a knife and cut off her nose and ear in oath; her siblings, knowing her resolve could not be changed, sighed and desisted.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She immediately took a knife and cut off her nose and ear in pledge; her siblings, seeing her resolve could not be changed, sighed and gave up.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋卒。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon after she died.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: She died soon afterward.

manualTranslations.literal: Yonglong first year, Turks again welcomed Jieli's paternal cousin's son Ashina Funian at Xia Zhou, intending to cross the river and install as khan—tribes again responded and followed.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonglong the Turks again welcomed Jieli's paternal cousin's son Ashina Funian at Xia Prefecture, intending to cross the river and install him as khan. The tribes once more answered and followed.

manualTranslations.zh: 又詔裴行儉率將軍曹繼叔、程務挺、李崇直、李文暕等討之。
manualTranslations.literal: Again ordered Pei Xingjian leading Generals Cao Jishu, Cheng Wuting, Li Chongzhi, Li Wenliang and others to suppress.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: The court again ordered Pei Xingjian, with Generals Cao Jishu, Cheng Wuting, Li Chongzhi, and Li Wenliang, to suppress them.

manualTranslations.zh: 伏念窘急，詣行儉降。
manualTranslations.literal: Funian in dire straits, came to Xingjian to surrender.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Funian, hard pressed, came to Xingjian and surrendered.

manualTranslations.zh: 行儉遂虜伏念詣京師，斬於東市。
manualTranslations.literal: Xingjian thereupon took Fuzhen captive and brought him to the capital, executing him at the Eastern Market.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Xingjian then marched Fuzhen as a prisoner to the capital and had him beheaded at the Eastern Market.

manualTranslations.literal: In the second year of Yongchun, Ashina Gutulu of the Turks rebelled again.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In 683, Ashina Gutulu of the Türks rose in rebellion once more.

sourceRange.text: 中宗即位，默啜又寇靈州鳴沙縣。靈武軍大總管沙咤忠義拒戰久之，官軍敗績，死者六千餘人。賊遂進寇原、會等州，掠隴右群牧馬萬餘匹而去，忠義坐免。中宗下制絕其請婚，仍購募能斬獲默啜者封國王，授諸衛大將軍，賞物二千段。又命內外官各進破突厥諸策。右補闕盧俌上疏曰：臣聞有虞咸熙，苗人逆命，殷宗大化，鬼方不賓，則戎狄交侵，其來遠矣。

sourceRange.text: 阿史那賀魯者，曳步利設射匱特勒之子也。初，阿史那步真既來歸國，咄陸可汗乃立賀魯為葉護，以繼步真。居於多邏斯川，在西州直北一千五百里，統處密、處月、姑蘇、歌羅祿、弩失畢五姓之眾。其後，咄陸西走吐火羅國，射匱可汗遣兵迫逐，賀魯不常厥居。貞觀二十二年，乃率其部落內屬，詔居廷州。尋授左驍衛將軍、瑤池都督。高宗即位，進拜左驍衛大將軍，瑤池都督如故。

manualTranslations.literal: Ashina Helu was the son of Yebuli She Shekui Teler.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Ashina Helu was the son of Yebuli She Shekui Teler.

manualTranslations.zh: 初，阿史那步真既來歸國，咄陸可汗乃立賀魯為葉護，以繼步真。
manualTranslations.literal: At first, after Ashina Buzhen came to submit to the Tang, Dulo Khan installed Helu as yabghu to succeed Buzhen.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: After Ashina Buzhen came over to the Tang, Dulo Khan installed Helu as yabghu to succeed him.

manualTranslations.zh: 居於多邏斯川，在西州直北一千五百里，統處密、處月、姑蘇、歌羅祿、弩失畢五姓之眾。
manualTranslations.literal: He dwelt on the Talas River, fifteen hundred li due north of Xizhou, commanding the five surname peoples of Chumi, Chuyue, Gusu, Qarluq, and Nishibi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He made his seat on the Talas River, fifteen hundred li due north of Xizhou, and ruled the five surname peoples of Chumi, Chuyue, Gusu, Qarluq, and Nishibi.

manualTranslations.zh: 其後，咄陸西走吐火羅國，射匱可汗遣兵迫逐，賀魯不常厥居。
manualTranslations.literal: Later, when Dulo fled west to Tuhuolo, Shekui Khan sent troops in pursuit; Helu had no fixed residence.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: Later, when Dulo fled west to Tuhuolo, Shekui Khan sent troops after him, and Helu had no fixed home.

manualTranslations.zh: 貞觀二十二年，乃率其部落內屬，詔居廷州。
manualTranslations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan he led his tribes to submit; an edict settled them in Tingzhou.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan he led his tribes to submit. An edict settled them in Tingzhou.

manualTranslations.zh: 尋授左驍衛將軍、瑤池都督。
manualTranslations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Left Brave Guards and Military Governor of Yaochi.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed General of the Left Brave Guards and Military Governor of Yaochi.

manualTranslations.zh: 高宗即位，進拜左驍衛大將軍，瑤池都督如故。
manualTranslations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Helu was promoted to Grand General of the Left Brave Guards, retaining the Yaochi governorship.
manualTranslations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Helu was promoted to Grand General of the Left Brave Guards while keeping his post as Military Governor of Yaochi.

sourceRange.text: 如意元年，為來俊臣誣謀反被害。其子獻，配流崖州。長安三年，召還。累授右驍衛大將軍，襲父興昔亡可汗，充安撫招慰十姓大使。獻本蕃漸為默啜及烏質勒所侵。遂不敢還國。開元中，累遷右金吾大將軍。卒於長安。阿史那步真者，在本蕃授左屯衛大將軍。與彌射討平賀魯，加授驃騎大將軍、行右衛大將軍、濛池都護、繼往絕可汗，押五弩失畢部落。尋卒。其子斛瑟羅，本蕃為步利設，垂拱初，授右玉鈐衛將軍兼濛池都護、襲繼往絕可汗，押五弩失畢部落。天授元年，拜左衛大將軍，改封竭忠事主可汗，仍賜濛池都護。尋卒。子懷道，神龍年累授右屯衛大將軍、光祿卿，轉太仆卿兼濛池都護、十姓可汗。自垂拱已後，十姓部落頻被突厥默啜侵掠，死散殆盡。及隨斛瑟羅才六七萬人，徙居內地，西突厥阿史那氏於是遂絕。

context.beforeSource: 尋進授元慶左衛大將軍。
context.afterSource: 突騎施烏質勒者，西突厥之別種也。
